oci_execute($s);
oci_fetch_all($s, $res);

sleep(30);
?>

note.title: Oracle version requirement
note.simpara: This function is available when PHP is linked with Oracle Database libraries from version 10g onwards.

tip.title: Performance
tip.simpara: With older versions of OCI8 or the Oracle Database, the client information can be set using the Oracle DBMS_APPLICATION_INFO package. This is less efficient than using oci_set_client_info.

caution.title: Round-trip Gotcha
caution.simpara: Some but not all OCI8 functions cause round-trips. Round-trips to the database may not occur with queries when result caching is enabled.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sets number of rows to be prefetched by queries

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sets the number of rows to be buffered by the Oracle Client libraries after a successful query call to oci_execute and for each subsequent internal fetch request to the database. For queries returning a large number of rows, performance can be significantly improved by increasing the prefetch count above the default oci8.default_prefetch value.

Prefetching is Oracle's efficient way of returning more than one data row from the database in each network request. This can result in better network and CPU utilization. The buffering of rows is internal to OCI8 and the behavior of OCI8 fetching functions is unchanged regardless of the prefetch count. For example, oci_fetch_row will always return one row. The prefetch buffer is per-statement and is not used by re-executed statements or by other connections.
Call oci_set_prefetch before calling oci_execute.

A tuning goal is to set the prefetch value to a reasonable size for the network and database to handle. For queries returning a very large number of rows, overall system efficiency might be better if rows are retrieved from the database in several chunks (i.e set the prefetch value smaller than the number of rows). This allows the database to handle other users' statements while the PHP script is processing the current set of rows.

Query prefetching was introduced in Oracle 8i. REF CURSOR prefetching was introduced in Oracle 11gR2 and occurs when PHP is linked with Oracle 11gR2 (or later) Client libraries. Nested cursor prefetching was introduced in Oracle 11gR2 and requires both the Oracle Client libraries and the database to be version 11gR2 or greater.
Prefetching is not supported when queries contain LONG or LOB columns. The prefetch value is ignored and single-row fetches will be used in all the situations when prefetching is not supported.
When using Oracle Database 12c, the prefetch value set by PHP can be overridden by Oracle's client oraaccess.xml configuration file. Refer to Oracle documentation for more detail.

listitem.simpara: A valid OCI8 statement identifier created by oci_parse and executed by oci_execute, or a REF CURSOR statement identifier.

listitem.para: The number of rows to be prefetched, >= 0

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refsect1.title: Examples

example.title: Changing the default prefetch value for a query
example.programlisting: \n"; while ($row = oci_fetch_array($stid, OCI_ASSOC+OCI_RETURN_NULLS)) { echo "\n"; foreach ($row as $item) { echo " ".($item !== null ? htmlentities($item, ENT_QUOTES) : " ")."\n"; } echo "\n"; } echo "\n"; oci_free_statement($stid); oci_close($conn); ?>

example.title: Changing the default prefetch for a REF CURSOR fetch
example.programlisting: \n"; while ($row = oci_fetch_array($refcur, OCI_ASSOC+OCI_RETURN_NULLS)) { echo "\n"; foreach ($row as $item) { echo " ".($item !== null ? htmlentities($item, ENT_QUOTES) : " ")."\n"; } echo "\n"; } echo "\n"; oci_free_statement($refcur); oci_free_statement($stid); oci_close($conn); ?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sets the amount of data prefetched for each CLOB or BLOB.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sets the internal buffer size used to fetch each CLOB or BLOB value when the implementation gets the internal Oracle LOB locator from the database after a successful query call to oci_execute and for each subsequent internal fetch request to the database. Increasing this value can improve the performance of fetching smaller LOBs by reducing round-trips between PHP and the database. Memory usage will change.
The value affects LOBs returned as OCILob instances and also those returned using OCI_RETURN_LOBS.
Call oci_set_prefetch_lob before calling oci_execute. If it is not called, the value of oci8.prefetch_lob_size is used.
The LOB prefetch value should only be set with Oracle Database 12.2 or later.

listitem.simpara: A valid OCI8 statement identifier created by oci_parse and executed by oci_execute, or a REF CURSOR statement identifier.

listitem.para: The number of bytes of each LOB to be prefetched, >= 0

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Changing the LOB prefetch value for a query
example.programlisting: \n"; while ($row = oci_fetch_array($stid, OCI_ASSOC+OCI_RETURN_NULLS+OCI_RETURN_LOBS)) { echo "\n"; foreach ($row as $item) { echo " ".($item !== null ? htmlentities($item, ENT_QUOTES) : " ")."\n"; } echo "\n"; } echo "\n"; oci_free_statement($stid); oci_close($conn); ?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the type of a statement

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns a keyword identifying the type of the OCI8 statement.

listitem.para: A valid OCI8 statement identifier from oci_parse.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para:
Returns the type of statement as one of the following strings.
Statement type
Return String Notes
ALTER
BEGIN
CALL
CREATE
DECLARE
DELETE
DROP
INSERT
SELECT
UPDATE
UNKNOWN
Returns false on error.

example.title: oci_statement_type example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$conn = oci_connect('hr', 'welcome', 'localhost/XE');

$stid = oci_parse($conn, 'DELETE FROM departments WHERE department_id = 130;');
if (oci_statement_type($stid) == "DELETE") {
    trigger_error('You are not allowed to delete from this table', E_USER_ERROR);
}
else {
    oci_execute($stid);  // delete the row
}

oci_free_statement($stid);
oci_close($conn);

?>

refsect1.para: Unregister the user-defined callback function registered to connection by oci_register_taf_callback. See OCI8 Transparent Application Failover (TAF) Support for information.

listitem.para: An Oracle connection identifier.

refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Flushes/writes buffer of the LOB to the server

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: OCILob::flush actually writes data to the server.

listitem.para: By default, resources are not freed, but using flag OCI_LOB_BUFFER_FREE you can do it explicitly. Be sure you know what you're doing - next read/write operation to the same part of LOB will involve a round-trip to the server and initialize new buffer resources. It is recommended to use OCI_LOB_BUFFER_FREE flag only when you are not going to work with the LOB anymore.

refsect1.title: Return Values

Returns false if buffering was not enabled or an error occurred.

preface.title: Introduction
preface.para: PostgreSQL database is an open source product and available without cost. Postgres, developed originally in the UC Berkeley Computer Science Department, pioneered many of the object-relational concepts now becoming available in some commercial databases. It provides SQL92/SQL99 language support, transactions, referential integrity, stored procedures and type extensibility. PostgreSQL is an open source descendant of this original Berkeley code.

section.title: Requirements
section.para: To use PostgreSQL support, you need libpq (the PostgreSQL C client library). As of PHP 8.0.0, libpq 9.1 or later is required. As of PHP 8.4.0, libpq 10.0 or later is required. PostgreSQL supports many character encodings including multibyte character encoding. The current version and more information about PostgreSQL is available at http://www.postgresql.org/ and the PostgreSQL Documentation.

section.title: Installation
section.para: In order to enable PostgreSQL support, --with-pgsql[=DIR] is required when you compile PHP. DIR is the PostgreSQL base install directory, defaults to /usr/local/pgsql. If shared object module is available, PostgreSQL module may be loaded using extension directive in php.ini or dl function.

section.title: Runtime Configuration
section.simpara: The behaviour of these functions is affected by settings in php.ini.
section.para:
PostgreSQL configuration options
Name Default Changeable Changelog
pgsql.allow_persistent "1" INI_SYSTEM
pgsql.max_persistent "-1" INI_SYSTEM
pgsql.max_links "-1" INI_SYSTEM
pgsql.auto_reset_persistent "0" INI_SYSTEM
pgsql.ignore_notice "0" INI_ALL
pgsql.log_notice "0" INI_ALL
For further details and definitions of the INI_* modes, see the .
section.simpara: Here's a short explanation of the configuration directives.

listitem.para: Whether to allow persistent Postgres connections.
The maximum number of persistent Postgres connections per process.
The maximum number of Postgres connections per process, including persistent connections.
Detect broken persistent links with pg_pconnect. Needs a little overhead.
Whether or not to ignore PostgreSQL backend notices.
Whether or not to log PostgreSQL backends notice messages. The PHP directive pgsql.ignore_notice must be off in order to log notice messages.

section.title: Resource Types
section.para: Prior to PHP 8.1.0, there were two resource types used in the PostgreSQL module. The first one is the link identifier for a database connection, the second a resource which holds the result of a query.

appendix.title: Predefined Constants
appendix.simpara: The constants below are defined by this extension, and will only be available when the extension has either been compiled into PHP or dynamically loaded at runtime.

listitem.simpara: Short libpq version that contains only numbers and dots.
Prior to PHP 8.0.0, the long libpq version that includes compiler information. As of PHP 8.0.0, the value is identical to PGSQL_LIBPQ_VERSION, and using PGSQL_LIBPQ_VERSION_STR is deprecated.

The result set is divided into multiple chunks, each containing a predefined number of rows. Available as of PHP 8.4.0 and libpq 17.

Returned by pg_result_status. Copy In (to server) data transfer started.

Passed to pg_result_error_field. The severity; the field contents are ERROR, FATAL, or PANIC (in an error message), or WARNING, NOTICE, DEBUG, INFO, or LOG (in a notice message), or a localized translation of one of these. Always present.

Passed to pg_result_error_field. The SQLSTATE code for the error. The SQLSTATE code identifies the type of error that has occurred; it can be used by front-end applications to perform specific operations (such as error handling) in response to a particular database error. This field is not localizable, and is always present.
Passed to pg_result_error_field. The primary human-readable error message (typically one line). Always present.
Passed to pg_result_error_field. Detail: an optional secondary error message carrying more detail about the problem. May run to multiple lines.

Passed to pg_result_error_field. Hint: an optional suggestion what to do about the problem. This is intended to differ from detail in that it offers advice (potentially inappropriate) rather than hard facts. May run to multiple lines.

Passed to pg_result_error_field. A string containing a decimal integer indicating an error cursor position as an index into the original statement string. The first character has index 1, and positions are measured in characters not bytes.

Passed to pg_result_error_field. This is defined the same as the PG_DIAG_STATEMENT_POSITION field, but it is used when the cursor position refers to an internally generated command rather than the one submitted by the client. The PG_DIAG_INTERNAL_QUERY field will always appear when this field appears.
Passed to pg_result_error_field. The text of a failed internally-generated command. This could be, for example, a SQL query issued by a PL/pgSQL function.

Passed to pg_result_error_field. An indication of the context in which the error occurred. Presently this includes a call stack traceback of active procedural language functions and internally-generated queries. The trace is one entry per line, most recent first.
Passed to pg_result_error_field. The file name of the PostgreSQL source-code location where the error was reported.
Passed to pg_result_error_field. The line number of the PostgreSQL source-code location where the error was reported.
Passed to pg_result_error_field. The name of the PostgreSQL source-code function reporting the error.

Passed to pg_insert, pg_select, pg_update and pg_delete. All parameters passed as is. Manual escape is required if parameters contain user supplied data. Use pg_escape_string for it.
Passed to pg_insert, pg_select, pg_update and pg_delete. Execute query by these functions.
Passed to pg_insert, pg_select, pg_update and pg_delete. Execute asynchronous query by these functions.
Passed to pg_insert, pg_select, pg_update and pg_delete. Return executed query string.

Passed to pg_insert, pg_select, pg_update and pg_delete. Apply escape to all parameters instead of calling pg_convert internally. This option omits meta data look up. Query could be as fast as pg_query and pg_send_query.
Returned by pg_connect_poll to indicate that the connection attempt failed.
Returned by pg_connect_poll to indicate that the connection is waiting for the PostgreSQL socket to be readable.
Returned by pg_connect_poll to indicate that the connection is waiting for the PostgreSQL socket to be writable.
Returned by pg_connect_poll to indicate that the connection is ready to be used.
Returned by pg_connect_poll to indicate that the connection is currently active.

The severity; the field contents are ERROR, FATAL, or PANIC (in an error message), or WARNING, NOTICE, DEBUG, INFO, or LOG (in a notice message). This is identical to the PG_DIAG_SEVERITY field except that the contents are never localized. This is present only in versions 9.6 and later / PHP 7.3.0 and later.
To be used with pg_set_error_context_visibility, the context is never shown. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
To be used with pg_set_error_context_visibility, the context's fields are included in error messages only. This is the default behaviour. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
To be used with pg_set_error_context_visibility, the context's fields are included in error, notice and warning messages. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.

section.title: Basic usage
Basic usage

note.para: Not all functions are supported by all builds. It depends on your libpq (The PostgreSQL C client library) version and how libpq is compiled. If PHP PostgreSQL extensions are missing, then it is because your libpq version does not support them.
Most PostgreSQL functions accept connection as the optional first parameter. If it is not provided, the last opened connection is used. If it doesn't exist, functions return false.

PostgreSQL automatically folds all identifiers (e.g. table/column names) to lower-case values at object creation time and at query time. To force the use of mixed or upper case identifiers, you must escape the identifier using double quotes ("").

PostgreSQL does not have special commands for fetching database schema information (eg. all the tables in the current database). Instead, there is a standard schema named information_schema containing system views with all the necessary information, in an easily queryable form. See the PostgreSQL Documentation for full details.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns number of affected records (tuples)

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_affected_rows returns the number of tuples (instances/records/rows) affected by INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE queries.
The server also returns the number of SELECTed rows.

note.para: This function used to be called pg_cmdtuples.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The number of rows affected by the query. If no tuple is affected, it will return 0.

row.entry: The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_affected_rows example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$result = pg_query($conn, "INSERT INTO authors VALUES ('Orwell', 2002, 'Animal Farm')");

$cmdtuples = pg_affected_rows($result);

echo $cmdtuples . " tuples are affected.\n";
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Cancel an asynchronous query

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_cancel_query cancels an asynchronous query sent with pg_send_query, pg_send_query_params or pg_send_execute. You cannot cancel a query executed using pg_query.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_cancel_query example
example.programlisting:
<?php
  $dbconn = pg_connect("dbname=publisher") or die("Could not connect");

  if (!pg_connection_busy($dbconn)) {
      pg_send_query($dbconn, "select * from authors; select count(*) from authors;");
  }
  
  $res1 = pg_get_result($dbconn);
  echo "First call to pg_get_result(): $res1\n";
  $rows1 = pg_num_rows($res1);
  echo "$res1 has $rows1 records\n\n";
  
  // Cancel the currently running query.  Will be the second query if it is
  // still running.
  pg_cancel_query($dbconn);
?>
example.screen: First call to pg_get_result(): Resource id #3 Resource id #3 has 3 records

refnamediv.refpurpose: Change a PostgreSQL user's password

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: pg_change_password changes the password of a PostgreSQL user. This function uses the PQchangePassword libpq function which handles password encryption automatically based on the server's settings.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.
The name of the PostgreSQL user whose password to change.
The new password.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets the client encoding

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: PostgreSQL supports automatic character set conversion between server and client for certain character sets. pg_client_encoding returns the client encoding as a string. The returned string will be one of the standard PostgreSQL encoding identifiers.

note.para: If libpq is compiled without multibyte encoding support, pg_client_encoding always returns SQL_ASCII. Supported encoding depends on PostgreSQL version. Refer to the PostgreSQL Documentation supported encodings.
The function used to be called pg_clientencoding.

listitem.para: An PgSql\Connection instance. When connection is null, the default connection is used. The default connection is the last connection made by pg_connect or pg_pconnect. As of PHP 8.1.0, using the default connection is deprecated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The client encoding.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_client_encoding example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// Assume $conn is a connection to a ISO-8859-1 database
$encoding = pg_client_encoding($conn);

echo "Client encoding is: ", $encoding, "\n";
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Closes a PostgreSQL connection

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_close closes the non-persistent connection to a PostgreSQL database associated with the given connection instance.

note.para: Using pg_close is not usually necessary, as non-persistent open connections are automatically closed at the end of the script.

refsect1.para: If there is open PgSql\Lob instance on the connection, do not close the connection before closing all PgSql\Lob instances.

listitem.para: An PgSql\Connection instance. When connection is null, the default connection is used. The default connection is the last connection made by pg_connect or pg_pconnect. As of PHP 8.1.0, using the default connection is deprecated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Always returns true.

row.entry: The return type is true now; previously, it was bool.
The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_close example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$dbconn = pg_connect("host=localhost port=5432 dbname=mary")
   or die("Could not connect");
echo "Connected successfully";
pg_close($dbconn);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Closes a prepared statement

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Closes a prepared statement on the server, freeing its resources and making its name available for reuse. It is an alternative to issuing a DEALLOCATE SQL command, which does not allow the statement name to be reused afterwards.
This function is only available if PHP has been built against libpq 17 or later.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.
The name of the prepared statement to close.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: A PgSql\Result instance on success, or false on failure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Throws a ValueError if statement_name is empty or contains any null bytes.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Open a PostgreSQL connection

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_connect opens a connection to a PostgreSQL database specified by the connection_string.
If a second call is made to pg_connect with the same connection_string as an existing connection, the existing connection will be returned unless you pass PGSQL_CONNECT_FORCE_NEW as flags.
The old syntax with multiple parameters $conn = pg_connect("host", "port", "options", "tty", "dbname") has been deprecated.

listitem.para: The connection_string can be empty to use all default parameters, or it can contain one or more parameter settings separated by whitespace. Each parameter setting is in the form keyword = value. Spaces around the equal sign are optional. To write an empty value or a value containing spaces, surround it with single quotes, e.g., keyword = 'a value'. Single quotes and backslashes within the value must be escaped with a backslash, i.e., \' and \\.

The currently recognized parameter keywords are: host, hostaddr, port, dbname (defaults to value of user), user, password, connect_timeout, options, tty (ignored), sslmode, requiressl (deprecated in favor of sslmode), and service. Which of these arguments exist depends on your PostgreSQL version.
The options parameter can be used to set command line parameters to be invoked by the server.
If PGSQL_CONNECT_FORCE_NEW is passed, then a new connection is created, even if the connection_string is identical to an existing connection.
If PGSQL_CONNECT_ASYNC is given, then the connection is established asynchronously. The state of the connection can then be checked via pg_connect_poll or pg_connection_status.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns an PgSql\Connection instance on success, or false on failure.

row.entry: A ValueError is now thrown if connection_string contains null bytes.
Returns an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was returned.

example.title: Using pg_connect
example.programlisting:
<?php
$dbconn = pg_connect("dbname=mary");
//connect to a database named "mary"

$dbconn2 = pg_connect("host=localhost port=5432 dbname=mary");
// connect to a database named "mary" on "localhost" at port "5432"

$dbconn3 = pg_connect("host=sheep port=5432 dbname=mary user=lamb password=foo");
//connect to a database named "mary" on the host "sheep" with a username and password

$conn_string = "host=sheep port=5432 dbname=test user=lamb password=bar";
$dbconn4 = pg_connect($conn_string);
//connect to a database named "test" on the host "sheep" with a username and password

$dbconn5 = pg_connect("host=localhost options='--client_encoding=UTF8'");
//connect to a database on "localhost" and set the command line parameter which tells the encoding is in UTF-8
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Poll the status of an in-progress asynchronous PostgreSQL connection attempt

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_connect_poll polls the status of a PostgreSQL connection created by calling pg_connect with the PGSQL_CONNECT_ASYNC option.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns PGSQL_POLLING_FAILED, PGSQL_POLLING_READING, PGSQL_POLLING_WRITING, PGSQL_POLLING_OK, or PGSQL_POLLING_ACTIVE.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get connection is busy or not

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_connection_busy determines whether or not a connection is busy. If it is busy, a previous query is still executing. If pg_get_result is used on the connection, it will be blocked.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the connection is busy, false otherwise.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_connection_busy example
example.programlisting:
<?php
  $dbconn = pg_connect("dbname=publisher") or die("Could not connect");
  $bs = pg_connection_busy($dbconn);
  if ($bs) {
      echo 'connection is busy';
  } else {
     echo 'connection is not busy';
  }
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Reset connection (reconnect)

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_connection_reset resets the connection. It is useful for error recovery.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_connection_reset example
example.programlisting:
<?php
  $dbconn = pg_connect("dbname=publisher") or die("Could not connect");
  $dbconn2 = pg_connection_reset($dbconn);
  if ($dbconn2) {
      echo "reset successful\n";
  } else {
      echo "reset failed\n";
  }
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get connection status

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_connection_status returns the status of the specified connection.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: PGSQL_CONNECTION_OK or PGSQL_CONNECTION_BAD.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_connection_status example
example.programlisting:
<?php
  $dbconn = pg_connect("dbname=publisher") or die("Could not connect");
  $stat = pg_connection_status($dbconn);
  if ($stat === PGSQL_CONNECTION_OK) {
      echo 'Connection status ok';
  } else {
      echo 'Connection status bad';
  }    
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Reads input on the connection

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_consume_input consumes any input waiting to be read from the database server.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: true if no error occurred, or false if there was an error. Note that true does not necessarily indicate that input was waiting to be read.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Convert associative array values into forms suitable for SQL statements

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_convert checks and converts the values in values into suitable values for use in an SQL statement. Precondition for pg_convert is the existence of a table table_name which has at least as many columns as values has elements. The fieldnames in table_name must match the indices in values and the corresponding datatypes must be compatible. Returns an array with the converted values on success, false otherwise.

note.para: Boolean values are accepted and converted to PostgreSQL booleans. String representations of boolean values are also supported. null is converted to PostgreSQL NULL.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

listitem.para: Name of the table against which to convert types.
Data to be converted.
Any number of PGSQL_CONV_IGNORE_DEFAULT, PGSQL_CONV_FORCE_NULL or PGSQL_CONV_IGNORE_NOT_NULL, combined.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array of converted values, or false on failure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: A ValueError or TypeError is thrown when the value or type of field does not match properly with a PostgreSQL's type.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_convert example
example.programlisting:
<?php 
  $dbconn = pg_connect('dbname=foo');
  
  $tmp = array(
      'author' => 'Joe Thackery',
      'year' => 2005,
      'title' => 'My Life, by Joe Thackery'
  );
  
  $vals = pg_convert($dbconn, 'authors', $tmp);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Insert records into a table from an array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_copy_from inserts records into a table from rows. It issues a COPY FROM SQL command internally to insert records.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

listitem.para: Name of the table into which to copy the rows.

An iterable data to be copied into table_name. Each value in rows becomes a row in table_name. Each value in rows should be a delimited string of the values to insert into each field. Values should be linefeed terminated.
The token that separates values for each field in each element of rows. Default is \t.
How SQL NULL values are represented in the rows. Default is \\N ("\\\\N").

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: rows is now of type iterable. Previously, it was of type array.
The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_copy_from example
example.programlisting:
<?php
   $db = pg_connect("dbname=publisher") or die("Could not connect");
   
   $rows = pg_copy_to($db, $table_name);
   
   pg_query($db, "DELETE FROM $table_name");
   
   pg_copy_from($db, $table_name, $rows);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Copy a table to an array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_copy_to copies a table to an array. It issues COPY TO SQL command internally to retrieve records.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

listitem.para: Name of the table from which to copy the data into rows.
The token that separates values for each field in each element of rows. Default is \t.
How SQL NULL values are represented in the rows. Default is \\N ("\\\\N").

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array with one element for each line of COPY data, or false on failure.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_copy_to example
example.programlisting:
<?php
   $db = pg_connect("dbname=publisher") or die("Could not connect");
   
   $rows = pg_copy_to($db, $table_name);
   
   pg_query($db, "DELETE FROM $table_name");
   
   pg_copy_from($db, $table_name, $rows);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the database name

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_dbname returns the name of the database that the given PostgreSQL connection instance.

listitem.para: An PgSql\Connection instance. When connection is null, the default connection is used. The default connection is the last connection made by pg_connect or pg_pconnect. As of PHP 8.1.0, using the default connection is deprecated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A string containing the name of the database the connection is to.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_dbname example
example.programlisting:
<?php
  error_reporting(E_ALL);

  pg_connect("host=localhost port=5432 dbname=mary");
  echo pg_dbname(); // mary
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Deletes records

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_delete deletes records from a table specified by the keys and values in conditions.
If flags is specified, pg_convert is applied to conditions with the specified flags.

By default pg_delete passes raw values. Values must be escaped or the PGSQL_DML_ESCAPE flag must be specified in flags. PGSQL_DML_ESCAPE quotes and escapes parameters/identifiers. Therefore, table/column names become case sensitive.
Note that neither escape nor prepared query can protect LIKE query, JSON, Array, Regex, etc. These parameters should be handled according to their contexts. i.e. Escape/validate values.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

listitem.para: Name of the table from which to delete rows.
An array whose keys are field names in the table table_name, and whose values are the values of those fields that are to be deleted.

Any number of PGSQL_CONV_FORCE_NULL, PGSQL_DML_NO_CONV, PGSQL_DML_ESCAPE, PGSQL_DML_EXEC, PGSQL_DML_ASYNC or PGSQL_DML_STRING combined. If PGSQL_DML_STRING is part of the flags then query string is returned. When PGSQL_DML_NO_CONV or PGSQL_DML_ESCAPE is set, it does not call pg_convert internally.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure. Returns string if PGSQL_DML_STRING is passed via flags.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_delete example
example.programlisting:
<?php 
  $db = pg_connect('dbname=foo');
  // This is safe somewhat, since all values are escaped.
  // However PostgreSQL supports JSON/Array. These are not
  // safe by neither escape nor prepared query.
  $res = pg_delete($db, 'post_log', $_POST, PG_DML_ESCAPE);
  if ($res) {
      echo "POST data is deleted: $res\n";
  } else {
      echo "User must have sent wrong inputs\n";
  }
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sync with PostgreSQL backend

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_end_copy syncs the PostgreSQL frontend (usually a web server process) with the PostgreSQL server after doing a copy operation performed by pg_put_line. pg_end_copy must be issued, otherwise the PostgreSQL server may get out of sync with the frontend and will report an error.

listitem.para: An PgSql\Connection instance. When connection is null, the default connection is used. The default connection is the last connection made by pg_connect or pg_pconnect. As of PHP 8.1.0, using the default connection is deprecated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_end_copy example
example.programlisting:
<?php 
  $conn = pg_pconnect("dbname=foo");
  pg_query($conn, "create table bar (a int4, b char(16), d float8)");
  pg_query($conn, "copy bar from stdin");
  pg_put_line($conn, "3\thello world\t4.5\n");
  pg_put_line($conn, "4\tgoodbye world\t7.11\n");
  pg_put_line($conn, "\\.\n");
  pg_end_copy($conn);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Escape a string for insertion into a bytea field

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_escape_bytea escapes string for bytea datatype. It returns escaped string.

note.para: When you SELECT a bytea type, PostgreSQL returns octal byte values prefixed with '\' (e.g. \032). Users are supposed to convert back to binary format manually.

This function requires PostgreSQL 7.2 or later. With PostgreSQL 7.2.0 and 7.2.1, bytea values must be cast when you enable multi-byte support. i.e. INSERT INTO test_table (image) VALUES ('$image_escaped'::bytea); PostgreSQL 7.2.2 or later does not need a cast. The exception is when the client and backend character encoding does not match, and there may be multi-byte stream error. User must then cast to bytea to avoid this error.

listitem.para: An PgSql\Connection instance. When connection is unspecified, the default connection is used. The default connection is the last connection made by pg_connect or pg_pconnect. As of PHP 8.1.0, using the default connection is deprecated.
A string containing text or binary data to be inserted into a bytea column.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A string containing the escaped data.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_escape_bytea example
example.programlisting:
<?php 
  // Connect to the database
  $dbconn = pg_connect('dbname=foo');
  
  // Read in a binary file
  $data = file_get_contents('image1.jpg');
  
  // Escape the binary data
  $escaped = pg_escape_bytea($data);
  
  // Insert it into the database
  pg_query("INSERT INTO gallery (name, data) VALUES ('Pine trees', '{$escaped}')");
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Escape an identifier for insertion into a text field

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_escape_identifier escapes an identifier (e.g. table, field names) for querying the database. It returns an escaped identifier string for PostgreSQL server. pg_escape_identifier adds double quotes before and after data. Users should not add double quotes. Use of this function is recommended for identifier parameters in query. For SQL literals (i.e. parameters except bytea), pg_escape_literal or pg_escape_string must be used. For bytea type fields, pg_escape_bytea must be used instead.

listitem.para: An PgSql\Connection instance. When connection is unspecified, the default connection is used. The default connection is the last connection made by pg_connect or pg_pconnect. As of PHP 8.1.0, using the default connection is deprecated.
A string containing text to be escaped.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A string containing the escaped data, or false on failure.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_escape_identifier example
example.programlisting:
<?php 
  // Connect to the database
  $dbconn = pg_connect('dbname=foo');
  
  // Escape the table name data
  $escaped = pg_escape_identifier($table_name);
  
  // Select rows from $table_name
  pg_query("SELECT * FROM {$escaped};");
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Escape a literal for insertion into a text field

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_escape_literal escapes a literal for querying the PostgreSQL database. It returns an escaped literal in the PostgreSQL format. pg_escape_literal adds quotes before and after data. Users should not add quotes. Use of this function is recommended instead of pg_escape_string. If the type of the column is bytea, pg_escape_bytea must be used instead. For escaping identifiers (e.g. table, field names), pg_escape_identifier must be used.

listitem.para: An PgSql\Connection instance. When connection is unspecified, the default connection is used. The default connection is the last connection made by pg_connect or pg_pconnect. As of PHP 8.1.0, using the default connection is deprecated.
A string containing text to be escaped.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A string containing the escaped data, or false on failure.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_escape_literal example
example.programlisting:
<?php 
  // Connect to the database
  $dbconn = pg_connect('dbname=foo');
  
  // Read in a text file (containing apostrophes and backslashes)
  $data = file_get_contents('letter.txt');
  
  // Escape the text data
  $escaped = pg_escape_literal($data);
  
  // Insert it into the database. Note that no quotes around {$escaped}
  pg_query("INSERT INTO correspondence (name, data) VALUES ('My letter', {$escaped})");
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Escape a string for query

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_escape_string escapes a string for querying the database. It returns an escaped string in the PostgreSQL format without quotes. pg_escape_literal is more preferred way to escape SQL parameters for PostgreSQL. addslashes must not be used with PostgreSQL. If the type of the column is bytea, pg_escape_bytea must be used instead. pg_escape_identifier must be used to escape identifiers (e.g. table names, field names)

listitem.para: An PgSql\Connection instance. When connection is unspecified, the default connection is used. The default connection is the last connection made by pg_connect or pg_pconnect. As of PHP 8.1.0, using the default connection is deprecated.
A string containing text to be escaped.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A string containing the escaped data.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_escape_string example
example.programlisting:
<?php 
  // Connect to the database
  $dbconn = pg_connect('dbname=foo');
  
  // Read in a text file (containing apostrophes and backslashes)
  $data = file_get_contents('letter.txt');
  
  // Escape the text data
  $escaped = pg_escape_string($data);
  
  // Insert it into the database
  pg_query("INSERT INTO correspondence (name, data) VALUES ('My letter', '{$escaped}')");
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sends a request to execute a prepared statement with given parameters, and waits for the result

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sends a request to execute a prepared statement with given parameters, and waits for the result.

pg_execute is like pg_query_params, but the command to be executed is specified by naming a previously-prepared statement, instead of giving a query string. This feature allows commands that will be used repeatedly to be parsed and planned just once, rather than each time they are executed. The statement must have been prepared previously in the current session.
The parameters are identical to pg_query_params, except that the name of a prepared statement is given instead of a query string.

listitem.para: An PgSql\Connection instance. When connection is unspecified, the default connection is used. The default connection is the last connection made by pg_connect or pg_pconnect. As of PHP 8.1.0, using the default connection is deprecated.

The name of the prepared statement to execute. if "" is specified, then the unnamed statement is executed. The name must have been previously prepared using pg_prepare, pg_send_prepare or a PREPARE SQL command.
An array of parameter values to substitute for the $1, $2, etc. placeholders in the original prepared query string. The number of elements in the array must match the number of placeholders.

warning.para: Elements are converted to strings by calling this function.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An PgSql\Result instance on success, or false on failure.

row.entry: Returns an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was returned.
The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: Using pg_execute
example.programlisting:
<?php
// Connect to a database named "mary"
$dbconn = pg_connect("dbname=mary");

// Prepare a query for execution
$result = pg_prepare($dbconn, "my_query", 'SELECT * FROM shops WHERE name = $1');

// Execute the prepared query.  Note that it is not necessary to escape
// the string "Joe's Widgets" in any way
$result = pg_execute($dbconn, "my_query", array("Joe's Widgets"));

// Execute the same prepared query, this time with a different parameter
$result = pg_execute($dbconn, "my_query", array("Clothes Clothes Clothes"));

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Fetches all rows from a result as an array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_fetch_all returns an array that contains all rows (records) in the PgSql\Result instance.

note.simpara: This function sets NULL fields to the PHP null value.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

An optional parameter that controls how the returned array is indexed. mode is a constant and can take the following values: PGSQL_ASSOC, PGSQL_NUM and PGSQL_BOTH. Using PGSQL_NUM, the function will return an array with numerical indices, using PGSQL_ASSOC it will return only associative indices while PGSQL_BOTH will return both numerical and associative indices.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array with all rows in the result. Each row is an array of field values indexed by field name.

row.entry: The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.
pg_fetch_all will now return an empty array instead of false for result sets with zero rows.

example.title: PostgreSQL fetch all
example.programlisting:
<?php 
$conn = pg_pconnect("dbname=publisher");
if (!$conn) {
    echo "An error occurred.\n";
    exit;
}

$result = pg_query($conn, "SELECT * FROM authors");
if (!$result) {
    echo "An error occurred.\n";
    exit;
}

$arr = pg_fetch_all($result);

print_r($arr);

?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Fetches all rows in a particular result column as an array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_fetch_all_columns returns an array that contains all rows (records) in a particular column of the PgSql\Result instance.

note.simpara: This function sets NULL fields to the PHP null value.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

listitem.para: Column number. Defaults to the first column if not specified.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array with all values in the result column.

row.entry: The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_fetch_all_columns example
example.programlisting:
<?php 
$conn = pg_pconnect("dbname=publisher");
if (!$conn) {
  echo "An error occurred.\n";
  exit;
}

$result = pg_query($conn, "SELECT title, name, address FROM authors");
if (!$result) {
  echo "An error occurred.\n";
  exit;
}

// Get an array of all author names
$arr = pg_fetch_all_columns($result, 1);

var_dump($arr);

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Fetch a row as an array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_fetch_array returns an array that corresponds to the fetched row (record).

pg_fetch_array is an extended version of pg_fetch_row. In addition to storing the data in the numeric indices (field number) to the result array, it can also store the data using associative indices (field name). It stores both indices by default.

note.simpara: This function sets NULL fields to the PHP null value.

refsect1.para: pg_fetch_array is NOT significantly slower than using pg_fetch_row, and is significantly easier to use.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

listitem.para: Row number in result to fetch. Rows are numbered from 0 upwards. If omitted or null, the next row is fetched.

listitem.simpara: An optional parameter that controls how the returned array is indexed. mode is a constant and can take the following values: PGSQL_ASSOC, PGSQL_NUM and PGSQL_BOTH. Using PGSQL_NUM, the function will return an array with numerical indices, using PGSQL_ASSOC it will return only associative indices while PGSQL_BOTH will return both numerical and associative indices.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array indexed numerically (beginning with 0) or associatively (indexed by field name), or both. Each value in the array is represented as a string. Database NULL values are returned as null.
false is returned if row exceeds the number of rows in the set, there are no more rows, or on any other error. Fetching from the result of a query other than SELECT will also return false.

row.entry: The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_fetch_array example
example.programlisting:
<?php 

$conn = pg_pconnect("dbname=publisher");
if (!$conn) {
  echo "An error occurred.\n";
  exit;
}

$result = pg_query($conn, "SELECT author, email FROM authors");
if (!$result) {
  echo "An error occurred.\n";
  exit;
}

$arr = pg_fetch_array($result, 0, PGSQL_NUM);
echo $arr[0] . " <- Row 1 Author\n";
echo $arr[1] . " <- Row 1 E-mail\n";

// The row parameter is optional; NULL can be passed instead,
// to pass a result_type.  Successive calls to pg_fetch_array
// will return the next row.
$arr = pg_fetch_array($result, NULL, PGSQL_ASSOC);
echo $arr["author"] . " <- Row 2 Author\n";
echo $arr["email"] . " <- Row 2 E-mail\n";

$arr = pg_fetch_array($result);
echo $arr["author"] . " <- Row 3 Author\n";
echo $arr[1] . " <- Row 3 E-mail\n";

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Fetch a row as an associative array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_fetch_assoc returns an associative array that corresponds to the fetched row (records).
pg_fetch_assoc is equivalent to calling pg_fetch_array with PGSQL_ASSOC as the optional third parameter. It only returns an associative array. If you need the numeric indices, use pg_fetch_row.

note.simpara: This function sets NULL fields to the PHP null value.

refsect1.para: pg_fetch_assoc is NOT significantly slower than using pg_fetch_row, and is significantly easier to use.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

listitem.para: Row number in result to fetch. Rows are numbered from 0 upwards. If omitted or null, the next row is fetched.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array indexed associatively (by field name). Each value in the array is represented as a string. Database NULL values are returned as null.
false is returned if row exceeds the number of rows in the set, there are no more rows, or on any other error.

row.entry: The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_fetch_assoc example
example.programlisting:
<?php 
$conn = pg_connect("dbname=publisher");
if (!$conn) {
  echo "An error occurred.\n";
  exit;
}

$result = pg_query($conn, "SELECT id, author, email FROM authors");
if (!$result) {
  echo "An error occurred.\n";
  exit;
}

while ($row = pg_fetch_assoc($result)) {
  echo $row['id'];
  echo $row['author'];
  echo $row['email'];
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Fetch a row as an object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_fetch_object returns an object with properties that correspond to the fetched row's field names. It can optionally instantiate an object of a specific class, and pass parameters to that class's constructor.

note.simpara: This function sets NULL fields to the PHP null value.

refsect1.para: Speed-wise, the function is identical to pg_fetch_array, and almost as fast as pg_fetch_row (the difference is insignificant).

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

listitem.para: Row number in result to fetch. Rows are numbered from 0 upwards. If omitted or null, the next row is fetched.
The name of the class to instantiate, set the properties of and return. If not specified, a stdClass object is returned.
An optional array of parameters to pass to the constructor for class objects.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An object with one attribute for each field name in the result. Database NULL values are returned as null.
false is returned if row exceeds the number of rows in the set, there are no more rows, or on any other error.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: A ValueError is thrown when the constructor_args is non-empty with the class not having a constructor.

row.entry: The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns values from a result instance

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_fetch_result returns the value of a particular row and field (column) in an PgSql\Result instance.

note.para: This function used to be called pg_result.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

listitem.para: Row number in result to fetch. Rows are numbered from 0 upwards. If omitted, next row is fetched.
A string representing the name of the field (column) to fetch, otherwise an int representing the field number to fetch. Fields are numbered from 0 upwards.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Boolean is returned as "t" or "f". All other types, including arrays are returned as strings formatted in the same default PostgreSQL manner that you would see in the psql program. Database NULL values are returned as null.
false is returned if row exceeds the number of rows in the set, or on any other error.

row.entry: The two argument signature of pg_fetch_result (result, field) is now deprecated. Use the three argument signature with row set to null instead.
The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_fetch_result example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$db = pg_connect("dbname=users user=me");

$res = pg_query($db, "SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2");

$val = pg_fetch_result($res, 1, 0);

echo "First field in the second row is: ", $val, "\n";
?>
example.screen: First field in the second row is: 2

refnamediv.refpurpose: Test if a field is SQL NULL

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_field_is_null tests if a field in an PgSql\Result instance is SQL NULL or not.

note.para: This function used to be called pg_fieldisnull.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

listitem.para: Row number in result to fetch. Rows are numbered from 0 upwards. If omitted, current row is fetched.
Field number (starting from 0) as an int or the field name as a string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns 1 if the field in the given row is SQL NULL, 0 if not. false is returned if the row is out of range, or upon any other error.

row.entry: The two argument signature of pg_field_is_null (result, field) is now deprecated. Use the three argument signature with row set to null instead.
The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_field_is_null example
example.programlisting:
<?php
  $dbconn = pg_connect("dbname=publisher") or die ("Could not connect");
  $res = pg_query($dbconn, "select * from authors where author = 'Orwell'");
  if ($res) {
      if (pg_field_is_null($res, 0, "year") == 1) {
          echo "The value of the field year is null.\n";
      }
      if (pg_field_is_null($res, 0, "year") == 0) {
          echo "The value of the field year is not null.\n";
    }
 }
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the name of a field

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_field_name returns the name of the field occupying the given field in the given result instance. Field numbering starts from 0.

note.para: This function used to be called pg_fieldname.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

listitem.para: Field number, starting from 0.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The field name.

row.entry: The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: Getting information about fields
example.programlisting:
<?php
  $dbconn = pg_connect("dbname=publisher") or die("Could not connect");

  $res = pg_query($dbconn, "select * from authors where author = 'Orwell'");
  $i = pg_num_fields($res);
  for ($j = 0; $j < $i; $j++) {
      echo "column $j\n";
      $fieldname = pg_field_name($res, $j);
      echo "fieldname: $fieldname\n";
      echo "printed length: " . pg_field_prtlen($res, $fieldname) . " characters\n";
      echo "storage length: " . pg_field_size($res, $j) . " bytes\n";
      echo "field type: " . pg_field_type($res, $j) . " \n\n";
  }
?>

column 1 fieldname: year printed length: 4 characters storage length: 2 bytes field type: int2
column 2 fieldname: title printed length: 24 characters storage length: -1 bytes field type: varchar

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the field number of the named field

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_field_num will return the number of the field number that corresponds to the field in the given result instance.

note.para: This function used to be called pg_fieldnum.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

listitem.para: The name of the field. The given name is treated like an identifier in an SQL command, that is, it is downcased unless double-quoted.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The field number (numbered from 0), or -1 on error.

row.entry: The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: Getting information about fields
example.programlisting:
<?php
  $dbconn = pg_connect("dbname=publisher") or die("Could not connect");

  $res = pg_query($dbconn, "select author, year, title from authors where author = 'Orwell'");
  
  echo "Column 'title' is field number: ", pg_field_num($res, 'title');
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the printed length

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_field_prtlen returns the actual printed length (number of characters) of a specific value in a PostgreSQL result. Row numbering starts at 0. This function will return false on an error.
field_name_or_number can be passed either as an int or as a string. If it is passed as an int, PHP recognises it as the field number, otherwise as field name.
See the example given at the pg_field_name page.

note.para: This function used to be called pg_fieldprtlen.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

listitem.para: Row number in result. Rows are numbered from 0 upwards. If omitted, current row is fetched.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The field printed length.

row.entry: The two argument signature of pg_field_prtlen (result, field_name_or_number) is now deprecated. Use the three argument signature with row set to null instead.
The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: Getting information about fields

      echo "storage length: " . pg_field_size($res, $j) . " bytes\n";
      echo "field type: " . pg_field_type($res, $j) . " \n\n";
  }
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the name or oid of the tables field

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_field_table returns the name of the table that field belongs to, or the table's oid if oid_only is true.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

listitem.para: Field number, starting from 0.
By default the tables name that field belongs to is returned but if oid_only is set to true, then the oid will instead be returned.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: On success either the fields table name or oid, or false on failure.

row.entry: The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: Getting table information about a field
example.programlisting:
<?php
$dbconn = pg_connect("dbname=publisher") or die("Could not connect");

$res = pg_query($dbconn, "SELECT bar FROM foo");

echo pg_field_table($res, 0);
echo pg_field_table($res, 0, true);

$res = pg_query($dbconn, "SELECT version()");
var_dump(pg_field_table($res, 0));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

note.para: Returning the oid is much faster than returning the table name because fetching the table name requires a query to the database system table.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the type name for the corresponding field number

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_field_type returns a string containing the base type name of the given field in the given result instance.

note.para: If the field uses a PostgreSQL domain (rather than a basic type), it is the name of the domain's underlying type that is returned, rather than the name of the domain itself.
This function used to be called pg_fieldtype.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

listitem.para: Field number, starting from 0.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A string containing the base name of the field's type.

row.entry: The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: Getting information about fields
example.programlisting:
<?php
  $dbconn = pg_connect("dbname=publisher") or die("Could not connect");

  // Assume 'title' is a varchar type
  $res = pg_query($dbconn, "select title from authors where author = 'Orwell'");

  echo "Title field type: ", pg_field_type($res, 0);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the type ID (OID) for the corresponding field number

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_field_type_oid returns an integer containing the OID of the base type of the given field in the given result instance.

You can get more information about the field type by querying PostgreSQL's pg_type system table using the OID obtained with this function. The PostgreSQL format_type function will convert a type OID into an SQL standard type name.

note.para: If the field uses a PostgreSQL domain (rather than a basic type), it is the OID of the domain's underlying type that is returned, rather than the OID of the domain itself.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

listitem.para: Field number, starting from 0.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The OID of the field's base type.

row.entry: The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: Getting information about fields
example.programlisting:
<?php
  $dbconn = pg_connect("dbname=publisher") or die("Could not connect");

  // Assume 'title' is a varchar type
  $res = pg_query($dbconn, "select title from authors where author = 'Orwell'");

  echo "Title field type OID: ", pg_field_type_oid($res, 0);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Flush outbound query data on the connection

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_flush flushes any outbound query data waiting to be sent on the connection.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the flush was successful or no data was waiting to be flushed, 0 if part of the pending data was flushed but more remains or false on failure.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Free result memory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_free_result frees the memory and data associated with the specified PgSql\Result instance.
This function need only be called if memory consumption during script execution is a problem. Otherwise, all result memory will be automatically freed when the script ends.

note.para: This function used to be called pg_freeresult.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Result instance, returned by pg_query, pg_query_params or pg_execute(among others).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: The result parameter expects an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_free_result example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$db = pg_connect("dbname=users user=me");

$res = pg_query($db, "SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2");

$val = pg_fetch_result($res, 1, 0);

echo "First field in the second row is: ", $val, "\n";

pg_free_result($res);
?>
example.screen: First field in the second row is: 2

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets SQL NOTIFY message

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_get_notify gets notifications generated by a NOTIFY SQL command. To receive notifications, the LISTEN SQL command must be issued.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

An optional parameter that controls how the returned array is indexed. mode is a constant and can take the following values: PGSQL_ASSOC, PGSQL_NUM and PGSQL_BOTH. Using PGSQL_NUM, the function will return an array with numerical indices, using PGSQL_ASSOC it will return only associative indices while PGSQL_BOTH will return both numerical and associative indices.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array containing the NOTIFY message name and backend PID. If supported by the server, the array also contains the server version and the payload. Otherwise if no NOTIFY is waiting, then false is returned.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: PostgreSQL NOTIFY message
example.programlisting:
<?php 
$conn = pg_pconnect("dbname=publisher");
if (!$conn) {
  echo "An error occurred.\n";
  exit;
}

// Listen 'author_updated' message from other processes
pg_query($conn, 'LISTEN author_updated;');
$notify = pg_get_notify($conn);
if (!$notify) {
  echo "No messages\n";
} else {
  print_r($notify);
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets the backend's process ID

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_get_pid gets the backend's (database server process) PID. The PID is useful to determine whether or not a NOTIFY message received via pg_get_notify is sent from another process or not.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The backend database process ID.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: PostgreSQL backend PID
example.programlisting:
<?php 
$conn = pg_pconnect("dbname=publisher");
if (!$conn) {
  echo "An error occurred.\n";
  exit;
}

// Backend process PID. Use PID with pg_get_notify()
$pid = pg_get_pid($conn);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get asynchronous query result

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pg_get_result gets an PgSql\Result instance from an asynchronous query executed by pg_send_query, pg_send_query_params or pg_send_execute.
pg_send_query and the other asynchronous query functions can send multiple queries to a PostgreSQL server and pg_get_result is used to get each query's results, one by one.

listitem.simpara: An PgSql\Connection instance.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An PgSql\Result instance, or false if no more results are available.

row.entry: Returns an PgSql\Result instance now; previously, a resource was returned.
The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.

example.title: pg_get_result example
example.programlisting:
<?php
  $dbconn = pg_connect("dbname=publisher") or die("Could not connect");

  if (!pg_connection_busy($dbconn)) {
      pg_send_query($dbconn, "select * from authors; select count(*) from authors;");
  }
  
  $res1 = pg_get_result($dbconn);
  echo "First call to pg_get_result(): $res1\n";
  $rows1 = pg_num_rows($res1);
  echo "$res1 has $rows1 records\n\n";
  
  $res2 = pg_get_result($dbconn);
  echo "Second call to pg_get_result(): $res2\n";
  $rows2 = pg_num_rows($res2);
  echo "$res2 has $rows2 records\n";
?>
example.screen:
First call to pg_get_result(): Resource id #3 Resource id #3 has 3 records
Second call to pg_get_result(): Resource id #4 Resource id #4 has 1 records

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the host name associated with the connection

refsect1.para: pg_host returns the host name of the given PostgreSQL connection instance is connected to.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A string containing the name of the host the connection is to, or an empty string on error.

row.entry: The connection parameter expects an PgSql\Connection instance now; previously, a resource was expected.
