Open for reading and writing; place the file pointer at the end of the file. If the file does not exist, attempt to create it. In this mode, fseek only affects the reading position, writes are always appended.
'x'
Create and open for writing only; place the file pointer at the beginning of the file. If the file already exists, the fopen call will fail by returning false and generating an error of level E_WARNING. If the file does not exist, attempt to create it. This is equivalent to specifying O_EXCL|O_CREAT flags for the underlying open(2) system call.
'x+'
Create and open for reading and writing; otherwise it has the same behavior as 'x'.
'c'
Open the file for writing only. If the file does not exist, it is created. If it exists, it is neither truncated (as opposed to 'w'), nor the call to this function fails (as is the case with 'x'). The file pointer is positioned on the beginning of the file. This may be useful if it's desired to get an advisory lock (see flock) before attempting to modify the file, as using 'w' could truncate the file before the lock was obtained (if truncation is desired, ftruncate can be used after the lock is requested).
'c+'
Open the file for reading and writing; otherwise it has the same behavior as 'c'.
'e'
Set close-on-exec flag on the opened file descriptor. Only available in PHP compiled on POSIX.1-2008 conformant systems.
'n'
Set non-blocking flag on the opened file descriptor. Only available in PHP compiled on POSIX.1-2008 conformant systems.

note.para: Different operating system families have different line-ending conventions. When you write a text file and want to insert a line break, you need to use the correct line-ending character(s) for your operating system. Unix based systems use \n as the line ending character, Windows based systems use \r\n as the line ending characters and Macintosh based systems (Mac OS Classic) used \r as the line ending character.
If you use the wrong line ending characters when writing your files, you might find that other applications that open those files will "look funny".

Windows offers a text-mode translation flag ('t') which will transparently translate \n to \r\n when working with the file. In contrast, you can also use 'b' to force binary mode, which will not translate your data. To use these flags, specify either 'b' or 't' as the last character of the mode parameter.

The default translation mode is 'b'. You can use the 't' mode if you are working with plain-text files and you use \n to delimit your line endings in your script, but expect your files to be readable with applications such as old versions of notepad. You should use the 'b' in all other cases.
If you specify the 't' flag when working with binary files, you may experience strange problems with your data, including broken image files and strange problems with \r\n characters.
For portability, it is also strongly recommended that you re-write code that uses or relies upon the 't' mode so that it uses the correct line endings and 'b' mode instead.

note.simpara: The mode is ignored for php://output, php://input, php://stdin, php://stdout, php://stderr and php://fd stream wrappers.

listitem.para: The optional third use_include_path parameter can be set to true if you want to search for the file in the include_path, too.

listitem.simpara: A context stream resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a file pointer resource on success, or false on failure

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Upon failure, an E_WARNING is emitted.

example.title: fopen examples
example.programlisting:
<?php
$handle = fopen("/home/rasmus/file.txt", "r");
$handle = fopen("/home/rasmus/file.gif", "wb");
$handle = fopen("http://www.example.com/", "r");
$handle = fopen("ftp://user:password@example.com/somefile.txt", "w");
?>

warning.simpara: When using SSL, Microsoft IIS will violate the protocol by closing the connection without sending a close_notify indicator. PHP will report this as "SSL: Fatal Protocol Error" when you reach the end of the data. To work around this, the value of error_reporting should be lowered to a level that does not include warnings. PHP can detect buggy IIS server software when you open the stream using the https:// wrapper and will suppress the warning. When using fsockopen to create an ssl:// socket, the developer is responsible for detecting and suppressing this warning.

note.para: If you are experiencing problems with reading and writing to files and you're using the server module version of PHP, remember to make sure that the files and directories you're using are accessible to the server process.
This function may also succeed when filename is a directory. If you are unsure whether filename is a file or a directory, you may need to use the is_dir function before calling fopen.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Output all remaining data on a file pointer

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Reads to EOF on the given file pointer from the current position and writes the results to the output buffer.
You may need to call rewind to reset the file pointer to the beginning of the file if you have already written data to the file.
If you just want to dump the contents of a file to the output buffer, without first modifying it or seeking to a particular offset, you may want to use the readfile, which saves you the fopen call.

listitem.simpara: The file pointer must be valid, and must point to a file successfully opened by fopen or fsockopen (and not yet closed by fclose).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the number of characters read from stream and passed through to the output.

example.title: Using fpassthru with binary files
example.programlisting:
<?php

// open the file in a binary mode
$name = './img/ok.png';
$fp = fopen($name, 'rb');

// send the right headers
header("Content-Type: image/png");
header("Content-Length: " . filesize($name));

// dump the picture and stop the script
fpassthru($fp);
exit;

?>

note.para: When using fpassthru on a binary file on Windows systems, you should make sure to open the file in binary mode by appending a b to the mode used in the call to fopen.
You are encouraged to use the b flag when dealing with binary files, even if your system does not require it, so that your scripts will be more portable.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Format line as CSV and write to file pointer

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: fputcsv formats a line (passed as a fields array) as CSV and writes it (terminated by a eol) to the specified stream.

listitem.simpara: The file pointer must be valid, and must point to a file successfully opened by fopen or fsockopen (and not yet closed by fclose).

listitem.para: An array of strings.
The separator parameter sets the field separator. It must be a single byte character.
The enclosure parameter sets the field enclosure character. It must be a single byte character.
The escape parameter sets the escape character. It must be a single byte character or the empty string. The empty string ("") disables the proprietary escape mechanism.

warning.simpara: In the input stream, the enclosure character can always be escaped by doubling it inside a quoted string, resulting in a single enclosure character in the parsed result. The escape character works differently: If a sequence of escape and enclosure characters appear in the input, both characters will be present in the parsed result. So for the default parameters, a CSV line like "a""b","c\"d" will have the fields parsed as a"b and c\"d, respectively.
As of PHP 8.4.0, depending on the default value of escape is deprecated. It needs to be provided explicitly either positionally or by the use of named arguments.

listitem.para: The optional eol parameter sets a custom End of Line sequence.

warning.simpara: When escape is set to anything other than an empty string ("") it can result in CSV that is not compliant with RFC 4180 or unable to survive a roundtrip through the PHP CSV functions. The default for escape is "\\" so it is recommended to set it to the empty string explicitly. The default value will change in a future version of PHP, no earlier than PHP 9.0.

note.para: If an enclosure character is contained in a field, it will be escaped by doubling it, unless it is immediately preceded by an escape.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the length of the written string or false on failure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Throws a ValueError if separator or enclosure is not one byte long.
Throws a ValueError if escape is not one byte long or the empty string.

row.entry: Relying on the default value of escape is now deprecated.
The optional eol parameter has been added.
The escape parameter now also accepts an empty string to disable the proprietary escape mechanism.

example.title: fputcsv example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$list = [
    ['aaa', 'bbb', 'ccc', 'dddd'],
    ['123', '456', '789'],
    ['"aaa"', '"bbb"']
];

$fp = fopen('file.csv', 'w');

foreach ($list as $fields) {
    fputcsv($fp, $fields, ',', '"', '');
}

fclose($fp);
?>
example.para: The above example will write the following to file.csv:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of fwrite

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: fwrite.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Binary-safe file read

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para:
fread reads up to length bytes from the file pointer referenced by stream. Reading stops as soon as one of the following conditions is met:
length bytes have been read
EOF (end of file) is reached
a packet becomes available or the socket timeout occurs (for network streams)
if the stream is read buffered and it does not represent a plain file, at most one read of up to a number of bytes equal to the chunk size (usually 8192) is made; depending on the previously buffered data, the size of the returned data may be larger than the chunk size.

listitem.simpara: A file system pointer resource that is typically created using fopen.

listitem.para: Up to length number of bytes read.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the read string or false on failure.

example.title: A simple fread example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// get contents of a file into a string
$filename = "/usr/local/something.txt";
$handle = fopen($filename, "r");
$contents = fread($handle, filesize($filename));
fclose($handle);
?>

example.title: Binary fread example

warning.para: On systems which differentiate between binary and text files (i.e. Windows) the file must be opened with 'b' included in fopen mode parameter.

example.programlisting:
<?php
$filename = "c:\\files\\somepic.gif";
$handle = fopen($filename, "rb");
$contents = fread($handle, filesize($filename));
fclose($handle);
?>

example.title: Remote fread examples

warning.para: When reading from anything that is not a regular local file, such as streams returned when reading remote files or from popen and fsockopen, reading will stop after a packet is available. This means that you should collect the data together in chunks as shown in the examples below.

example.programlisting:
<?php
$handle = fopen("http://www.example.com/", "rb");
$contents = stream_get_contents($handle);
fclose($handle);
?>

<?php
$handle = fopen("http://www.example.com/", "rb");
if (FALSE === $handle) {
    exit("Failed to open stream to URL");
}

$contents = '';

while (!feof($handle)) {
    $contents .= fread($handle, 8192);
}
fclose($handle);
?>

note.para: If you just want to get the contents of a file into a string, use file_get_contents as it has much better performance than the code above.
Note that fread reads from the current position of the file pointer. Use ftell to find the current position of the pointer and rewind to rewind the pointer position.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Parses input from a file according to a format

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The function fscanf is similar to sscanf, but it takes its input from a file associated with stream and interprets the input according to the specified format.
Any whitespace in the format string matches any whitespace in the input stream. This means that even a tab (\t) in the format string can match a single space character in the input stream.
Each call to fscanf reads one line from the file.

listitem.simpara: A file system pointer resource that is typically created using fopen.

listitem.para:
The interpreted format for string, which is described in the documentation for sprintf with following differences:
Function is not locale-aware.
F, g, G and b are not supported.
D stands for decimal number.
i stands for integer with base detection.
n stands for number of characters processed so far.
s stops reading at any whitespace character.
* instead of argnum$ suppresses the assignment of this conversion specification.

listitem.simpara: The optional assigned values.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: If only two parameters were passed to this function, the values parsed will be returned as an array. Otherwise, if optional parameters are passed, the function will return the number of assigned values. The optional parameters must be passed by reference.
If there are more substrings expected in the format than there are available within string, null will be returned. On other errors, false will be returned.
When optional parameters are used and the end of the input read from stream is reached before any value has been parsed, -1 is returned.

example.title: fscanf Example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$handle = fopen("users.txt", "r");
while ($userinfo = fscanf($handle, "%s\t%s\t%s\n")) {
    list ($name, $profession, $countrycode) = $userinfo;
    //... do something with the values
}
fclose($handle);
?>

example.title: Contents of users.txt
example.programlisting: javier argonaut pe hiroshi sculptor jp robert slacker us luigi florist it

refnamediv.refpurpose: Seeks on a file pointer

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sets the file position indicator for the file referenced by stream. The new position, measured in bytes from the beginning of the file, is obtained by adding offset to the position specified by whence.

In general, it is allowed to seek past the end-of-file; if data is then written, reads in any unwritten region between the end-of-file and the sought position will yield bytes with value 0. However, certain streams may not support this behavior, especially when they have an underlying fixed size storage.

listitem.simpara: A file system pointer resource that is typically created using fopen.

listitem.para: The offset.
To move to a position before the end-of-file, a negative value in the offset must be passed and the whence parameter must be set to SEEK_END.

whence values are:
SEEK_SET - Set position equal to offset bytes from the start of the file. SEEK_CUR - Set position to current location plus offset bytes. SEEK_END - Set position to end-of-file plus offset bytes.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Upon success, returns 0; otherwise, returns -1.

warning.simpara: This function was created to imitate the C language function of the same name. Please pay attention to the return values as they differ from what one would expect in PHP.

example.title: fseek example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$fp = fopen('somefile.txt', 'r');

// read some data
$data = fgets($fp, 4096);

// move back to the beginning of the file
// same as rewind($fp);
fseek($fp, 0);

?>

note.para: If you have opened the file in append (a or a+) mode, any data you write to the file will always be appended, regardless of the file position, and the result of calling fseek will be undefined.
Not all streams support seeking. For those that do not support seeking, forward seeking from the current position is accomplished by reading and discarding data; other forms of seeking will fail.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets information about a file using an open file pointer

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gathers the statistics of the file opened by the file pointer stream. This function is similar to the stat function except that it operates on an open file pointer instead of a filename.

listitem.simpara: A file system pointer resource that is typically created using fopen.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns an array with the statistics of the file; the format of the array is described in detail on the stat manual page. Returns false on failure.

example.title: fstat example
example.programlisting:
<?php

// open a file
$fp = fopen("/etc/passwd", "r");

// gather statistics
$fstat = fstat($fp);

// close the file
fclose($fp);

// print only the associative part
print_r(array_slice($fstat, 13));

?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

note.simpara: This function will not work on remote files as the file to be examined must be accessible via the server's filesystem.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Synchronizes changes to the file (including meta-data)

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function synchronizes changes to the file, including its meta-data. This is similar to fflush, but it also instructs the operating system to write to the storage media.

listitem.simpara: The file pointer must be valid, and must point to a file successfully opened by fopen or fsockopen (and not yet closed by fclose).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: fsync example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$file = 'test.txt';

$stream = fopen($file, 'w');
fwrite($stream, 'test data');
fwrite($stream, "\r\n");
fwrite($stream, 'additional data');

fsync($stream);
fclose($stream);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the current position of the file read/write pointer

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the position of the file pointer referenced by stream.

listitem.para: The file pointer must be valid, and must point to a file successfully opened by fopen or popen. ftell gives undefined results for append-only streams (opened with "a" flag).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the position of the file pointer referenced by stream as an integer; i.e., its offset into the file stream.
If an error occurs, returns false.

note.simpara: Because PHP's integer type is signed and many platforms use 32bit integers, some filesystem functions may return unexpected results for files which are larger than 2GB.

example.title: ftell example
example.programlisting:
<?php

// opens a file and read some data
$fp = fopen("/etc/passwd", "r");
$data = fgets($fp, 12);

// where are we ?
echo ftell($fp); // 11

fclose($fp);

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Truncates a file to a given length

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Takes the filepointer, stream, and truncates the file to length, size.

listitem.para: The file pointer.

note.para: The stream must be open for writing.

listitem.para: The size to truncate to.

note.para: If size is larger than the file then the file is extended with null bytes.
If size is smaller than the file then the file is truncated to that size.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: File truncation example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$filename = 'lorem_ipsum.txt';

$handle = fopen($filename, 'r+');
ftruncate($handle, rand(1, filesize($filename)));
rewind($handle);
echo fread($handle, filesize($filename));
fclose($handle);
?>

note.para: The file pointer is not changed.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Binary-safe file write

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: fwrite writes the contents of data to the file stream pointed to by stream.

listitem.simpara: A file system pointer resource that is typically created using fopen.

listitem.para: The string that is to be written.
If length is an int, writing will stop after length bytes have been written or the end of data is reached, whichever comes first.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: fwrite returns the number of bytes written, or false on failure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: fwrite raises E_WARNING on failure.

example.title: A simple fwrite example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$filename = 'test.txt';
$somecontent = "Add this to the file\n";

// Let's make sure the file exists and is writable first.
if (is_writable($filename)) {

    // In our example we're opening $filename in append mode.
    // The file pointer is at the bottom of the file hence
    // that's where $somecontent will go when we fwrite() it.
    if (!$fp = fopen($filename, 'a')) {
         echo "Cannot open file ($filename)";
         exit;
    }

    // Write $somecontent to our opened file.
    if (fwrite($fp, $somecontent) === FALSE) {
        echo "Cannot write to file ($filename)";
        exit;
    }

    echo "Success, wrote ($somecontent) to file ($filename)";

    fclose($fp);

} else {
    echo "The file $filename is not writable";
}
?>

note.para: On systems which differentiate between binary and text files (i.e. Windows) the file must be opened with 'b' included in fopen mode parameter.

If stream was fopened in append mode, fwrites are atomic (unless the size of data exceeds the filesystem's block size, on some platforms, and as long as the file is on a local filesystem). That is, there is no need to flock a resource before calling fwrite; all of the data will be written without interruption.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Find pathnames matching a pattern

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The glob function searches for all the pathnames matching pattern according to the rules used by the libc glob() function, which is similar to the rules used by common shells.
refsect1.simpara: The behavior on Unix systems and macOS is determined by the system's implementation of glob(). On Windows, an implementation that conforms to the POSIX 1003.2 definition for glob() is used, and it includes an extension to handle the [!...] convention for negating a range.

listitem.para: The pattern. No tilde expansion or parameter substitution is done.

Special characters:
* - Matches zero or more characters.
? - Matches exactly one character (any character).
[...] - Matches one character from a group of characters. If the first character is !, matches any character not in the group.
{a,b,c} - Matches one string from a group of strings delimited by a comma when the GLOB_BRACE flag is used.
\ - Escapes the following character, except when the GLOB_NOESCAPE flag is used.
Any of the GLOB_* constants.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns an array containing the matched files/directories, an empty array if no file matched or false on error. Unless GLOB_NOSORT was used, the names will be sorted alphanumerically.

example.title: Convenient way how glob can replace opendir and friends.
example.programlisting:
<?php
foreach (glob("*.txt") as $filename) {
    echo "$filename size " . filesize($filename) . "\n";
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: funclist.txt size 44686 funcsummary.txt size 267625 quickref.txt size 137820

example.title: Example with a more complex pattern
example.programlisting:
<?php
foreach (glob("path/*/*.{txt,md}", \GLOB_BRACE) as $filename) {
    echo "$filename\n";
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

note.simpara: This function will not work on remote files as the file to be examined must be accessible via the server's filesystem.
This function isn't available on some systems (e.g. old Sun OS).

refnamediv.refpurpose: Tells whether the filename is a directory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Tells whether the given filename is a directory.

listitem.para: Path to the file. If filename is a relative filename, it will be checked relative to the current working directory. If filename is a symbolic or hard link then the link will be resolved and checked. If you have enabled open_basedir further restrictions may apply.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the filename exists and is a directory, false otherwise.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Upon failure, an E_WARNING is emitted.

example.title: is_dir example
example.programlisting:
<?php
var_dump(is_dir('a_file.txt'));
var_dump(is_dir('bogus_dir/abc'));

var_dump(is_dir('..')); //one dir up
?>

note.simpara: The results of this function are cached. See clearstatcache for more details.

tip.simpara: As of PHP 5.0.0, this function can also be used with some URL wrappers. Refer to to determine which wrappers support stat family of functionality.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Tells whether the filename is executable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Tells whether the filename is executable.

listitem.para: Path to the file.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the filename exists and is executable, or false on error. On POSIX systems, a file is executable if the executable bit of the file permissions is set. For Windows, see the note below.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Upon failure, an E_WARNING is emitted.

example.title: is_executable example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$file = '/home/vincent/somefile.sh';

if (is_executable($file)) {
    echo $file.' is executable';
} else {
    echo $file.' is not executable';
}

?>

note.simpara: The results of this function are cached. See clearstatcache for more details.

tip.simpara: As of PHP 5.0.0, this function can also be used with some URL wrappers. Refer to to determine which wrappers support stat family of functionality.

note.simpara: On Windows, a file is considered executable, if it is a properly executable file as reported by the Win API GetBinaryType(); for BC reasons, files with a .bat or .cmd extension are also considered executable. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, any non-empty file with a .exe or .com extension was considered executable. Note that PATHEXT is irrelevant for is_executable.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Tells whether the filename is a regular file

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Tells whether the given file is a regular file. If filename is a symbolic link, it will resolve the symlink and will give information about the referred file.

listitem.para: Path to the file.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the filename exists and is a regular file, false otherwise.

note.simpara: Because PHP's integer type is signed and many platforms use 32bit integers, some filesystem functions may return unexpected results for files which are larger than 2GB.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Upon failure, an E_WARNING is emitted.

example.title: is_file example
example.programlisting:
<?php
var_dump(is_file('a_file.txt')) . "\n";
var_dump(is_file('/usr/bin/')) . "\n";
?>

note.simpara: The results of this function are cached. See clearstatcache for more details.

tip.simpara: As of PHP 5.0.0, this function can also be used with some URL wrappers. Refer to to determine which wrappers support stat family of functionality.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Tells whether the filename is a symbolic link

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Tells whether the given file is a symbolic link.

listitem.para: Path to the file.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the filename exists and is a symbolic link, false otherwise.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Upon failure, an E_WARNING is emitted.

example.title: Create and confirm if a file is a symbolic link
example.programlisting:
<?php
$link = 'uploads';

if (is_link($link)) {
    echo readlink($link);
} else {
    symlink('uploads.php', $link);
}
?>

note.simpara: The results of this function are cached. See clearstatcache for more details.

tip.simpara: As of PHP 5.0.0, this function can also be used with some URL wrappers. Refer to to determine which wrappers support stat family of functionality.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Tells whether a file exists and is readable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Tells whether a file exists and is readable.

listitem.para: Path to the file.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the file or directory specified by filename exists and is readable, false otherwise.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Upon failure, an E_WARNING is emitted.

example.title: is_readable example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$filename = 'test.txt';
if (is_readable($filename)) {
    echo 'The file is readable';
} else {
    echo 'The file is not readable';
}
?>

refsect1.title: Notes
refsect1.para: Keep in mind that PHP may be accessing the file as the user id that the web server runs as (often 'nobody').

note.simpara: The results of this function are cached. See clearstatcache for more details.

tip.simpara: As of PHP 5.0.0, this function can also be used with some URL wrappers. Refer to to determine which wrappers support stat family of functionality.

note.para: The check is done using the real UID/GID instead of the effective one.

refsect1.para: This function may return true for directories. Use is_dir to distinguish file and directory.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Tells whether the file was uploaded via HTTP POST

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns true if the file named by filename was uploaded via HTTP POST. This is useful to help ensure that a malicious user hasn't tried to trick the script into working on files upon which it should not be working--for instance, /etc/passwd.
This sort of check is especially important if there is any chance that anything done with uploaded files could reveal their contents to the user, or even to other users on the same system.

For proper working, the function is_uploaded_file needs an argument like $_FILES['userfile']['tmp_name'], - the name of the uploaded file on the client's machine $_FILES['userfile']['name'] does not work.

listitem.para: The filename being checked.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: is_uploaded_file example
example.programlisting:
<?php

if (is_uploaded_file($_FILES['userfile']['tmp_name'])) {
   echo "File ". $_FILES['userfile']['name'] ." uploaded successfully.\n";
   echo "Displaying contents\n";
   readfile($_FILES['userfile']['tmp_name']);
} else {
   echo "Possible file upload attack: ";
   echo "filename '". $_FILES['userfile']['tmp_name'] . "'.";
}

?>

simplelist.member: See Handling file uploads for a simple usage example.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Tells whether the filename is writable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns true if the filename exists and is writable. The filename argument may be a directory name allowing you to check if a directory is writable.
Keep in mind that PHP may be accessing the file as the user id that the web server runs as (often 'nobody').

listitem.para: The filename being checked.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the filename exists and is writable.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Upon failure, an E_WARNING is emitted.

example.title: is_writable example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$filename = 'test.txt';
if (is_writable($filename)) {
    echo 'The file is writable';
} else {
    echo 'The file is not writable';
}
?>

note.simpara: The results of this function are cached. See clearstatcache for more details.

tip.simpara: As of PHP 5.0.0, this function can also be used with some URL wrappers. Refer to to determine which wrappers support stat family of functionality.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of is_writable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: is_writable.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Changes group ownership of symlink

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Attempts to change the group of the symlink filename to group.
Only the superuser may change the group of a symlink arbitrarily; other users may change the group of a symlink to any group of which that user is a member.

listitem.para: Path to the symlink.
The group specified by name or number.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Changing the group of a symbolic link
example.programlisting:
<?php
$target = 'output.php';
$link = 'output.html';
symlink($target, $link);

lchgrp($link, 8);
?>

note.simpara: This function will not work on remote files as the file to be examined must be accessible via the server's filesystem.
This function is not implemented on Windows platforms.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Changes user ownership of symlink

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Attempts to change the owner of the symlink filename to user user.
Only the superuser may change the owner of a symlink.

listitem.para: Path to the file.
User name or number.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Changing the owner of a symbolic link
example.programlisting:
<?php
$target = 'output.php';
$link = 'output.html';
symlink($target, $link);

lchown($link, 8);
?>

note.simpara: This function will not work on remote files as the file to be examined must be accessible via the server's filesystem.
This function is not implemented on Windows platforms.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Create a hard link

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: link creates a hard link.

listitem.para: Target of the link.
The link name.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: The function fails, and issues E_WARNING, if link already exists, or if target does not exist.

example.title: Creating a simple hard link
example.programlisting:
<?php $target = 'source.ext'; // This is the file that already exists $link = 'newfile.ext'; // This the filename that you want to link it to
link($target, $link); ?>

note.simpara: This function will not work on remote files as the file to be examined must be accessible via the server's filesystem.
For Windows only: This function requires PHP to run in an elevated mode or with the UAC disabled.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets information about a link

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets information about a link.
This function is used to verify if a link (pointed to by path) really exists (using the same method as the S_ISLNK macro defined in stat.h).

listitem.para: Path to the link.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: linkinfo returns the st_dev field of the Unix C stat structure returned by the lstat system call. Returns a non-negative integer on success, -1 in case the link was not found, or false if an open.base_dir violation occurs.

example.title: linkinfo example
example.programlisting:
<?php
echo linkinfo('/vmlinuz'); // 835
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gives information about a file or symbolic link

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gathers the statistics of the file or symbolic link named by filename.

listitem.para: Path to a file or a symbolic link.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: See the manual page for stat for information on the structure of the array that lstat returns. This function is identical to the stat function except that if the filename parameter is a symbolic link, the status of the symbolic link is returned, not the status of the file pointed to by the symbolic link.
On failure, false is returned.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Upon failure, an E_WARNING is emitted.

example.title: Comparison of stat and lstat
example.programlisting:
<?php
symlink('uploads.php', 'uploads');

// Contrast information for uploads.php and uploads
array_diff(stat('uploads'), lstat('uploads'));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.para: Information that differs between the two files.

note.simpara: The results of this function are cached. See clearstatcache for more details.

tip.simpara: As of PHP 5.0.0, this function can also be used with some URL wrappers. Refer to to determine which wrappers support stat family of functionality.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Makes directory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Attempts to create the directory specified by directory.

listitem.para: The directory path. A URL can be used as a filename with this function if the fopen wrappers have been enabled. See fopen for more details on how to specify the filename. See the for links to information about what abilities the various wrappers have, notes on their usage, and information on any predefined variables they may provide.
The permissions are 0777 by default, which means the widest possible access. For more information on permissions, read the details on the chmod page.

note.para: permissions is ignored on Windows.

listitem.para: Note that you probably want to specify the permissions as an octal number, which means it should have a leading zero. The permissions is also modified by the current umask, which you can change using umask.
If true, then any parent directories to the directory specified will also be created, with the same permissions.

listitem.simpara: A context stream resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

note.para: If the directory to be created already exists, that is considered an error and false will still be returned. Use is_dir or file_exists to check if the directory already exists before trying to create it.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: Emits an E_WARNING level error if the directory already exists.
Emits an E_WARNING level error if the relevant permissions prevent creating the directory.

example.title: mkdir example
example.programlisting:
<?php
mkdir("/path/to/my/dir", 0700);
?>

example.title: mkdir using the recursive parameter
example.programlisting:
<?php
// Desired directory structure
$structure = './depth1/depth2/depth3/';

// To create the nested structure, the $recursive parameter 
// to mkdir() must be specified.

if (!mkdir($structure, 0777, true)) {
    die('Failed to create directories...');
}

// ...
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Moves an uploaded file to a new location

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function checks to ensure that the file designated by from is a valid upload file (meaning that it was uploaded via PHP's HTTP POST upload mechanism). If the file is valid, it will be moved to the filename given by to.
This sort of check is especially important if there is any chance that anything done with uploaded files could reveal their contents to the user, or even to other users on the same system.

listitem.para: The filename of the uploaded file.
The destination of the moved file.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success.
If from is not a valid upload file, then no action will occur, and move_uploaded_file will return false.
If from is a valid upload file, but cannot be moved for some reason, no action will occur, and move_uploaded_file will return false. Additionally, a warning will be issued.

example.title: Uploading multiple files
example.programlisting:
<?php
$uploads_dir = '/uploads';
foreach ($_FILES["pictures"]["error"] as $key => $error) {
    if ($error == UPLOAD_ERR_OK) {
        $tmp_name = $_FILES["pictures"]["tmp_name"][$key];
        // basename() may prevent filesystem traversal attacks;
        // further validation/sanitation of the filename may be appropriate
        $name = basename($_FILES["pictures"]["name"][$key]);
        move_uploaded_file($tmp_name, "$uploads_dir/$name");
    }
}
?>

note.para: move_uploaded_file is open_basedir aware. However, restrictions are placed only on the to path as to allow the moving of uploaded files in which from may conflict with such restrictions. move_uploaded_file ensures the safety of this operation by allowing only those files uploaded through PHP to be moved.

warning.para: If the destination file already exists, it will be overwritten.

simplelist.member: See Handling file uploads for a simple usage example

refnamediv.refpurpose: Parse a configuration file

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: parse_ini_file loads in the ini file specified in filename, and returns the settings in it in an associative array.
The structure of the ini file is the same as the php.ini's.

warning.simpara: This function must not be used with untrusted inputs, unless scanner_mode is INI_SCANNER_RAW since the parsed output might contain the values of sensitive constants, such as constants holding a database password.

listitem.para: The filename of the ini file being parsed. If a relative path is used, it is evaluated relative to the current working directory, then the include_path.
By setting the process_sections parameter to true, you get a multidimensional array, with the section names and settings included. The default for process_sections is false
Can either be INI_SCANNER_NORMAL (default) or INI_SCANNER_RAW. If INI_SCANNER_RAW is supplied, then option values will not be parsed.
listitem.simpara: As of PHP 5.6.1 can also be specified as INI_SCANNER_TYPED. In this mode boolean, null and integer types are preserved when possible. String values "true", "on" and "yes" are converted to true. "false", "off", "no" and "none" are considered false. "null" is converted to null in typed mode. Also, all numeric strings are converted to integer type if it is possible.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The settings are returned as an associative array on success, and false on failure.

example.title: Contents of sample.ini
example.programlisting:
; This is a sample configuration file ; Comments start with ';', as in php.ini
[first_section] one = 1 five = 5 animal = BIRD
[second_section] path = "/usr/local/bin" URL = "http://www.example.com/~username"
[third_section] phpversion[] = "5.0" phpversion[] = "5.1" phpversion[] = "5.2" phpversion[] = "5.3"
urls[svn] = "http://svn.php.net" urls[git] = "http://git.php.net"

example.title: parse_ini_file example
example.para: Constants (but not "magic constants" like __FILE__) may also be parsed in the ini file so if you define a constant as an ini value before running parse_ini_file, it will be integrated into the results. Only ini values are evaluated, and the value must be just the constant. For example:
example.programlisting:
<?php

define('BIRD', 'Dodo bird');

// Parse without sections
$ini_array = parse_ini_file("sample.ini");
print_r($ini_array);

// Parse with sections
$ini_array = parse_ini_file("sample.ini", true);
print_r($ini_array);

?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

example.title: parse_ini_file parsing a php.ini file
example.programlisting:
<?php
// A simple function used for comparing the results below
function yesno($expression)
{
    return($expression ? 'Yes' : 'No');
}

// Get the path to php.ini using the php_ini_loaded_file() function
$ini_path = php_ini_loaded_file();

// Parse php.ini
$ini = parse_ini_file($ini_path);

// Print and compare the values, note that using get_cfg_var()
// will give the same results for parsed and loaded here
echo '(parsed) magic_quotes_gpc = ' . yesno($ini['magic_quotes_gpc']) . PHP_EOL;
echo '(loaded) magic_quotes_gpc = ' . yesno(get_cfg_var('magic_quotes_gpc')) . PHP_EOL;
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

example.title: Value Interpolation
example.para: In addition to evaluating constants, certain characters have special meaning in an ini value. Additionally, environment variables and previously defined configuration options (see get_cfg_var) may be read using ${} syntax.
example.programlisting:
; | is used for bitwise OR three = 2|3
; & is used for bitwise AND four = 6&5
; ^ is used for bitwise XOR five = 3^6
; ~ is used for bitwise negate negative_two = ~1
; () is used for grouping seven = (8|7)&(6|5)
; Interpolate the PATH environment variable path = ${PATH}
; Interpolate the configuration option 'memory_limit' configured_memory_limit = ${memory_limit}

example.title: Escaping Characters
example.para: Some characters have special meaning in double-quoted strings and must be escaped by the backslash prefix. First of all, these are the double quote " as the boundary marker, and the backslash \ itself (if followed by one of the special characters):
example.programlisting: quoted = "She said \"Exactly my point\"." ; Results in a string with quote marks in it. hint = "Use \\\" to escape double quote" ; Results in: Use \" to escape double quote
example.para: There is an exception made for Windows-like paths: it's possible to not escape trailing backslash if the quoted string is directly followed by a linebreak:
example.programlisting: save_path = "C:\Temp\"
example.para: If one does need to escape double quote followed by linebreak in a multiline value, it's possible to use value concatenation in the following way (there is one double-quoted string directly followed by another one):
example.programlisting: long_text = "Lorem \"ipsum\""" dolor" ; Results in: Lorem "ipsum"\n dolor
example.para: Another character with special meaning is $ (the dollar sign). It must be escaped if followed by the open curly brace:
example.programlisting: code = "\${test}"
example.para: Escaping characters is not supported in the INI_SCANNER_RAW mode (in this mode all characters are processed "as is").
Note that the ini parser doesn't support standard escape sequences (\n, \t, etc.). If necessary, post-process the result of parse_ini_file with stripcslashes function.

note.para: This function has nothing to do with the php.ini file. It is already processed by the time you run your script. This function can be used to read in your own application's configuration files.
If a value in the ini file contains any non-alphanumeric characters it needs to be enclosed in double-quotes (").

note.simpara: There are reserved words which must not be used as keys for ini files. These include: null, yes, no, true, false, on, off, none. Values null, off, no and false result in "", and values on, yes and true result in "1", unless INI_SCANNER_TYPED mode is used. Characters ?{}|&~!()^" must not be used anywhere in the key and have a special meaning in the value.

note.para: Entries without an equal sign are ignored. For example, "foo" is ignored whereas "bar =" is parsed and added with an empty value. For example, MySQL has a "no-auto-rehash" setting in my.cnf that does not take a value, so it is ignored.

ini files are generally treated as plain text by web servers and thus served to browsers if requested. That means for security you must either keep your ini files outside of your docroot or reconfigure your web server to not serve them. Failure to do either of those may introduce a security risk.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Parse a configuration string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: parse_ini_string returns the settings in string ini_string in an associative array.
The structure of the ini string is the same as the php.ini's.

warning.simpara: This function must not be used with untrusted inputs, unless scanner_mode is INI_SCANNER_RAW since the parsed output might contain the values of sensitive constants, such as constants holding a database password.

listitem.para: The contents of the ini file being parsed.
By setting the process_sections parameter to true, you get a multidimensional array, with the section names and settings included. The default for process_sections is false
Can either be INI_SCANNER_NORMAL (default) or INI_SCANNER_RAW. If INI_SCANNER_RAW is supplied, then option values will not be parsed.
listitem.simpara: As of PHP 5.6.1 can also be specified as INI_SCANNER_TYPED. In this mode boolean, null and integer types are preserved when possible. String values "true", "on" and "yes" are converted to true. "false", "off", "no" and "none" are considered false. "null" is converted to null in typed mode. Also, all numeric strings are converted to integer type if it is possible.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The settings are returned as an associative array on success, and false on failure.

note.simpara: There are reserved words which must not be used as keys for ini files. These include: null, yes, no, true, false, on, off, none. Values null, off, no and false result in "", and values on, yes and true result in "1", unless INI_SCANNER_TYPED mode is used. Characters ?{}|&~![()^" must not be used anywhere in the key and have a special meaning in the value.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns information about a file path

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pathinfo returns information about path: either an associative array or a string, depending on flags.

note.para: For information on retrieving the current path info, read the section on predefined reserved variables.
pathinfo operates naively on the input string, and is not aware of the actual filesystem, or path components such as "..".
On Windows systems only, the \ character will be interpreted as a directory separator. On other systems it will be treated like any other character.

caution.para: pathinfo is locale aware, so for it to parse a path containing multibyte characters correctly, the matching locale must be set using the setlocale function.

listitem.para: The path to be parsed.
If present, specifies a specific element to be returned; one of PATHINFO_DIRNAME, PATHINFO_BASENAME, PATHINFO_EXTENSION or PATHINFO_FILENAME.
If flags is not specified, returns all available elements.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: If the flags parameter is not passed, an associative array containing the following elements is returned: dirname, basename, extension (if any), and filename.

note.para: If the path has more than one extension, PATHINFO_EXTENSION returns only the last one and PATHINFO_FILENAME only strips the last one. (see first example below).
If the path does not have an extension, no extension element will be returned (see second example below).
If the basename of the path starts with a dot, the following characters are interpreted as extension, and the filename is empty (see third example below).

refsect1.para: If flags is present, returns a string containing the requested element.

example.title: pathinfo Example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$path_parts = pathinfo('/www/htdocs/inc/lib.inc.php');

echo $path_parts['dirname'], "\n";
echo $path_parts['basename'], "\n";
echo $path_parts['extension'], "\n";
echo $path_parts['filename'], "\n";
?>

example.title: pathinfo example showing difference between null and no extension
example.programlisting:
<?php
$path_parts = pathinfo('/path/emptyextension.');
var_dump($path_parts['extension']);

$path_parts = pathinfo('/path/noextension');
var_dump($path_parts['extension']);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen:
string(0) ""
Notice: Undefined index: extension in test.php on line 6 NULL

example.title: pathinfo example for a dot-file
example.programlisting:
<?php
print_r(pathinfo('/some/path/.test'));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

example.title: pathinfo example with array dereferencing
example.para: The flags parameter is not a bitmask. Only a single value may be provided. To select only a limited set of parsed values, use array destructuring like so:
example.programlisting:
<?php
['basename' => $basename, 'dirname' => $dirname] = pathinfo('/www/htdocs/inc/lib.inc.php');

var_dump($basename, $dirname);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Closes process file pointer

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Closes a file pointer to a pipe opened by popen.

listitem.para: The file pointer must be valid, and must have been returned by a successful call to popen.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the termination status of the process that was run. In case of an error then -1 is returned.

note.simpara: If PHP has been compiled with --enable-sigchild, the return value of this function is undefined.

example.title: pclose example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$handle = popen('/bin/ls', 'r');
pclose($handle);
?>

note.title: Unix Only:
note.para: pclose is internally implemented using the waitpid(3) system call. To obtain the real exit status code the pcntl_wexitstatus function should be used.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Opens process file pointer

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Opens a pipe to a process executed by forking the command given by command.

listitem.para: The command
The mode. Either 'r' for reading, or 'w' for writing.

On Windows, popen defaults to text mode, i.e. any \n characters written to or read from the pipe will be translated to \r\n. If this is not desired, binary mode can be enforced by setting mode to 'rb' and 'wb', respectively.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a file pointer identical to that returned by fopen, except that it is unidirectional (may only be used for reading or writing) and must be closed with pclose. This pointer may be used with fgets, fgetss, and fwrite. When the mode is 'r', the returned file pointer equals to the STDOUT of the command, when the mode is 'w', the returned file pointer equals to the STDIN of the command.
If an error occurs, returns false.

refsect1.title: Examples

example.title: popen example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$handle = popen("/bin/ls", "r");
?>

note.para: If you're looking for bi-directional support (two-way), use proc_open.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Outputs a file

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Reads a file and writes it to the output buffer.

listitem.para: The filename being read.
You can use the optional second parameter and set it to true, if you want to search for the file in the include_path, too.

listitem.simpara: A context stream resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the number of bytes read from the file on success, or false on failure

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Upon failure, an E_WARNING is emitted.

example.title: Forcing a download using readfile
example.programlisting:
<?php
$file = 'monkey.gif';

if (file_exists($file)) {
    header('Content-Description: File Transfer');
    header('Content-Type: application/octet-stream');
    header('Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="'.basename($file).'"');
    header('Expires: 0');
    header('Cache-Control: must-revalidate');
    header('Pragma: public');
    header('Content-Length: ' . filesize($file));
    readfile($file);
    exit;
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

note.para: readfile will not present any memory issues, even when sending large files, on its own. If you encounter an out of memory error ensure that output buffering is off with ob_get_level.

tip.simpara: A URL can be used as a filename with this function if the fopen wrappers have been enabled. See fopen for more details on how to specify the filename. See the for links to information about what abilities the various wrappers have, notes on their usage, and information on any predefined variables they may provide.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the target of a symbolic link

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: readlink does the same as the readlink C function.

listitem.para: The symbolic link path.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the contents of the symbolic link path or false on error.

note.simpara: The function fails if path is not a symlink, except on Windows, where the normalized path will be returned.

example.title: readlink example
example.programlisting:
<?php

// output e.g. /boot/vmlinux-2.4.20-xfs
echo readlink('/vmlinuz');

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns canonicalized absolute pathname

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: realpath expands all symbolic links and resolves references to /./, /../ and extra / characters in the input path and returns the canonicalized absolute pathname.

listitem.para:
The path being checked.
Whilst a path must be supplied, the value can be an empty string. In this case, the value is interpreted as the current directory.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the canonicalized absolute pathname on success. The resulting path will have no symbolic link, /./ or /../ components. Trailing delimiters, such as \ and /, are also removed.
realpath returns false on failure, e.g. if the file does not exist.

note.para: The running script must have executable permissions on all directories in the hierarchy, otherwise realpath will return false.
For case-insensitive filesystems realpath may or may not normalize the character case.
The function realpath will not work for a file which is inside a Phar as such path would be a virtual path, not a real one.
On Windows, junctions and symbolic links to directories are only expanded by one level.

note.simpara: Because PHP's integer type is signed and many platforms use 32bit integers, some filesystem functions may return unexpected results for files which are larger than 2GB.

example.title: realpath example
example.programlisting:
<?php
chdir('/var/www/');
echo realpath('./../../etc/passwd') . PHP_EOL;

echo realpath('/tmp/') . PHP_EOL;
?>

example.title: realpath on Windows
example.para: On windows realpath will change unix style paths to windows style.
example.programlisting:
<?php
echo realpath('/windows/system32'), PHP_EOL;

echo realpath('C:\Program Files\\'), PHP_EOL;
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get realpath cache entries

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Get the contents of the realpath cache.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns an array of realpath cache entries. The keys are original path entries, and the values are arrays of data items, containing the resolved path, expiration date, and other options kept in the cache.

example.title: realpath_cache_get example
example.programlisting:
<?php
var_dump(realpath_cache_get());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: array(2) { ["/test"]=> array(4) { ["key"]=> int(123456789) ["is_dir"]=> bool(true) ["realpath"]=> string(5) "/test" ["expires"]=> int(1260318939) } ["/test/test.php"]=> array(4) { ["key"]=> int(987654321) ["is_dir"]=> bool(false) ["realpath"]=> string(12) "/root/test.php" ["expires"]=> int(1260318939) } }

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get realpath cache size

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Get the amount of memory used by the realpath cache.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns how much memory realpath cache is using.

example.title: realpath_cache_size example
example.programlisting:
<?php
var_dump(realpath_cache_size());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Renames a file or directory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Attempts to rename from to to, moving it between directories if necessary. If renaming a file and to exists, it will be overwritten. If renaming a directory and to exists, this function will emit a warning.

listitem.para: The old name.

note.para: The wrapper used in from must match the wrapper used in to.

listitem.para:
The new name.
On Windows, if to already exists, it must be writable. Otherwise rename fails and issues E_WARNING.

listitem.simpara: A context stream resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Example with rename
example.programlisting:
<?php
rename("/tmp/tmp_file.txt", "/home/user/login/docs/my_file.txt");
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Rewind the position of a file pointer

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sets the file position indicator for stream to the beginning of the file stream.

note.para: If you have opened the file in append ("a" or "a+") mode, any data you write to the file will always be appended, regardless of the file pointer position.

listitem.para: The file pointer must be valid, and must point to a file successfully opened by fopen.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: rewind overwriting example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$handle = fopen('output.txt', 'r+');

fwrite($handle, 'Really long sentence.');
rewind($handle);
fwrite($handle, 'Foo');
rewind($handle);

echo fread($handle, filesize('output.txt'));

fclose($handle);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Removes directory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Attempts to remove the directory named by directory. The directory must be empty, and the relevant permissions must permit this. A E_WARNING level error will be generated on failure.

listitem.para: Path to the directory.

listitem.simpara: A context stream resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: rmdir example
example.programlisting:
<?php
if (!is_dir('examples')) {
    mkdir('examples');
}

rmdir('examples');
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of stream_set_write_buffer

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: stream_set_write_buffer.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gives information about a file

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gathers the statistics of the file named by filename. If filename is a symbolic link, statistics are from the file itself, not the symlink. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, on Windows NTS builds the size, atime, mtime and ctime statistics have been from the symlink, in this case.
lstat is identical to stat except it would instead be based off the symlinks status.

listitem.para: Path to the file.

refsect1.title: Return Values

row.entry: time of last inode change (Unix timestamp)

refsect1.para: * On Windows this will always be 0.
** Only valid on systems supporting the st_blksize type - other systems (e.g. Windows) return -1.

*** On Windows, as of PHP 7.4.0, this is the serial number of the volume that contains the file, which is a 64-bit unsigned integer, so may overflow. Previously, it was the numeric representation of the drive letter (e.g. 2 for C:) for stat, and 0 for lstat.
**** On Windows, as of PHP 7.4.0, this is the identifier associated with the file, which is a 64-bit unsigned integer, so may overflow. Previously, it was always 0.

***** On Windows, the writable permission bit is set according to the read-only file attribute, and the same value is reported for all users, group and owner. The ACL is not taken into account, contrary to is_writable.

The value of mode contains information read by several functions. When written in octal, starting from the right, the first three digits are returned by chmod. The next digit is ignored by PHP. The next two digits indicate the file type:
mode file types
mode in octal Meaning
0140000 socket
0120000 link
0100000 regular file
0060000 block device
0040000 directory
0020000 character device
0010000 fifo
So for example a regular file could be 0100644 and a directory could be 0040755.
In case of error, stat returns false.

note.simpara: Because PHP's integer type is signed and many platforms use 32bit integers, some filesystem functions may return unexpected results for files which are larger than 2GB.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: Upon failure, an E_WARNING is emitted.

row.entry: On Windows, the device number is now the serial number of the volume that contains the file, and the inode number is the identifier associated with the file.
The size, atime, mtime and ctime statistics of symlinks are always those of the target. This was previously not the case for NTS builds on Windows.

example.title: stat example
example.programlisting:
<?php
/* Get file stat */
$stat = stat('C:\php\php.exe');

/*
 * Print file access time, this is the same 
 * as calling fileatime()
 */
echo 'Access time: ' . $stat['atime'];

/*
 * Print file modification time, this is the 
 * same as calling filemtime()
 */
echo 'Modification time: ' . $stat['mtime'];

/* Print the device number */
echo 'Device number: ' . $stat['dev'];
?>

example.title: Using stat information together with touch
example.programlisting:
<?php
/* Get file stat */
$stat = stat('C:\php\php.exe');

/* Did we failed to get stat information? */
if (!$stat) {
    echo 'stat() call failed...';
} else {
    /*
     * We want the access time to be 1 week 
     * after the current access time.
     */
    $atime = $stat['atime'] + 604800;

    /* Touch the file */
    if (!touch('some_file.txt', time(), $atime)) {
        echo 'Failed to touch file...';
    } else {
        echo 'touch() returned success...';
    }
}
?>

note.simpara: Note that time resolution may differ from one file system to another.
The results of this function are cached. See clearstatcache for more details.

tip.simpara: As of PHP 5.0.0, this function can also be used with some URL wrappers. Refer to to determine which wrappers support stat family of functionality.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Creates a symbolic link

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: symlink creates a symbolic link to the existing target with the specified name link.

listitem.para: Target of the link.
The link name.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: The function fails, and issues E_WARNING, if link already exists. On Windows, the function also fails, and issues E_WARNING, if target does not exist.

example.title: Create a symbolic link
example.programlisting:
<?php
$target = 'uploads.php';
$link = 'uploads';
symlink($target, $link);

echo readlink($link);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Create file with unique file name

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Creates a file with a unique filename, with access permission set to 0600, in the specified directory. If the directory does not exist or is not writable, tempnam may generate a file in the system's temporary directory, and return the full path to that file, including its name.

listitem.para: The directory where the temporary filename will be created.
The prefix of the generated temporary filename.

note.simpara: Only the first 63 characters of the prefix are used, the rest are ignored. Windows uses only the first three characters of the prefix.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the new temporary filename (with path), or false on failure.

row.entry: The name of files created by tempnam are now 13 bytes longer. The total length is still platform-dependent.
tempnam now emits a notice when falling back to the temp directory of the system.

example.title: tempnam example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$tmpfname = tempnam("/tmp", "FOO");

$handle = fopen($tmpfname, "w");
fwrite($handle, "writing to tempfile");
fclose($handle);

// do something here

unlink($tmpfname);
?>

note.simpara: If PHP cannot create a file in the specified directory parameter, it falls back on the system default. On NTFS this also happens if the specified directory contains more than 65534 files.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Creates a temporary file

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Creates a temporary file with a unique name in read-write-binary (w+b) mode and returns a file handle.
The file is automatically removed when closed (for example, by calling fclose, or when there are no remaining references to the file handle returned by tmpfile), or when the script ends.

caution.simpara: If the script terminates unexpectedly, the temporary file may not be deleted.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a file handle, similar to the one returned by fopen, for the new file or false on failure.

example.title: tmpfile example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$temp = tmpfile();
fwrite($temp, "writing to tempfile");
fseek($temp, 0);
echo fread($temp, 1024);
fclose($temp); // this removes the file
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sets access and modification time of file

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Attempts to set the access and modification times of the file named in the filename parameter to the value given in mtime. Note that the access time is always modified, regardless of the number of parameters.
If the file does not exist, it will be created.

listitem.para: The name of the file being touched.
The touch time. If mtime is null, the current system time is used.
If not null, the access time of the given filename is set to the value of atime. Otherwise, it is set to the value passed to the mtime parameter. If both are null, the current system time is used.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: mtime and atime are now nullable.

example.title: touch example
example.programlisting:
<?php
if (touch($filename)) {
    echo $filename . ' modification time has been changed to present time';
} else {
    echo 'Sorry, could not change modification time of ' . $filename;
}
?>

example.title: touch using the mtime parameter
example.programlisting:
<?php
// This is the touch time, we'll set it to one hour in the past.
$time = time() - 3600;

// Touch the file
if (!touch('some_file.txt', $time)) {
    echo 'Whoops, something went wrong...';
} else {
    echo 'Touched file with success';
}
?>

note.simpara: Note that time resolution may differ from one file system to another.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Changes the current umask

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: umask sets PHP's umask to mask & 0777 and returns the old umask. When PHP is being used as a server module, the umask is restored when each request is finished.

listitem.para: The new umask.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: If mask is null, umask simply returns the current umask otherwise the old umask is returned.

example.title: umask example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$old = umask(0);
chmod("/path/some_dir/some_file.txt", 0755);
umask($old);

// Checking
if ($old != umask()) {
    die('An error occurred while changing back the umask');
}
?>

note.para: Avoid using this function in multithreaded webservers. It is better to change the file permissions with chmod after creating the file. Using umask can lead to unexpected behavior of concurrently running scripts and the webserver itself because they all use the same umask.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Deletes a file

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Deletes filename. Similar to the Unix C unlink() function. An E_WARNING level error will be generated on failure.

listitem.para: Path to the file.
If the file is a symlink, the symlink will be deleted. On Windows, to delete a symlink to a directory, rmdir has to be used instead.

listitem.simpara: A context stream resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: On Windows, it is now possible to unlink files with handles in use, while formerly that would fail. However, it is still not possible to re-create the unlinked file, until all handles to it have been closed.

example.title: Basic unlink usage
example.programlisting: Hello world!'); fclose($fh); unlink('test.html'); ?>

preface.title: Introduction
preface.simpara: The inotify extension exposes the inotify functions inotify_init, inotify_add_watch and inotify_rm_watch.

As the C inotify_init function returns a file descriptor, PHP's inotify_init returns a stream resource, usable with standard stream functions, like stream_select, stream_set_blocking and fclose. inotify_read replaces the C way of reading inotify events.

section.title: Installing/Configuring
section.simpara: This PECL extension is not bundled with PHP.

Information for installing this PECL extension may be found in the manual chapter titled Installation of PECL extensions. Additional information such as new releases, downloads, source files, maintainer information, and a CHANGELOG, can be located here: https://pecl.php.net/package/inotify.

section.title: Resource Types
section.simpara: This extension defines a stream resource returned by inotify_init.

appendix.title: Predefined Constants
appendix.simpara: The constants below are defined by this extension, and will only be available when the extension has either been compiled into PHP or dynamically loaded at runtime.

variablelist.title: Inotify constants usable with inotify_add_watch and/or returned by inotify_read

listitem.simpara: File was accessed (read) (*)
File was modified (*)
Metadata changed (e.g. permissions, mtime, etc.) (*)
File opened for writing was closed (*)
File not opened for writing was closed (*)
File was opened (*)
File moved into watched directory (*)
File moved out of watched directory (*)
File or directory created in watched directory (*)
File or directory deleted in watched directory (*)
Watched file or directory was deleted
Watch file or directory was moved
Equals to IN_CLOSE_WRITE | IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE
Equals to IN_MOVED_FROM | IN_MOVED_TO
Bitmask of all the above constants
File system containing watched object was unmounted
Event queue overflowed (wd is -1 for this event)
Watch was removed (explicitly by inotify_rm_watch or because file was removed or filesystem unmounted
Subject of this event is a directory
Only watch pathname if it is a directory (Since Linux 2.6.15)
Do not dereference pathname if it is a symlink (Since Linux 2.6.15)
Add events to watch mask for this pathname if it already exists (instead of replacing mask).
Monitor pathname for one event, then remove from watch list.

note.simpara: The events marked with an asterisk (*) above can occur for files in watched directories.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Add a watch to an initialized inotify instance

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: inotify_add_watch adds a new watch or modify an existing watch for the file or directory specified in pathname.
Using inotify_add_watch on a watched object replaces the existing watch. Using the IN_MASK_ADD constant adds (OR) events to the existing watch.

listitem.simpara: Resource returned by inotify_init
File or directory to watch
Events to watch for. See Predefined Constants.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The return value is a unique (inotify instance wide) watch descriptor, or false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Initialize an inotify instance

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Initialize an inotify instance for use with inotify_add_watch

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: A stream resource or false on error.

example.title: Example usage of inotify
example.programlisting:
<?php
// Open an inotify instance
$fd = inotify_init();

// Watch __FILE__ for metadata changes (e.g. mtime)
$watch_descriptor = inotify_add_watch($fd, __FILE__, IN_ATTRIB);

// generate an event
touch(__FILE__);

// Read events
$events = inotify_read($fd);
print_r($events);

// The following methods allows to use inotify functions without blocking on inotify_read():

// - Using stream_select() on $fd:
$read = array($fd);
$write = null;
$except = null;
stream_select($read,$write,$except,0);

// - Using stream_set_blocking() on $fd
stream_set_blocking($fd, 0);
inotify_read($fd); // Does no block, and return false if no events are pending

// - Using inotify_queue_len() to check if event queue is not empty
$queue_len = inotify_queue_len($fd); // If > 0, inotify_read() will not block

// Stop watching __FILE__ for metadata changes
inotify_rm_watch($fd, $watch_descriptor);

// Close the inotify instance
// This may have closed all watches if this was not already done
fclose($fd);

?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Return a number upper than zero if there are pending events

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function allows to know if inotify_read will block or not. If a number upper than zero is returned, there are pending events and inotify_read will not block.

listitem.simpara: Resource returned by inotify_init

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a number upper than zero if there are pending events.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Read events from an inotify instance

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Read inotify events from an inotify instance.

listitem.simpara: Resource returned by inotify_init

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para:
An array of inotify events or false if no events was pending and inotify_instance is non-blocking. Each event is an array with the following keys:
wd is a watch descriptor returned by inotify_add_watch mask is a bit mask of events cookie is a unique id to connect related events (e.g. IN_MOVE_FROM and IN_MOVE_TO) name is the name of a file (e.g. if a file was modified in a watched directory)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Remove an existing watch from an inotify instance

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: inotify_rm_watch removes the watch watch_descriptor from the inotify instance inotify_instance.

listitem.simpara: Resource returned by inotify_init
Watch to remove from the instance

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

preface.title: Introduction
preface.para: The xattr extension allows for the manipulation of extended attributes on a filesystem.

section.title: Requirements
section.para: To use xattr, you will need libattr installed. It is available at http://savannah.nongnu.org/projects/attr/.

note.para: These functions only work on filesystems that support extended attributes, and have them enabled at mount time. Some common filesystems that support extended attributes are ext2, ext3, reiserfs, jfs, and xfs.

section.title: Installation
section.para: Information for installing this PECL extension may be found in the manual chapter titled Installation of PECL extensions. Additional information such as new releases, downloads, source files, maintainer information, and a CHANGELOG, can be located here: https://pecl.php.net/package/xattr.
A DLL for this PECL extension is currently unavailable. See also the building on Windows section.

appendix.title: Predefined Constants
appendix.simpara: The constants below are defined by this extension, and will only be available when the extension has either been compiled into PHP or dynamically loaded at runtime.

listitem.simpara: Set attribute in root (trusted) namespace. Requires root privileges.
Do not follow the symbolic link but operate on symbolic link itself.
Function will fail if extended attribute already exists.
Function will fail if extended attribute doesn't exist.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get an extended attribute

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function gets the value of an extended attribute of a file.
refsect1.simpara: Extended attributes have two different namespaces: user and root. The user namespace is available to all users, while the root namespace is available only to users with root privileges. xattr operates on the user namespace by default, but this can be changed with the flags parameter.

listitem.para: The file from which we get the attribute.
The name of the attribute.

row.entry: Do not follow the symbolic link but operate on symbolic link itself.
Set attribute in root (trusted) namespace. Requires root privileges.

refsect1.title: Return Values
