section.title: Basic usage
section.para: This example forks off a daemon process with a signal handler.

example.title: Process Control Example
example.programlisting:
<?php
pcntl_async_signals(true);

$pid = pcntl_fork();
if ($pid == -1) {
     die("could not fork"); 
} else if ($pid) {
     exit(); // we are the parent 
} else {
     // we are the child
}

// detach from the controlling terminal
if (posix_setsid() == -1) {
    die("could not detach from terminal");
}

// setup signal handlers
pcntl_signal(SIGTERM, "sig_handler");
pcntl_signal(SIGHUP, "sig_handler");

// loop forever performing tasks
while (1) {

    // do something interesting here

}

function sig_handler($signo) 
{

     switch ($signo) {
         case SIGTERM:
             // handle shutdown tasks
             exit;
             break;
         case SIGHUP:
             // handle restart tasks
             break;
         default:
             // handle all other signals
     }

}

?>

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: The Pcntl\QosClass enum is used to specify the user process priority with pcntl_setqos_class.

enumitem.enumitemdescription: Runs the process as the highest priority level.
Runs the process at high priority level but below UserInteractive ones.
Runs the process after all high-priority processes but before the low-priority ones.
Pcntl\QosClass::Utility description
Runs the process after all high-priority ones had ran their courses.

partintro.title: See Also
partintro.para: A look at the section about POSIX functions may be useful.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set an alarm clock for delivery of a signal

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Creates a timer that will send a SIGALRM signal to the process after the given number of seconds. Any call to pcntl_alarm will cancel any previously set alarm.

listitem.para: The number of seconds to wait. If seconds is zero, no new alarm is created.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the time in seconds that any previously scheduled alarm had remaining before it was to be delivered, or 0 if there was no previously scheduled alarm.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Enable/disable asynchronous signal handling or return the old setting

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: If the enable parameter is null, pcntl_async_signals returns whether asynchronous signal handling is enabled. Otherwise, asynchronous signal handling is enabled or disabled.

listitem.para: Whether asynchronous signal handling should be enabled.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: When used as getter (enable parameter is null) it returns whether asynchronous signal handling is enabled. When used as setter (enable parameter is not null), it returns whether asynchronous signal handling was enabled before the function call.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of pcntl_get_last_error

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: pcntl_get_last_error

refnamediv.refpurpose: Executes specified program in current process space

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Executes the program with the given arguments.

listitem.para: path must be the path to a binary executable or a script with a valid path pointing to an executable in the shebang ( #!/usr/local/bin/perl for example) as the first line. See your system's man execve(2) page for additional information.
args is an array of argument strings passed to the program.

env_vars is an array of strings which are passed as environment to the program. The array is in the format of name => value, the key being the name of the environmental variable and the value being the value of that variable.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns false on failure. On success the function does not return, because the current process image is replaced by the executed program.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: As of PHP 8.5.0, a ValueError is thrown if any entry of args contains a null byte, or if any entry or key of env_vars contains a null byte.

row.entry: A ValueError is now thrown if any entry of args contains a null byte, or if any entry or key of env_vars contains a null byte.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Forks the currently running process

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The pcntl_fork function creates a child process that differs from the parent process only in its PID and PPID. Please see your system's fork(2) man page for specific details as to how fork works on your system.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: On success, the PID of the child process is returned in the parent's thread of execution, and a 0 is returned in the child's thread of execution. On failure, a -1 will be returned in the parent's context, no child process will be created, and a PHP error is raised.

example.title: pcntl_fork example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$pid = pcntl_fork();
if ($pid == -1) {
     die('could not fork');
} else if ($pid) {
     // we are the parent
     pcntl_wait($status); //Protect against Zombie children
} else {
     // we are the child
}

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Create a child process using forkx(2)

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The pcntl_forkx function creates a child process using the forkx(2) system call, which is available on illumos and Solaris systems.

listitem.simpara: The flags parameter controls the behavior of the fork. Pass 0 for default behavior or FORK_NOSIGCHLD to prevent the SIGCHLD signal from being sent to the parent when the child terminates.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: On success, the PID of the child process is returned in the parent's thread of execution, and a 0 is returned in the child's thread of execution. On failure, a -1 will be returned in the parent's context, no child process will be created, and a PHP error is raised.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve the error number set by the last pcntl function which failed

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Retrieve the error number (errno) set by the last pcntl function that failed. The system error message associated with the error number may be checked with pcntl_strerror.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the error number (errno) set by the last pcntl function that failed. If there was no error, 0 is returned.

example.title: pcntl_get_last_error example
example.para: This example will attempt to wait on child processes in a situation where no child process exists, then will print out the corresponding error message.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$pid = pcntl_wait($status);
if ($pid === -1) {
    $errno = pcntl_get_last_error();
    $message = pcntl_strerror($errno);
    fwrite(STDERR, 'pcntl_wait failed with errno ' . $errno
           . ': ' . $message . PHP_EOL);
}
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: pcntl_wait failed with errno 10: No child processes

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the CPU number on which the calling process last executed

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: pcntl_getcpu returns the number of the CPU on which the calling process was last executed. This function uses the sched_getcpu(3) system call available on Linux.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the CPU number as an int.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the cpu affinity of a process

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieve the cpu affinity of the process_id.

listitem.simpara: If null, the current process ID is used.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the cpu affinity mask of the process, or false on failure.

warning.simpara: This function may return Boolean false, but may also return a non-Boolean value which evaluates to false. Please read the section on Booleans for more information. Use the === operator for testing the return value of this function.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: A ValueError is thrown when process_id is an invalid process id or the cpu mask had failed to be created.
If process_id is a process for which the current user has no allowed permission, a E_WARNING is emitted.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the priority of any process

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pcntl_getpriority gets the priority of process_id. Because priority levels can differ between system types and kernel versions, please see your system's getpriority(2) man page for specific details.

listitem.para: If null, the process id of the current process is used.
One of PRIO_PGRP, PRIO_USER, PRIO_PROCESS, PRIO_DARWIN_BG or PRIO_DARWIN_THREAD.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: pcntl_getpriority returns the priority of the process or false on error. A lower numerical value causes more favorable scheduling.

warning.simpara: This function may return Boolean false, but may also return a non-Boolean value which evaluates to false. Please read the section on Booleans for more information. Use the === operator for testing the return value of this function.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the QoS class of the current thread

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieves the Quality of Service (QoS) class of the current thread.

note.simpara: This function is only available on Apple platforms.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the current QoS class as a Pcntl\QosClass.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Throws an Error if the underlying call to pthread_get_qos_class_np() fails.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Manipulates process resources

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Manipulates process resources.

listitem.para: The flags parameter determines which resources of the invoking process (parent) are shared by the new process (child) or initialized to their default values.

flags is the logical OR of some subset of:
RFPROC: If set a new process is created; otherwise changes affect the current process.
RFNOWAIT: If set, the child process will be dissociated from the parent. Upon exit the child will not leave a status for the parent to collect.
RFFDG: If set, the invoker's file descriptor table is copied; otherwise the two processes share a single table.
RFCFDG: If set, the new process starts with a clean file descriptor table. Is mutually exclusive with RFFDG.
RFLINUXTHPN: If set, the kernel will return SIGUSR1 instead of SIGCHLD upon thread exit for the child. This is intended to do Linux clone exit parent notification.
RFTSIGZMB: If set, the kernel will deliver the signal specified by the signal parameter to the parent upon the child exit, instead of the default SIGCHLD. Specifying signal number 0 disables signal delivery upon the child exit.
RFTHREAD: If set, the new process shares file descriptor to process leaders table with its parent. Only applies when neither RFFDG nor RFCFDG are set.

listitem.simpara: The signal number to deliver to the parent when the child exits. This is only used when the RFTSIGZMB flag is set. Specifying 0 disables signal delivery upon the child exit.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: On success, the PID of the child process is returned in the parent's thread of execution, and a 0 is returned in the child's thread of execution. On failure, a -1 will be returned in the parent's context, no child process will be created, and a PHP error is raised.

example.title: pcntl_rfork example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$pid = pcntl_rfork(RFNOWAIT|RFTSIGZMB, SIGUSR1);
if ($pid > 0) {
  // This is the parent process.
  var_dump($pid);
} else {
  // This is the child process.
  var_dump($pid);
  sleep(2); // as the child does not wait, so we see its "pid"
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

note.para: This function is only available on BSD systems.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set the cpu affinity of a process

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sets the cpu affinity for the process_id with the cpu affinity mask given by cpu_ids.

listitem.simpara: If null, the current process ID is used.
The cpu affinity mask comprised of one or more cpu id for binding the process to.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: A TypeError is thrown if one of the cpu id from the cpu_ids is invalid. A ValueError is thrown if process_id is an invalid process id or the cpu mask had failed to be created.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Reassociate the calling process with a namespace of another process

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Reassociates the calling process with a Linux namespace of the process specified by process_id, using a pidfd obtained via pidfd_open(2) and setns(2).

listitem.simpara: The process ID of the target process whose namespace to join. If null, the calling process's own PID is used.
The namespace type to reassociate with. Defaults to CLONE_NEWNET (network namespace). Possible values include CLONE_NEWNET, CLONE_NEWIPC, CLONE_NEWUTS, and others.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Change the priority of any process

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pcntl_setpriority sets the priority of process_id.

listitem.para: priority is generally a value in the range -20 to 20. The default priority is 0 while a lower numerical value causes more favorable scheduling. Because priority levels can differ between system types and kernel versions, please see your system's setpriority(2) man page for specific details.
If null, the process id of the current process is used.
One of PRIO_PGRP, PRIO_USER, PRIO_PROCESS, PRIO_DARWIN_BG or PRIO_DARWIN_THREAD.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set the QoS class of the current thread

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sets the Quality of Service (QoS) class of the current thread.

listitem.simpara: The Quality of Service class to assign to the current thread. The operating system uses this as a hint to schedule CPU time, I/O priority, and energy usage, with higher classes preempting lower ones. See Pcntl\QosClass for the available cases.
Highest priority. Intended for work that directly drives a user interface and must complete virtually instantly to avoid perceived delay, such as event handling or drawing.
High priority, just below UserInteractive. Intended for work the user has explicitly initiated and is actively waiting on, expected to complete within a few seconds.
Standard priority, used when no more specific class applies. Runs after higher-priority work but ahead of Utility and Background.
Lower priority, intended for long-running work the user is aware of but not actively waiting on, such as downloads, imports, or bulk computation. Scheduled in an energy-efficient manner.
Lowest priority, intended for work the user is not aware of, such as prefetching, indexing, or maintenance. Heavily optimized for energy efficiency and may be deferred when the system is under load.

note.simpara: This function is only available on Apple platforms.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Throws an Error if the underlying call to pthread_set_qos_class_self_np() fails.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Installs a signal handler

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The pcntl_signal function installs a new signal handler or replaces the current signal handler for the signal indicated by signal.

listitem.para: The signal number.

listitem.simpara: The signal handler. This may be either a callable, which will be invoked to handle the signal, or either of the two global constants SIG_IGN or SIG_DFL, which will ignore the signal or restore the default signal handler respectively.
listitem.para: If a callable is given, it must implement the following signature:

listitem.simpara: The signal being handled.
If operating systems supports siginfo_t structures, this will be an array of signal information dependent on the signal.

note.simpara: When a handler is set to an object method, the reference count of that object is increased, which makes it persist until the handler is changed to something else, or the script ends.

listitem.para: Specifies whether system call restarting should be used when this signal arrives.

note.simpara: Although this parameter defaults to true, that default does not apply to SIGALRM: when restart_syscalls is not passed and signal is SIGALRM, system call restarting is disabled. Pass true explicitly to enable system call restarting for SIGALRM.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: A ValueError is thrown if signal is less than 1 or greater than or equal to NSIG, or if handler is an int other than SIG_DFL or SIG_IGN.
A TypeError is thrown if handler is neither a callable nor an int.

row.entry: restart_syscalls is now honoured for SIGALRM; previously system call restarting was always disabled for that signal. When the argument is not passed, system call restarting remains disabled for SIGALRM.

As of PHP 7.1.0 the handler callback is given a second argument containing the siginfo of the specific signal. This data is only supplied if the operating system has the siginfo_t structure. If the OS does not implement siginfo_t NULL is supplied.

example.title: pcntl_signal example
example.programlisting:
<?php
pcntl_async_signals(true);

// signal handler function
function sig_handler($signo)
{

     switch ($signo) {
         case SIGTERM:
             // handle shutdown tasks
             exit;
             break;
         case SIGHUP:
             // handle restart tasks
             break;
         case SIGUSR1:
             echo "Caught SIGUSR1...\n";
             break;
         default:
             // handle all other signals
     }

}

echo "Installing signal handler...\n";

// setup signal handlers
pcntl_signal(SIGTERM, "sig_handler");
pcntl_signal(SIGHUP,  "sig_handler");
pcntl_signal(SIGUSR1, "sig_handler");

// or use an object
// pcntl_signal(SIGUSR1, array($obj, "do_something"));

echo"Generating signal SIGUSR1 to self...\n";

// send SIGUSR1 to current process id
// posix_* functions require the posix extension
posix_kill(posix_getpid(), SIGUSR1);

echo "Done\n";

?>

refsect1.title: Notes
refsect1.simpara: pcntl_signal does not stack the signal handlers, but replaces them.

refsect2.title: Dispatch Methods
refsect2.para:
There are several methods of dispatching signal handlers:
Asynchronous dispatch with pcntl_async_signals enabled. This is the recommended method Setting tick frequency Manual dispatch with pcntl_signal_dispatch
When signals are dispatched asynchronously or using tick-based execution, blocking functions like sleep may be interrupted.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Calls signal handlers for pending signals

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The pcntl_signal_dispatch function calls the signal handlers installed by pcntl_signal for each pending signal.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: pcntl_signal_dispatch example
example.programlisting:
<?php
echo "Installing signal handler...\n";
pcntl_signal(SIGHUP,  function($signo) {
     echo "signal handler called\n";
});

echo "Generating signal SIGHUP to self...\n";
posix_kill(posix_getpid(), SIGHUP);

echo "Dispatching...\n";
pcntl_signal_dispatch();

echo "Done\n";

?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: Installing signal handler... Generating signal SIGHUP to self... Dispatching... signal handler called Done

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the current handler for specified signal

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The pcntl_signal_get_handler function will get the current handler for the specified signal.

listitem.para: The signal number.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: This function may return an integer value that refers to SIG_DFL or SIG_IGN. If a custom handler has been set, that callable is returned.

example.title: pcntl_signal_get_handler example
example.programlisting:
<?php
var_dump(pcntl_signal_get_handler(SIGUSR1)); // Outputs: int(0)

function pcntl_test($signo) {}
pcntl_signal(SIGUSR1, 'pcntl_test');
var_dump(pcntl_signal_get_handler(SIGUSR1)); // Outputs: string(10) "pcntl_test"

pcntl_signal(SIGUSR1, SIG_DFL);
var_dump(pcntl_signal_get_handler(SIGUSR1)); // Outputs: int(0)

pcntl_signal(SIGUSR1, SIG_IGN);
var_dump(pcntl_signal_get_handler(SIGUSR1)); // Outputs: int(1)
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sets and retrieves blocked signals

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The pcntl_sigprocmask function adds, removes or sets blocked signals, depending on the mode parameter.

listitem.para:
Sets the behavior of pcntl_sigprocmask. Possible values:
SIG_BLOCK: Add the signals to the currently blocked signals. SIG_UNBLOCK: Remove the signals from the currently blocked signals. SIG_SETMASK: Replace the currently blocked signals by the given list of signals.
List of signals.
The old_signals parameter is set to an array containing the list of the previously blocked signals.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: A ValueError is thrown if signals is empty, unless mode is SIG_SETMASK.
A TypeError is thrown if signals value is not an int.
A ValueError is thrown if signals value is invalid.
A ValueError is thrown if mode value is not SIG_BLOCK, SIG_UNBLOCK or SIG_SETMASK.

example.title: pcntl_sigprocmask example
example.programlisting:
<?php
pcntl_sigprocmask(SIG_BLOCK, array(SIGHUP));
$oldset = array();
pcntl_sigprocmask(SIG_UNBLOCK, array(SIGHUP), $oldset);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Waits for signals, with a timeout

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The pcntl_sigtimedwait function operates in exactly the same way as pcntl_sigwaitinfo except that it takes two additional parameters, seconds and nanoseconds, which enable an upper bound to be placed on the time for which the script is suspended.

listitem.para: Array of signals to wait for.
The info is set to an array containing information about the signal. See pcntl_sigwaitinfo.
Timeout in seconds.
Timeout in nanoseconds.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: pcntl_sigtimedwait returns a signal number on success, or false on failure.

row.entry: On failure, false is now returned; previously -1 was returned in some cases.
A ValueError is thrown if signals is empty.
A TypeError is thrown if signals value is not an int.
A ValueError is thrown if signals value is invalid.
A ValueError is thrown if seconds value is less than 0.
A ValueError is thrown if nanoseconds value is not between 0 and 1e9.
A ValueError is thrown if both seconds and nanoseconds values are 0.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Waits for signals

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The pcntl_sigwaitinfo function suspends execution of the calling script until one of the signals given in signals are delivered. If one of the signal is already pending (e.g. blocked by pcntl_sigprocmask), pcntl_sigwaitinfo will return immediately.

listitem.para: Array of signals to wait for.
The info parameter is set to an array containing information about the signal.

The following elements are set for all signals:
signo: Signal number errno: An error number code: Signal code

The following elements may be set for the SIGCHLD signal:
status: Exit value or signal utime: User time consumed stime: System time consumed pid: Sending process ID uid: Real user ID of sending process

The following elements may be set for the SIGILL, SIGFPE, SIGSEGV and SIGBUS signals:
addr: Memory location which caused fault

The following element may be set for the SIGPOLL signal:
band: Band event fd: File descriptor number

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a signal number on success, or false on failure.

row.entry: On failure, false is now returned; previously -1 was returned in some cases.
A ValueError is thrown if signals is empty.
A TypeError is thrown if signals value is not an int.
A ValueError is thrown if signals value is invalid.

example.title: pcntl_sigwaitinfo example
example.programlisting:
<?php
echo "Blocking SIGHUP signal\n";
pcntl_sigprocmask(SIG_BLOCK, array(SIGHUP));

echo "Sending SIGHUP to self\n";
posix_kill(posix_getpid(), SIGHUP);

echo "Waiting for signals\n";
$info = array();
pcntl_sigwaitinfo(array(SIGHUP), $info);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve the system error message associated with the given errno

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the system error message associated with the given error_code (errno) of the last pcntl function that failed. The error_code parameter may be obtained by calling pcntl_get_last_error.

listitem.para: An error number (errno), returned by pcntl_get_last_error.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the error message, as a string.

example.title: pcntl_strerror example
example.para: This example will attempt to wait on child processes in a situation where no child process exists, then will print out the corresponding error message.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$pid = pcntl_wait($status);
if ($pid === -1) {
    $errno = pcntl_get_last_error();
    $message = pcntl_strerror($errno);
    fwrite(STDERR, 'pcntl_wait failed with errno ' . $errno
           . ': ' . $message . PHP_EOL);
}
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: pcntl_wait failed with errno 10: No child processes

refnamediv.refpurpose: Dissociates parts of the process execution context

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pcntl_unshare allows a process to disassociate parts of its execution context that are currently being shared with other processes. The main use of pcntl_unshare is to allow a process to control its shared execution context without creating a new process.

listitem.para:
The flags parameter is a bitmask that specifies which parts of the execution context should be unshared. This parameter is specified by ORing together zero or more of the CLONE_* constants:
CLONE_NEWNS CLONE_NEWIPC CLONE_NEWUTS CLONE_NEWNET CLONE_NEWPID CLONE_NEWUSER CLONE_NEWCGROUP

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure. On failure it sets an error code, that can be retrieved with pcntl_get_last_error.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Waits on or returns the status of a forked child

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The wait function suspends execution of the current process until a child has exited, or until a signal is delivered whose action is to terminate the current process or to call a signal handling function. If a child has already exited by the time of the call (a so-called "zombie" process), the function returns immediately. Any system resources used by the child are freed. Please see your system's wait(2) man page for specific details as to how wait works on your system.

note.para: This function is equivalent to calling pcntl_waitpid with a -1 process_id and no flags.

listitem.para: pcntl_wait will store status information in the status parameter which can be evaluated using the following functions: pcntl_wifexited, pcntl_wifstopped, pcntl_wifsignaled, pcntl_wexitstatus, pcntl_wtermsig and pcntl_wstopsig.

If wait3 is available on your system (mostly BSD-style systems), you can provide the optional flags parameter. If this parameter is not provided, wait will be used for the system call. If wait3 is not available, providing a value for flags will have no effect. The value of flags is the value of zero or more of the following two constants OR'ed together:
Possible values for flags
WNOHANG
Return immediately if no child has exited.
WUNTRACED
Return for children which are stopped, and whose status has not been reported.

listitem.simpara: The resource_usage parameter is set to an associative array containing resource usage statistics from the child process. For information on the contents see getrusage.

This is only supported if the wait3(2) system call is available on the system; otherwise the parameter is left untouched. If no child process was reaped, that is if the function returns 0 or -1, the parameter is set to an empty array.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: pcntl_wait returns the process ID of the child which exited, -1 on error or zero if WNOHANG was provided as an option (on wait3-available systems) and no child was available.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Waits for a child process to change state

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Obtains status information pertaining to termination, stop, and/or continue events in one of the caller's child processes.

Unless WNOHANG flag is passed, the calling process will become blocked until an error occurs, or status information becomes available that satisfies all of the following:
The status information is from one of the child processes in the set of child processes specified by the idtype and id arguments.
The state change in the status information matches one of the state change flags set in the flags argument.

If matching status information is available prior to the call to pcntl_waitid, return shall be immediate. If matching status information is available for two or more child processes, the order in which their status is reported is unspecified.

note.para: This documentation covers the POSIX specification of the waitid function, along with some additional parameters specific to implementations on Linux, NetBSD and FreeBSD. Please see your system's waitid(2) man page for specific details as to how waitid works on your system.

listitem.simpara: The idtype and id arguments are used to specify which children to wait for.

table.title: POSIX standard idtype and id arguments

row.entry: wait for any child process, id is ignored.
wait for the child with process ID equal to id.
wait for any child with process group ID equal to id.

table.title: Linux specific idtype and id arguments

row.entry: wait for the child referred to by the PID file descriptor specified in id. (See the Linux pidfd_open(2) man page for further information on PID file descriptors.)

table.title: NetBSD and FreeBSD specific idtype and id arguments

row.entry: wait for processes whose effective user ID is equal to id.
wait for processes whose effective group ID is equal to id.

wait for processes whose session ID is equal to id. If the child process started its own session, its session ID will be the same as its process ID. Otherwise the session ID of a child process will match the caller's session ID.

table.title: FreeBSD specific idtype and id arguments

row.entry: wait for processes within a jail whose jail identifier is equal to id.

listitem.para: The info parameter is set to an array containing information about the signal.

info array may contain the following keys:
signo: Signal number errno: System error number code: Signal code status: Exit value or signal pid: Sending process ID uid: Real user ID of sending process utime: User time consumed stime: System time consumed

The value of flags is the value of zero or more of the following constants OR'ed together:
possible values for flags
WCONTINUED
Status shall be returned for any continued child process whose status either has not been reported since it continued from a job control stop or has been reported only by calls to pcntl_waitid with the WNOWAIT flag set.
WEXITED
Wait for processes that have exited.
WNOHANG
Do not hang if no status is available; return immediately.
WNOWAIT
Keep the process whose status is returned in info in a waitable state. This shall not affect the state of the process; the process may be waited for again after this call completes.
WSTOPPED
Status shall be returned for any child that has stopped upon receipt of a signal, and whose status either has not been reported since it stopped or has been reported only by calls to pcntl_waitid with the WNOWAIT flag set.

listitem.simpara: The resource_usage parameter is set to an associative array containing resource usage statistics from the child process. For information on the contents see getrusage.
This is only supported if the wait6(2) system call is available, for example on FreeBSD, or on Linux through the raw waitid(2) system call; otherwise the parameter is left untouched.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: pcntl_waitid returns true if WNOHANG was specified and status is not available for any process specified by idtype and id.
pcntl_waitid returns true due to the change of state of one of its children.
Otherwise, false is returned and pcntl_get_last_error can be used to get the errno error number.

note.para: Once an errno error number has been obtained, pcntl_strerror can be used to get the text message associated with it.

row.entry: The calling process has no existing unwaited-for child processes.
pcntl_waitid was interrupted by a signal.
An invalid value was specified for flags, or idtype and id specify an invalid set of processes.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Waits on or returns the status of a forked child

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Suspends execution of the current process until a child as specified by the process_id argument has exited, or until a signal is delivered whose action is to terminate the current process or to call a signal handling function.

If a child as requested by process_id has already exited by the time of the call (a so-called "zombie" process), the function returns immediately. Any system resources used by the child are freed. Please see your system's waitpid(2) man page for specific details as to how waitpid works on your system.

listitem.para:
The value of process_id can be one of the following:
possible values for process_id
< -1
wait for any child process whose process group ID is equal to the absolute value of process_id.
-1
wait for any child process; this is the same behaviour that the pcntl_wait function exhibits.
0
wait for any child process whose process group ID is equal to that of the calling process.
> 0
wait for the child whose process ID is equal to the value of process_id.

note.para: Specifying -1 as the process_id is equivalent to the functionality pcntl_wait provides (minus flags).

listitem.para: pcntl_waitpid will store status information in the status parameter which can be evaluated using the following functions: pcntl_wifexited, pcntl_wifstopped, pcntl_wifsignaled, pcntl_wexitstatus, pcntl_wtermsig and pcntl_wstopsig.

The value of flags is the value of zero or more of the following two global constants OR'ed together:
possible values for flags
WNOHANG
return immediately if no child has exited.
WUNTRACED
return for children which are stopped, and whose status has not been reported.

listitem.simpara: The resource_usage parameter is set to an associative array containing resource usage statistics from the child process. For information on the contents see getrusage.

This is only supported if the wait4(2) system call is available on the system; otherwise the parameter is left untouched. If no child process was reaped, that is if the function returns 0 or -1, the parameter is set to an empty array.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: pcntl_waitpid returns the process ID of the child which exited, -1 on error or zero if WNOHANG was used and no child was available

example.title: pcntl_waitpid example
example.programlisting:
<?php
function checkChild(int $pid, bool $wait): void
{
    $flags = ($wait ? 0 : WNOHANG);
    $deadPid = pcntl_waitpid($pid, $status, $flags, $rusage);
    if ($deadPid === -1) {
        $errNo = pcntl_get_last_error();
        $errMsg = pcntl_strerror($errNo);
        print "PARENT pcntl_waitpid FAILED ({$errNo}): {$errMsg}\n";
    } elseif ($deadPid === 0) {
        print "PARENT pcntl_waitpid: No exited children.\n";
    } elseif (pcntl_wifexited($status)) {
        print "PARENT pcntl_waitpid: Child PID {$deadPid} exited with status: "
            . pcntl_wexitstatus($status) . "\n";
        var_dump($rusage);
    } else {
        print "PARENT pcntl_waitpid: Child PID {$deadPid} was terminated by signal: "
            . pcntl_wtermsig($status) . "\n";
    }
}

$parentPid = getmypid();
$forkedPid = pcntl_fork();
if ($forkedPid == -1) {
    die('Could not fork');
} else if ($forkedPid) {
    // Parent process
    print "PARENT {$parentPid} has forked {$forkedPid}\n";

    print "PARENT is checking for exited children\n";
    checkChild($forkedPid, false);

    // Prevents children remaining as a "zombie process"
    print "PARENT is waiting for a child to exit\n";
    checkChild($forkedPid, true);

    print "PARENT is checking for exited children\n";
    checkChild($forkedPid, false);

    print "PARENT is exiting\n";
} else {
    // Child process
    $pid = getmypid();
    print "CHILD {$pid} is sleeping\n";
    sleep(10);
    print "CHILD is exiting\n";
    exit(7);
}

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the return code of a terminated child

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the return code of a terminated child. This function is only useful if pcntl_wifexited returned true.

listitem.simpara: The status parameter is the status parameter supplied to a successful call to pcntl_waitpid.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the return code. If the functionality is not supported by the OS, false is returned.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks whether the child process has continued from a job control stop

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Checks whether the child process which caused the return of pcntl_waitpid has continued from a job control stop. This function is only useful if the call to pcntl_waitpid was done using the WCONTINUED option.

listitem.simpara: The status parameter is the status parameter supplied to a successful call to pcntl_waitpid.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the child process which caused the return of pcntl_waitpid has continued from a job control stop, false otherwise.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks if status code represents a normal exit

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks whether the child status code represents a normal exit.

listitem.simpara: The status parameter is the status parameter supplied to a successful call to pcntl_waitpid.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the child status code represents a normal exit, false otherwise.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks whether the status code represents a termination due to a signal

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks whether the child process exited because of a signal which was not caught.

listitem.simpara: The status parameter is the status parameter supplied to a successful call to pcntl_waitpid.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the child process exited because of a signal which was not caught, false otherwise.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks whether the child process is currently stopped

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks whether the child process which caused the return is currently stopped; this is only possible if the call to pcntl_waitpid was done using the option WUNTRACED.

listitem.simpara: The status parameter is the status parameter supplied to a successful call to pcntl_waitpid.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the child process which caused the return is currently stopped, false otherwise.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the signal which caused the child to stop

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the number of the signal which caused the child to stop. This function is only useful if pcntl_wifstopped returned true.

listitem.simpara: The status parameter is the status parameter supplied to a successful call to pcntl_waitpid.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the signal number. If the functionality is not supported by the OS, false is returned.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the signal which caused the child to terminate

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the number of the signal that caused the child process to terminate. This function is only useful if pcntl_wifsignaled returned true.

listitem.simpara: The status parameter is the status parameter supplied to a successful call to pcntl_waitpid.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the signal number. If the functionality is not supported by the OS, false is returned.

preface.title: Introduction
preface.para: This module contains an interface to those functions defined in the IEEE 1003.1 (POSIX.1) standards document which are not accessible through other means.

warning.para: Sensitive data can be retrieved with the POSIX functions, e.g. posix_getpwnam and friends.

note.simpara: This extension is not available on Windows platforms.

section.title: Installation
section.para: This extension is enabled by default. It may be disabled by using the following option at compile time: --disable-posix

appendix.title: Predefined Constants
appendix.simpara: The constants below are defined by this extension, and will only be available when the extension has either been compiled into PHP or dynamically loaded at runtime.

note.para: Please note that some of these constants may not be available on every system.

listitem.simpara: Check whether the file exists.
Check whether the file exists and has read permissions.
Check whether the file exists and has write permissions.
Check whether the file exists and has execute permissions.

note.para: Please note that some of them may not be available on your system.

listitem.simpara: Block special file
Character special file
FIFO (named pipe) special file
Normal file
Socket

note.para: Please note that some of them may not be available on your system.

You may wish to read the below notes in conjunction with the manpage for setrlimit on your specific operating system, as there is variance in how these limits are interpreted, even across operating systems that claim to implement POSIX in full.

listitem.simpara: The maximum size of the process's address space in bytes. See also PHP's memory_limit configuration directive.
The maximum size of a core file. If the limit is set to 0, no core file will be generated.

The maximum amount of CPU time that the process can use, in seconds. When the soft limit is hit, a SIGXCPU signal will be sent, which can be caught with pcntl_signal. Depending on the operating system, additional SIGXCPU signals may be sent each second until the hard limit is hit, at which point an uncatchable SIGKILL signal is sent.
See also set_time_limit.
The maximum size of the process's data segment, in bytes. It is extremely unlikely that this will have any effect on the execution of PHP unless an extension is in use that calls brk or sbrk.
The maximum size of files that the process can create, in bytes.
The maximum number of locks that the process can create. This is only supported on extremely old Linux kernels.
The maximum number of bytes that can be locked into memory.

The maximum number of bytes that can be allocated for POSIX message queues. PHP does not ship with support for POSIX message queues, so this limit will not have any effect unless you are using an extension that implements that support.
The maximum value to which the process can be reniced to. The value that will be used will be 20 - limit, as resource limit values cannot be negative.
A value one greater than the maximum file descriptor number that can be opened by this process.
The maximum number of processes (and/or threads, on some operating systems) that can be created for the real user ID of the process.
The maximum size of the process's resident set, in pages.
The maximum real time priority that can be set via the sched_setscheduler and sched_setparam system calls.
The maximum amount of CPU time, in microseconds, that the process can consume without making a blocking system call if it is using real time scheduling.
The maximum number of signals that can be queued for the real user ID of the process.
The maximum size of the process stack, in bytes.
Used to indicate an infinite value for a resource limit.
The maximum number of kqueues this user id is allowed to create (FreeBSD). Available as of PHP 8.1.0.
The maximum number of pseudo-terminals this user id is allowed to create (FreeBSD). Available as of PHP 8.1.0.
The maximum number of links a given file or directory can have. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
The maximum number of bytes in a terminal canonical input buffer (pathname being then a character special file). Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
The maximum number of bytes of a terminal input queue (pathname being then a character special file). Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
The maximum number of characters for a file name alone, not its path. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
The maximum number of characters for a full path name. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
The maximum number of bytes that can be written to a pipe in one operation. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
If privileges are required to be allow chown to work. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
If a file name (or files under a directory) is longer than POSIX_PC_NAME_MAX. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
The minimum number of bytes of storage allocated for any portion of a file. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
The maximum number of symbolic links a given file or directory can have. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
The maximum number of bytes in a symbolic link. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
The maximum number of bytes the arguments (and environment variables) can have. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
The number of bytes of the current page. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
The number of cpus configured system wise. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
The number of cpus currently active system wise. Available as of PHP 8.3.0.
The maximum number of simultaneous processes per user. Available as of PHP 8.4.0.
The number of clock ticks per second. Available as of PHP 8.4.0.

partintro.title: See Also
partintro.para: The section about Process Control Functions maybe of interest for you.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Determine accessibility of a file

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: posix_access checks the user's permission of a file.

listitem.para: The name of the file to be tested.
A mask consisting of one or more of POSIX_F_OK, POSIX_R_OK, POSIX_W_OK and POSIX_X_OK.

POSIX_R_OK, POSIX_W_OK and POSIX_X_OK request checking whether the file exists and has read, write and execute permissions, respectively. POSIX_F_OK just requests checking for the existence of the file.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: posix_access example
example.para: This example will check if the $file is readable and writable, otherwise will print an error message.
example.programlisting:
<?php

$file = 'some_file';

if (posix_access($file, POSIX_R_OK | POSIX_W_OK)) {
    echo 'The file is readable and writable!';

} else {
    $error = posix_get_last_error();

    echo "Error $error: " . posix_strerror($error);
}

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get path name of controlling terminal

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Generates a string which is the pathname for the current controlling terminal for the process. On error this will set errno, which can be checked using posix_get_last_error

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Upon successful completion, returns string of the pathname to the current controlling terminal. Otherwise false is returned and errno is set, which can be checked with posix_get_last_error.

example.title: posix_ctermid example
example.para: This example will display the path to the current TTY.
example.programlisting:
<?php
echo "I am running from ".posix_ctermid();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Determine accessibility of a file

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: posix_eaccess checks the effective user's permission of a file

listitem.para: The name of a file to be tested.
A mask consisting of one or more of POSIX_F_OK, POSIX_R_OK, POSIX_W_OK and POSIX_X_OK.

POSIX_R_OK, POSIX_W_OK and POSIX_X_OK request checking whether the file exists and has read, write and execute permissions, respectively. POSIX_F_OK just requests checking for the existence of the file.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: Checks the effective user/group for a file, differing from posix_access which checks from the real user/group.

example.title: posix_eaccess example
example.para: This example will check if the $file is readable and writable, otherwise will print an error message.
example.programlisting:
<?php

$file = 'some_file';

if (posix_eaccess($file, POSIX_R_OK | POSIX_W_OK)) {
    echo 'The file is readable and writable!';

} else {
    $error = posix_get_last_error();

    echo "Error $error: " . posix_strerror($error);
}

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of posix_get_last_error

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: posix_get_last_error.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the value of a configurable limit

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the value of a configurable limit from name for file_descriptor.

listitem.simpara: The file descriptor, which is expected to be either a file resource or an int. An int will be assumed to be a file descriptor that can be passed directly to the underlying system call.

listitem.para: The name of the configurable limit, one of the following. POSIX_PC_LINK_MAX, POSIX_PC_MAX_CANON, POSIX_PC_MAX_INPUT, POSIX_PC_NAME_MAX, POSIX_PC_PATH_MAX, POSIX_PC_PIPE_BUF, POSIX_PC_CHOWN_RESTRICTED, POSIX_PC_NO_TRUNC, POSIX_PC_ALLOC_SIZE_MIN, POSIX_PC_SYMLINK_MAX.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the configurable limit or false.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: Throws a ValueError when resource is invalid.

row.entry: Now sets last_error to EBADF and raises an E_WARNING when an invalid file descriptor is encountered.

example.title: posix_fpathconf example
example.para: This example will get the max path name's length in bytes for the current dir.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$fd = fopen(__DIR__, "r");
echo posix_fpathconf($fd, POSIX_PC_PATH_MAX);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve the error number set by the last posix function that failed

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Retrieve the error number set by the last posix function that failed. The system error message associated with the errno may be checked with posix_strerror.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the errno (error number) set by the last posix function that failed. If no errors exist, 0 is returned.

example.title: posix_get_last_error example
example.para: This example attempt to kill a bogus process id, which will set the last error. We will then print out the last errno.
example.programlisting: <?php posix_kill(999459,SIGKILL); echo 'Your error returned was '.posix_get_last_error(); //Your error was ___ ?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Pathname of current directory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets the absolute pathname of the script's current working directory. On error, it sets errno which can be checked using posix_get_last_error

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a string of the absolute pathname on success. On error, returns false and sets errno which can be checked with posix_get_last_error.

example.title: posix_getcwd example
example.para: This example will return the absolute path of the current working directory of the script.
example.programlisting:
<?php
echo 'My current working directory is '.posix_getcwd();
?>

note.para:
This function can fail on
Read or Search permission was denied
Pathname no longer exists

refnamediv.refpurpose: Return the effective group ID of the current process

refsect1.para: Return the numeric effective group ID of the current process.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns an int of the effective group ID.

example.title: posix_getegid example
example.para: This example will print out the effective group id, once it is changed with posix_setegid.
example.programlisting: <?php echo 'My real group id is '.posix_getgid(); //20 posix_setegid(40); echo 'My real group id is '.posix_getgid(); //20 echo 'My effective group id is '.posix_getegid(); //40 ?>

refsect1.title: Notes
refsect1.para: posix_getegid is different than posix_getgid because effective group ID can be changed by a calling process using posix_setegid.

refsect1.simpara: Return the numeric effective user ID of the current process. See also posix_getpwuid for information on how to convert this into a usable username.

refsect1.title: Return Values

example.title: posix_geteuid example
example.para: This example will show the current user id then set the effective user id to a separate id using posix_seteuid, then show the difference between the real id and the effective id.

<?php echo posix_getuid()."
"; //10001 echo posix_geteuid()."
"; //10001 posix_seteuid(10000); echo posix_getuid()."

"; //10000 ?>

example.programlisting: <?php echo 'My real group id is '.posix_getgid(); //20 posix_setegid(40); echo 'My real group id is '.posix_getgid(); //20 echo 'My effective group id is '.posix_getegid(); //40 ?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Return info about a group by group id

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets information about a group provided its id.

listitem.para: The group id.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para:
The array elements returned are:
The group information array
Element Description
name
The name element contains the name of the group. This is a short, usually less than 16 character "handle" of the group, not the real, full name.
passwd
The passwd element contains the group's password in an encrypted format. Often, for example on a system employing "shadow" passwords, an asterisk is returned instead.
gid
Group ID, should be the same as the group_id parameter used when calling the function, and hence redundant.
members
This consists of an array of string's for all the members in the group.
The function returns false on failure.

example.title: Example use of posix_getgrgid
example.programlisting:
<?php

$groupid   = posix_getegid();
$groupinfo = posix_getgrgid($groupid);

print_r($groupinfo);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: Array ( [name] => toons [passwd] => x [members] => Array ( [0] => tom [1] => jerry ) [gid] => 42 )

passwd

gid

members
This consists of an array of string's for all the members in the group.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Return info about a user by username

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns an array of information about the given user.

listitem.para: An alphanumeric username.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para:
On success an array with the following elements is returned, else false is returned:
The user information array
Element Description
name
The name element contains the username of the user. This is a short, usually less than 16 character "handle" of the user, not the real, full name. This should be the same as the username parameter used when calling the function, and hence redundant.
passwd
The passwd element contains the user's password in an encrypted format. Often, for example on a system employing "shadow" passwords, an asterisk is returned instead.
uid
User ID of the user in numeric form.
gid
The group ID of the user. Use the function posix_getgrgid to resolve the group name and a list of its members.
gecos
GECOS is an obsolete term that refers to the finger information field on a Honeywell batch processing system. The field, however, lives on, and its contents have been formalized by POSIX. The field contains a comma separated list containing the user's full name, office phone, office number, and home phone number. On most systems, only the user's full name is available.
dir
This element contains the absolute path to the home directory of the user.
shell
The shell element contains the absolute path to the executable of the user's default shell.

example.title: Example use of posix_getpwnam
example.programlisting:
<?php

$userinfo = posix_getpwnam("tom");

print_r($userinfo);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

Element Description
name

passwd
The passwd element contains the user's password in an encrypted format. Often, for example on a system employing "shadow" passwords, an asterisk is returned instead.
uid
User ID, should be the same as the user_id parameter used when calling the function, and hence redundant.
gid
The group ID of the user. Use the function posix_getgrgid to resolve the group name and a list of its members.
gecos
GECOS is an obsolete term that refers to the finger information field on a Honeywell batch processing system. The field, however, lives on, and its contents have been formalized by POSIX. The field contains a comma separated list containing the user's full name, office phone, office number, and home phone number. On most systems, only the user's full name is available.
dir
This element contains the absolute path to the home directory of the user.
shell
The shell element contains the absolute path to the executable of the user's default shell.
The function returns false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Return info about system resource limits

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: posix_getrlimit returns an array of information about the current resource's soft and hard limits.
refsect1.simpara: Each resource has an associated soft and hard limit. The soft limit is the value that the kernel enforces for the corresponding resource. The hard limit acts as a ceiling for the soft limit. An unprivileged process may only set its soft limit to a value from 0 to the hard limit, and irreversibly lower its hard limit.

listitem.para: If null, all current resource limits will be returned. Otherwise, specify the resource limit constant to retrieve a specific limit.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para:
Returns an associative array of elements for each limit that is defined. Each limit has a soft and a hard limit.
List of possible limits returned
Limit name Limit description
core
The maximum size of the core file. When 0, not core files are created. When core files are larger than this size, they will be truncated at this size.
totalmem
The maximum size of the memory of the process, in bytes.
virtualmem
The maximum size of the virtual memory for the process, in bytes.
data
The maximum size of the data segment for the process, in bytes.
stack
The maximum size of the process stack, in bytes.
rss
The maximum number of virtual pages resident in RAM
maxproc
The maximum number of processes that can be created for the real user ID of the calling process.
memlock
The maximum number of bytes of memory that may be locked into RAM.
cpu
The amount of time the process is allowed to use the CPU.
filesize
The maximum size of the data segment for the process, in bytes.
openfiles
One more than the maximum number of open file descriptors.
The function returns false on failure.

row.entry: The optional resource parameter has been added.

example.title: Example use of posix_getrlimit
example.programlisting:
<?php

$limits = posix_getrlimit();

print_r($limits);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: Array ( [soft core] => 0 [hard core] => unlimited [soft data] => unlimited [hard data] => unlimited [soft stack] => 8388608 [hard stack] => unlimited [soft totalmem] => unlimited [hard totalmem] => unlimited [soft rss] => unlimited [hard rss] => unlimited [soft maxproc] => unlimited [hard maxproc] => unlimited [soft memlock] => unlimited [hard memlock] => unlimited [soft cpu] => unlimited [hard cpu] => unlimited [soft filesize] => unlimited [hard filesize] => unlimited [soft openfiles] => 1024 [hard openfiles] => 1024 )

refnamediv.refpurpose: Determine if a file descriptor is an interactive terminal

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Determines if the file descriptor file_descriptor refers to a valid terminal type device.

listitem.simpara: The file descriptor, which is expected to be either a file resource or an int. An int will be assumed to be a file descriptor that can be passed directly to the underlying system call.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if file_descriptor is an open descriptor connected to a terminal and false otherwise.

row.entry: Now raises an E_WARNING when an invalid file_descriptor is encountered.
Set errno (error number) to EBADF when the file descriptor/stream passed is invalid.
Type error E_WARNINGs are now raised for integer coercions following the usual PHP type coercion semantics.

refsect1.title: Return Values

row.entry: Now throws a ValueError when process_id is lower or greater than what the platform supports (signed integer or long range).

simplelist.member: The kill(2) manual page of the POSIX system, which contains additional information about negative process identifiers, the special pid 0, the special pid -1, and the signal number 0.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Create a fifo special file (a named pipe)

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: posix_mkfifo creates a special FIFO file which exists in the file system and acts as a bidirectional communication endpoint for processes.

listitem.para: Path to the FIFO file.

The second parameter permissions has to be given in octal notation (e.g. 0644). The permission of the newly created FIFO also depends on the setting of the current umask. The permissions of the created file are (mode & ~umask).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Create a special or ordinary file (POSIX.1)

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Creates a special or ordinary file.

listitem.para: The file to create
This parameter is constructed by a bitwise OR between file type (one of the following constants: POSIX_S_IFREG, POSIX_S_IFCHR, POSIX_S_IFBLK, POSIX_S_IFIFO or POSIX_S_IFSOCK) and permissions.
The major device kernel identifier (required to pass when using S_IFCHR or S_IFBLK).
The minor device kernel identifier.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: A posix_mknod example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$file = '/tmp/tmpfile';  // file name
$type = POSIX_S_IFBLK;   // file type
$permissions = 0777;     // octal
$major = 1;
$minor = 8;              // /dev/random

if (!posix_mknod($file, $type | $permissions, $major, $minor)) {
    die('Error ' . posix_get_last_error() . ': ' . posix_strerror(posix_get_last_error()));
}

?>
