refnamediv.refpurpose: Create or open shared memory block

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: shmop_open can create or open a shared memory block.

listitem.simpara: System's id for the shared memory block. Can be passed as a decimal or hex.

listitem.para:
The flags that you can use:
"a" for access (sets SHM_RDONLY for shmat) use this flag when you need to open an existing shared memory segment for read only
"c" for create (sets IPC_CREATE) use this flag when you need to create a new shared memory segment or if a segment with the same key exists, try to open it for read and write
"w" for read & write access use this flag when you need to read and write to a shared memory segment, use this flag in most cases.
"n" create a new memory segment (sets IPC_CREATE|IPC_EXCL) use this flag when you want to create a new shared memory segment but if one already exists with the same flag, fail. This is useful for security purposes, using this you can prevent race condition exploits.

listitem.simpara: The permissions that you wish to assign to your memory segment, those are the same as permission for a file. Permissions need to be passed in octal form, like for example 0644
The size of the shared memory block you wish to create in bytes

note.simpara: Note: the 3rd and 4th should be entered as 0 if you are opening an existing memory segment.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: On success shmop_open will return a Shmop instance that you can use to access the shared memory segment you've created. false is returned on failure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: If mode is invalid, or size is less than or equal to zero, a ValueError is thrown. On other failures, E_WARNING is emitted.

row.entry: On success, this function returns an Shmop instance now; previously, a resource was returned.
If mode is invalid, or size is less than or equal to zero, a ValueError is thrown; previously E_WARNING was emitted instead, and the function returned false.

refsect1.title: Examples

example.title: Create a new shared memory block
example.programlisting:
<?php
$shm_key = ftok(__FILE__, 't');
$shm_id = shmop_open($shm_key, "c", 0644, 100);
?>

refsect1.simpara: This example opened a shared memory block with a system id returned by ftok.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: shmop_read will read a string from shared memory block.

listitem.simpara: The shared memory block identifier created by shmop_open
Offset from which to start reading; must be greater than or equal to zero and less than or equal to the actual size of the shared memory segment.

The number of bytes to read; must be greater than or equal to zero, and the sum of offset and size must be less than or equal to the actual size of the shared memory segment. 0 reads shmop_size($shmid) - $start bytes.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the data.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: If offset or size are out of range, a ValueError is thrown.

row.entry: shmop expects a Shmop instance now; previously, a resource was expected.
If offset or size are out of range, a ValueError is thrown; previously E_WARNING was emitted, and false was returned,

?>

refsect1.simpara: This example will read 50 bytes from shared memory block and place the data inside $shm_data.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: shmop_size is used to get the size, in bytes of the shared memory block.

listitem.simpara: The shared memory block identifier created by shmop_open

refsect1.simpara: Returns an int, which represents the number of bytes the shared memory block occupies.

refsect1.simpara: shmop_write will write a string into shared memory block.

listitem.simpara: The shared memory block identifier created by shmop_open
A string to write into shared memory block
Specifies where to start writing data inside the shared memory segment. The offset must be greater than or equal to zero and less than or equal to the actual size of the shared memory segment.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The size of the written data.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: If offset is out of range, or a read-only shared memory segment should be written to, a ValueError is thrown.

preface.title: Introduction
preface.simpara: The sync extension introduces cross-platform synchronization objects into PHP. Named and unnamed Mutex, Semaphore, Event, Reader-Writer, and named Shared Memory objects provide OS-level synchronization on both POSIX (e.g. Linux) and Windows platforms.

Automatic cleanup of acquired synchronization objects takes place during extension teardown. This means that if PHP prematurely terminates a script (e.g. script execution time is exceeded), objects will not be left in an unknown state. The only exception to this is if PHP itself crashes (e.g. an internal buffer overflow).
Unnamed synchronization objects don't have a lot of use outside of a multithreaded scenario. Unnamed objects are more useful in conjunction with the pthreads PECL extension.

note.simpara: Named objects require additional care to be used on all systems. If an object is instantiated with a specific set of parameters, it must always be instantiated with those parameters or the object will probably end up in an inconsistent state until the next reboot or a system administrator cleans up the mess.

section.title: Requirements
section.simpara: A system with support for POSIX shared memory (shm_open()) or running Windows.

section.title: Installation
section.simpara: Information for installing this PECL extension may be found in the manual chapter titled Installation of PECL extensions. Additional information such as new releases, downloads, source files, maintainer information, and a CHANGELOG, can be located here: https://pecl.php.net/package/sync.

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: A cross-platform, native implementation of named and unnamed countable mutex objects.

A mutex is a mutual exclusion object that restricts access to a shared resource (e.g. a file) to a single instance. Countable mutexes acquire the mutex a single time and internally track the number of times the mutex is locked. The mutex is unlocked as soon as it goes out of scope or is unlocked the same number of times that it was locked.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Constructs a new SyncMutex object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Constructs a named or unnamed countable mutex.

listitem.simpara: The name of the mutex if this is a named mutex object.

note.simpara: If the name already exists, it must be able to be opened by the current user that the process is running as or an exception will be thrown with a meaningless error message.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The new SyncMutex object.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: An exception is thrown if the mutex cannot be created or opened.

example.title: SyncMutex::__construct named mutex with lock timeout example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$mutex = new SyncMutex("UniqueName");

if (!$mutex->lock(3000))
{
    echo "Unable to lock mutex.";

    exit();
}

/* ... */

$mutex->unlock();
?>

example.title: SyncMutex::__construct unnamed mutex example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$mutex = new SyncMutex();

$mutex->lock();

/* ... */

$mutex->unlock();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Waits for an exclusive lock

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Obtains an exclusive lock on a SyncMutex object. If the lock is already acquired, then this increments an internal counter.

listitem.simpara: The number of milliseconds to wait for the exclusive lock. A value of -1 is infinite.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: SyncMutex::lock example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$mutex = new SyncMutex("UniqueName");

if (!$mutex->lock(3000))
{
    echo "Unable to lock mutex.";

    exit();
}

/* ... */

$mutex->unlock();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Unlocks the mutex

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Decreases the internal counter of a SyncMutex object. When the internal counter reaches zero, the actual lock on the object is released.

listitem.simpara: Specifies whether or not to set the internal counter to zero and therefore release the lock.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: SyncMutex::unlock example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$mutex = new SyncMutex("UniqueName");

$mutex->lock();

/* ... */

$mutex->unlock();
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: A cross-platform, native implementation of named and unnamed semaphore objects.

A semaphore restricts access to a limited resource to a limited number of instances. Semaphores differ from mutexes in that they can allow more than one instance to access a resource at one time while a mutex only allows one instance at a time.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Constructs a new SyncSemaphore object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Constructs a named or unnamed semaphore.

listitem.simpara: The name of the semaphore if this is a named semaphore object.

note.simpara: If the name already exists, it must be able to be opened by the current user that the process is running as or an exception will be thrown with a meaningless error message.

listitem.simpara: The initial value of the semaphore. This is the number of locks that may be obtained.
Specifies whether or not to automatically unlock the semaphore at the conclusion of the PHP script.

warning.simpara: If an object is: A named semaphore with an autounlock of false, the object is locked, and the PHP script concludes before the object is unlocked, then the underlying semaphore will end up in an inconsistent state.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The new SyncSemaphore object.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: An exception is thrown if the semaphore cannot be created or opened.

example.title: SyncSemaphore::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$semaphore = new SyncSemaphore("LimitedResource_2clients", 2);

if (!$semaphore->lock(3000))
{
    echo "Unable to lock semaphore.";

    exit();
}

/* ... */

$semaphore->unlock();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Decreases the count of the semaphore or waits

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Decreases the count of a SyncSemaphore object or waits until the semaphore becomes non-zero.

listitem.simpara: The number of milliseconds to wait for the semaphore. A value of -1 is infinite.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: SyncSemaphore::lock example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$semaphore = new SyncSemaphore("LimitedResource_2clients", 2);

if (!$semaphore->lock(3000))
{
    echo "Unable to lock semaphore.";

    exit();
}

/* ... */

$semaphore->unlock();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Increases the count of the semaphore

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Increases the count of a SyncSemaphore object.

listitem.simpara: Returns the previous count of the semaphore.

example.title: SyncSemaphore::unlock example

$semaphore = new SyncSemaphore("LimitedResource_2clients", 2);

if (!$semaphore->lock(3000))

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: A cross-platform, native implementation of named and unnamed event objects. Both automatic and manual event objects are supported.

An event object waits, without polling, for the object to be fired/set. One instance waits on the event object while another instance fires/sets the event. Event objects are useful wherever a long-running process would otherwise poll a resource (e.g. checking to see if uploaded data needs to be processed).

refnamediv.refpurpose: Constructs a new SyncEvent object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Constructs a named or unnamed event object.

listitem.simpara: The name of the event if this is a named event object.

note.simpara: If the name already exists, it must be able to be opened by the current user that the process is running as or an exception will be thrown with a meaningless error message.

listitem.simpara: Specifies whether or not the event object must be reset manually.

note.simpara: Manual reset event objects allow all waiting processes through until the object is reset.

listitem.simpara: Specifies whether or not to prefire (signal) the event object.

note.simpara: Only has impact if the calling process/thread is the first to create the object.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The new SyncEvent object.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: An exception is thrown if the event object cannot be created or opened.

example.title: SyncEvent::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// In a web application:
$event = new SyncEvent("GetAppReport");
$event->fire();

// In a cron job:
$event = new SyncEvent("GetAppReport");
$event->wait();
?>

entry.simpara: Added prefire.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Fires/sets the event

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Fires/sets a SyncEvent object. Lets multiple threads through that are waiting if the event object was created with a manual value of true.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: SyncEvent::fire example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// In a web application:
$event = new SyncEvent("GetAppReport");
$event->fire();

// In a cron job:
$event = new SyncEvent("GetAppReport");
$event->wait();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Resets a manual event

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Resets a SyncEvent object that has been fired/set. Only valid for manual event objects.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: SyncEvent::reset example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// In a web application:
$event = new SyncEvent("DemoApplication", true);
$event->wait();

// In a cron job:
$event = new SyncEvent("DemoApplication", true);
$event->reset();
/* ... Do some maintenance task(s) ... */
$event->fire();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Waits for the event to be fired/set

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Waits for the SyncEvent object to be fired.

listitem.simpara: The number of milliseconds to wait for the event to be fired. A value of -1 is infinite.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: SyncEvent::wait example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// In a web application:
$event = new SyncEvent("GetAppReport");
$event->fire();

// In a cron job:
$event = new SyncEvent("GetAppReport");
$event->wait();
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: A cross-platform, native implementation of named and unnamed reader-writer objects.

A reader-writer object allows many readers or one writer to access a resource. This is an efficient solution for managing resources where access will primarily be read-only but exclusive write access is occasionally necessary.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Constructs a new SyncReaderWriter object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Constructs a named or unnamed reader-writer object.

listitem.simpara: The name of the reader-writer if this is a named reader-writer object.

note.simpara: If the name already exists, it must be able to be opened by the current user that the process is running as or an exception will be thrown with a meaningless error message.
On Windows, name must not contain backslashes.

listitem.simpara: Specifies whether or not to automatically unlock the reader-writer at the conclusion of the PHP script.

warning.simpara: If an object is: A named reader-writer with an autounlock of FALSE, the object is locked for either reading or writing, and the PHP script concludes before the object is unlocked, then the underlying objects will end up in an inconsistent state.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The new SyncReaderWriter object.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: An exception is thrown if the reader-writer cannot be created or opened.

example.title: SyncReaderWriter::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$readwrite = new SyncReaderWriter("FileCacheLock");
$readwrite->readlock();
/* ... */
$readwrite->readunlock();

$readwrite->writelock();
/* ... */
$readwrite->writeunlock();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Waits for a read lock

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Obtains a read lock on a SyncReaderWriter object.

listitem.simpara: The number of milliseconds to wait for a lock. A value of -1 is infinite.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: SyncReaderWriter::readlock example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$readwrite = new SyncReaderWriter("FileCacheLock");
$readwrite->readlock();
/* ... */
$readwrite->readunlock();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Releases a read lock

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Releases a read lock on a SyncReaderWriter object.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: SyncReaderWriter::readunlock example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$readwrite = new SyncReaderWriter("FileCacheLock");
$readwrite->readlock();
/* ... */
$readwrite->readunlock();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Waits for an exclusive write lock

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Obtains an exclusive write lock on a SyncReaderWriter object.

listitem.simpara: The number of milliseconds to wait for a lock. A value of -1 is infinite.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: SyncReaderWriter::writelock example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$readwrite = new SyncReaderWriter("FileCacheLock");
$readwrite->writelock();
/* ... */
$readwrite->writeunlock();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Releases a write lock

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Releases a write lock on a SyncReaderWriter object.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: SyncReaderWriter::writeunlock example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$readwrite = new SyncReaderWriter("FileCacheLock");
$readwrite->writelock();
/* ... */
$readwrite->writeunlock();
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: A cross-platform, native, consistent implementation of named shared memory objects.

Shared memory lets two separate processes communicate without the need for complex pipes or sockets. There are several integer-based shared memory implementations for PHP. Named shared memory is an alternative.
Synchronization objects (e.g. SyncMutex) are still required to protect most uses of shared memory.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Constructs a new SyncSharedMemory object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Constructs a named shared memory object.

listitem.simpara: The name of the shared memory object.

note.simpara: If the name already exists, it must be able to be opened by the current user that the process is running as or an exception will be thrown with a meaningless error message.

listitem.simpara: The size, in bytes, of shared memory to reserve.

note.simpara: The amount of memory cannot be resized later. Request sufficient storage up front.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The new SyncSharedMemory object.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: An exception is thrown if the shared memory object cannot be created or opened.

example.title: SyncSharedMemory::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// You will probably need to protect shared memory with other synchronization objects.
// Shared memory goes away when the last reference to it disappears.
$mem = new SyncSharedMemory("AppReportName", 1024);
if ($mem->first())
{
    // Do first time initialization work here.
}

$result = $mem->write(json_encode(array("name" => "my_report.txt")));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check to see if the object is the first instance system-wide of named shared memory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieves the system-wide first instance status of a SyncSharedMemory object.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: SyncSharedMemory::first example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$mem = new SyncSharedMemory("AppReportName", 1024);
if ($mem->first())
{
    // Do first time initialization work here.
}

var_dump($mem->first());

$mem2 = new SyncSharedMemory("AppReportName", 1024);

var_dump($mem2->first());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Copy data from named shared memory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Copies data from named shared memory.

listitem.simpara: The start/offset, in bytes, to begin reading.

note.simpara: If the value is negative, the starting position will begin at the specified number of bytes from the end of the shared memory segment.

listitem.simpara: The number of bytes to read.

note.simpara: If unspecified, reading will stop at the end of the shared memory segment.
If the value is negative, reading will stop the specified number of bytes from the end of the shared memory segment.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: A string containing the data read from shared memory.

example.title: SyncSharedMemory::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// You will probably need to protect shared memory with other synchronization objects.
// Shared memory goes away when the last reference to it disappears.
$mem = new SyncSharedMemory("AppReportName", 1024);
if ($mem->first())
{
    // Do first time initialization work here.
}

$result = $mem->write("report.txt");

$result = $mem->read(3, -4);
var_dump($result);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the size of the named shared memory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieves the shared memory size of a SyncSharedMemory object.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: An integer containing the size of the shared memory. This will be the same size that was passed to the constructor.

example.title: SyncSharedMemory::size example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$mem = new SyncSharedMemory("AppReportName", 1024);
var_dump($mem->size());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Copy data to named shared memory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Copies data to named shared memory.

listitem.simpara: The data to write to shared memory.

note.simpara: If the size of the data exceeds the size of the shared memory, the number of bytes written returned will be less than the length of the input.

listitem.simpara: The start/offset, in bytes, to begin writing.

note.simpara: If the value is negative, the starting position will begin at the specified number of bytes from the end of the shared memory segment.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: An integer containing the number of bytes written to shared memory.

example.title: SyncSharedMemory::write example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// You will probably need to protect shared memory with other synchronization objects.
// Shared memory goes away when the last reference to it disappears.
$mem = new SyncSharedMemory("AppReportName", 1024);
if ($mem->first())
{
    // Do first time initialization work here.
}

$result = $mem->write("report.txt");
var_dump($result);

$result = $mem->write("report.txt", -3);
var_dump($result);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

preface.title: Introduction
preface.simpara: The GeoIP extension allows you to find the location of an IP address. City, State, Country, Longitude, Latitude, and other information as all, such as ISP and connection type can be obtained with the help of GeoIP.

warning.simpara: This extension does not support MaxMind's current "GeoIP2" databases, only the "GeoIP legacy" database files.

section.title: Requirements
section.simpara: This extension requires the GeoIP C library version 1.4.0 or higher to be installed. You can grab the latest version from http://www.maxmind.com/app/c and compile it yourself.
By default, you will only have access to the Free GeoIP Country or GeoLite City databases. While this module can work with other types of database, you must buy a commercial license from Maxmind.

section.title: Installation
section.simpara: This PECL extension is not bundled with PHP.

Information for installing this PECL extension may be found in the manual chapter titled Installation of PECL extensions. Additional information such as new releases, downloads, source files, maintainer information, and a CHANGELOG, can be located here: https://pecl.php.net/package/geoip.

section.title: Runtime Configuration
section.simpara: The behaviour of these functions is affected by settings in php.ini.
Here's a short explanation of the configuration directives.

listitem.simpara: Empty by default, but can be set to force a different database path than the one compiled in the library.

appendix.title: Predefined Constants
appendix.simpara: The constants below are defined by this extension, and will only be available when the extension has either been compiled into PHP or dynamically loaded at runtime.
The following constants are for net speed:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the Autonomous System Numbers (ASN)

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_asnum_by_name function will return the Autonomous System Numbers (ASN) associated with an IP address.

listitem.simpara: The hostname or IP address.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the ASN on success, or false if the address cannot be found in the database.

example.title: A geoip_asnum_by_name example
example.simpara: This will output the ASN of the host www.example.com.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$asn = geoip_asnum_by_name('www.example.com');

if ($asn) {
    echo 'The ASN is: ' . $asn;
}
?>
example.screen: The ASN is: AS15133 EdgeCast Networks, Inc

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the two letter continent code

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_continent_code_by_name function will return the two letter continent code corresponding to a hostname or an IP address.

listitem.simpara: The hostname or IP address whose location is to be looked-up.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the two letter continent code on success, or false if the address cannot be found in the database.

example.title: A geoip_continent_code_by_name example
example.simpara: This will print where the host example.com is located.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$continent = geoip_continent_code_by_name('www.example.com');
if ($continent) {
    echo 'This host is located in: ' . $continent;
}
?>
example.screen: This host is located in: NA

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the two letter country code

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_country_code_by_name function will return the two letter country code corresponding to a hostname or an IP address.

listitem.simpara: The hostname or IP address whose location is to be looked-up.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the two letter ISO country code on success, or false if the address cannot be found in the database.

example.title: A geoip_country_code_by_name example
example.simpara: This will print where the host example.com is located.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$country = geoip_country_code_by_name('www.example.com');
if ($country) {
    echo 'This host is located in: ' . $country;
}
?>
example.screen: This host is located in: US

caution.simpara: Please see http://www.maxmind.com/en/iso3166 for a complete list of possible return values, including special codes.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_country_code3_by_name function will return the three letter country code corresponding to a hostname or an IP address.

listitem.simpara: The hostname or IP address whose location is to be looked-up.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the three letter country code on success, or false if the address cannot be found in the database.

example.title: A geoip_country_code3_by_name example
example.simpara: This will print where the host example.com is located.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$country = geoip_country_code3_by_name('www.example.com');

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the full country name

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_country_name_by_name function will return the full country name corresponding to a hostname or an IP address.

listitem.simpara: The hostname or IP address whose location is to be looked-up.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the country name on success, or false if the address cannot be found in the database.

example.title: A geoip_country_name_by_name example
example.simpara: This will print where the host example.com is located.
example.programlisting:

$country = geoip_country_name_by_name('www.example.com');

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get GeoIP Database information

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_database_info function returns the corresponding GeoIP Database version as it is defined inside the binary file.
If this function is called without arguments, it returns the version of the GeoIP Free Country Edition.

listitem.simpara: The database type as an integer. You can use the various constants defined with this extension (ie: GEOIP_*_EDITION).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the corresponding database version, or null on error.

example.title: A geoip_database_info example
example.simpara: This will output information regarding the database.
example.programlisting:
<?php
print geoip_database_info(GEOIP_COUNTRY_EDITION);
?>
example.screen: GEO-106FREE 20060801 Build 1 Copyright (c) 2006 MaxMind LLC All Rights Reserved

refnamediv.refpurpose: Determine if GeoIP Database is available

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_db_avail function returns if the corresponding GeoIP Database is available and can be opened on disk.
It does not indicate if the file is a proper database, only if it is readable.

listitem.simpara: The database type as an integer. You can use the various constants defined with this extension (ie: GEOIP_*_EDITION).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true is database exists, false if not found, or null on error.

example.title: A geoip_db_avail example
example.simpara: This will output the current database version string.
example.programlisting:
<?php

if (geoip_db_avail(GEOIP_COUNTRY_EDITION))
    print geoip_database_info(GEOIP_COUNTRY_EDITION);
?>
example.screen: GEO-106FREE 20080801 Build 1 Copyright (c) 2006 MaxMind LLC All Rights Reserved

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the filename of the corresponding GeoIP Database

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_db_filename function returns the filename of the corresponding GeoIP Database.
It does not indicate if the file exists or not on disk, only where the library is looking for the database.

listitem.simpara: The database type as an integer. You can use the various constants defined with this extension (ie: GEOIP_*_EDITION).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the filename of the corresponding database, or null on error.

example.title: A geoip_db_filename example
example.simpara: This will output the filename of the corresponding database.
example.programlisting:
<?php

print geoip_db_filename(GEOIP_COUNTRY_EDITION);

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns detailed information about all GeoIP database types

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_db_get_all_info function will return detailed information as a multi-dimensional array about all the GeoIP database types.
This function is available even if no databases are installed. It will simply list them as non-available.
The names of the different keys of the returning associative array are as follows:

listitem.simpara: "available" -- Boolean, indicate if DB is available (see geoip_db_avail)
"description" -- The database description
"filename" -- The database filename on disk (see geoip_db_filename)

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the associative array.

example.title: A geoip_db_get_all_info example
example.simpara: This will print the array containing all the information.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$infos = geoip_db_get_all_info();
if (is_array($infos)) {
    var_dump($infos);
}
?>

example.title: A geoip_db_get_all_info example
example.simpara: You can use the various constants as keys to get only parts of the information.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$infos = geoip_db_get_all_info();
if ($infos[GEOIP_COUNTRY_EDITION]['available']) {
    echo $infos[GEOIP_COUNTRY_EDITION]['description'];
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the second level domain name

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_domain_by_name function will return the second level domain names associated with a hostname or an IP address.
This function is currently only available to users who have bought a commercial GeoIP Domain Edition. A warning will be issued if the proper database cannot be located.

listitem.simpara: The hostname or IP address.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the domain name on success, or false if the address cannot be found in the database.

example.title: A geoip_domain_by_name example
example.simpara: This will output the domain associated with IP 61.106.139.1.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$domain = geoip_domain_by_name('61.106.139.1');

if ($domain) {
    echo 'The domain is: '. $domain;
}

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the Internet connection type

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_id_by_name function will return the Internet connection type corresponding to a hostname or an IP address.
The return value is numeric and can be compared to the following constants:

listitem.simpara: GEOIP_UNKNOWN_SPEED
GEOIP_DIALUP_SPEED
GEOIP_CABLEDSL_SPEED
GEOIP_CORPORATE_SPEED
The hostname or IP address whose connection type is to be looked-up.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the connection type.

example.title: A geoip_id_by_name example
example.simpara: This will output the connection type of the host example.com.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$netspeed = geoip_id_by_name('www.example.com');

echo 'The connection type is ';

switch ($netspeed) {
    case GEOIP_DIALUP_SPEED:
        echo 'dial-up';
        break;
    case GEOIP_CABLEDSL_SPEED:
        echo 'cable or DSL';
        break;
    case GEOIP_CORPORATE_SPEED:
        echo 'corporate';
        break;
    case GEOIP_UNKNOWN_SPEED:
    default:
        echo 'unknown';
}
?>

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_isp_by_name function will return the name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP) that an IP is assigned to.
This function is currently only available to users who have bought a commercial GeoIP ISP Edition. A warning will be issued if the proper database cannot be located.

This function is currently only available to users who have bought a commercial GeoIP Organization, ISP or AS Edition. A warning will be issued if the proper database cannot be located.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the organization name on success, or false if the address cannot be found in the database.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the detailed City information found in the GeoIP Database

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_record_by_name function will return the record information corresponding to a hostname or an IP address.
This function is available for both GeoLite City Edition and commercial GeoIP City Edition. A warning will be issued if the proper database cannot be located.
The names of the different keys of the returning associative array are as follows:

listitem.simpara: "continent_code" -- Two letter continent code (as of version 1.0.4 with libgeoip 1.4.3 or newer)
"country_code" -- Two letter country code (see geoip_country_code_by_name)
"country_code3" -- Three letter country code (see geoip_country_code3_by_name)
"country_name" -- The country name (see geoip_country_name_by_name)
"region" -- The region code (ex: CA for California)
"city" -- The city.
"postal_code" -- The Postal Code, FSA or Zip Code.
"latitude" -- The Latitude as signed float.
"longitude" -- The Longitude as signed float.
"dma_code" -- Designated Market Area code (USA and Canada only)
"area_code" -- The PSTN area code (ex: 212)

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The geoip_region_name_by_code function will return the region name corresponding to a country and region code combo.

In the United States, the region code corresponds to the two-letter abbreviation of each state. In Canada, the region code corresponds to the two-letter province or territory code as attributed by Canada Post.
For the rest of the world, GeoIP uses FIPS 10-4 codes to represent regions. You can check http://www.maxmind.com/app/fips10_4 for a detailed list of FIPS 10-4 codes.
This function is always available if using GeoIP Library version 1.4.1 or newer. The data is taken directly from the GeoIP Library and not from any database.

preface.title: Introduction
preface.para: PHP binding for FANN (Fast Artificial Neural Network) Library which implements multilayer artificial neural networks with support for both fully connected and sparsely connected networks. It includes a framework for easy handling of training data sets. It is easy to use, versatile, well documented, and fast.

section.title: Requirements
section.para: PHP >= 5.2.0 and libfann >= 2.1.0

section.title: Installation
section.para: The FANN PHP extension should work on all Linux systems.

section.title: FANN Library Installation
section.para: Before you start installation make sure that libfann is installed on your system. It's part of the main repository in the most Linux distributions (search for fann). You need a development version.

If it is not installed, you need to install it first. Either download it from the official site or get it from your distro repository. For example on Fedora:
$ sudo yum install fann-devel
or Ubuntu:
$ sudo apt-get install libfann-dev
If the library is re-installed manually, then all old library file should be removed before re-installing otherwise the old library version could be linked.

section.title: PECL Installation
section.para:
This extension is available on PECL. The installation is very simple. Just run:
$ sudo pecl install fann

section.title: Manual Installation
section.para:
For developers and people interested in the latest changes, you can compile the driver from the latest source code on Github. Go to Github and click the "Download ZIP" button. Then run:
$ unzip php-fann-master.zip $ cd php-fann-master $ phpize $ ./configure $ make all $ sudo make install
Make the following changes to php.ini:

listitem.para:
Make sure the extension_dir variable is pointing to the directory containing fann.so. The build will display where it is installing the PHP driver with output that looks something like:
Installing '/usr/lib/php/extensions/no-debug-non-zts-20060613/fann.so'
Make sure that it is the same as the PHP extension directory by running:
$ php -i | grep extension_dir extension_dir => /usr/lib/php/extensions/no-debug-non-zts-20060613 => /usr/lib/php/extensions/no-debug-non-zts-20060613
If it's not, change the extension_dir in php.ini or move fann.so.

To load the extension on PHP startup, add a line:
extension=fann.so

appendix.title: Predefined Constants
appendix.simpara: The constants below are defined by this extension, and will only be available when the extension has either been compiled into PHP or dynamically loaded at runtime.

listitem.simpara: Standard backpropagation algorithm, where the weights are updated after each training pattern. This means that the weights are updated many times during a single epoch. For this reason some problems, will train very fast with this algorithm, while other more advanced problems will not train very well.

Standard backpropagation algorithm, where the weights are updated after calculating the mean square error for the whole training set. This means that the weights are only updated once during an epoch. For this reason, some problems will train slower with this algorithm. But since the mean square error is calculated more correctly than in incremental training, some problems will reach better solutions with this algorithm.

A more advanced batch training algorithm which achieves good results for many problems. The RPROP training algorithm is adaptive, and therefore does not use the learning_rate. Some other parameters can however be set to change the way the RPROP algorithm works, but it is only recommended for users with insight in how the RPROP training algorithm works. The RPROP training algorithm is described by [Riedmiller and Braun, 1993], but the actual learning algorithm used here is the iRPROP- training algorithm which is described by [Igel and Husken, 2000] which is a variety of the standard RPROP training algorithm.

A more advanced batch training algorithm which achieves good results for many problems. The quickprop training algorithm uses the learning_rate parameter along with other more advanced parameters, but it is only recommended to change these advanced parameters for users with insight into how the quickprop training algorithm works. The quickprop training algorithm is described by [Fahlman, 1988].
Even more advance training algorithm. Only for version 2.2
Linear activation function.
Threshold activation function.
Threshold activation function.
Sigmoid activation function.
Stepwise linear approximation to sigmoid.
Symmetric sigmoid activation function, aka. tanh.
Stepwise linear approximation to symmetric sigmoid
Gaussian activation function.
Symmetric Gaussian activation function.
Stepwise Gaussian activation function.
Fast (sigmoid-like) activation function defined by David Elliott.
Fast (symmetric sigmoid-like) activation function defined by David Elliott.
Bounded linear activation function.
Bounded linear activation function.
Periodical sinus activation function.
Periodical cosinus activation function.
Periodical sinus activation function.
Periodical cosinus activation function.
Standard linear error function.

Tanh error function; usually better but may require a lower learning rate. This error function aggressively targets outputs that differ much from the desired output, while not targeting outputs that differ only slightly. Not recommended for cascade or incremental training.
Stop criteria is Mean Square Error (MSE) value.

Stop criterion is number of bits that fail. The number of bits means the number of output neurons which differ more than the bit fail limit (see fann_get_bit_fail_limit, fann_set_bit_fail_limit). The bits are counted in all of the training data, so this number can be higher than the number of training data.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The cascade output change fraction is a number between 0 and 1 determining how large a fraction the fann_get_MSE value should change within fann_get_cascade_output_stagnation_epochs during training of the output connections, in order for the training not to stagnate. If the training stagnates, the training of the output connections will be ended and new candidates will be prepared.

This training uses the parameters set using the fann_set_cascade_..., but it also uses another training algorithm as it’s internal training algorithm. This algorithm can be set to either FANN_TRAIN_RPROP or FANN_TRAIN_QUICKPROP by fann_set_training_algorithm, and the parameters set for these training algorithms will also affect the cascade training.

example.title: fann_create_train_from_callback example
example.programlisting:
<?php
function create_train_callback($num_data, $num_input, $num_output) {
    return array(
        "input" => array_fill(0, $num_input, 1),
        "output" => array_fill(0, $num_output, 1),
    );
}

$num_data = 3;
$num_input = 2;
$num_output = 1;
$train_data = fann_create_train_from_callback($num_data, $num_input, $num_output, "create_train_callback");
if ($train_data) {
    // Do something with $train_data
}
?>

refsect1.para: Get the activation steepness for neuron number neuron in layer number layer, counting the input layer as layer 0.
It is not possible to get activation steepness for the neurons in the input layer.

The steepness of an activation function says something about how fast the activation function goes from the minimum to the maximum. A high value for the activation function will also give a more aggressive training.
When training neural networks where the output values should be at the extremes (usually 0 and 1, depending on the activation function), a steep activation function can be used (e.g. 1.0).
The default activation steepness is 0.5.

refsect1.para: The number of fail bits; means the number of output neurons which differ more than the bit fail limit (see fann_get_bit_fail_limit, fann_set_bit_fail_limit). The bits are counted in all of the training data, so this number can be higher than the number of training data.
This value is reset by fann_reset_MSE and updated by all the same functions which also updates the MSE value (e.g. fann_test_data, fann_train_epoch)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the bit fail limit used during training

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the bit fail limit used during training.
The bit fail limit is used during training where the stop function is set to FANN_STOPFUNC_BIT.

The limit is the maximum accepted difference between the desired output and the actual output during training. Each output that diverges more than this limit is counted as an error bit. This difference is divided by two when dealing with symmetric activation functions, so that symmetric and not symmetric activation functions can use the same limit.
The default bit fail limit is 0.35.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the cascade candidate change fraction

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The cascade candidate change fraction is a number between 0 and 1 determining how large a fraction the fann_get_MSE value should change within fann_get_cascade_candidate_stagnation_epochs during training of the candidate neurons, in order for the training not to stagnate. If the training stagnates, the training of the candidate neurons will be ended and the best candidate will be selected.

It means that if the MSE does not change by a fraction of fann_get_cascade_candidate_change_fraction during a period of fann_get_cascade_candidate_stagnation_epochs, the training of the candidate neurons is stopped because the training has stagnated.
If the cascade candidate change fraction is low, the candidate neurons will be trained more and if the fraction is high they will be trained less.
refsect1.simpara: The default cascade candidate change fraction is 0.01, which is equivalent to a 1% change in MSE.

listitem.simpara: Neural network resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The cascade candidate change fraction, or false on error.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Return the candidate limit

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The candidate limit is a limit for how much the candidate neuron may be trained. The limit is a limit on the proportion between the MSE and candidate score.
Set this to a lower value to avoid overfitting and to a higher if overfitting is not a problem.
The default candidate limit is 1000.0.

listitem.simpara: Neural network resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The candidate limit, or false on error.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the number of cascade candidate stagnation epochs

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The number of cascade candidate stagnation epochs determines the number of epochs training is allowed to continue without changing the MSE by a fraction of fann_get_cascade_candidate_change_fraction.
See more info about this parameter in fann_get_cascade_candidate_change_fraction.
The default number of cascade candidate stagnation epochs is 12.

listitem.simpara: Neural network resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The number of cascade candidate stagnation epochs, or false on error.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the maximum candidate epochs

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The maximum candidate epochs determines the maximum number of epochs the input connections to the candidates may be trained before adding a new candidate neuron.
The default max candidate epochs is 150.

listitem.simpara: Neural network resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The maximum candidate epochs, or false on error.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the maximum out epochs

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The maximum out epochs determines the maximum number of epochs the output connections may be trained after adding a new candidate neuron.
The default max out epochs is 150.

listitem.simpara: Neural network resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The maximum out epochs, or false on error.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the minimum candidate epochs

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The minimum candidate epochs determines the minimum number of epochs the input connections to the candidates may be trained before adding a new candidate neuron.
The default min candidate epochs is 50.

listitem.simpara: Neural network resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The minimum candidate epochs, or false on error.

note.simpara: This function is only available if the fann extension has been build against libfann >= 2.2.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the minimum out epochs

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The minimum out epochs determines the minimum number of epochs the output connections must be trained after adding a new candidate neuron.
The default min out epochs is 50.

listitem.simpara: Neural network resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The minimum out epochs, or false on error.

note.simpara: This function is only available if the fann extension has been build against libfann >= 2.2.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the number of candidate groups

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The number of candidate groups is the number of groups of identical candidates which will be used during training.
This number can be used to have more candidates without having to define new parameters for the candidates.
See fann_get_cascade_num_candidates for a description of which candidate neurons will be generated by this parameter.
The default number of candidate groups is 2.

listitem.simpara: Neural network resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The number of candidate groups, or false on error.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the number of candidates used during training

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The number of candidates used during training (calculated by multiplying fann_get_cascade_activation_functions_count, fann_get_cascade_activation_steepnesses_count and fann_get_cascade_num_candidate_groups).

The actual candidates is defined by the fann_get_cascade_activation_functions and fann_get_cascade_activation_steepnesses arrays. These arrays define the activation functions and activation steepnesses used for the candidate neurons. If there are 2 activation functions in the activation function array and 3 steepnesses in the steepness array, then there will be 2x3=6 different candidates which will be trained. These 6 different candidates can be copied into several candidate groups, where the only difference between these groups is the initial weights. If the number of groups is set to 2, then the number of candidate neurons will be 2x3x2=12. The number of candidate groups is defined by fann_set_cascade_num_candidate_groups.
The default number of candidates is 6x4x2 = 48

listitem.simpara: Neural network resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The number of candidates used during training, or false on error.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the cascade output change fraction

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The cascade output change fraction is a number between 0 and 1 determining how large a fraction of the fann_get_MSE value should change within fann_get_cascade_output_stagnation_epochs during training of the output connections, in order for the training not to stagnate. If the training stagnates, the training of the output connections will be ended and new candidates will be prepared.

It means that if the MSE does not change by a fraction of fann_get_cascade_output_change_fraction during a period of fann_get_cascade_output_stagnation_epochs, the training of the output connections is stopped because the training has stagnated.
If the cascade output change fraction is low, the output connections will be trained more and if the fraction is high, they will be trained less.
refsect1.simpara: The default cascade output change fraction is 0.01, which is equivalent to a 1% change in MSE.

listitem.simpara: Neural network resource.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The cascade output change fraction, or false on error.

The default number of cascade output stagnation epochs is 12.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The number of cascade output stagnation epochs, or false on error.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Initialize the weights using Widrow + Nguyen’s algorithm

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Initialize the weights using Widrow + Nguyen’s algorithm.

This function behaves similarly to fann_randomize_weights. It will use the algorithm developed by Derrick Nguyen and Bernard Widrow to set the weights in such a way as to speed up training. This technique is not always successful, and in some cases can be less efficient than a purely random initialization.

The algorithm requires access to the range of the input data (for example largest and smallest input), and therefore accepts a second argument, data, which is the training data that will be used to train the network.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sets the activation steepness for supplied neuron and layer number

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Set the activation steepness for neuron number neuron in layer number layer, counting the input layer as layer 0.
It is not possible to set activation steepness for the neurons in the input layer.

The steepness of an activation function says something about how fast the activation function goes from the minimum to the maximum. A high value for the activation function will also give a more aggressive training.
When training neural networks where the output values should be at the extremes (usually 0 and 1, depending on the activation function), a steep activation function can be used (e.g. 1.0).
The default activation steepness is 0.5.

listitem.simpara: Neural network resource.

listitem.para: The activation steepness.
Layer number.
Neuron number.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success, or false otherwise.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sets the callback function for use during training

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sets the callback function for use during training. It means that it is called from fann_train_on_data or fann_train_on_file.

listitem.simpara: Neural network resource.

listitem.para:
The supplied callback function takes following parameters:
ann - The neural network resource train - The train data resource or null if called from fann_train_on_file max_epochs - The maximum number of epochs the training should continue epochs_between_reports - The number of epochs between calling this function desired_error - The desired fann_get_MSE or fann_get_bit_fail, depending on the stop function chosen by fann_set_train_stop_function epochs - The current epoch
The callback should return true. If it returns false, the training will terminate.
