refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets line from stream resource up to a given delimiter

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets a line from the given handle.
Reading ends when length bytes have been read, when the non-empty string specified by ending is found (which is not included in the return value), or on EOF (whichever comes first).
This function is nearly identical to fgets except in that it allows end of line delimiters other than the standard \n, \r, and \r\n, and does not return the delimiter itself.

listitem.para: A valid file handle.
The maximum number of bytes to read from the handle. Negative values are not supported. Zero (0) means the default socket chunk size, i.e. 8192 bytes.
An optional string delimiter.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a string of up to length bytes read from the file pointed to by stream, or false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieves header/meta data from streams/file pointers

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns information about an existing stream.

listitem.para: The stream can be any stream created by fopen, fsockopen pfsockopen and stream_socket_client.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The result array contains the following items:

listitem.para: timed_out (bool) - true if the stream timed out while waiting for data on the last call to fread or fgets.
blocked (bool) - true if the stream is in blocking IO mode. See stream_set_blocking.

eof (bool) - true if the stream has reached end-of-file. Note that for socket streams this member can be true even when unread_bytes is non-zero. To determine if there is more data to be read, use feof instead of reading this item.
unread_bytes (int) - the number of bytes currently contained in the PHP's own internal buffer.

note.simpara: You shouldn't use this value in a script.

listitem.para: stream_type (string) - a label describing the underlying implementation of the stream.
wrapper_type (string) - a label describing the protocol wrapper implementation layered over the stream. See for more information about wrappers.
wrapper_data (mixed) - wrapper specific data attached to this stream. See for more information about wrappers and their wrapper data.
mode (string) - the type of access required for this stream (see Table 1 of the fopen() reference)
seekable (bool) - whether the current stream can be seeked.
uri (string) - the URI/filename associated with this stream.
crypto (array) - the TLS connection metadata for this stream. (Note: Only provided when the resource's stream uses TLS.)

example.title: stream_get_meta_data example using fopen with http
example.programlisting:
<?php
$url = 'http://www.example.com/';

if (!$fp = fopen($url, 'r')) {
    trigger_error("Unable to open URL ($url)", E_USER_ERROR);
}

$meta = stream_get_meta_data($fp);

var_dump($meta);

fclose($fp);
?>

example.title: stream_get_meta_data example using stream_socket_client with https
example.programlisting:
<?php
$streamContext = stream_context_create(
    [
        'ssl' => [
            'capture_peer_cert' => true,
            'capture_peer_cert_chain' => true,
            'disable_compression' => true,
        ],
    ]
);

$client = stream_socket_client(
    'ssl://www.example.com:443',
    $errorNumber,
    $errorDescription,
    40,
    STREAM_CLIENT_CONNECT,
    $streamContext
);


$meta = stream_get_meta_data($client);

var_dump($meta);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: A callback function for the notification context parameter

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: A callable function, used by the notification context parameter, called during an event.

note.para: This is not a real function, only a prototype of how the function should be.

listitem.para: One of the STREAM_NOTIFY_* notification constants.
One of the STREAM_NOTIFY_SEVERITY_* notification constants.
Passed if a descriptive message is available for the event.
Passed if a descriptive message code is available for the event.
The meaning of this value is dependent on the specific wrapper in use.
If applicable, the bytes_transferred will be populated.
If applicable, the bytes_max will be populated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

row.entry: Support for STREAM_NOTIFY_COMPLETED implemented, earlier PHP versions would never trigger this notification.

example.title: stream_notification_callback example
example.programlisting:
<?php
function stream_notification_callback($notification_code, $severity, $message, $message_code, $bytes_transferred, $bytes_max) {

    switch($notification_code) {
        case STREAM_NOTIFY_RESOLVE:
        case STREAM_NOTIFY_AUTH_REQUIRED:
        case STREAM_NOTIFY_COMPLETED:
        case STREAM_NOTIFY_FAILURE:
        case STREAM_NOTIFY_AUTH_RESULT:
            var_dump($notification_code, $severity, $message, $message_code, $bytes_transferred, $bytes_max);
            /* Ignore */
            break;

        case STREAM_NOTIFY_REDIRECTED:
            echo "Being redirected to: ", $message;
            break;

        case STREAM_NOTIFY_CONNECT:
            echo "Connected...";
            break;

        case STREAM_NOTIFY_FILE_SIZE_IS:
            echo "Got the filesize: ", $bytes_max;
            break;

        case STREAM_NOTIFY_MIME_TYPE_IS:
            echo "Found the mime-type: ", $message;
            break;

        case STREAM_NOTIFY_PROGRESS:
            echo "Made some progress, downloaded ", $bytes_transferred, " so far";
            break;
    }
    echo "\n";
}

$ctx = stream_context_create();
stream_context_set_params($ctx, array("notification" => "stream_notification_callback"));

file_get_contents("http://php.net/contact", false, $ctx);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: Connected... Found the mime-type: text/html; charset=utf-8 Being redirected to: http://no.php.net/contact Connected... Got the filesize: 0 Found the mime-type: text/html; charset=utf-8 Being redirected to: http://no.php.net/contact.php Connected... Got the filesize: 4589 Found the mime-type: text/html;charset=utf-8 Made some progress, downloaded 0 so far Made some progress, downloaded 0 so far Made some progress, downloaded 0 so far Made some progress, downloaded 1440 so far Made some progress, downloaded 2880 so far Made some progress, downloaded 4320 so far Made some progress, downloaded 5760 so far Made some progress, downloaded 6381 so far Made some progress, downloaded 7002 so far

example.title: Simple progressbar for commandline download client
example.programlisting:
<?php
function usage($argv) {
    echo "Usage:\n";
    printf("\tphp %s <http://example.com/file> <localfile>\n", $argv[0]);
    exit(1);
}

function stream_notification_callback($notification_code, $severity, $message, $message_code, $bytes_transferred, $bytes_max) {
    static $filesize = null;

    switch($notification_code) {
    case STREAM_NOTIFY_RESOLVE:
    case STREAM_NOTIFY_AUTH_REQUIRED:
    case STREAM_NOTIFY_COMPLETED:
    case STREAM_NOTIFY_FAILURE:
    case STREAM_NOTIFY_AUTH_RESULT:
        /* Ignore */
        break;

    case STREAM_NOTIFY_REDIRECTED:
        echo "Being redirected to: ", $message, "\n";
        break;

    case STREAM_NOTIFY_CONNECT:
        echo "Connected...\n";
        break;

    case STREAM_NOTIFY_FILE_SIZE_IS:
        $filesize = $bytes_max;
        echo "Filesize: ", $filesize, "\n";
        break;

    case STREAM_NOTIFY_MIME_TYPE_IS:
        echo "Mime-type: ", $message, "\n";
        break;

    case STREAM_NOTIFY_PROGRESS:
        if ($bytes_transferred > 0) {
            if (!isset($filesize)) {
                printf("\rUnknown filesize.. %2d kb done..", $bytes_transferred/1024);
            } else {
                $length = (int) (($bytes_transferred/$filesize)*100);
                printf("\r[%-100s] %d%% (%2d/%2d kb)", str_repeat("=", $length). ">", $length, ($bytes_transferred/1024), $filesize/1024);
            }
        }
        break;
    }
}

isset($argv[1], $argv[2]) or usage($argv);

$ctx = stream_context_create();
stream_context_set_params($ctx, array("notification" => "stream_notification_callback"));

$fp = fopen($argv[1], "r", false, $ctx);
if (is_resource($fp) && file_put_contents($argv[2], $fp)) {
    echo "\nDone!\n";
    exit(0);
}

$err = error_get_last();
echo "\nErrrrrorr..\n", $err["message"], "\n";
exit(1);
?>
example.para: Executing the example above with: php -n fetch.php http://no2.php.net/get/php-5-LATEST.tar.bz2/from/this/mirror php-latest.tar.bz2 will output something similar too:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Runs the equivalent of the select() system call on the given arrays of streams with a timeout specified by seconds and microseconds

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The stream_select function accepts arrays of streams and waits for them to change status. It is the stream counterpart of socket_select, but the two do not behave alike in every respect: they report invalid arguments differently, and stream_select can return without consulting the operating system at all, as described in the notes below.

listitem.para: The streams listed in the read array will be watched to see if characters become available for reading (more precisely, to see if a read will not block - in particular, a stream resource is also ready on end-of-file, in which case an fread will return a zero length string).
The streams listed in the write array will be watched to see if a write will not block.
The streams listed in the except array will be watched for high priority exceptional ("out-of-band") data arriving.

note.para: When stream_select returns, the arrays read, write and except are modified to indicate which stream resource(s) actually changed status. The original keys of the arrays are preserved.

listitem.para: The seconds and microseconds together form the timeout parameter, seconds specifies the number of seconds while microseconds the number of microseconds. The timeout is an upper bound on the amount of time that stream_select will wait before it returns. If seconds is set to 0 and microseconds is 0 or null, stream_select will not wait for data - instead it will return immediately, indicating the current status of the streams.
If seconds is null stream_select can block indefinitely, returning only when an event on one of the watched streams occurs (or if a signal interrupts the system call).

warning.para: Using a timeout value of 0 allows you to instantaneously poll the status of the streams, however, it is NOT a good idea to use a 0 timeout value in a loop as it will cause your script to consume too much CPU time.

It is much better to specify a timeout value of a few seconds, although if you need to be checking and running other code concurrently, using a timeout value of at least 200000 microseconds will help reduce the CPU usage of your script.

listitem.para: See seconds description.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: On success stream_select returns the number of stream resources contained in the modified arrays, which may be zero if the timeout expires before anything interesting happens. On error false is returned and a warning raised (this can happen if the system call is interrupted by an incoming signal).

example.title: stream_select Example
example.para: This example checks to see if data has arrived for reading on either $stream1 or $stream2. Since the timeout value is 0 it will return immediately:
example.programlisting:
<?php
/* Prepare the read array */
$read   = array($stream1, $stream2);
$write  = NULL;
$except = NULL;
if (false === ($num_changed_streams = stream_select($read, $write, $except, 0))) {
    /* Error handling */
} elseif ($num_changed_streams > 0) {
    /* At least on one of the streams something interesting happened */
}
?>

note.para:
Due to a limitation in the current Zend Engine it is not possible to pass a constant modifier like null directly as a parameter to a function which expects this parameter to be passed by reference. Instead use a temporary variable or an expression with the leftmost member being a temporary variable:
<?php $e = NULL; stream_select($r, $w, $e, 0); ?>

note.simpara: When reading from or writing to a stream returned in the arrays, be aware that the full amount of data requested is not necessarily read or written. Be prepared for as little as a single byte.
Some streams (like zlib) cannot be selected by this function.

A stream that already holds buffered data on the PHP side is reported as ready without the underlying select() call being made. When that happens the write and except arrays are emptied without having been examined, so a stream that was ready for writing goes unreported and the return value counts the readable streams only.

note.title: Windows compatibility
note.para: Use of stream_select on file descriptors returned by proc_open will fail and return false under Windows.
STDIN from a console changes status as soon as any input events are available, but reading from the stream may still block.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set blocking/non-blocking mode on a stream

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sets blocking or non-blocking mode on a stream.
This function works for any stream that supports non-blocking mode (currently, regular files and socket streams).

listitem.para: The stream.

If enable is false, the given stream will be switched to non-blocking mode, and if true, it will be switched to blocking mode. This affects calls like fgets and fread that read from the stream. In non-blocking mode an fgets call will always return right away while in blocking mode it will wait for data to become available on the stream.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

note.para: On Windows, this has no affect on local files. Non-blocking IO for local files is not supported on Windows.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set the stream chunk size

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Set the stream chunk size.

listitem.para: The target stream.
The desired new chunk size.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the previous chunk size on success.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: A ValueError is thrown if size is less than 1 or greater than PHP_INT_MAX.

row.entry: A ValueError is now thrown if size is less than 1 or greater than PHP_INT_MAX. Previously, an E_WARNING level error was emitted and false was returned.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set read file buffering on the given stream

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sets the read buffer. It's the equivalent of stream_set_write_buffer, but for read operations.

listitem.para: The file pointer.

The number of bytes to buffer. If size is 0 then read operations are unbuffered. This ensures that all reads with fread are completed before other processes are allowed to read from that input stream.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns 0 on success, or another value if the request cannot be honored.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set timeout period on a stream

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sets the timeout value on stream, expressed in the sum of seconds and microseconds.
When the stream times out, the 'timed_out' key of the array returned by stream_get_meta_data is set to true, although no error/warning is generated.

listitem.para: The target stream.
The seconds part of the timeout to be set.
The microseconds part of the timeout to be set.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: stream_set_timeout example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$fp = fsockopen("www.example.com", 80);
if (!$fp) {
    echo "Unable to open\n";
} else {

    fwrite($fp, "GET / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n");
    stream_set_timeout($fp, 2);
    $res = fread($fp, 2000);

    $info = stream_get_meta_data($fp);
    fclose($fp);

    if ($info['timed_out']) {
        echo 'Connection timed out!';
    } else {
        echo $res;
    }

}
?>

refsect1.title: Notes

note.para: This function doesn't work with advanced operations like stream_socket_recvfrom, use stream_select with timeout parameter instead.

refsect1.para: This function was previously called as set_socket_timeout and later socket_set_timeout but this usage is deprecated.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sets write file buffering on the given stream

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sets the buffering for write operations on the given stream to size bytes.

listitem.para: The file pointer.

The number of bytes to buffer. If size is 0 then write operations are unbuffered. This ensures that all writes with fwrite are completed before other processes are allowed to write to that output stream.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns 0 on success, or another value if the request cannot be honored.

example.title: stream_set_write_buffer example
example.para: The following example demonstrates how to use stream_set_write_buffer to create an unbuffered stream.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$fp = fopen($file, "w");
if ($fp) {
  if (stream_set_write_buffer($fp, 0) !== 0) {
      // changing the buffering failed
  }
  fwrite($fp, $output);
  fclose($fp);
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Accept a connection on a socket created by stream_socket_server

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Accept a connection on a socket previously created by stream_socket_server.

listitem.para: The server socket to accept a connection from.
Override the default socket accept timeout. Time should be given in seconds. By default, default_socket_timeout is used.
Will be set to the name (address) of the client which connected, if included and available from the selected transport.

note.para: Can also be determined later using stream_socket_get_name.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a stream to the accepted socket connection or false on failure.

warning.para: This function should not be used with UDP server sockets. Instead, use stream_socket_recvfrom and stream_socket_sendto.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Open Internet or Unix domain socket connection

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Initiates a stream or datagram connection to the destination specified by address. The type of socket created is determined by the transport specified using standard URL formatting: transport://target. For Internet Domain sockets (AF_INET) such as TCP and UDP, the target portion of the address parameter should consist of a hostname or IP address followed by a colon and a port number. For Unix domain sockets, the target portion should point to the socket file on the filesystem.

note.para: The stream will by default be opened in blocking mode. You can switch it to non-blocking mode by using stream_set_blocking.

listitem.para: Address to the socket to connect to.
Will be set to the system level error number if connection fails.
Will be set to the system level error message if the connection fails.

Number of seconds until the connect() system call should timeout. By default, default_socket_timeout is used.
This parameter only applies when not making asynchronous connection attempts.
To set a timeout for reading/writing data over the socket, use the stream_set_timeout, as the timeout only applies while making connecting the socket.

Bitmask field which may be set to any combination of connection flags. Currently the select of connection flags is limited to STREAM_CLIENT_CONNECT (default), STREAM_CLIENT_ASYNC_CONNECT and STREAM_CLIENT_PERSISTENT.
A valid context resource created with stream_context_create.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: On success a stream resource is returned which may be used together with the other file functions (such as fgets, fgetss, fwrite, fclose, and feof), false on failure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: On failure the error_code and error_message arguments will be populated with the actual system level error that occurred in the system-level connect() call. If the value returned in error_code is 0 and the function returned false, it is an indication that the error occurred before the connect() call. This is most likely due to a problem initializing the socket. Note that the error_code and error_message arguments will always be passed by reference.

warning.simpara: UDP sockets will sometimes appear to have opened without an error, even if the remote host is unreachable. The error will only become apparent when you read or write data to/from the socket. refnamediv.refpurpose: Turns encryption on/off on an already connected socket

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Enable or disable encryption on the stream.
Once the crypto settings are established, cryptography can be turned on and off dynamically by passing true or false in the enable parameter.

listitem.para: The stream resource.
Enable/disable cryptography on the stream.

Setup encryption on the stream. Valid methods are
STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_SSLv2_CLIENT STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_SSLv3_CLIENT STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_SSLv23_CLIENT STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_ANY_CLIENT STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLS_CLIENT STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_0_CLIENT STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_1_CLIENT STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_2_CLIENT STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_3_CLIENT (as of PHP 7.4.0) STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_SSLv2_SERVER STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_SSLv3_SERVER STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_SSLv23_SERVER STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_ANY_SERVER STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLS_SERVER STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_0_SERVER STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_1_SERVER STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_2_SERVER STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_TLSv1_3_SERVER (as of PHP 7.4.0)
If omitted, the crypto_method context option on the stream's SSL context will be used instead.
Seed the stream with settings from session_stream.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success, false if negotiation has failed or 0 if there isn't enough data and you should try again (only for non-blocking sockets).

example.title: stream_socket_enable_crypto example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$fp = stream_socket_client("tcp://myproto.example.com:31337", $errno, $errstr, 30);
if (!$fp) {
    die("Unable to connect: $errstr ($errno)");
}

/* Turn on encryption for login phase */
stream_socket_enable_crypto($fp, true, STREAM_CRYPTO_METHOD_SSLv23_CLIENT);
fwrite($fp, "USER god\r\n");
fwrite($fp, "PASS secret\r\n");

/* Turn off encryption for the rest */
stream_socket_enable_crypto($fp, false);

while ($motd = fgets($fp)) {
    echo $motd;
}

fclose($fp);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Creates a pair of connected, indistinguishable socket streams

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: stream_socket_pair creates a pair of connected, indistinguishable socket streams. This function is commonly used in IPC (Inter-Process Communication).

listitem.para: The protocol family to be used: STREAM_PF_INET, STREAM_PF_INET6 or STREAM_PF_UNIX
The type of communication to be used: STREAM_SOCK_DGRAM, STREAM_SOCK_RAW, STREAM_SOCK_RDM, STREAM_SOCK_SEQPACKET or STREAM_SOCK_STREAM
The protocol to be used: STREAM_IPPROTO_ICMP, STREAM_IPPROTO_IP, STREAM_IPPROTO_RAW, STREAM_IPPROTO_TCP or STREAM_IPPROTO_UDP

note.simpara: Please consult the Streams constant list for further details on each constant.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns an array with the two socket resources on success, or false on failure.

example.title: A stream_socket_pair example
example.para: This example shows the basic usage of stream_socket_pair in Inter-Process Communication.
example.programlisting:
<?php

$sockets = stream_socket_pair(STREAM_PF_UNIX, STREAM_SOCK_STREAM, STREAM_IPPROTO_IP);
$pid     = pcntl_fork();

if ($pid == -1) {
     die('could not fork');

} else if ($pid) {
     /* parent */
    fclose($sockets[0]);

    fwrite($sockets[1], "child PID: $pid\n");
    echo fgets($sockets[1]);

    fclose($sockets[1]);

} else {
    /* child */
    fclose($sockets[1]);

    fwrite($sockets[0], "message from child\n");
    echo fgets($sockets[0]);

    fclose($sockets[0]);
}

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Receives data from a socket, connected or not

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: stream_socket_recvfrom accepts data from a remote socket up to length bytes.

listitem.para: The remote socket.
The number of bytes to receive from the socket.

The value of flags can be any combination of the following:
Possible values for flags
STREAM_OOB
Process OOB (out-of-band) data.
STREAM_PEEK
Retrieve data from the socket, but do not consume the buffer. Subsequent calls to fread or stream_socket_recvfrom will see the same data.
If address is provided it will be populated with the address of the remote socket.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the read data, as a string, or false on failure.

example.title: stream_socket_recvfrom example
example.programlisting:
<?php
/* Open a server socket to port 1234 on localhost */
$server = stream_socket_server('tcp://127.0.0.1:1234');

/* Accept a connection */
$socket = stream_socket_accept($server);

/* Grab a packet (1500 is a typical MTU size) of OOB data */
echo "Received Out-Of-Band: '" . stream_socket_recvfrom($socket, 1500, STREAM_OOB) . "'\n";

/* Take a peek at the normal in-band data, but don't consume it. */
echo "Data: '" . stream_socket_recvfrom($socket, 1500, STREAM_PEEK) . "'\n";

/* Get the exact same packet again, but remove it from the buffer this time. */
echo "Data: '" . stream_socket_recvfrom($socket, 1500) . "'\n";

/* Close it up */
fclose($socket);
fclose($server);
?>

note.para: If a message received is longer than the length parameter, excess bytes may be discarded depending on the type of socket the message is received from (such as UDP).
Calls to stream_socket_recvfrom on socket-based streams, after calls to buffer-based stream functions (like fread or stream_get_line) read data directly from the socket and bypass the stream buffer.

The value of flags can be any combination of the following:
possible values for flags
STREAM_OOB
Process OOB (out-of-band) data.
The address specified when the socket stream was created will be used unless an alternate address is specified in address.
If specified, it must be in dotted quad (or [ipv6]) format.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a result code, as an integer, or false on failure.

example.title: stream_socket_sendto Example
example.programlisting:
<?php
/* Open a socket to port 1234 on localhost */
$socket = stream_socket_client('tcp://127.0.0.1:1234');

/* Send ordinary data via ordinary channels. */
fwrite($socket, "Normal data transmit.");

/* Send more data out of band. */
stream_socket_sendto($socket, "Out of Band data.", STREAM_OOB);

/* Close it up */
fclose($socket);
?>

<?php

refnamediv.refpurpose: Register a URL wrapper implemented as a PHP class

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Allows you to implement your own protocol handlers and streams for use with all the other filesystem functions (such as fopen, fread etc.).

listitem.para: The wrapper name to be registered. Valid protocol names must contain alphanumerics, dots (.), plusses (+), or hyphens (-) only.
The classname which implements the protocol.
Should be set to STREAM_IS_URL if protocol is a URL protocol. Default is 0, local stream.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.
stream_wrapper_register will return false if the protocol already has a handler.

example.title: How to register a stream wrapper
example.programlisting:
<?php
$existed = in_array("var", stream_get_wrappers());
if ($existed) {
    stream_wrapper_unregister("var");
}
stream_wrapper_register("var", "VariableStream");
$myvar = "";

$fp = fopen("var://myvar", "r+");

fwrite($fp, "line1\n");
fwrite($fp, "line2\n");
fwrite($fp, "line3\n");

rewind($fp);
while (!feof($fp)) {
    echo fgets($fp);
}
fclose($fp);
var_dump($myvar);

if ($existed) {
    stream_wrapper_restore("var");
}

?>

preface.title: Introduction
preface.para:
Swoole is a parallel network communication engine based on asynchronous event-driven and coroutine, written in C++, providing coroutine and high-performance network programming support for PHP. It provides various network server and client modules for multiple communication protocols, making it easy to quickly implement TCP/UDP services, high-performance Web, WebSocket services, IoT, real-time communication, games, microservices, etc., breaking the limits of PHP in traditional web domains.
To get started, please check the Swoole Docs.

note.simpara: This extension is not available on Windows platforms.

section.title: Requirements
section.para: Swoole requires the libbrotli library.
Enabling --enable-swoole-curl option requires the libcurl library, and both PHP and Swoole must link to the same libcurl shared library and headers to avoid undefined behavior.
Enabling --enable-iouring option requires liburing library (version >= 2.0) and Linux kernel (version >= 5.12).
Enabling --enable-swoole-thread option requires PHP to be in ZTS (Zend Thread Safety) mode.
Enabling the --enable-cares option requires the libc-ares library.
Enabling the --enable-zstd option requires the libzstd library (version >= 1.4.0).
Enabling the --enable-swoole-sqlite option requires the libsqlite library.
Enabling the --enable-swoole-pgsql option requires the libpq library.
Enabling the --with-swoole-odbc option requires the unixodbc-dev library.
Enabling the --with-swoole-oracle option requires the Oracle Instant Client libraries.

section.title: Installation
section.para: Use --with-swoole[=DIR] when compiling PHP.

Information for installing this PECL extension may be found in the manual chapter titled Installation of PECL extensions. Additional information such as new releases, downloads, source files, maintainer information, and a CHANGELOG, can be located here: https://pecl.php.net/package/swoole

section.title: Introduction
section.para: Swoole 6.0.1 introduced a coroutine lock that supports inter-process and inter-thread sharing. This lock is designed with non-blocking behavior and enables efficient coroutine synchronization in multi-process and multi-thread environments.

When compiled with the --enable-iouring option and the Linux kernel supports the io_uring futex feature, Swoole's coroutine lock implements synchronization using io_uring futex. In this case, coroutines wait for lock wakeups using an efficient queuing mechanism, significantly improving performance.

Without io_uring futex, the coroutine lock falls back to an exponential backoff sleep mechanism, where the wait time increases by 2^n milliseconds (n being the number of failures) after each failed attempt to acquire the lock. While this approach avoids busy waiting, it introduces additional CPU scheduling overhead and latency.
The coroutine lock is reentrant, allowing the currently holding coroutine to safely perform multiple lock operations.

warning.para: Do not create locks in callback functions like onReceive, as this will cause continuous memory growth and lead to memory leaks.
Locking and unlocking must be performed in the same coroutine, otherwise it will break static conditions.

example.title: Basic usage
example.programlisting:
<?php
use Swoole\Coroutine\Lock;
use Swoole\Coroutine\WaitGroup;
use function Swoole\Coroutine\go;
use function Swoole\Coroutine\run;

$lock = new Lock();
$waitGroup = new WaitGroup();

run(function() use ($lock, $waitGroup) {
    go(function() use ($lock, $waitGroup) {
        $waitGroup->add();
        $lock->lock();
        sleep(1);
        $lock->unlock();
        $waitGroup->done();
    });

    go(function() use ($lock, $waitGroup) {
        $waitGroup->add();
        $lock->lock(); // Wait for the holding coroutine to unlock
        sleep(1);
        $lock->unlock();
        $waitGroup->done();
    });

    echo 'Lock does not block the process';
    $waitGroup->wait();
});

refnamediv.refpurpose: Acquire the lock, blocking if necessary

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: When executing the lock operation, if the lock is already held by another coroutine, the current coroutine will actively yield CPU control and enter a suspended state. When the coroutine holding the lock calls unlock(), the waiting coroutine will be awakened and try to acquire the lock again.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the lock was acquired successfully, false otherwise.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Attempt to acquire the lock without blocking

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: When calling the lock operation, if the lock is already held by another coroutine, the function will immediately return false without suspending the current coroutine or yielding CPU control. This non-blocking design allows the caller to flexibly handle contention situations, such as retrying, giving up, or executing other logic.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the lock was acquired successfully, false if the lock is not available.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Release the lock

listitem.para: With io_uring futex: the system will precisely wake up one coroutine in the waiting queue.
Without io_uring futex: waiting coroutines need to wait for their backoff time to end and compete to reacquire the lock.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the lock was released successfully, false otherwise.

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: The Swoole extension provides low-level interfaces to directly manipulate the underlying epoll/kqueue/poll/select event loop. It allows adding sockets created by other extensions or PHP's stream/socket extensions to Swoole's EventLoop.

note.simpara: The Event module is low-level, being a basic encapsulation of epoll. Users should have experience with IO multiplexing programming.

listitem.simpara: Signal handler callback functions set via Process::signal
Timer callback functions set via Timer::tick and Timer::after
Deferred execution functions set via Event::defer
Periodic callback functions set via Event::cycle
File descriptors, including Swoole\Client->$sock, Swoole\Process->$pipe, or any other file descriptor (fd).
Resources created by stream_socket_client/fsockopen.
Resources created by socket_create from the sockets extension require the --enable-sockets flag during Swoole compilation.
Swoole automatically converts Swoole\Process into UnixSocket and Swoole\Client into connected client sockets at the underlying level.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Add a socket to the underlying reactor event listener

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Adds a socket to the underlying reactor event listener. This function can be used in both Server and Client modes.

warning.simpara: A socket that has already been added cannot be added again. Use swoole_event_set to modify the corresponding callback functions and event types for the socket.

listitem.simpara: File descriptor, stream resource, sockets resource, or object.
Callback function for readable events.
Callback function for writable events.
Event type mask (e.g. SWOOLE_EVENT_READ, SWOOLE_EVENT_WRITE or SWOOLE_EVENT_READ | SWOOLE_EVENT_WRITE).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Swoole\Event::add example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$fp = stream_socket_client("tcp://www.qq.com:80", $errno, $errstr, 30);
fwrite($fp,"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: www.qq.com\r\n\r\n");

Swoole\Event::add($fp, function($fp) {
    $resp = fread($fp, 8192);
    Swoole\Event::del($fp);
    fclose($fp);
});
echo "Finish\n";
?>

example.title: Basic usage
example.programlisting:
<?php

    var_dump($id);
});

Swoole\Event::cycle(function () {
    echo "hello [1]\n";
    Swoole\Event::cycle(function () {
        echo "hello [2]\n";
        Swoole\Event::cycle(null);
    });
});

Swoole\Event::wait();

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check if a socket is being monitored in the event loop

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Checks whether the specified file descriptor is being monitored for the given event types in the event loop.

listitem.simpara: File descriptor (stream/socket resource, integer, or object).
Event types to check (bitmask of SWOOLE_EVENT_READ and/or SWOOLE_EVENT_WRITE).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Checking event monitoring status
example.programlisting:
<?php
$fp = stream_socket_client("tcp://www.qq.com:80");
Swoole\Event::add($fp, function ($fp) {
    echo fread($fp, 8192);
}, null, SWOOLE_EVENT_READ);

var_dump(Swoole\Event::isset($fp, SWOOLE_EVENT_READ)); // Output: true
var_dump(Swoole\Event::isset($fp, SWOOLE_EVENT_WRITE)); // Output: false

refnamediv.refpurpose: Modify event listener callbacks and mask

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Modifies the event listener callbacks and mask for the given file descriptor.

note.simpara: When $read_callback is not null, the readable event callback function will be modified to the specified function.
When $write_callback is not null, the writable event callback function will be updated to the specified function.
Setting SWOOLE_EVENT_READ alone disables write event listening, while setting SWOOLE_EVENT_WRITE alone disables read event listening.

warning.simpara: Swoole\Event::set replaces callbacks but does not free them. Specifying null for callbacks (e.g., read_callback/write_callback) preserves the existing callbacks instead of clearing them.
Listening for SWOOLE_EVENT_READ without a read_callback (or SWOOLE_EVENT_WRITE without a write_callback) will cause the operation to fail and return false.

listitem.simpara: File descriptor, stream resource, sockets resource, or object.
Callback function for readable events.
Callback function for writable events.
Event type mask (e.g. SWOOLE_EVENT_READ, SWOOLE_EVENT_WRITE or SWOOLE_EVENT_READ | SWOOLE_EVENT_WRITE).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Start event loop

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Starts the event loop. Place this at the end of your PHP program.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No return value.

example.title: Swoole\Event::wait example
example.programlisting:
<?php
Swoole\Timer::tick(1000, function () {
    echo "hello\n";
});

Swoole\Event::wait();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Write data to socket asynchronously

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Makes data sending asynchronous for stream/sockets resources.

note.simpara: If data is continuously written to a socket but the peer cannot read fast enough, the socket buffer will eventually fill up. In this case, the Swoole underlying layer will store the excess data in an in-memory buffer and wait for the writable event to trigger before attempting to write to the socket again. However, if the in-memory buffer also becomes full, Swoole will throw a "pipe buffer overflow, reactor will block" error and switch to blocking mode, pausing further writes until space becomes available.
The buffer-full return of false is an atomic operation—it guarantees either complete success (all data written) or total failure (nothing written).

warning.simpara: Event::write cannot be used with SSL/TLS-encrypted streams or sockets (tunneled connections).
Upon successful execution, Event::write will automatically switch the $socket to non-blocking mode.

listitem.simpara: File descriptor (stream/socket resource, integer, or object).
Data to send (length must not exceed socket buffer size).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Swoole\Event::write example
example.programlisting:
<?php
use Swoole\Event;

$fp = stream_socket_client('tcp://127.0.0.1:9501');
$data = str_repeat('A', 1024 * 1024*2);
Event::add($fp, function($fp) {
     echo fread($fp);
});
Event::write($fp, $data);
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Millisecond precision timer. The underlying implementation is based on epoll_wait and setitimer, using a min-heap data structure that supports adding a large number of timers.
In synchronous I/O processes, such as the Manager and TaskWorker processes, it is implemented using setitimer and signals.
In asynchronous I/O processes, it is implemented using the timeout of epoll_wait/kevent/poll/select.

Timer Correction: The execution time of the timer callback function does not affect the timing of the next timer execution. For example, setting a tick timer of 10ms after 0.002s, the first callback will be executed at 0.012s, if the callback function takes 5ms to execute, the next timer will still trigger at 0.022s, not at 0.027s.

However, if the execution time of the timer callback function is too long, even covering the time of the next timer execution, the underlying system will perform time correction, discarding the expired behavior and triggering the timer callback at the next available time. For example, if the callback function at 0.012s takes 15ms to execute, causing the timer at 0.022s to be delayed, the timer callback will be triggered again at 0.032s.
By default, when a timer is triggered, a coroutine is automatically created to execute the callback function. This can be disabled with swoole_async_set.

warning.simpara: Timer only works within the current process space.
Timer is purely asynchronous and incompatible with synchronous I/O functions.
Timer execution may experience minor timing deviations.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Execute a function after a specified time

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Creates a one-shot timer, which is destroyed once its callback has run. Unlike sleep, it does not block the current process.

listitem.simpara: The delay in milliseconds. Must be greater than or equal to 1; a lower value emits an E_WARNING and the call fails.
The function to execute once the delay has elapsed. It is called as callback(mixed ...$params). Unlike Swoole\Timer::tick, the timer ID is not passed to the callback.
Additional values passed to callback.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the timer ID, which can be passed to Swoole\Timer::clear to cancel the timer before it fires. Returns false if the timer could not be created, in particular when ms is less than 1.

example.title: Swoole\Timer::after example
example.programlisting:
<?php
Swoole\Timer::after(1000, function (string $name) {
    echo "Hello, $name\n";
}, "Swoole");
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Delete a timer by ID

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Deletes the timer with the given ID. Only timers created by the current process can be removed; timers belonging to other processes are not visible here.

listitem.simpara: The timer ID returned by Swoole\Timer::tick or Swoole\Timer::after.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure. false is returned when no timer with this ID exists in the current process, or when the ID refers to an internal timer.

example.title: Swoole\Timer::clear example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$timer_id = Swoole\Timer::after(1000, function () {
    echo "never printed\n";
});
var_dump(Swoole\Timer::clear($timer_id));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Clear all timers in the current process.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Clear all timers in the current process. As of Swoole 4.4.0.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure. false is returned when no timer has been created in this process yet. Only timers created from PHP are removed; internal timers are left in place.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check if a timer is existed.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Checks whether a timer with the given ID exists in the current process.

listitem.simpara: The timer ID returned by Swoole\Timer::tick or Swoole\Timer::after.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if a timer with this ID exists in the current process, false otherwise.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get information about a timer.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Get information about a timer. As of Swoole 4.4.0.

listitem.simpara: The timer ID returned by Swoole\Timer::tick or Swoole\Timer::after.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns an array describing the timer, or null if no timer with this ID exists in the current process. The array contains the following keys:

listitem.simpara: The time of the next execution, in milliseconds, counted from the moment the timer subsystem was started. It is not a duration.
The number of times the callback has been executed. Available as of Swoole 4.8.0.
The interval of the timer, in milliseconds.
The number of the timer loop round in which the timer was created.
Whether the timer has been removed.

example.title: Swoole\Timer::info example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$timer_id = Swoole\Timer::tick(1000, function () {});
var_dump(Swoole\Timer::info($timer_id));
Swoole\Timer::clear($timer_id);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: array(5) { ["exec_msec"]=> int(1000) ["exec_count"]=> int(0) ["interval"]=> int(1000) ["round"]=> int(0) ["removed"]=> bool(false) }

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get an iterator over the timers of the current process

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns an iterator over the IDs of the timers created from PHP in the current process. Timers created internally by Swoole are not listed. As of Swoole 4.4.0.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a Swoole\Timer\Iterator object, which extends ArrayIterator and yields the timer IDs as int values. The iterator is a snapshot taken when the method is called; it is empty when no timer exists.

example.title: Swoole\Timer::list example
example.programlisting:
<?php
Swoole\Timer::tick(1000, function () {});
Swoole\Timer::after(5000, function () {});

foreach (Swoole\Timer::list() as $timer_id) {
    echo $timer_id, "\n";
    Swoole\Timer::clear($timer_id);
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

warning.simpara: This method was deprecated in Swoole 4.6.0 and removed in Swoole 6.0.0. Use swoole_async_set instead.

listitem.simpara: An associative array of options. Only enable_coroutine is recognised: when set to false, the timer callbacks are executed directly instead of inside a newly created coroutine.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set a repeating interval timer

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sets a timer that triggers every ms milliseconds. Unlike a timer created with Swoole\Timer::after, it keeps triggering until it is removed with Swoole\Timer::clear.

listitem.simpara: The interval in milliseconds. Must be greater than or equal to 1; a lower value emits an E_WARNING and the call fails.
The function to execute on every tick. It is called as callback(int $timer_id, mixed ...$params): the ID of the timer is passed as the first argument, followed by the values given in params.
Additional values passed to callback after the timer ID.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the timer ID, which can be passed to Swoole\Timer::clear. Returns false if the timer could not be created, in particular when ms is less than 1.

example.title: Swoole\Timer::tick example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$ticks = 0;
Swoole\Timer::tick(1000, function (int $timer_id, string $label) use (&$ticks) {
    echo "tick #", ++$ticks, " ($label)\n";
    if ($ticks === 3) {
        Swoole\Timer::clear($timer_id);
    }
}, "job");
?>

preface.title: Introduction
preface.para: Tidy is a binding for the Tidy HTML clean and repair utility which allows you to not only clean and otherwise manipulate HTML, XHTML, and XML documents, but also traverse the document tree, including ones with embedded scripting languages such as PHP or ASP within them using object-oriented constructs.

section.title: Requirements
section.para: To use Tidy, you will need libtidy installed, available on the tidy homepage. As of PHP 7.1.0, the HTML5 aware successor libtidy5 can be used alternatively. As of PHP 7.3.0, another option is to use libtidyp.

section.title: Installation
section.para: This extension is bundled with PHP, and is installed using the --with-tidy configure option.

section.title: Runtime Configuration
section.simpara: The behaviour of these functions is affected by settings in php.ini.
section.para:
Tidy Configuration Options
Name Default Changeable Changelog
tidy.default_config "" INI_SYSTEM
tidy.clean_output "0" INI_USER
For further details and definitions of the INI_* modes, see the .
section.simpara: Here's a short explanation of the configuration directives.

listitem.para: Default path for tidy config file.
Turns on/off the output repairing by Tidy.

warning.para: Do not turn on tidy.clean_output if you are generating non-html content such as dynamic images.

appendix.title: Predefined Constants
appendix.simpara: The constants below are defined by this extension, and will only be available when the extension has either been compiled into PHP or dynamically loaded at runtime.
appendix.para: Each TIDY_TAG_* represents a HTML tag. For example, TIDY_TAG_A represents a "link" tag.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Constructs a new tidy object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Constructs a new tidy object.

listitem.para: If the filename parameter is given, this function will also read that file and initialize the object with the file, acting like tidy_parse_file.

The config config can be passed either as an array or as a string. If a string is passed, it is interpreted as the name of the configuration file, otherwise, it is interpreted as the options themselves.
For an explanation about each option, visit http://api.html-tidy.org/#quick-reference.

The encoding parameter sets the encoding for input/output documents. The possible values for encoding are: ascii, latin0, latin1, raw, utf8, iso2022, mac, win1252, ibm858, utf16, utf16le, utf16be, big5, and shiftjis.
Search for the file in the include_path.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Throws an exception when the constructor fails (e.g. failing to open a file).

row.entry: Now throws a ValueError if config contains an unknown option or attempts to set a read-only one, and a TypeError if a configuration key is not a string, or if an option does not accept the given value.
Failures when executing the constructor now throw instead of silently creating an unusable object.
filename, config, encoding and useIncludePath are nullable now.

HTML;

get_nodes($tidy->html());

function get_nodes($node) {

    // check if the current node is of requested type
    if($node->isAsp()) {
        echo "\n\n# asp node #" . ++$GLOBALS['num'] . "\n";
        echo $node->value;
    }

    // check if the current node has children
    if($node->hasChildren()) {
        foreach($node->child as $child) {
            get_nodes($child);
        }
    }
}

?>

function get_nodes($node) {

    // check if the current node is of requested type
    if($node->isComment()) {
        echo "\n\n# comment node #" . ++$GLOBALS['num'] . "\n";

preface.title: Introduction
preface.para: The tokenizer functions provide an interface to the PHP tokenizer embedded in the Zend Engine. Using these functions you may write your own PHP source analyzing or modification tools without having to deal with the language specification at the lexical level.
See also the appendix about tokens.

section.title: Installation
section.para: This extension is enabled by default. It may be disabled by using the following option at compile time: --disable-tokenizer
section.simpara: The Windows version of PHP has built-in support for this extension. You do not need to load any additional extensions in order to use these functions.

appendix.title: Predefined Constants
appendix.para: When the extension has either been compiled into PHP or dynamically loaded at runtime, the tokens listed in are defined as constants.

listitem.simpara: Recognises the ability to use reserved words in specific contexts.

appendix.title: Examples
appendix.para: Here is a simple example PHP script using the tokenizer that will read in a PHP file, strip all comments from the source and print the pure code only.

example.title: Strip comments with the tokenizer
example.programlisting:
<?php
$source = file_get_contents('example.php');
$tokens = token_get_all($source);

foreach ($tokens as $token) {
   if (is_string($token)) {
       // simple 1-character token
       echo $token;
   } else {
       // token array
       list($id, $text) = $token;

       switch ($id) { 
           case T_COMMENT: 
           case T_DOC_COMMENT:
               // no action on comments
               break;

           default:
               // anything else -> output "as is"
               echo $text;
               break;
       }
   }
}
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.para: This class provides an alternative to token_get_all. While the function returns tokens either as a single-character string, or an array with a token ID, token text and line number, PhpToken::tokenize normalizes all tokens into PhpToken objects, which makes code operating on tokens more memory efficient and readable.

listitem.para: One of the T_* constants, or an ASCII codepoint representing a single-char token.
The textual content of the token.
The starting line number (1-based) of the token.
The starting position (0-based) in the tokenized string (the number of bytes).

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns a new PhpToken object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns a new PhpToken object

listitem.para: One of the T_* constants (see ), or an ASCII codepoint representing a single-char token.
The textual content of the token.
The starting line number (1-based) of the token.
The starting position (0-based) in the tokenized string (the number of bytes).

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the name of the token.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the name of the token.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An ASCII character for single-char tokens, or one of T_* constant names for known tokens (see ), or null for unknown tokens.

example.title: PhpToken::getTokenName example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// known token
$token = new PhpToken(T_ECHO, 'echo');
var_dump($token->getTokenName());   // -> string(6) "T_ECHO"

// single-char token
$token = new PhpToken(ord(';'), ';');
var_dump($token->getTokenName());   // -> string(1) ";"

// unknown token
$token = new PhpToken(10000 , "\0");
var_dump($token->getTokenName());   // -> NULL

refnamediv.refpurpose: Tells whether the token is of given kind.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Tells whether the token is of given kind.

listitem.para: Either a single value to match the token's id or textual content, or an array thereof.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A boolean value whether the token is of given kind.

example.title: PhpToken::is example
example.programlisting: <?php $token = new PhpToken(T_ECHO, 'echo'); var_dump($token->is(T_ECHO)); // -> bool(true) var_dump($token->is('echo')); // -> bool(true) var_dump($token->is(T_FOREACH)); // -> bool(false) var_dump($token->is('foreach')); // -> bool(false)

example.title: Usage with array
example.programlisting:
<?php
function isClassType(PhpToken $token): bool {
    return $token->is([T_CLASS, T_INTERFACE, T_TRAIT]);
}

$interface = new PhpToken(T_INTERFACE, 'interface');
var_dump(isClassType($interface));   // -> bool(true)

$function = new PhpToken(T_FUNCTION, 'function');
var_dump(isClassType($function));    // -> bool(false)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Tells whether the token would be ignored by the PHP parser.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Tells whether the token would be ignored by the PHP parser.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A boolean value whether the token would be ignored by the PHP parser (such as whitespace or comments).

example.title: PhpToken::isIgnorable example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$echo = new PhpToken(T_ECHO, 'echo');
var_dump($echo->isIgnorable());   // -> bool(false)

$space = new PhpToken(T_WHITESPACE, ' ');
var_dump($space->isIgnorable());  // -> bool(true)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the textual content of the token.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the textual content of the token.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A textual content of the token.

example.title: PhpToken::__toString example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$token = new PhpToken(T_ECHO, 'echo');
echo $token;

refnamediv.refpurpose: Splits given source into PHP tokens, represented by PhpToken objects.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns an array of PhpToken objects representing given code.

listitem.para: The PHP source to parse.

Valid flags:
TOKEN_PARSE - Recognises the ability to use reserved words in specific contexts.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array of PHP tokens represented by instances of PhpToken or its descendants. This method returns static[] so that PhpToken can be seamlessly extended.

example.title: PhpToken::tokenize example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$tokens = PhpToken::tokenize('<?php echo; ?>');

foreach ($tokens as $token) {
    echo "Line {$token->line}: {$token->getTokenName()} ('{$token->text}')", PHP_EOL;
}
example.screen: Line 1: T_OPEN_TAG ('<?php ') Line 1: T_ECHO ('echo') Line 1: ; (';') Line 1: T_WHITESPACE (' ') Line 1: T_CLOSE_TAG ('?>')

example.title: Extending PhpToken
example.programlisting:
<?php

class MyPhpToken extends PhpToken {
    public function getUpperText() {
        return strtoupper($this->text);
    }
}

$tokens = MyPhpToken::tokenize('<?php echo; ?>');
echo "'{$tokens[0]->getUpperText()}'";

refnamediv.refpurpose: Split given source into PHP tokens

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: token_get_all parses the given code string into PHP language tokens using the Zend engine's lexical scanner.
For a list of parser tokens, see , or use token_name to translate a token value into its string representation.

listitem.para: The PHP source to parse.

Valid flags:
TOKEN_PARSE - Recognises the ability to use reserved words in specific contexts.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array of token identifiers. Each individual token identifier is either a single character (i.e.: ;, ., >, !, etc...), or a three element array containing the token index in element 0, the string content of the original token in element 1 and the line number in element 2.

refsect1.title: Examples

example.title: token_get_all example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$tokens = token_get_all('<?php echo; ?>');

foreach ($tokens as $token) {
    if (is_array($token)) {
        echo "Line {$token[2]}: ", token_name($token[0]), " ('{$token[1]}')", PHP_EOL;
    }
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: Line 1: T_OPEN_TAG ('<?php ') Line 1: T_ECHO ('echo') Line 1: T_WHITESPACE (' ') Line 1: T_CLOSE_TAG ('?>')

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the symbolic name of a given PHP token

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: token_name gets the symbolic name for a PHP id value.

listitem.para: The token value.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The symbolic name of the given id.

example.title: token_name example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// 260 is the token value for the T_EVAL token
echo token_name(260);        // -> "T_EVAL"

// a token constant maps to its own name
echo token_name(T_FUNCTION); // -> "T_FUNCTION"
?>

preface.title: Introduction
preface.simpara: This chapter describes the functions that allow you to work with Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs). A URI is a string of characters used to identify a resource. URIs are used in web technologies to identify resources on the Internet.
This extension implements functionality that follows the RFC 3986, Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax and WHATWG URL Standard specifications.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Construct the Uri object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Constructs the Uri\Rfc3986\Uri object.

listitem.simpara: URI to parse.
When a string is passed, uri is applied on baseUrl, if uri is a relative reference. If either null is passed, or uri is a not a relative reference, then baseUrl doesn't have any effect.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: If the resulting URI is invalid, a Uri\InvalidUriException is thrown.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Return the internal state of the URI

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns the internal state of the URI.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the internal state of the URI as an array.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check if two URIs are equivalent

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Checks if two URIs are equivalent.

listitem.simpara: URI to compare the current URI against.
Whether the fragment component is taken into account of the comparison (Uri\UriComparisonMode::IncludeFragment) or not (Uri\UriComparisonMode::ExcludeFragment). By default, the fragment is excluded.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the two URIs are equivalent, or false otherwise.

example.title: Uri\Rfc3986\Uri::equals basic example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$uri1 = new \Uri\Rfc3986\Uri("https://example.com");
$uri2 = new \Uri\Rfc3986\Uri("HTTPS://example.com");

var_dump($uri1->equals($uri2));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Parse a URI

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Parses a URI.

listitem.simpara: URI to parse.
When a string is passed, uri is applied on baseUrl, if uri is a relative reference. If either null is passed, or uri is a not a relative reference, then baseUrl doesn't have any effect.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a Uri\Rfc3986\Uri instance on success, or null on failure.

example.title: Uri\Rfc3986\Uri::parse basic example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$uri = \Uri\Rfc3986\Uri::parse("https://example.com");

if ($uri !== null) {
    echo "Valid URI: " . $uri->toString();
} else {
    echo "Invalid URI";
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Resolve a URI with the current object as the base URL

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Resolves a URI - which may potentially be a relative reference - with the current object as the base URL.

listitem.simpara: A URI to apply on the current object.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: A new Uri\Rfc3986\Uri instance.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: If the resulting URI is invalid, a Uri\InvalidUriException is thrown.

example.title: Uri\Rfc3986\Uri::resolve basic example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$uri = new \Uri\Rfc3986\Uri("https://example.com");
$uri = $uri->resolve("/foo");

echo $uri->toRawString();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Construct the Url object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Constructs the Uri\Rfc3986\Uri object.

listitem.simpara: A valid URL string to parse (e.g. /foo or (e.g. https://example.com/foo).
When a string is passed, uri is applied on baseUrl, if uri is a relative-URL string. If either null is passed, or uri is a not a relative-URL string, then baseUrl doesn't have any effect.
An array to pass a list of Uri\WhatWg\UrlValidationError instances by reference to provide extended information about the errors triggered during parsing.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: If the resulting URL is invalid, a Uri\WhatWg\InvalidUrlException is thrown.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check if two URLs are equivalent

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Checks if two URLs are equivalent.

listitem.simpara: URL to compare the current URL against.
Whether the fragment component is taken into account of the comparison (Uri\UriComparisonMode::IncludeFragment) or not (Uri\UriComparisonMode::ExcludeFragment). By default, the fragment is excluded.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the two URLs are equivalent, or false otherwise.

example.title: Uri\WhatWg\Url::equals basic example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$url1 = new \Uri\WhatWg\Url("https://example.com");
$url2 = new \Uri\WhatWg\Url("HTTPS://example.com");

var_dump($url1->equals($url2));
?>
