refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the response object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieve the Yaf_Response_Abstract instance used by the dispatcher.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The Yaf_Response_Abstract instance, or null if the application is not initialized.

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::getResponse example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class CharsetPlugin extends Yaf_Plugin_Abstract
{
    public function preDispatch(Yaf_Request_Abstract $request, Yaf_Response_Abstract $response)
    {
        // Same response object as the one held by the dispatcher
        Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->getResponse()->setHeader(
            "Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8"
        );
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve router instance

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieve the Yaf_Router instance used by the dispatcher to route requests.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The Yaf_Router instance, or null if the application is not initialized.

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::getRouter example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Bootstrap extends Yaf_Bootstrap_Abstract
{
    public function _initRoute(Yaf_Dispatcher $dispatcher)
    {
        $router = $dispatcher->getRouter();

        // Route /product/42 to ProductController::detailAction
        $router->addRoute("product", new Yaf_Route_Rewrite(
            "product/:id",
            array("controller" => "product", "action" => "detail")
        ));
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Initialize view and return it

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Initialize and return a Yaf_View_Simple instance bound to the dispatcher, using the given template directory.

listitem.simpara: The directory that holds the view templates.
Options passed to the view engine, see Yaf_View_Simple::__construct.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: A Yaf_View_Interface instance on success, or false / null on failure.

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::initView example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app = new Yaf_Application(dirname(__FILE__) . "/conf/application.ini");

$view = Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->initView(
    dirname(__FILE__) . "/application/views",
    array("tpl_suffix" => ".html")
);

$view->assign("title", "Home");
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Register a plugin

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Register a plugin (see Yaf_Plugin_Abstract). Generally, plugins are registered in Bootstrap (see Yaf_Bootstrap_Abstract).

listitem.simpara: A Yaf_Plugin_Abstract instance.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the Yaf_Dispatcher object itself on success, or false / null on failure.

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::registerPlugin example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Bootstrap extends Yaf_Bootstrap_Abstract {
  public function _initPlugin(Yaf_Dispatcher $dispatcher) {
    /**
    * Yaf assumes plugin scripts under [application.directory] .  "/plugins" 
    * for this case, it will be:
    * [application.directory] . "/plugins/" . "User" . [application.ext]
    */ 
    $user = new UserPlugin();
    $dispatcher->registerPlugin($user);
  }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Switch on/off returning the response

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Switch whether Yaf_Application::run returns the response object instead of sending it to the client directly. When enabled, $response = $app->run() gives you the Yaf_Response_Abstract instance so it can be further manipulated. Available since Yaf 3.2.2.

listitem.simpara: Whether to return the response instead of sending it.

note.simpara: If this parameter is not given, the current state is returned instead.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the Yaf_Dispatcher object itself when flag is given, or a bool indicating the current state when it is not.

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::returnResponse example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app = new Yaf_Application(dirname(__FILE__) . "/conf/application.ini");

Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->returnResponse(true);

// $app->run() now returns the response instead of flushing it
$response = $app->run();

$response->setHeader("X-Generator", "Yaf");
$response->response();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Change default action name

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Change the action name which is used when an action name can not be extracted from the request URI. The name is normalized to lowercase.

listitem.simpara: The name of the action.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the Yaf_Dispatcher object itself on success, or false if the application is not initialized.

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::setDefaultAction example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app = new Yaf_Application(dirname(__FILE__) . "/conf/application.ini");

// Requests without an action part are now routed to "main" instead of
// "index", e.g. /user maps to UserController::mainAction
Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->setDefaultAction("main");

$app->run();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Change default controller name

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Change the controller name which is used when a controller name can not be extracted from the request URI. The name is normalized to capitalize the first letter.

listitem.simpara: The name of the controller.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the Yaf_Dispatcher object itself on success, or false if the application is not initialized.

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::setDefaultController example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app = new Yaf_Application(dirname(__FILE__) . "/conf/application.ini");

// Requests without a controller part now go to HomeController, the name
// is normalized to capitalize the first letter
Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->setDefaultController("home");

$app->run();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Change default module name

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Change the module name which is used when a module name can not be extracted from the request URI. The module must be a registered one, see Yaf_Application::getModules.

listitem.simpara: The name of a registered module.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the Yaf_Dispatcher object itself on success, false if the given module is not registered (and a YAF_ERR_TYPE_ERROR is triggered) or if the application is not initialized, or null otherwise.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Triggers a YAF_ERR_TYPE_ERROR error if module is not a registered module name.

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::setDefaultModule example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app = new Yaf_Application(dirname(__FILE__) . "/conf/application.ini");

// "Home" must be a registered module, e.g. via
// application.modules = "Index,Home,Admin" in conf/application.ini
Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->setDefaultModule("Home");

$app->run();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set error handler

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Set an error handler for Yaf. When application.dispatcher.throwException is off, Yaf triggers catchable errors when unexpected errors occur.
This method is a wrapper of set_error_handler; the handler is called whenever such an error is raised.

listitem.simpara: A callable callback, with the same semantics as the callback passed to set_error_handler.
The error types to handle, same as the error_levels parameter of set_error_handler. Defaults to handling all error types.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the Yaf_Dispatcher object itself on success, false if calling set_error_handler failed, or null if the application is not initialized.

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::setErrorHandler example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app = new Yaf_Application(dirname(__FILE__) . "/conf/application.ini");

Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->setErrorHandler(function ($errno, $errstr) {
    // Route errors to ErrorController::errorAction
    $request = Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->getRequest();
    $request->setControllerName("Error");
    $request->setActionName("error");
});

$app->run();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set the request object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Set the request object used by the dispatcher. This allows using a custom request implementation instead of the built-in Yaf_Request_Http or Yaf_Request_Simple.

listitem.simpara: A Yaf_Request_Abstract instance.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the Yaf_Dispatcher object itself on success, or null if the application is not initialized.

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::setRequest example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app = new Yaf_Application(dirname(__FILE__) . "/conf/application.ini");

// Run the application from a cron job:
// $ php cron.php index/index/cleanup
$request = new Yaf_Request_Simple("CLI");

Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->setRequest($request);

$app->run();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set the response object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Set the response object used by the dispatcher. This allows using a custom response implementation instead of the built-in ones.

listitem.simpara: A Yaf_Response_Abstract instance.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the Yaf_Dispatcher object itself on success, or null if the application is not initialized.

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::setResponse example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class ApiResponse extends Yaf_Response_Http
{
    public function response()
    {
        header("Content-Type: application/json");
        parent::response();
    }
}

$app = new Yaf_Application(dirname(__FILE__) . "/conf/application.ini");

Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->setResponse(new ApiResponse());

$app->run();
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set a custom view engine

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This method provides a solution if you want use a custom view engine instead of Yaf_View_Simple

listitem.para: A Yaf_View_Interface instance

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the Yaf_Dispatcher object itself on success, or null if the application is not initialized.

example.title: A custom View engine example
example.programlisting:
<?php
require "/path/to/smarty/Smarty.class.php";

class Smarty_Adapter implements Yaf_View_Interface
{
    /**
     * Smarty object
     * @var Smarty
     */
    public $_smarty;
 
    /**
     * Constructor
     *
     * @param string $tmplPath
     * @param array $extraParams
     * @return void
     */
    public function __construct($tmplPath = null, $extraParams = array()) {
        $this->_smarty = new Smarty;
 
        if (null !== $tmplPath) {
            $this->setScriptPath($tmplPath);
        }
 
        foreach ($extraParams as $key => $value) {
            $this->_smarty->$key = $value;
        }
    }
 
    /**
     * Set the path to the templates
     *
     * @param string $path The directory to set as the path.
     * @return void
     */
    public function setScriptPath($path)
    {
        if (is_readable($path)) {
            $this->_smarty->template_dir = $path;
            return;
        }
 
        throw new Exception('Invalid path provided');
    }
 
    /**
     * Assign a variable to the template
     *
     * @param string $key The variable name.
     * @param mixed $val The variable value.
     * @return void
     */
    public function __set($key, $val)
    {
        $this->_smarty->assign($key, $val);
    }
 
    /**
     * Allows testing with empty() and isset() to work
     *
     * @param string $key
     * @return boolean
     */
    public function __isset($key)
    {
        return (null !== $this->_smarty->get_template_vars($key));
    }
 
    /**
     * Allows unset() on object properties to work
     *
     * @param string $key
     * @return void
     */
    public function __unset($key)
    {
        $this->_smarty->clear_assign($key);
    }
 
    /**
     * Assign variables to the template
     *
     * Allows setting a specific key to the specified value, OR passing
     * an array of key => value pairs to set en masse.
     *
     * @see __set()
     * @param string|array $spec The assignment strategy to use (key or
     * array of key => value pairs)
     * @param mixed $value (Optional) If assigning a named variable,
     * use this as the value.
     * @return void
     */
    public function assign($spec, $value = null) {
        if (is_array($spec)) {
            $this->_smarty->assign($spec);
            return;
        }
 
        $this->_smarty->assign($spec, $value);
    }
 
    /**
     * Clear all assigned variables
     *
     * Clears all variables assigned to Yaf_View either via
     * {@link assign()} or property overloading
     * ({@link __get()}/{@link __set()}).
     *
     * @return void
     */
    public function clearVars() {
        $this->_smarty->clear_all_assign();
    }
 
    /**
     * Processes a template and returns the output.
     *
     * @param string $name The template to process.
     * @return string The output.
     */
    public function render($name, $value = NULL) {
        return $this->_smarty->fetch($name);
    }

    public function display($name, $value = NULL) {
        echo $this->_smarty->fetch($name);
    }

}
?>

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::setView example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Bootstrap extends Yaf_Bootstrap_Abstract {

    /**
     * there are some config for smarty in the config:
     *
     * smarty.left_delimiter   = "{{"
     * smarty.right_delimiter  = "}}"
     * smarty.template_dir     = APPLICATION_PATH "/views/scripts/"
     * smarty.compile_dir      = APPLICATION_PATH "/views/templates_c/"
     * smarty.cache_dir        = APPLICATION_PATH "/views/templates_d/"
     *
     */
    public function _initConfig() {
        $config = Yaf_Application::app()->getConfig();
        Yaf_Registry::set("config", $config);
    }

    public function _initLocalName() {
        /** we put class Smarty_Adapter under the local library directory */
        Yaf_Loader::getInstance()->registerLocalNamespace('Smarty');
    }

    public function _initSmarty(Yaf_Dispatcher $dispatcher) {
        $smarty = new Smarty_Adapter(null, Yaf_Registry::get("config")->get("smarty"));
        $dispatcher->setView($smarty);
        /* now the Smarty view engine become the default view engine of Yaf */
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Switch on/off exception throwing

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Switch on/off exception throwing when an unexpected error occurs. When this is on, Yaf throws exceptions instead of triggering catchable errors.
You can also use application.dispatcher.throwException to achieve the same purpose.

listitem.simpara: Whether Yaf should throw exceptions on errors.

note.simpara: Since Yaf 2.2.0, if this parameter is not given, the current state is returned instead.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the Yaf_Dispatcher object itself when flag is given, or a bool indicating whether exception throwing is enabled when it is not.

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::throwException example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$config = array(
    'application' => array(
        'directory' => dirname(__FILE__),
    ),
);
$app = new Yaf_Application($config);

$app->getDispatcher()->throwException(true);

try {
    $app->run();
} catch (Yaf_Exception $e) {
    var_dump($e->getMessage());
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

example.title: Yaf_Dispatcher::throwException example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$config = array(
    'application' => array(
        'directory' => dirname(__FILE__),
    ),
);
$app = new Yaf_Application($config);

$app->getDispatcher()->throwException(false);

$app->run();
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: PHP Catchable fatal error: Yaf_Application::run(): Could not find controller script /tmp/controllers/Index.php in /tmp/1.php on line 12

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Config_Abstract is the base class of the configuration adapters. It provides a uniform way to access a set of configuration values through nested property syntax ($config->section->key), array access and iteration. Concrete implementations are Yaf_Config_Ini (read-only, INI files with section inheritance) and Yaf_Config_Simple (PHP arrays, mutable).

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve a configuration value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieves a configuration value by name. If name is omitted or null, the configuration object itself is returned, which can be used to iterate over all values.

listitem.simpara: The configuration key. Dot notation (e.g. database.host) may be used to access nested values.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The value associated with name. Array values are wrapped in a Yaf_Config_Abstract object. Returns null if the key does not exist, or the configuration object itself when name is null.

example.title: Yaf_Config_Abstract::get example
example.programlisting:
<?php
/**
 * Assume /etc/myapp/application.ini contains:
 * [common]
 * database.host = "localhost"
 * database.port = 3306
 */
$config = new Yaf_Config_Ini('/etc/myapp/application.ini', 'common');
echo $config->get('database.host'), "\n";

$simple = new Yaf_Config_Simple([
    'database' => ['host' => '127.0.0.1'],
]);

// Array values are exposed as Yaf_Config_Abstract instances
echo $simple->get('database')->host, "\n";

var_dump($config->get('missing.key'));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check if configuration is read-only

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Checks whether the configuration is read-only. This method is abstract and must be implemented by subclasses.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the configuration is read-only, false otherwise.

example.title: Yaf_Config_Abstract::readonly example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$ini = new Yaf_Config_Ini('/etc/myapp/application.ini', 'common');
var_dump($ini->readonly()); // Yaf_Config_Ini is always read-only

$writable = new Yaf_Config_Simple(['env' => 'development']);
var_dump($writable->readonly());

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Config_Ini enables developers to store configuration data in a familiar INI format and read it in the application by using nested object property syntax. The INI format is specialized to provide both the ability to have a hierarchy of configuration data keys and inheritance between configuration data sections. Configuration data hierarchies are supported by separating the keys with the dot or period character ("."). A section may extend or inherit from another section by following the section name with a colon character (":") and the name of the section from which data are to be inherited.

note.simpara: Yaf_Config_Ini utilizes the parse_ini_file PHP function. Please review this documentation to be aware of its specific behaviors, which propagate to Yaf_Config_Ini, such as how the special values of "true", "false", "yes", "no", and "null" are handled.

tip.simpara: Yaf_Config_Ini parses the configuration file on every request. If an application manages a large amount of (mostly static) configuration, consider the Yaconf extension instead: it keeps configuration in shared memory across the whole PHP lifecycle, so it is parsed only once and can be accessed much more efficiently. Yaconf understands the very same INI syntax — keys separated by dots, and inheritance between sections through "[section : parent]" — so the existing application.ini can be served by Yaconf as-is; only the way it is passed to Yaf_Application::__construct changes (see the tip in Application Configuration).

example.title: Yaf_Config_Iniexample
example.para: This example illustrates a basic use of Yaf_Config_Ini for loading configuration data from an INI file. In this example there are configuration data for both a production system and for a staging system. Because the staging system configuration data are very similar to those for production, the staging section inherits from the production section. In this case, the decision is arbitrary and could have been written conversely, with the production section inheriting from the staging section, though this may not be the case for more complex situations. Suppose, then, that the following configuration data are contained in /path/to/config.ini:
example.programlisting:
; Production site configuration data [production] webhost = www.example.com database.adapter = pdo_mysql database.params.host = db.example.com database.params.username = dbuser database.params.password = secret database.params.dbname = dbname
; Staging site configuration data inherits from production and ; overrides values as necessary [staging : production] database.params.host = dev.example.com database.params.username = devuser database.params.password = devsecret

<?php
$config = new Yaf_Config_Ini('/path/to/config.ini', 'staging');
 
var_dump($config->database->params->host); 
var_dump($config->database->params->dbname);
var_dump($config->get("database.params.username"));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

<?php
/**
 * Assume /etc/myapp/application.ini contains:

 * application.name = "MyApp"

 * database.port    = 3306
 *

 */

example.title: Yaf_Config_Ini::current example
example.programlisting:
<?php
/**
 * Assume /etc/myapp/application.ini contains:
 * [common]
 * application.name = "MyApp"
 * version          = "1.0"
 */
$config = new Yaf_Config_Ini('/etc/myapp/application.ini', 'common');

$config->rewind();
while ($config->valid()) {
    $value = $config->current();
    if ($value instanceof Yaf_Config_Abstract) {
        echo $config->key(), " => <config section>\n";
    } else {
        echo $config->key(), " => ", $value, "\n";
    }
    $config->next();
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve a configuration value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieves a configuration value by name. Dot notation (e.g. database.host) can be used to access nested values. If name is omitted or null, the configuration object itself is returned.

example.title: Yaf_Config_Ini::get example
example.programlisting:
<?php
/**
 * Assume /etc/myapp/application.ini contains:
 * [common]
 * application.name = "MyApp"
 * database.host    = "localhost"
 * database.port    = 3306
 */
$config = new Yaf_Config_Ini('/etc/myapp/application.ini', 'common');

// Dot notation for nested access
echo $config->get('database.host'), "\n";

// Array values are wrapped in a Yaf_Config_Ini object
echo $config->get('database')->port, "\n";

// No argument: the configuration object itself is returned
echo $config->get()->application->name, "\n";

var_dump($config->get('missing.key'));
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Config_Simple is a configuration adapter backed by a PHP array (or, optionally, an INI file). In contrast to Yaf_Config_Ini it is mutable by default: values can be changed at runtime, which makes it suitable both for programmatically built configuration and for configuration that needs to be adjusted during the request.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Creates a new Yaf_Config_Simple instance from an array of configuration values.

<?php

    'application' => ['name' => 'MyApp', 'env' => 'production'],
    'database'    => ['host' => 'localhost', 'port' => 3306],
]);

echo $config->application->name, "\n";
echo $config->database->host, "\n";

// The optional second argument makes the configuration read-only
$frozen = new Yaf_Config_Simple(['env' => 'testing'], true);
var_dump($frozen->readonly());
?>

// Array values are wrapped in a Yaf_Config_Simple object
echo $config['application']->name, "\n";
echo $config['database']['host'], "\n";
var_dump($config['missing']);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set a configuration value (ArrayAccess)

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sets a configuration value using array syntax. This method is an alias of Yaf_Config_Simple::set. The assignment fails silently if the configuration is read-only.

The value to assign.

example.title: Yaf_Config_Simple::offsetSet example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$config = new Yaf_Config_Simple(['env' => 'development']);

// Writable by default
$config['env'] = 'production';
$config['cache'] = ['enable' => true];
echo $config['env'], "\n";
var_dump($config['cache']['enable']);

// Assignments to a read-only configuration fail silently
$frozen = new Yaf_Config_Simple(['env' => 'development'], true);
$frozen['env'] = 'production';
echo $frozen['env'], "\n";
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Remove a key (ArrayAccess)

example.title: Yaf_Config_Simple::offsetUnset example

$config = new Yaf_Config_Simple([
    'cache' => ['enable' => true],
    'env'   => 'development',
]);

var_dump(isset($config['cache']));

// Read-only configurations cannot be modified: a warning is emitted
$frozen = new Yaf_Config_Simple(['env' => 'development'], true);

var_dump(isset($frozen['env']));
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.para: Yaf_Controller_Abstract is the heart of Yaf's system. MVC stands for Model-View-Controller and is a design pattern targeted at separating application logic from display logic.
Every custom controller shall inherit Yaf_Controller_Abstract.
section.simpara: Since Yaf_Controller_Abstract::__construct is called by Yaf with no arguments, Yaf_Controller_Abstract provides an alternative constructor-like hook: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::init.
section.para: If you have defined a init() method in your custom controller, it will be called as long as the controller was instantiated.

Action may have arguments, when a request coming, if there are the same name variable in the request parameters(see Yaf_Request_Abstract::getParam) after routed, Yaf will pass them to the action method (see Yaf_Action_Abstract::execute).
These arguments are directly fetched without filtering, it should be carefully processed before use them.

listitem.simpara: The name of the module the controller belongs to.
The name of the controller.
The current Yaf_Request_Abstract object.
The current Yaf_Response_Abstract object.
The invocation arguments passed to the action through Yaf_Controller_Abstract::forward, as an array keyed by argument name.
The Yaf_View_Interface object used to render views.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Constructor of Yaf_Controller_Abstract

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::__construct is called by Yaf when a controller object is created during dispatching. It takes no arguments, and users should not call it directly. Since it is not intended to be overridden with custom logic, Yaf_Controller_Abstract::init is provided as the userland initialization hook instead.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class IndexController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    // __construct() is called by Yaf_Dispatcher when the controller
    // is instantiated during dispatching, and should be neither
    // called manually nor overridden. Define init() instead:

    public function init() {
        // by the time init() runs, the dispatcher has already wired
        // up the controller: the request, response and view engine
        // are all available
        var_dump($this->getRequest() instanceof Yaf_Request_Abstract);
        var_dump($this->getResponse() instanceof Yaf_Response_Abstract);
        var_dump($this->getView() instanceof Yaf_View_Interface);
    }

    public function indexAction() {
        // ...
    }
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Render and display a view

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Renders the view script tpl and sends the result directly, unlike Yaf_Controller_Abstract::render, which returns the rendered output instead. Auto-rendering of the default action template is controlled by Yaf_Dispatcher::autoRender.

listitem.simpara: The view script name, relative to the view path.
An associative array of variables to export to the view script for this rendering, overriding those assigned through the view engine.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success, or false / null on failure.

example.title: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::display example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class ProductController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function listAction() {
        // render product/list.phtml and send the result directly
        // to the client, exporting $products to this rendering
        $this->display("product/list.phtml", array(
            "products" => array("yaf", "php"),
        ));
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Forward the current request to another action

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Forward the current request to another action. The target is determined from the number and types of the arguments:

simplelist.member: action only: forward to another action of the current controller.
controller and action: forward to another controller.
module, controller and action: forward to another module.
The optional parameters array carries invocation arguments retrievable with Yaf_Request_Abstract::getParam.

note.simpara: This method does not switch to the destination action immediately; the switch takes place after the current flow finishes. To hand over control right away, return from the current action method (returning false also tells Yaf not to auto-render the current view).

listitem.simpara: The destination module name. If the current module is given, it is used as is.
The destination controller name.
The destination action name.
Invocation arguments for the destination action, retrievable with Yaf_Request_Abstract::getParam.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success, or false / null on failure.

example.title: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::forward example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class IndexController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction() {
        $logined = $_SESSION["login"];
        if (!$logined) {
            $this->forward("login", array("from" => "Index")); // forward to the login action
            return false; // this is important, it ends the current flow
                          // and tells Yaf not to auto-render
        }

        // other processes
    }

    public function loginAction() {
        echo "login, redirected from ", $this->_request->getParam("from") , " action";
    }
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve one action invocation argument

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns a single invocation argument of the current action, given its name. Invocation arguments are passed to the action through Yaf_Controller_Abstract::forward.

listitem.simpara: The name of the invocation argument to retrieve.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The argument value, or null if it does not exist.

example.title: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::getInvokeArg example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class UserController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction() {
        // forward to the profile action of this controller,
        // carrying invocation arguments
        $this->forward("profile", array("name" => "laruence"));
        return false; // ends the current flow
    }

    public function profileAction() {
        // retrieve one invocation argument by name
        var_dump($this->getInvokeArg("name"));
        var_dump($this->getInvokeArg("missing"));
    }
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve all action invocation arguments

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns all invocation arguments of the current action, as an array keyed by argument name. Invocation arguments are passed to the action through Yaf_Controller_Abstract::forward.

refsect1.title: Parameters

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: An array of invocation arguments, or null if none were given.

example.title: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::getInvokeArgs example

<?php
class ProductController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction() {
        $this->forward("list", array("category" => "book", "page" => 2));
        return false; // ends the current flow
    }

    public function listAction() {
        // all invocation arguments of the current action
        var_dump($this->getInvokeArgs());
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve current response object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns the Yaf_Response_Abstract instance associated with this controller.

example.title: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::getResponse example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class ProductController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function apiAction() {
        // build the answer ourselves, no template needed
        Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->disableView();

        $response = $this->getResponse();
        $response->setHeader("Content-Type", "application/json");
        $response->setBody(json_encode(array("name" => "yaf")));
        // Yaf sends the body after the dispatch loop finishes
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Controller initializer

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::__construct is not meant to be overridden with custom logic, so Yaf_Controller_Abstract::init is provided as the userland initialization hook. If it is defined in a controller, it is called right after the controller object is instantiated.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::init example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class IndexController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    // init() is called right after the controller is instantiated,
    // before any action is dispatched
    public function init() {
        $this->getView()->assign("sitename", "Yaf Tutorial");
    }

    public function indexAction() {
        // ...
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Initialize the view and return it

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns the view engine bound to this controller. The view engine is initialized by the Yaf_Dispatcher during dispatching, using the template path set for the current controller.

listitem.simpara: Options passed to the view engine, see Yaf_View_Simple::__construct.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: A Yaf_View_Interface instance on success, or null on failure.

example.title: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::initView example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class ProductController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction() {
        // fetch the view engine bound to this controller, initialized
        // with its template path, e.g. application/views/;
        // options would be forwarded to the view engine, see
        // Yaf_View_Simple::__construct()
        $view = $this->initView();
        $view->assign("products", array("yaf", "php"));
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Redirect to a URL

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Redirects the client to another URL by sending a Location header (HTTP status 302).

listitem.simpara: The URL to redirect to.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success, or false / null on failure.

example.title: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::redirect example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class AccountController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function loginAction() {
        if (!$this->getRequest()->getParam("user")) {
            // send a Location header with HTTP status 302
            $this->redirect("http://www.example.com/account/login/");
            return false; // skip auto-rendering
        }
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Render view template

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Renders the view script tpl and returns the output, unlike Yaf_Controller_Abstract::display.

listitem.simpara: The view script name, relative to the view path.
An associative array of variables to export to the view script for this rendering.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The rendered output as a string on success, or false on failure.

example.title: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::render example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class ProductController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction() {
        // do not auto-render the default template
        Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->disableView();

        // render product/index.phtml and return the output
        // instead of sending it directly (as display() would)
        $html = $this->render("product/index.phtml", array(
            "products" => array("yaf", "php"),
        ));

        // post-process and set it as the response body
        $this->getResponse()->setBody($html);
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set the view path

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sets the template directory of the view engine bound to this controller.

listitem.simpara: The directory that holds the view templates.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success, or false / null on failure.

example.title: Yaf_Controller_Abstract::setViewpath example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class ProductController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function init() {
        // from now on templates of this controller are looked up
        // under application/themes/dark/views/
        $this->setViewpath(APPLICATION_PATH . "/themes/dark/views");
    }

    public function indexAction() {
        // renders application/themes/dark/views/product/index.phtml
        $this->display("product/index.phtml");
    }
}
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: An action can be defined in a separate file in Yaf (see Yaf_Controller_Abstract). That is, an action method can also be a Yaf_Action_Abstract class.
section.para: Since there should be a entry point which can be called by Yaf, you must implement the abstract method Yaf_Action_Abstract::execute in your custom action class.

listitem.simpara: The controller instance that owns this action, retrievable with Yaf_Action_Abstract::getController.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Action entry point

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para:
user should always define this method for an action, this is the entry point of an action. Yaf_Action_Abstract::execute may have arguments.
The value retrieved from the request is not safe. you should do some filtering work before you use it.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The return value of the action method is not used by Yaf; output is written directly or collected by the view engine.

example.title: Yaf_Action_Abstract::executeexample
example.programlisting:
<?php
/** 
 * A controller example
 */
class ProductController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract {
      protected $actions = array(
          "index" => "actions/Index.php",
      );
}
?>

example.title: Yaf_Action_Abstract::executeexample
example.programlisting:
<?php
/** 
 * ListAction
 */
class ListAction extends Yaf_Action_Abstract {
     public function execute ($name, $id) {
         assert($name == $this->getRequest()->getParam("name"));
         assert($id   == $this->getRequest()->getParam("id"));
     }
}
?>

class ListAction extends Yaf_Action_Abstract
{

        $controller = $this->getController();
        var_dump($controller instanceof Yaf_Controller_Abstract);

        // e.g. to reach its view engine
        $controller->getView()->assign("products", array("yaf", "php"));

section.title: Introduction
section.para: Yaf provides a ability for developers to use custom view engine instead of built-in engine which is Yaf_View_Simple. There is a example to explain how to do this, please see Yaf_Dispatcher::setView.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Assign a variable to the view

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Assigns a variable to the view. Assigned variables are available to the template under their names.

listitem.simpara: The name under which the variable becomes available to the template.
The value to assign.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The return value is defined by the concrete implementation. Yaf_View_Simple, the default view engine, returns the view instance.

example.title: Yaf_View_Interface::assign example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class MyView implements Yaf_View_Interface
{
    private $tpl_dir;
    private $vars = array();

    public function __construct($template_dir, $options = null)
    {
        $this->tpl_dir = $template_dir;
    }

    public function assign($name, $value = null)
    {
        $this->vars[$name] = $value;
        return true;
    }

    public function display($tpl, $tpl_vars = null)
    {
        echo $this->render($tpl, $tpl_vars);
        return true;
    }

    public function render($tpl, $tpl_vars = null)
    {
        extract($this->vars);
        if ($tpl_vars !== null) {
            extract($tpl_vars);
        }
        ob_start();
        include $this->tpl_dir . "/" . $tpl;
        return ob_get_clean();
    }

    public function setScriptPath($template_dir)
    {
        $this->tpl_dir = $template_dir;
        return $this;
    }

    public function getScriptPath()
    {
        return $this->tpl_dir;
    }
}

/* plug the custom view engine into the dispatcher in the bootstrap */
class Bootstrap extends Yaf_Bootstrap_Abstract
{
    public function _initView(Yaf_Dispatcher $dispatcher)
    {
        $dispatcher->setView(new MyView(APPLICATION_PATH . "/views"));
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Render and emit a template

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Renders a template and emits the result directly to the output.

listitem.simpara: The path to the template, relative to the template directory.
Optional variables to assign for this template only; they override assigned variables with the same name.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success, or false on failure.

example.title: Yaf_View_Interface::display example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class MyView implements Yaf_View_Interface
{
    private $tpl_dir;
    private $vars = array();

    public function __construct($template_dir, $options = null)
    {
        $this->tpl_dir = $template_dir;
    }

    public function assign($name, $value = null)
    {
        $this->vars[$name] = $value;
        return true;
    }

    public function display($tpl, $tpl_vars = null)
    {
        echo $this->render($tpl, $tpl_vars);
        return true;
    }

    public function render($tpl, $tpl_vars = null)
    {
        extract($this->vars);
        if ($tpl_vars !== null) {
            extract($tpl_vars);
        }
        ob_start();
        include $this->tpl_dir . "/" . $tpl;
        return ob_get_clean();
    }

    public function setScriptPath($template_dir)
    {
        $this->tpl_dir = $template_dir;
        return $this;
    }

    public function getScriptPath()
    {
        return $this->tpl_dir;
    }
}

/* plug the custom view engine into the dispatcher in the bootstrap */
class Bootstrap extends Yaf_Bootstrap_Abstract
{
    public function _initView(Yaf_Dispatcher $dispatcher)
    {
        $dispatcher->setView(new MyView(APPLICATION_PATH . "/views"));
    }
}
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.para: Yaf_View_Simple is the built-in template engine in Yaf, it is a simple but fast template engine, and only support PHP script template.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Assign a variable to the view

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Assigns a variable to the view. Assigned variables are available to the template under their names. When called with a single array argument, every key/value pair is assigned, with the keys becoming the variable names.

listitem.simpara: The name under which the variable becomes available to the template, or an array of variables to assign.
The value to assign.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true.

example.title: Yaf_View_Simple::assign example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class IndexController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction()
    {
        $this->getView()->assign("foo", "bar");
        $this->_view->assign(array("key" => "value", "name" => "value"));
    }
}
?>

example.title: Template example
example.programlisting: <html> <head> <title><?php echo $foo; ?></title> </head> <body> <?php foreach ($this->_tpl_vars as $name => $value) { echo $$name; // or echo $this->_tpl_vars[$name]; } ?> </body> </html>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of Yaf_View_Simple::assign

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Assigns a variable to the view by reference. Unlike Yaf_View_Simple::assign, the value is passed by reference, so later changes to the caller's variable become visible to the template.

listitem.simpara: The name under which the variable becomes available to the template.
The value to assign.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true.

example.title: Yaf_View_Simple::assignRef example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class IndexController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction()
    {
        $value = "bar";
        $this->getView()->assignRef("foo", $value);

        /* later changes to $value are visible in the template,
         * because the variable was assigned by reference */
        $value = "changed";

        //prevent the auto-render
        Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->autoRender(false);
    }
}
?>

example.title: Template example
example.programlisting: <html> <head> <title><?php echo $foo; ?></title> </head> <body> </body> </html>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: /* accessing the index controller will result: */ changed

refnamediv.refpurpose: Remove an assigned variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Removes an assigned variable from the view. When called without an argument, all assigned variables are removed.

listitem.simpara: The name of the variable to remove, or omitted/null to remove all assigned variables.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true.

example.title: Yaf_View_Simple::clear example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class IndexController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction()
    {
        $this->getView()->clear("foo")->clear("bar"); // clear "foo" and "bar"
        $this->_view->clear(); // clear all assigned variables
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Constructor of Yaf_View_Simple

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Yaf_View_Simple is the default and only view engine Yaf supports out of the box. An instance is created automatically by the Yaf_Dispatcher when the application starts; instantiating it directly is only needed to render templates outside of the dispatch flow.
The template_dir argument must point to an existing directory containing the view scripts; it becomes the script path of the view and can later be changed with Yaf_View_Simple::setScriptPath.

listitem.simpara: The directory where the template scripts are stored.
Optional view options as an array. Reserved for custom view engine implementations; the built-in engine accepts but does not use it.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Yaf_View_Simple::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php
define("TEMPLATE_DIRECTORY", APPLICATION_PATH . '/views');
$view = new Yaf_View_Simple(TEMPLATE_DIRECTORY);
$view->assign("name", "world");
echo $view->render("greeting.phtml");
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Render and store a template in the response

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Renders a template and appends the result to the Yaf_Response_Abstract body.

note.simpara: Unlike Yaf_View_Simple::render, the result is not returned but stored in the response, and Yaf_Application sends it when the response is emitted.

listitem.simpara: The path to the template, relative to the template directory set by Yaf_View_Simple::setScriptPath or application.view.directory.
Optional variables to assign for this template only; they override assigned variables with the same name.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success, or false on failure.

example.title: Yaf_View_Simple::display example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class IndexController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction()
    {
        $this->getView()->assign("title", "My Homepage");

        /* render index/index.phtml and store the result
         * in the response body */
        $this->getView()->display("index/index.phtml");

        return false; // we rendered ourselves, skip auto-rendering
    }
}
?>

example.title: Template example
example.programlisting: <html> <head> <title><?php echo $title; ?></title> </head> </html>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Render a template string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Renders a template given as a string and returns the result.

note.simpara: Since no template file is involved, the template directory is not consulted.

listitem.simpara: The template content as a string.
Optional variables to assign for this render; they override assigned variables with the same name.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The rendered result as a string, or false on failure.

example.title: Yaf_View_Simple::eval example
example.programlisting: "; /* render the template string without touching the filesystem */ $html = $this->getView()->eval($template, array("title" => "Breaking News")); $this->getResponse()->setBody($html); return false; // skip auto-rendering } } ?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get an assigned variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Gets a variable previously assigned to the view. When called without an argument, all assigned variables are returned.

listitem.simpara: The name of the variable to retrieve, or omitted/null to retrieve all assigned variables.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The value assigned under name, or null if there is no variable with that name. When called without an argument, an array of all assigned variables is returned.

example.title: Yaf_View_Simple::get example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class IndexController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction()
    {
        $view = $this->getView();
        $view->assign("foo", "bar");

        var_dump($view->get("foo"));
        var_dump($view->get()); // all assigned variables
    }
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the template directory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Gets the directory in which templates are looked up.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The template directory as a string, or null if it has not been set yet.

example.title: Yaf_View_Simple::getScriptPath example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class IndexController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction()
    {
        /* the directory in which templates are looked up,
         * usually application.view.directory */
        echo $this->getView()->getScriptPath();
    }
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check whether a variable is assigned

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Checks whether a variable is assigned to the view. This method is called when isset() is used on a view object.

listitem.simpara: The name of the variable to check.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if a variable is assigned under name, false otherwise.

example.title: Yaf_View_Simple::__isset example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class IndexController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction()
    {
        $view = $this->getView();
        $view->assign("title", "Welcome");

        var_dump(isset($view->title));
        var_dump(isset($view->unknown));
    }
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Render a template

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Renders a template and returns the result as a string. The template is included as a plain PHP script, so any PHP code in it is executed, and assigned variables are available under their names.

note.simpara: Unlike Yaf_View_Simple::display, the result is returned instead of being appended to the Yaf_Response_Abstract body.

listitem.simpara: The path to the template, relative to the template directory set by Yaf_View_Simple::setScriptPath or application.view.directory.
Optional variables to assign for this render; they override assigned variables with the same name.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The rendered result as a string, or false on failure.

example.title: Yaf_View_Simple::render example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class ProductController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function detailAction()
    {
        /* render the template and post-process the result */
        $html = $this->getView()->render("product/detail.phtml", array(
            "name"  => "Yaf in Action",
            "price" => "29.90",
        ));

        $this->getResponse()->setBody($html);
        return false; // skip auto-rendering
    }
}
?>

example.title: Template example
example.programlisting: Price: EUR
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Assign a variable via property write

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Assigns a variable to the view. This method is called when writing to a property of a view object, and behaves the same as Yaf_View_Simple::assign.

listitem.simpara: The name under which the variable becomes available to the template.
The value to assign.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Yaf_View_Simple::__set example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class IndexController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction()
    {
        $this->getView()->foo = "bar"; // same as assign("foo", "bar");
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set the template directory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sets the directory in which templates are looked up.

listitem.simpara: The directory where the template scripts are stored.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the view instance, or false if template_dir is not an absolute path.

example.title: Yaf_View_Simple::setScriptPath example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class IndexController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction()
    {
        /* render templates from another directory */
        $this->getView()->setScriptPath(APPLICATION_PATH . "/modules/admin/views");

        $this->getView()->display("dashboard/index.phtml");

        return false; // we rendered ourselves, skip auto-rendering
    }
}
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.para: Yaf_Loader introduces a comprehensive autoloading solution for Yaf.
The first time an instance of Yaf_Application is retrieved, Yaf_Loader will instance a singleton, and registers itself with spl_autoload. You retrieve an instance using the Yaf_Loader::getInstance

Yaf_Loader attempt to load a class only one shot, if failed, depend on yaf.use_spl_autoload, if this config is On Yaf_Loader::autoload will return false, thus give the chance to other autoload function. if it is Off (by default), Yaf_Loader::autoload will return true, and more important is that a very useful warning will be triggered (very useful to find out why a class could not be loaded).
Please keep yaf.use_spl_autoload Off unless there is some library have their own autoload mechanism and impossible to rewrite it.
By default, Yaf_Loader assume all library (class defined script) store in the global library directory, which is defined in the php.ini(yaf.library).

If you want Yaf_Loader search some classes(libraries) in the local class directory(which is defined in application.ini, and by default, it is application.directory . "/library"), you should register the class prefix using the Yaf_Loader::registerLocalNameSpace
You may noticed that all the folder with the first letter capitalized, you can make them lowercase by set yaf.lowcase_path = On in php.ini

Yaf_Loader is also designed to load the MVC classes, and the rule is:
MVC class loading example
Controller Classes => // APPLICATION_PATH/controllers/
Model Classes => // APPLICATION_PATH/models/
Plugin Classes => // APPLICATION_PATH/plugins/
Yaf identify a class's suffix(this is by default, you can also change to the prefix by change the configure yaf.name_suffix) to decide whether it is a MVC class:
MVC class distinctions
Controller Classes => // ***Controller
Model Classes => // ***Model
Plugin Classes => // ***Plugin
some examples:
MVC loading example
class IndexController // APPLICATION_PATH/controllers/Index.php
class DataModel => // APPLICATION_PATH/models/Data.php
class DummyPlugin => // APPLICATION_PATH/plugins/Dummy.php
class A_B_TestModel => // APPLICATION_PATH/models/A/B/Test.php
As of 2.1.18, Yaf supports Controllers autoloading for user script side, (which means the autoloading triggered by user php script, eg: access a controller static property in Bootstrap or Plugins), but autoloader only try to locate controller class script under the default module folder, which is "APPLICATION_PATH/controllers/".
also, the directory will be affected by yaf.lowcase_path.

listitem.para: By default, this value is application.directory . "/library", you can change this either in the application.ini(application.library) or call to Yaf_Loader::setLibraryPath

refnamediv.refpurpose: Autoload a class

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Load a class by its name. The class name is converted to a file path: underscores and namespace separators become directory separators.

MVC classes (classes whose names contain _Controller, _Action or _Plugin) are looked up under the application directory, while other classes are looked up in the library directories: the local library for locally registered class prefixes, otherwise the global library.

listitem.simpara: The class name to load.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success, or false on failure.

example.title: Yaf_Loader::autoload example
example.programlisting:
<?php
/*
 * autoload() is normally invoked implicitly by the engine
 * whenever an undefined class is referenced, but it can also
 * be called explicitly to force loading of a class file.
 */
$loader = Yaf_Loader::getInstance("/var/www/shop/application/library");

/* looks up /var/www/shop/application/library/Catalog/PriceService.php */
$loader->autoload("Catalog_PriceService");

/* MVC classes are looked up under the application directory */
$loader->autoload("ProductController");
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Clear registered namespaces

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Clear all registered local namespaces.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success.

example.title: Yaf_Loader::clearLocalNamespace example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app    = new Yaf_Application(__DIR__ . "/conf/application.ini");
$loader = Yaf_Loader::getInstance();

$loader->registerLocalNamespace(array("Models", "Services"));
var_dump(count($loader->getLocalNamespace()));

$loader->clearLocalNamespace();
var_dump(count($loader->getLocalNamespace()));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: The constructor is private

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Constructs a new loader. The constructor is private; Yaf_Loader is a singleton. Use Yaf_Loader::getInstance to obtain the instance.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Obtaining the Yaf_Loader singleton
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app = new Yaf_Application(__DIR__ . "/conf/application.ini");

/* the constructor is private; use getInstance() instead */
$loader = Yaf_Loader::getInstance();
var_dump($loader instanceof Yaf_Loader);

/* instantiating directly raises an Error */
try {
    $loader = new Yaf_Loader();
} catch (Error $e) {
    echo $e->getMessage(), PHP_EOL;
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: bool(true) Call to private Yaf_Loader::__construct() from global scope

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve the Yaf_Loader instance

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieve the singleton Yaf_Loader instance.
If the library paths are given, they are applied to the existing instance.

listitem.simpara: The local library directory, usually the same as the application.library.directory ini setting.
The global library directory. If not given, the local one is used.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The Yaf_Loader instance, or false if the loader has not been initialized (which is normally done by Yaf_Application).

example.title: Yaf_Loader::getInstance example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app = new Yaf_Application(__DIR__ . "/conf/application.ini");

/* Yaf_Application has initialized the loader, so the
 * singleton instance is available now */
$loader = Yaf_Loader::getInstance();
$loader->registerNamespace("Vendor", APPLICATION_PATH . "/library/Vendor");
?>

example.title: Yaf_Loader::getInstance before initialization
example.programlisting:
<?php
/* no Yaf_Application has been created yet */
var_dump(Yaf_Loader::getInstance());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve the library path

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieve the library directory.

listitem.simpara: Whether to retrieve the global library directory instead of the local one.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The library directory as a string, or an empty string when the global library directory is requested but not set.

example.title: Yaf_Loader::getLibraryPath example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$loader = Yaf_Loader::getInstance(
    "/var/www/shop/application/library",
    "/usr/local/share/yaf/library"
);

/* the local library directory */
echo $loader->getLibraryPath(), PHP_EOL;

/* the global library directory */
echo $loader->getLibraryPath(true), PHP_EOL;
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve registered namespaces

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieve all registered local namespaces and their paths.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: An array of the registered local namespaces, keyed by the namespace prefix, or an empty array if none are registered.

example.title: Yaf_Loader::getLocalNamespace example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app    = new Yaf_Application(__DIR__ . "/conf/application.ini");
$loader = Yaf_Loader::getInstance();

$loader->registerLocalNamespace("Models");
$loader->registerLocalNamespace("Vendor", APPLICATION_PATH . "/library/Vendor");

print_r($loader->getLocalNamespace());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve the library path of a class

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieve the library directory a class would be looked up in.

listitem.simpara: The class name whose library directory is requested.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The local library directory if the class belongs to a registered local namespace, otherwise the global library directory (falling back to the local one when the global one is not set).

example.title: Yaf_Loader::getNamespacePath example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app    = new Yaf_Application(__DIR__ . "/conf/application.ini");
$loader = Yaf_Loader::getInstance();

$loader->registerLocalNamespace("Models");
$loader->setLibraryPath("/usr/local/share/yaf/library", true);

/* "Models" is a registered local namespace */
echo $loader->getNamespacePath("Models_Product"), PHP_EOL;

/* other classes fall back to the global library directory */
echo $loader->getNamespacePath("Vendor_Payment"), PHP_EOL;
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of getLocalNamespace

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Alias of Yaf_Loader::getLocalNamespace.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: An array of the registered local namespaces, keyed by the namespace prefix, or an empty array if none are registered.

example.title: Yaf_Loader::getNamespaces example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app    = new Yaf_Application(__DIR__ . "/conf/application.ini");
$loader = Yaf_Loader::getInstance();
$loader->registerLocalNamespace(array("Models", "Services"));

/* getNamespaces() is an alias of getLocalNamespace() */
var_dump($loader->getNamespaces() === $loader->getLocalNamespace());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Load a PHP script

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Load a PHP script file once. If the file is not an absolute path, it is looked up under the local library directory.
A file is only included once; calling Yaf_Loader::import again with the same file returns true without re-including it.

listitem.simpara: The file to load.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success (including when the file was already loaded), or false on failure.

example.title: Yaf_Loader::import example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Bootstrap extends Yaf_Bootstrap_Abstract
{
    public function _initHelpers()
    {
        /* a relative path is looked up under the library
         * directory, i.e. APPLICATION_PATH/library/functions/format.php */
        Yaf_Loader::import("functions/format.php");
    }
}
?>

example.title: A file is imported only once
example.programlisting:
<?php
/* an absolute path is used as-is */
Yaf_Loader::import("/var/www/shop/application/library/Legacy/csv_export.php");

/* importing the same file again does nothing and returns true */
var_dump(
    Yaf_Loader::import("/var/www/shop/application/library/Legacy/csv_export.php")
);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Whether a class is local

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Determine whether a class name should be looked up in the local library directory, i.e. whether its prefix belongs to a registered local namespace.

listitem.simpara: The class name to check.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the class name belongs to a registered local namespace, false otherwise.

example.title: Yaf_Loader::isLocalName example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app    = new Yaf_Application(__DIR__ . "/conf/application.ini");
$loader = Yaf_Loader::getInstance();
$loader->registerLocalNamespace(array("Models", "Services"));

var_dump($loader->isLocalName("Models_Product"));
var_dump($loader->isLocalName("Vendor_Session"));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Register local namespace

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Register a local namespace. Classes whose prefix belongs to a local namespace are looked up under the given path (or the local library directory when no path is given) instead of the global one.
This lets you place your own classes into the local library directory, while shared classes live in the global library directory (see the yaf.library ini setting).

listitem.simpara: A namespace prefix string, or an array of prefix/path pairs (when the value is a path string) or prefix strings.

A prefix only matches at an underscore or backslash boundary: registering Models makes Models_User and Models itself local, but not ModelsUser. A leading backslash is ignored, and a class name written with backslashes is looked up as if they were underscores.
The directory to look up the namespace in. If not given, the local library directory is used.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the loader instance itself on success, or false if an invalid parameter is provided.

example.title: Yaf_Loader::registerLocalNamespace example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Bootstrap extends Yaf_Bootstrap_Abstract
{
    public function _initLoader()
    {
        $loader = Yaf_Loader::getInstance();

        /* Models_User is now looked up in
         * APPLICATION_PATH/library/Models/User.php */
        $loader->registerLocalNamespace("Models");

        /* register several prefixes at once, each with its
         * own lookup directory */
        $loader->registerLocalNamespace(array(
            "Services" => APPLICATION_PATH . "/services",
            "Vendor"   => APPLICATION_PATH . "/vendor",
        ));
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of registerLocalNamespace

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Alias of Yaf_Loader::registerLocalNamespace.

listitem.simpara: A namespace prefix string, or an array of prefix/path pairs (when the value is a path string) or prefix strings.
The directory to look up the namespace in. If not given, the local library directory is used.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the loader instance itself on success, or false if an invalid parameter is provided.

example.title: Yaf_Loader::registerNamespace example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Bootstrap extends Yaf_Bootstrap_Abstract
{
    public function _initLoader()
    {
        /* registerNamespace() is an alias of registerLocalNamespace() */
        Yaf_Loader::getInstance()->registerNamespace(
            "Vendor",
            APPLICATION_PATH . "/library/Vendor"
        );
    }
}

/* new Vendor_Payment_Gateway() is now looked up in
 * APPLICATION_PATH/library/Vendor/Payment/Gateway.php */
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Change the library path

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Change the library directory.

listitem.simpara: The new library directory.
Whether to change the global library directory instead of the local one.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the loader instance itself.

example.title: Yaf_Loader::setLibraryPath example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$app    = new Yaf_Application(__DIR__ . "/conf/application.ini");
$loader = Yaf_Loader::getInstance();

/* change the local library directory */
$loader->setLibraryPath("/var/www/shop/application/library");

/* change the global library directory */
$loader->setLibraryPath("/usr/local/share/yaf/library", true);

echo $loader->getLibraryPath(), PHP_EOL;
echo $loader->getLibraryPath(true), PHP_EOL;
?>
