section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Route_Static is the default route of Yaf_Router: it parses the URI path as /module/controller/action segments and is designed to handle most routing needs out of the box.

note.simpara: It is unnecessary to instantiate a Yaf_Route_Static, or to add it to the route stack of Yaf_Router: there is always one present in the stack, and it is always tried last.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Assemble a url

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Assemble a url.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a string.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: Throws Yaf_Exception_TypeError if info keys ':c' and ':a' are not set.

example.title: Yaf_Route_Static::assembleexample
example.programlisting:
<?php

$router = new Yaf_Router();

$route  = new Yaf_Route_Static();

$router->addRoute("static", $route);

var_dump($router->getRoute('static')->assemble(
            array(
                ':a' => 'yafaction',
                'tkey' => 'tval',
                ':c' => 'yafcontroller',
                ':m' => 'yafmodule'
            ),
        )
);

var_dump($router->getRoute('static')->assemble(
            array(
                ':a' => 'yafaction',
                'tkey' => 'tval',
                ':c' => 'yafcontroller',
                ':m' => 'yafmodule'
            ),
            array(
                'tkey1' => 'tval1',
                'tkey2' => 'tval2'
            )
        )
);
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Whether the route matches a URI

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Determine whether the static route matches a URI. Since the static route matches any URI, this method always returns true.

listitem.simpara: The URI to check.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Always returns true.

example.title: Yaf_Route_Static::match example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$route = new Yaf_Route_Static();

/* the static route matches any URI */
var_dump($route->match("/product/detail/id/10"));
var_dump($route->match("/"));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Route a request

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Route the request according to the PATH_INFO style URI: the first path segment is treated as the module name only if it is one of the registered modules, otherwise the segments are mapped to the controller and the action in order. The remaining segments become request parameters.
For example, with no module named foo, /foo/bar/age/10 routes to the controller Foo, the action bar, with a parameter age of 10.

listitem.simpara: The Yaf_Request_Abstract instance to route.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Always returns true.

example.title: Yaf_Route_Static::route example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$request = new Yaf_Request_Http("/product/detail/id/10");

/* the static route is the default route of Yaf_Router,
 * registered under the name "_default" */
$route = Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->getRouter()->getRoute("_default");
var_dump($route->route($request));

var_dump($request->getControllerName());
var_dump($request->getActionName());
var_dump($request->getParam("id"));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Route_Supervar is a built-in route that resolves the request target from a single GET parameter (the supervar). The value of that parameter is parsed the same way as PATH_INFO, so a request such as /?r=/user/list maps to controller user and action list when the supervar name is r.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Assemble a url

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Assemble a url.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a string.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: Throws Yaf_Exception_TypeError if info keys ':c' and ':a' are not set.

example.title: Yaf_Route_Supervar::assemble example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$router = new Yaf_Router();

$route  = new Yaf_Route_Supervar('r');

$router->addRoute("supervar", $route);

var_dump($router->getRoute('supervar')->assemble(
        array(
              ':a' => 'yafaction',
              'tkey' => 'tval',
              ':c' => 'yafcontroller',
              ':m' => 'yafmodule'
        ),
        array(
              'tkey1' => 'tval1',
              'tkey2' => 'tval2'
        )
));

try {
var_dump($router->getRoute('supervar')->assemble(
        array(
              ':a' => 'yafaction',
              'tkey' => 'tval',
              ':m' => 'yafmodule'
        ),
        array(
              'tkey1' => 'tval1',
              'tkey2' => 'tval2',
              1 => array(),
        )
));
} catch (Exception $e) {
    var_dump($e->getMessage());
}
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: string(%d) "?r=/yafmodule/yafcontroller/yafaction&tkey1=tval1&tkey2=tval2" string(%d) "You need to specify the controller by ':c'"

refnamediv.refpurpose: Construct a supervar route

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Construct a supervar route. A supervar route expects a query variable to carry a PATH_INFO style URI.

listitem.simpara: The name of the query variable that carries the URI.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Yaf_Route_Supervar::__construct example
example.programlisting: <?php /** * Add a supervar route to the Yaf_Router route stack. * * The URI is expected in the query variable named below, * e.g. http://yourdomain.com/index.php?_url=/product/detail/id/10 */ Yaf_Dispatcher::getInstance()->getRouter()->addRoute("supervar", new Yaf_Route_Supervar("_url") ); ?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen:
/* http://yourdomain.com/index.php?_url=/product/detail/id/10 * routes to the following values: */ array( "controller" => "product", "module" => "index", //(default) "action" => "detail", //(default) )
/** * and request parameters: */ array( "id" => 10 )

refnamediv.refpurpose: Route a request

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Route the request with a super variable: the query variable named as the one given to the constructor is expected to carry a PATH_INFO style URI, which is then parsed like Yaf_Route_Static does.

listitem.simpara: The Yaf_Request_Abstract instance to route.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the variable is present and holds a string, false otherwise, which makes the router try the next route.

example.title: Yaf_Route_Supervar::route example
example.programlisting:
<?php
/* assume the request was made with
 * http://yourdomain.com/index.php?_url=/product/detail/id/10 */
$request = new Yaf_Request_Http("/index.php");

$route = new Yaf_Route_Supervar("_url");
var_dump($route->route($request));

var_dump($request->getControllerName());
var_dump($request->getActionName());
var_dump($request->getParam("id"));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Session is a namespaced wrapper around PHP's native session support. It is accessed as a singleton through Yaf_Session::getInstance and works directly on $_SESSION: session data written through one interface is visible in the other.

Session entries can be accessed and manipulated through property syntax, method calls (Yaf_Session::get, Yaf_Session::set, Yaf_Session::del, Yaf_Session::has), array access (ArrayAccess), iteration (Iterator) and count().

refnamediv.refpurpose: Constructor of Yaf_Session

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The constructor is private: Yaf_Session implements the singleton pattern and cannot be instantiated directly. Use Yaf_Session::getInstance to obtain the session instance.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Yaf_Session::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// The constructor is private, so Yaf_Session cannot be
// instantiated with "new". Access it through the singleton:
$session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
$session->start();

$session->set("user_id", 42);
echo $session->get("user_id");
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Count session entries

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns the number of entries in the session.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The number of session entries as an integer.

example.title: Yaf_Session::count example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
$session->start();

$session->set("user_id", 42);
$session->set("cart_items", 3);

var_dump(count($session));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get current session entry value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns the value of the current session entry during iteration.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The value of the current session entry.

example.title: Yaf_Session::current example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
$session->start();

$session->set("user_id", 42);
$session->set("is_vip", true);

foreach ($session as $key => $value) {
    // Yaf_Session::current() yields each value while iterating
    echo "$key => ";
    var_dump($value);
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Remove a session key

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Removes a session key and its value.

listitem.simpara: The session key to remove.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success, or false on failure.

example.title: Yaf_Session::del example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class VerifyController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function captchaAction()
    {
        $session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
        $session->start();

        $expected = $session->get("captcha_code");

        // one-time code: remove it right after use
        $session->del("captcha_code");

        if ($expected === null
            || $this->getRequest()->getPost("code") !== $expected) {
            echo "invalid captcha";
        }
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get a session value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieves a session value by name. If name is omitted or null, the entire session array is returned.

listitem.simpara: The session key to retrieve, or null to get all session data.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The session value, or null if the key does not exist. When name is null, the full session array is returned.

example.title: Yaf_Session::get example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class ProfileController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction()
    {
        $session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
        $session->start();

        $userId = $session->get("user_id");
        if ($userId === null) {
            return $this->redirect("/account/login");
        }

        echo "welcome back, user #", $userId;
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the session singleton

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns the singleton Yaf_Session instance, creating it if necessary. The session is started automatically on first access.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The Yaf_Session singleton instance, or null if the session could not be started.

example.title: Yaf_Session::getInstance example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
$session->start();
$session->set("user_id", 42);

// ... later, elsewhere in the application
$same = Yaf_Session::getInstance();

var_dump($same === $session);
var_dump($same->get("user_id"));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check if a session key exists

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Checks whether a session key exists.

listitem.simpara: The session key to check.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the key exists, false otherwise.

example.title: Yaf_Session::has example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class BaseController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function requireLogin()
    {
        $session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
        $session->start();

        if (!$session->has("user_id")) {
            $this->redirect("/account/login");
            return false;
        }

        return true;
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check if a session key exists

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Checks whether a session key exists. This method is an alias of Yaf_Session::has and is called when isset() is used on a session object.

listitem.simpara: The session key to check.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the key exists, false otherwise.

example.title: Yaf_Session::__isset example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
$session->start();

$session->user_id = 42;

var_dump(isset($session->user_id));
var_dump(isset($session->user_name));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get current session entry key

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns the key of the current session entry during iteration.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The key of the current session entry.

example.title: Yaf_Session::key example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
$session->start();

$session->set("user_id", 42);
$session->set("lang", "en");

for ($session->rewind(); $session->valid(); $session->next()) {
    echo $session->key(), " => ", var_export($session->current(), true), PHP_EOL;
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Advance to next session entry

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Moves the internal iterator to the next session entry.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Yaf_Session::next example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
$session->start();

$session->set("user_id", 42);
$session->set("lang", "en");

$session->rewind();
echo $session->key(), PHP_EOL;

$session->next();
echo $session->key(), PHP_EOL;
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check if a session key exists (ArrayAccess)

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Checks whether a session key exists. This method is an alias of Yaf_Session::has and is called when isset() is used with array syntax.

listitem.simpara: The session key to check.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the key exists, false otherwise.

example.title: Yaf_Session::offsetExists example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
$session->start();

$session["user_id"] = 42;

var_dump(isset($session["user_id"]));
var_dump(isset($session["user_name"]));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get a session value (ArrayAccess)

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieves a session value by key. This method is an alias of Yaf_Session::get and is called when array syntax is used to read a session object.

listitem.simpara: The session key to retrieve.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The session value, or null if the key does not exist.

example.title: Yaf_Session::offsetGet example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class IndexController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction()
    {
        $session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
        $session->start();

        // reading with array syntax calls offsetGet()
        $userId = $session["user_id"];
        if ($userId === null) {
            return $this->redirect("/account/login");
        }

        echo "logged in as user #", $userId;
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set a session value (ArrayAccess)

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sets a session value. This method is called when array syntax is used to write to a session object.

listitem.simpara: The session key to set.
The value to store.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Yaf_Session::offsetSet example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class LoginController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction()
    {
        // ... verify the credentials against the database
        $session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
        $session->start();

        // writing with array syntax calls offsetSet()
        $session["user_id"] = $user->getId();
        $session["login_time"] = time();

        return $this->redirect("/dashboard");
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Remove a session key (ArrayAccess)

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Removes a session key and its value. This method is called when unset() is used with array syntax on a session object.

listitem.simpara: The session key to remove.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Yaf_Session::offsetUnset example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
$session->start();

$session["captcha_code"] = "8X2Q";

// ... after verifying the captcha, drop the one-time code
unset($session["captcha_code"]);

var_dump(isset($session["captcha_code"]));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Reset session iterator to first entry

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Rewinds the internal iterator to the first session entry.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Yaf_Session::rewind example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
$session->start();

$session->set("user_id", 42);
$session->set("lang", "en");

foreach ($session as $key => $value) {
    echo "$key => $value", PHP_EOL;
}

// a new foreach implicitly calls rewind() again
foreach ($session as $key => $value) {
    echo "$key => $value", PHP_EOL;
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: user_id => 42 lang => en user_id => 42 lang => en

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set a session value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sets a session value.

listitem.simpara: The session key to set.
The value to store.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success, or false on failure.

example.title: Yaf_Session::set example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class LoginController extends Yaf_Controller_Abstract
{
    public function indexAction()
    {
        // ... verify the credentials against the database
        $session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
        $session->start();

        $session->set("user_id", $user->getId());
        $session->set("login_time", time());

        return $this->redirect("/dashboard");
    }
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Start the session

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Starts the session if it has not been started yet. This calls PHP's native session start mechanism. Calling this method multiple times is safe.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the Yaf_Session instance.

example.title: Yaf_Session::start example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// typically done once per request, e.g. in a bootstrap
$session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
$session->start();

$session->set("user_id", 42);
echo $session->get("user_id");
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Remove a session key

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Removes a session key and its value. This method is called when unset() is used on a session object property.

listitem.simpara: The session key to remove.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Yaf_Session::__unset example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();
$session->start();

$session->user_id = 42;

// ... when the user logs out
unset($session->user_id);

var_dump(isset($session->user_id));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check if current session position is valid

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Checks whether the current session iterator position is valid.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the current position is valid, false otherwise.

example.title: Yaf_Session::valid example

<?php
$session = Yaf_Session::getInstance();

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Exception is the base class of all exceptions thrown by Yaf. Every other Yaf exception class extends it.
It extends RuntimeException when the SPL extension is loaded, and the built-in Exception otherwise. Exceptions raised by Yaf carry an error code that identifies the type of failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Construct a Yaf exception

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Constructs a new Yaf_Exception. The code carries the Yaf error code that identifies the type of failure, and is exposed via Exception::getCode.

listitem.simpara: The exception message.
The Yaf error code.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Yaf_Exception::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php
throw new Yaf_Exception(
    "Failed to find the controller 'Product'",
    YAF_ERR_NOTFOUND_CONTROLLER /* 516 */
);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: PHP Fatal error: Uncaught Yaf_Exception: Failed to find the controller 'Product' in /path/to/index.php:2

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve the previous exception

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This method is inherited from the base Throwable hierarchy and returns the exception that was chained as the previous one, if any.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the previous Throwable if available, null otherwise.

example.title: Yaf_Exception::getPrevious example
example.programlisting:
<?php
try {
    $previous = new RuntimeException("Failed to open view script", 1024);
    throw new Yaf_Exception(
        "Failed to dispatch the request",
        YAF_ERR_DISPATCH_FAILED,
        $previous
    );
} catch (Yaf_Exception $e) {
    var_dump($e->getCode());
    $prev = $e->getPrevious();
    var_dump(get_class($prev));
    var_dump($prev->getMessage());
    var_dump($prev->getCode());
}
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: int(514) string(16) "RuntimeException" string(26) "Failed to open view script" int(1024)

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Exception_TypeError is thrown when an argument passed to a Yaf method is of an unexpected type or an invalid value. Its error code is 521.

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Exception_StartupError is thrown when the application fails to start up, i.e. when an error occurs during the initialization of Yaf_Application before routing begins. Its error code is 512.

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Exception_DispatchFailed is thrown when the dispatcher fails to dispatch the routed request to a controller action. Its error code is 514.

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Exception_RouterFailed is thrown when routing fails, for instance when no registered route matches the incoming request. Its error code is 513.

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Exception_LoadFailed is thrown when the loader fails to load a required script. Its error code is 520. The more specific failures are represented by its subclasses Yaf_Exception_LoadFailed_Module, Yaf_Exception_LoadFailed_Controller, Yaf_Exception_LoadFailed_Action and Yaf_Exception_LoadFailed_View.

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Exception_LoadFailed_Module is thrown when the requested module cannot be found or loaded. Its error code is 515.

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Exception_LoadFailed_Controller is thrown when the requested controller cannot be found or loaded. Its error code is 516.

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Exception_LoadFailed_Action is thrown when the requested action cannot be found or loaded. Its error code is 517.

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaf_Exception_LoadFailed_View is thrown when the requested view (template) script cannot be found or loaded. Its error code is 518.

preface.title: Introduction
preface.simpara: Yet Another Configurations Container (Yaconf) is a configuration container. It parses INI files when PHP starts up and keeps the result in persistent memory for the whole PHP lifecycle, so every retrieval is a fast hash lookup with no file I/O and no per-request parsing.

Yaconf stores all configurations as interned strings or immutable arrays. They are not refcounted, so retrieving a configuration from Yaconf is effectively zero-copy. Since Yaconf 1.2.0, the whole parsed configuration tree is additionally compacted into a single contiguous block, which lowers memory overhead and improves cache locality.

The parsed configuration lives in persistent memory shared by all PHP-FPM workers through copy-on-write: until a configuration file changes, the workers share the same physical memory pages no matter how many of them are running.

Yaconf supports sections and section inheritance in INI files. On non-ZTS builds it also reloads the files automatically when they change; on ZTS (thread-safe) builds, configurations are loaded at startup and a restart is required to pick up changes.

Since Yaconf 1.2.0, sub-directories of the configured directory are loaded recursively (up to 16 levels deep) and addressed with the directory name as a key level: for example, Yaconf::get("users.database.master") reads the master key from the file database.ini placed in the users/ sub-directory.

Storing sensitive configurations outside the web tree also lowers the attack surface. Configuration files under the web root can be retrieved by an attacker, for example through a file disclosure vulnerability. With Yaconf, the .ini files can instead be placed in a directory readable only by root, such as /etc/yaconf: the PHP-FPM master loads the configurations when the service starts, while the forked workers — which run under an unprivileged user and are the ones executing web requests — do not need, and are not given, access to that directory.
Yaconf requires PHP 7.0 or greater.

section.title: Requirements
section.para: Yaconf requires PHP 7.0 and above.

section.title: Installation
section.simpara: Yaconf can be installed in one of three ways: via PECL, via PIE, or by building it from source.
section.para: This PECL extension is not bundled with PHP.

Information for installing this PECL extension may be found in the manual chapter titled Installation of PECL extensions. Additional information such as new releases, downloads, source files, maintainer information, and a CHANGELOG, can be located here: https://pecl.php.net/package/yaconf.
Windows binaries (DLL files) for this PECL extension are available from the PECL website.

example.title: Installing Yaconf with PECL
example.programlisting: pecl install yaconf

section.simpara: Since Yaconf 1.2.0, the extension can be installed with PIE, the PHP Installer for Extensions, by running the following on the command line.

example.title: Installing Yaconf with PIE
example.programlisting: pie install laruence/yaconf

section.simpara: The source code is hosted on GitHub. To build the extension from source, run the following on the command line, replacing the paths with those of the local PHP installation.

example.title: Building Yaconf from source
example.programlisting: /path/to/phpize ./configure --with-php-config=/path/to/php-config make && make install

section.title: Runtime Configuration
section.simpara: The behaviour of these functions is affected by settings in php.ini.
Here's a short explanation of the configuration directives.

listitem.simpara: The directory where all INI configuration files are placed. Only files with the .ini extension are loaded. Sub-directories are loaded recursively (up to 16 levels deep); each one acts as a key level, so a file database.ini placed in the users/ sub-directory is addressed as "users.database". Available since Yaconf 1.2.0; before that only files directly in the directory were loaded.
The examples below assume the following database.ini placed in the configured directory, alongside a features.ini that carries per-feature settings.

example.title: INI file syntax
example.programlisting:
; database.ini name=production ; scalar value version=PHP_VERSION ; PHP constants are resolved connection_string=${DATABASE_URL} ; environment variables are resolved options.max_connections=50 ; nested hash key options.timeout=30
; array entries, both notations are equivalent replicas.0=replica-1.example.com replicas[]=replica-2.example.com

example.title: INI sections example
example.programlisting:
; features.ini [default] cache_enabled=on rate_limit=100
; the "premium" section inherits every key from "default" and ; overrides the ones it redefines [premium:default] rate_limit=1000

listitem.simpara: The interval, in seconds, at which Yaconf checks whether any loaded INI file has changed and reloads the changed ones (the change is detected by comparing directory modification times). Setting it to 0 makes Yaconf check on every request.

note.simpara: This directive is only registered in non-ZTS builds. On ZTS (thread-safe) builds configurations are loaded at startup and automatic reloading is not available; restart PHP to pick up changes.

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Yaconf is a configurations container, it parses INI files, stores the result in PHP when PHP is started, the result lives with the whole PHP lifecycle.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Inspect how a configuration value is stored

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns debugging information about the value stored under name: the memory address of the stored value and whether the value still lives inside Yaconf's compacted storage block.

warning.simpara: This method exists solely for Yaconf's own test suite, which uses it to verify that the extension is working correctly. Do not use it in production code, and do not rely on the format of its output: the returned array may change at any time.

listitem.simpara: The configuration name to inspect, using the same dot notation as Yaconf::get.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: An array with four entries when the configuration exists, null otherwise:

listitem.simpara: key — the name that was looked up.
address — the memory address of the stored value. Values are stored as interned strings or immutable arrays, so this address stays constant until the configuration is reloaded.
val — the stored value itself.

changed — false while the value's data still lives inside the compacted storage block, meaning the operating system has not had to copy the page (copy-on-write still applies); true when the value has been re-allocated outside the block.

example.title: Yaconf::__debug_info example
example.programlisting:
<?php // assuming app.ini contains name="shop" var_dump(Yaconf::__debug_info("app.name")); /* array(4) { ["key"]=> string(8) "app.name" ["address"]=> string(14) "0x7f8b1c0a3d20" ["val"]=> string(4) "shop" ["changed"]=> bool(false) } */
var_dump(Yaconf::__debug_info("app.missing")); // NULL ?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve a configuration value by name

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Retrieves the configuration value stored under name. Names use dot notation to traverse nested keys: "app" addresses the whole parsed app.ini file, "app.name" a key inside it, and since Yaconf 1.2.0 "users.database.master" a key in the file database.ini placed in the users/ sub-directory. The dot notation supports up to 64 levels of nesting.

listitem.simpara: The configuration name to look up, using dot notation to traverse nested keys, for example "app.name", "app.features.1" or, since Yaconf 1.2.0, "users.database.master" for files in sub-directories.
The value to return when name is not found. When omitted, null is returned.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The stored configuration value, a string or an array, when name exists; otherwise the default (or null when no default was given).

refsect1.title: Examples
refsect1.simpara: The examples below assume the following two files placed in the directory configured with yaconf.directory.
refsect1.programlisting: ; app.ini name="shop" ; scalar value debug=0 ; number features[]="checkout" ; array entries, both notations features.1="wishlist"
; users/database.ini, in a sub-directory (Yaconf 1.2.0+) master="192.168.0.10" replica="192.168.0.20"

example.title: Yaconf::get example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// fetch a whole parsed file as an array
var_dump(Yaconf::get("app"));

// dot notation traverses nested keys
var_dump(Yaconf::get("app.name"));           // string(4) "shop"
var_dump(Yaconf::get("app.features.1"));     // string(8) "wishlist"

// since 1.2.0: files in sub-directories are namespaced by the
// directory name
var_dump(Yaconf::get("users.database.master")); // string(12) "192.168.0.10"

// when the key is missing, the default is returned
var_dump(Yaconf::get("app.missing"));             // NULL
var_dump(Yaconf::get("app.missing", "fallback")); // string(8) "fallback"
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check whether a configuration value exists

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Determines whether a configuration value exists under name, which uses the same dot notation as Yaconf::get: for example, "app.name" or, since Yaconf 1.2.0, "users.database.master" for files in sub-directories.

listitem.simpara: The configuration name to look up, using dot notation to traverse nested keys, for example "app.name" or "users.database.master".

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if a configuration value exists at name, false otherwise.

refsect1.title: Examples
refsect1.simpara: The examples below assume an app.ini placed in the directory configured with yaconf.directory, holding the keys name="shop" and debug=0.

example.title: Yaconf::has example
example.programlisting:
<?php
var_dump(Yaconf::has("app.name"));     // bool(true)
var_dump(Yaconf::has("app.missing"));  // bool(false)

// useful to distinguish a stored empty value from a missing key,
// where Yaconf::get() would return the same default for both
if (Yaconf::has("app.debug")) {
    $debug = (bool) Yaconf::get("app.debug");
}
?>

preface.title: Introduction
preface.simpara: Taint is an extension for detecting XSS code (tainted strings). It can also be used to spot SQL injection, command injection, file path injection and similar vulnerabilities.

When taint is enabled, strings received from user input — $_GET, $_POST and $_COOKIE — are marked as tainted at request startup, and the mark is tracked through string operations. When a tainted string reaches a dangerous sink (output, SQL query, shell command, file path, ...), taint raises a warning pointing at that spot. See Propagation and Checked Sinks for the complete lists.

Taint is a development and auditing tool, not a runtime defense: it only reports possible problems and never blocks or alters data. It is deliberately conservative and may over-report, so a clean run means only "nothing taint could see", never "provably secure". Do not enable it in production environments.

example.title: Taint example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$a = trim($_GET['a']);

$file_name = '/tmp/' . $a;
$output    = "Welcome, {$a} !!!";
$sql       = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = " . $a;

echo $output;
print $output;
include $file_name;
mysqli_query($link, $sql);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen:
Warning: main() [echo]: Attempt to echo a string that might be tainted in /path/to/script.php on line 9
Warning: main() [print]: Attempt to print a string that might be tainted in /path/to/script.php on line 10
Warning: main() [include]: File path contains data that might be tainted in /path/to/script.php on line 11
Warning: main() [mysqli_query]: SQL statement contains data that might be tainted in /path/to/script.php on line 12

section.title: Requirements
section.simpara: Taint 3.x requires PHP 8.0 or newer. For PHP 7.x use the taint 2.1.x releases, and for PHP 5.x the taint 1.x releases.

section.title: Installation
section.simpara: Information for installing this PECL extension may be found in the manual chapter titled Installation of PECL extensions. Additional information such as new releases, downloads, source files, maintainer information, and a CHANGELOG, can be located here: https://pecl.php.net/package/taint.
Install it with PECL:
section.para:
The source code is hosted on GitHub. To build the extension from source:
$ git clone https://github.com/laruence/taint.git $ cd taint $ phpize $ ./configure $ make $ sudo make install
section.simpara: Then enable the extension by adding extension=taint.so (or extension=php_taint.dll on Windows) to php.ini, and set taint.enable to 1.

warning.simpara: Taint is a development and auditing tool. Do not enable it in production environments: the instrumentation slows every request down and disables the OPcache JIT, and the warnings may leak request data into logs.

section.title: Runtime Configuration
section.simpara: The behaviour of these functions is affected by settings in php.ini.
Here's a short explanation of the configuration directives.

listitem.simpara: Master switch. When enabled, taint hooks the executor and marks strings from $_GET, $_POST and $_COOKIE as tainted at request startup.
This is an php.ini-only directive: enabling it requires a process restart, so it cannot be toggled per request or per directory.

note.simpara: Do not enable this directive in production environments: the instrumentation slows every request down and is incompatible with the OPcache JIT.

listitem.simpara: The error level used when taint reports a possibly tainted string. Defaults to E_USER_WARNING (512).
Because this directive is INI_ALL, it can be changed at runtime. For example, to silence taint warnings for the current script:

para.programlisting:
<?php
ini_set('taint.error_level', 0);
?>

section.title: Resource Types
section.simpara: Taint defines no resource types. The taint mark itself is stored in the internal zend_string structure, not in a user-visible resource.

section.title: How the taint mark is propagated
section.simpara: The taint mark is a single bit stored on the string itself, not on the variable holding it. Assigning, passing or otherwise sharing a tainted string keeps the mark. String concatenation and interpolation propagate it as well:

table.title: Operators which propagate the taint mark

row.entry: "{$var}" (string interpolation, including the ROPE fast path)

section.simpara: In addition, taint understands a fixed set of string functions: when any of the relevant string arguments is tainted, the returned string is marked tainted too. Both the regular call and, on PHP 8.4+, the frameless fast-path call are covered.

table.title: Functions which propagate the taint mark

row.entry: explode (every element of the resulting array)
implode/join (a tainted separator taints the result as well)
sprintf, vsprintf (only the %s specifier carries the mark; sprintf("%d", $t) returns a clean string)

section.simpara: Any function taint does not explicitly understand returns a fresh, unmarked string — including escaping helpers such as htmlspecialchars, htmlentities or mysqli_real_escape_string. This is deliberate: taint over-reports rather than trying to decide whether a value is safe for a particular output context. Use untaint to clear the mark on values you have validated yourself.

section.title: Where taint raises warnings
section.simpara: When a tainted string reaches one of the sinks below, taint raises a warning (by default an E_USER_WARNING; the level is configurable via taint.error_level). Only top-level string arguments are inspected; dumping an array that merely contains tainted values does not warn.

row.entry: the format string and the substituted values
the value being dumped, when it is a string
both the source and destination paths
mysql_query, sqlite_query, sqlite_single_query, oci_parse, pg_query, pg_send_query
exec, system, passthru, shell_exec (including the backtick operator)
dynamic calls such as $func(), $obj->$method(), call_user_func, array callables
preg_match, preg_match_all, preg_replace, preg_split, preg_grep, preg_replace_callback
the pattern (and the callback name for preg_replace_callback)
to, subject, additional parameters and additional headers (the message body is content and is not checked)

section.simpara: Warnings follow the format function_name() [sink]: message, where sink identifies the checked operation (for example echo, include or the function name) and the message describes what was found to be possibly tainted.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check whether a string is tainted

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Checks whether the given value carries the taint mark. Only strings can ever be tainted; any other type returns false.

listitem.simpara: The value to check.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the value is a tainted string, false otherwise. Always returns false when taint.enable is off.

example.title: is_tainted example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$name = $_GET['name'] ?? 'world';
var_dump(is_tainted($name));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Mark strings as tainted

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Manually marks the given strings as tainted, as if they had arrived from user input. The variables are passed by reference, but the mark itself is stored on the string rather than on the variable: every variable sharing the same string becomes tainted at once.
This is mainly useful for testing, and for simulating user input in CLI scripts where the $_GET, $_POST and $_COOKIE superglobals are not populated.

listitem.simpara: A variable holding the string to mark.
Further variables to mark.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Always returns true. When taint.enable is off, the function does nothing and still returns true.

example.title: taint example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$name = "world";
taint($name);
var_dump(is_tainted($name));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

note.simpara: Only non-empty strings are marked; variables holding other types, or empty strings, are silently ignored.
Interned, persistent and permanent strings (string literals, opcache shared strings) can never carry the mark and are silently skipped.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Remove the taint mark from strings

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Clears the taint mark on the given strings.

The mark is stored on the string itself, not on the variable, so this clears it for every variable sharing the same string at once. Use it to whitelist values you have validated yourself, for example after a strict allow-list check.

listitem.simpara: A variable holding the string to clean.
Further variables to clean.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Always returns true. When taint.enable is off, the function does nothing and still returns true.

example.title: untaint example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$id = "42";
taint($id);
if (preg_match('/^\d+$/', $id)) {
    // strictly validated as digits: safe to trust
    untaint($id);
}
var_dump(is_tainted($id));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

note.simpara: Only string values can carry the mark; passing a non-string is a no-op.

preface.title: Introduction
preface.para: Efficient data structures for PHP 7, provided as an alternative to the array.
See this blog post for benchmarks, discussion and frequently asked questions.

section.title: Requirements
section.para: PHP 7 is required by both the extension and the compatibility polyfill.

section.title: Installation
section.para:
The easiest way to install the extension is via PECL
pecl install ds

You can also build directly from source:
# Dependencies you might need to install # sudo apt-get install git build-essential php7.0-dev
git clone https://github.com/php-ds/extension "php-ds" cd php-ds
# Build and install the extension phpize ./configure make make install
# Clean up the build files make clean phpize --clean

note.para: If you're using Composer, it's highly recommended that you include php-ds/php-ds in your project so that your code is still functional in an environment where the extension is not installed. The extension will take priority if installed.

example.title: Vector
example.programlisting:
<?php

$vector = new \Ds\Vector();

$vector->push('a');
$vector->push('b', 'c');

$vector[] = 'd';

print_r($vector);

?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: Ds\Vector Object ( [0] => a [1] => b [2] => c [3] => d )

example.title: Map
example.programlisting:
<?php

$map = new \Ds\Map();

$map->put('a', 1);
$map->put('b', 2);

$map['c'] = 3;

print_r($map);

?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen:
Ds\Map Object ( [0] => Ds\Pair Object ( [key] => a [value] => 1 )
[1] => Ds\Pair Object ( [key] => b [value] => 2 )
[2] => Ds\Pair Object ( [key] => c [value] => 3 )
)

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Collection is the base interface which covers functionality common to all the data structures in this library. It guarantees that all structures are traversable, countable, and can be converted to json using json_encode.

row.entry: Collection implements IteratorAggregate now instead of just Traversable. (This change came to the polyfill in 1.4.1.)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Removes all values

refsect1.title: Description

refsect1.title: Parameters

refsect1.title: Return Values

example.title: Ds\Collection::clear example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$collection = new \Ds\Vector([1, 2, 3]);
print_r($collection);

$collection->clear();
print_r($collection);
?>

$a = new \Ds\Vector([1, 2, 3]);

refsect1.para: Converts the collection to an array.

note.para: Casting to an array is not supported yet.

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Hashable is an interface which allows objects to be used as keys. It’s an alternative to spl_object_hash, which determines an object’s hash based on its handle: this means that two objects that are considered equal by an implicit definition would not be treated as equal because they are not the same instance.

hash is used to return a scalar value to be used as the object's hash value, which determines where it goes in the hash table. While this value does not have to be unique, objects which are equal must have the same hash value.
equals is used to determine if two objects are equal. It's guaranteed that the comparing object will be an instance of the same class as the subject.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Determines whether an object is equal to the current instance

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Determines whether another object is equal to the current instance.
This method allows objects to be used as keys in structures such as Ds\Map and Ds\Set, or any other lookup structure that honors this interface.

note.para: It's guaranteed that obj is an instance of the same class.

caution.para: It's important that objects which are equal also have the same hash value. See Ds\Hashable::hash.

listitem.para: The object to compare the current instance to, which is always an instance of the same class.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: true if equal, false otherwise.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns a scalar value to be used as a hash value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns a scalar value to be used as the hash value of the objects.

While the hash value does not define equality, all objects that are equal according to Ds\Hashable::equals must have the same hash value. Hash values of equal objects don't have to be unique, for example you could just return true for all objects and nothing would break - the only implication would be that hash tables then turn into linked lists because all your objects will be hashed to the same bucket. It's therefore very important that you pick a good hash value, such as an ID or email address.
This method allows objects to be used as keys in structures such as Ds\Map and Ds\Set, or any other lookup structure that honors this interface.

caution.para: Do not pick a value that might change within the object, such as a public property. Hash table lookups would fail because the hash has changed.
All objects that are equal must have the same hash value.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A scalar value to be used as this object's hash value.

example.title: Ds\Hashable::hash example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class HashableObject implements \Ds\Hashable
{
    private $name;
    private $email;

    public function __construct($name, $email)
    {
        $this->name  = $name;
        $this->email = $email;
    }

    /**
     * Should return the same value for all equal objects, but doesn't have to
     * be unique. This value will not be used to determine equality.
     */
    public function hash()
    {
        return $this->email;
    }

    /**
     * This determines equality, usually during a hash table lookup to determine
     * if the bucket's key matches the lookup key. The hash has to be equal if
     * the objects are equal, otherwise this determination wouldn't be reached.
     */
    public function equals($obj): bool
    {
        return $this->name  === $obj->name
            && $this->email === $obj->email;
    }
}
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.para:
A Sequence describes the behaviour of values arranged in a single, linear dimension. Some languages refer to this as a "List". It’s similar to an array that uses incremental integer keys, with the exception of a few characteristics:
Values will always be indexed as [0, 1, 2, …, size - 1]. Only allowed to access values by index in the range [0, size - 1].

Use cases:
Wherever you would use an array as a list (not concerned with keys). A more efficient alternative to SplDoublyLinkedList and SplFixedArray.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Allocates enough memory for a required capacity

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Ensures that enough memory is allocated for a required capacity. This removes the need to reallocate the internal buffer as values are added.

listitem.simpara: The number of values for which capacity should be allocated.

note.simpara: Capacity will stay the same if this value is less than or equal to the current capacity.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Ds\Sequence::allocate example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$sequence = new \Ds\Vector();
var_dump($sequence->capacity());

$vector->allocate(100);
var_dump($sequence->capacity());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Updates all values by applying a callback function to each value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Updates all values by applying a callback function to each value in the sequence.

listitem.simpara: A callable to apply to each value in the sequence.
The callback should return what the value should be replaced by.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Ds\Sequence::apply example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$sequence = new \Ds\Vector([1, 2, 3]);
$sequence->apply(function($value) { return $value * 2; });

print_r($sequence);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the current capacity

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns the current capacity.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The current capacity.

example.title: Ds\Sequence::capacity example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$sequence = new \Ds\Vector();
var_dump($sequence->capacity());

$sequence->push(...range(1, 50));
var_dump($sequence->capacity());

$sequence[] = "a";
var_dump($sequence->capacity());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Determines if the sequence contains given values

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Determines if the sequence contains all values.

listitem.simpara: Values to check.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: false if any of the provided values are not in the sequence, true otherwise.

example.title: Ds\Sequence::contains example
example.programlisting:
<?php $sequence = new \Ds\Vector(['a', 'b', 'c', 1, 2, 3]);
var_dump($sequence->contains('a')); // true var_dump($sequence->contains('a', 'b')); // true var_dump($sequence->contains('c', 'd')); // false
var_dump($sequence->contains(...['c', 'b', 'a'])); // true
// Always strict var_dump($sequence->contains(1)); // true var_dump($sequence->contains('1')); // false
var_dump($sequence->contains(...[])); // true ?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: bool(true) bool(true) bool(false) bool(true) bool(true) bool(false) bool(true)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Creates a new sequence using a callable to determine which values to include

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Creates a new sequence using a callable to determine which values to include.

listitem.simpara: Optional callable which returns true if the value should be included, false otherwise.
If a callback is not provided, only values which are true (see converting to boolean) will be included.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: A new sequence containing all the values for which either the callback returned true, or all values that convert to true if a callback was not provided.

example.title: Ds\Sequence::filter example using callback function
example.programlisting:
<?php
$sequence = new \Ds\Vector([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);

var_dump($sequence->filter(function($value) {
    return $value % 2 == 0;
}));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

example.title: Ds\Sequence::filter example without a callback function
example.programlisting:
<?php
$sequence = new \Ds\Vector([0, 1, 'a', true, false]);

var_dump($sequence->filter());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Attempts to find a value's index

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns the index of the value, or false if not found.

listitem.simpara: The value to find.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The index of the value, or false if not found.

note.simpara: Values will be compared by value and by type.

example.title: Ds\Sequence::find example

example.title: Ds\Sequence::reduce with initial value example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$sequence = new \Ds\Vector([1, 2, 3]);

$callback = function($carry, $value) {
    return $carry * $value;
};

var_dump($sequence->reduce($callback, 5));

// Iterations:
//
// $carry = $initial = 5
//
// $carry = $carry * 1 =  5
// $carry = $carry * 2 = 10
// $carry = $carry * 3 = 30
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

example.title: Ds\Sequence::reduce without an initial value example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$sequence = new \Ds\Vector([1, 2, 3]);

var_dump($sequence->reduce(function($carry, $value) {
    return $carry + $value + 5;
}));

// Iterations:
//
// $carry = $initial = null
//
// $carry = $carry + 1 + 5 =  6
// $carry = $carry + 2 + 5 = 13
// $carry = $carry + 3 + 5 = 21
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Rotates the sequence by a given number of rotations

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Rotates the sequence by a given number of rotations, which is equivalent to successively calling $sequence->push($sequence->shift()) if the number of rotations is positive, or $sequence->unshift($sequence->pop()) if negative.

listitem.simpara: The number of times the sequence should be rotated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.. The sequence of the current instance will be rotated.

example.title: Ds\Sequence::rotate example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$sequence = new \Ds\Vector(["a", "b", "c", "d"]);

$sequence->rotate(1);  // "a" is shifted, then pushed.
print_r($sequence);

$sequence->rotate(2);  // "b" and "c" are both shifted, then pushed.
print_r($sequence);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns a sub-sequence of a given range

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Creates a sub-sequence of a given range.

listitem.simpara: The index at which the sub-sequence starts.
If positive, the sequence will start at that index in the sequence. If negative, the sequence will start that far from the end.

If a length is given and is positive, the resulting sequence will have up to that many values in it.
If the length results in an overflow, only values up to the end of the sequence will be included.
If a length is given and is negative, the sequence will stop that many values from the end.
If a length is not provided, the resulting sequence will contain all values between the index and the end of the sequence.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: A sub-sequence of the given range.

example.title: Ds\Sequence::slice example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$sequence = new \Ds\Vector(["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"]);

// Slice from 2 onwards
print_r($sequence->slice(2));

// Slice from 1, for a length of 3
print_r($sequence->slice(1, 3));

// Slice from 1 onwards
print_r($sequence->slice(1));

// Slice from 2 from the end onwards
print_r($sequence->slice(-2));

// Slice from 1 to 1 from the end
print_r($sequence->slice(1, -1));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: Ds\Vector Object ( [0] => c [1] => d [2] => e ) Ds\Vector Object ( [0] => b [1] => c [2] => d ) Ds\Vector Object ( [0] => b [1] => c [2] => d [3] => e ) Ds\Vector Object ( [0] => d [1] => e ) Ds\Vector Object ( [0] => b [1] => c [2] => d )

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sorts the sequence in-place

refsect1.title: Description

listitem.simpara: The comparison function must return an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero if the first argument is considered to be respectively less than, equal to, or greater than the second.

caution.simpara: Returning non-integer values from the comparison function, such as float, will result in an internal cast to int of the callback's return value. So values such as 0.99 and 0.1 will both be cast to an integer value of 0, which will compare such values as equal.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

section.title: Introduction
section.para: A Vector is a sequence of values in a contiguous buffer that grows and shrinks automatically. It’s the most efficient sequential structure because a value’s index is a direct mapping to its index in the buffer, and the growth factor isn't bound to a specific multiple or exponent.

simplelist.member: Uses less overall memory than an array for the same number of values.
Automatically frees allocated memory when its size drops low enough.
Capacity does not have to be a power of 2.
get, set, push, pop are all O(1).
shift, unshift, insert and remove are all O(n).

refnamediv.refpurpose: Allocates enough memory for a required capacity

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Ensures that enough memory is allocated for a required capacity. This removes the need to reallocate the internal buffer as values are added.

listitem.para: The number of values for which capacity should be allocated.

note.para: Capacity will stay the same if this value is less than or equal to the current capacity.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

example.title: Ds\Vector::allocate example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$vector = new \Ds\Vector();
var_dump($vector->capacity());

$vector->allocate(100);
var_dump($vector->capacity());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

example.title: Ds\Vector::contains example
example.programlisting:
<?php $vector = new \Ds\Vector(['a', 'b', 'c', 1, 2, 3]);
var_dump($vector->contains('a')); // true var_dump($vector->contains('a', 'b')); // true var_dump($vector->contains('c', 'd')); // false
var_dump($vector->contains(...['c', 'b', 'a'])); // true
// Always strict var_dump($vector->contains(1)); // true var_dump($vector->contains('1')); // false
var_dump($vector->contains(...[])); // true ?>

var_dump($vector->reduce($callback, 5));

// Iterations:
//
// $carry = $initial = 5
//
// $carry = $carry * 1 =  5
// $carry = $carry * 2 = 10
// $carry = $carry * 3 = 30
?>

//
// $carry = $carry + 1 + 5 =  6

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns a sub-vector of a given range

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Creates a sub-vector of a given range.

listitem.para: The index at which the sub-vector starts.
If positive, the vector will start at that index in the vector. If negative, the vector will start that far from the end.

If a length is given and is positive, the resulting vector will have up to that many values in it.
If the length results in an overflow, only values up to the end of the vector will be included.
If a length is given and is negative, the vector will stop that many values from the end.
If a length is not provided, the resulting vector will contain all values between the index and the end of the vector.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A sub-vector of the given range.

example.title: Ds\Vector::slice example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$vector = new \Ds\Vector(["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"]);

// Slice from 2 onwards
print_r($vector->slice(2));

// Slice from 1, for a length of 3
print_r($vector->slice(1, 3));

// Slice from 1 onwards
print_r($vector->slice(1));

// Slice from 2 from the end onwards
print_r($vector->slice(-2));

// Slice from 1 to 1 from the end
print_r($vector->slice(1, -1));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: Ds\Vector Object ( [0] => c [1] => d [2] => e ) Ds\Vector Object ( [0] => b [1] => c [2] => d ) Ds\Vector Object ( [0] => b [1] => c [2] => d [3] => e ) Ds\Vector Object ( [0] => d [1] => e ) Ds\Vector Object ( [0] => b [1] => c [2] => d )

section.title: Introduction
section.para: A Deque (pronounced “deck”) is a sequence of values in a contiguous buffer that grows and shrinks automatically. The name is a common abbreviation of “double-ended queue” and is used internally by Ds\Queue.

Two pointers are used to keep track of a head and a tail. The pointers can “wrap around” the end of the buffer, which avoids the need to move other values around to make room. This makes shift and unshift very fast — something a Ds\Vector can’t compete with.
Accessing a value by index requires a translation between the index and its corresponding position in the buffer: ((head + position) % capacity).

simplelist.member: Uses less overall memory than an array for the same number of values.
Automatically frees allocated memory when its size drops low enough.
get, set, push, pop, shift, and unshift are all O(1).
Capacity must be a power of 2.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Allocates enough memory for a required capacity

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Ensures that enough memory is allocated for a required capacity. This removes the need to reallocate the internal buffer as values are added.

listitem.para: The number of values for which capacity should be allocated.

note.para: Capacity will stay the same if this value is less than or equal to the current capacity.
Capacity will always be rounded up to the nearest power of 2.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

example.title: Ds\Deque::allocate example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$deque = new \Ds\Deque();
var_dump($deque->capacity());

$deque->allocate(100);
var_dump($deque->capacity());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Reduces the deque to a single value using a callback function

example.title: Ds\Deque::reduce with initial value example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$deque = new \Ds\Deque([1, 2, 3]);

$callback = function($carry, $value) {
    return $carry * $value;
};

var_dump($deque->reduce($callback, 5));

// Iterations:
//
// $carry = $initial = 5
//
// $carry = $carry * 1 =  5
// $carry = $carry * 2 = 10
// $carry = $carry * 3 = 30
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

    return $carry + $value + 5;
}));

// Iterations:
//
// $carry = $initial = null
//
// $carry = $carry + 1 + 5 =  6
// $carry = $carry + 2 + 5 = 13
// $carry = $carry + 3 + 5 = 21
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Rotates the deque by a given number of rotations

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Rotates the deque by a given number of rotations, which is equivalent to successively calling $deque->push($deque->shift()) if the number of rotations is positive, or $deque->unshift($deque->pop()) if negative.

refsect1.title: Return Values

$deque->rotate(1);  // "a" is shifted, then pushed.
print_r($deque);

$deque->rotate(2);  // "b" and "c" are both shifted, then pushed.
print_r($deque);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns a sub-deque of a given range

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Creates a sub-deque of a given range.

listitem.para: The index at which the sub-deque starts.
If positive, the deque will start at that index in the deque. If negative, the deque will start that far from the end.

If a length is given and is positive, the resulting deque will have up to that many values in it.
If the length results in an overflow, only values up to the end of the deque will be included.
If a length is given and is negative, the deque will stop that many values from the end.
If a length is not provided, the resulting deque will contain all values between the index and the end of the deque.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A sub-deque of the given range.

example.title: Ds\Deque::slice example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$deque = new \Ds\Deque(["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"]);

// Slice from 2 onwards
print_r($deque->slice(2));

// Slice from 1, for a length of 3
print_r($deque->slice(1, 3));

// Slice from 1 onwards
print_r($deque->slice(1));

// Slice from 2 from the end onwards
print_r($deque->slice(-2));

// Slice from 1 to 1 from the end
print_r($deque->slice(1, -1));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: Ds\Deque Object ( [0] => c [1] => d [2] => e ) Ds\Deque Object ( [0] => b [1] => c [2] => d ) Ds\Deque Object ( [0] => b [1] => c [2] => d [3] => e ) Ds\Deque Object ( [0] => d [1] => e ) Ds\Deque Object ( [0] => b [1] => c [2] => d )

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sorts the deque in-place

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sorts the deque in-place, using an optional comparator function.

listitem.simpara: The comparison function must return an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero if the first argument is considered to be respectively less than, equal to, or greater than the second.

caution.simpara: Returning non-integer values from the comparison function, such as float, will result in an internal cast to int of the callback's return value. So values such as 0.99 and 0.1 will both be cast to an integer value of 0, which will compare such values as equal.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

example.programlisting:

print_r($deque);
?>

example.programlisting:
<?php
$deque = new \Ds\Deque([4, 5, 1, 3, 2]);

$deque->sort(function($a, $b) {
    return $b <=> $a;
});

print_r($deque);
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.para: A Map is a sequential collection of key-value pairs, almost identical to an array used in a similar context. Keys can be any type, but must be unique. Values are replaced if added to the map using the same key.

simplelist.member: Keys and values can be any type, including objects.
Performance and memory efficiency is very similar to an array.
Automatically frees allocated memory when its size drops low enough.
Can’t be converted to an array when objects are used as keys.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Allocates enough memory for a required capacity

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Allocates enough memory for a required capacity.

listitem.para: The number of values for which capacity should be allocated.

note.para: Capacity will stay the same if this value is less than or equal to the current capacity.
Capacity will always be rounded up to the nearest power of 2.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

example.title: Ds\Map::allocate example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$map = new \Ds\Map();
var_dump($map->capacity());

$map->allocate(100);
var_dump($map->capacity());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Updates all values by applying a callback function to each value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Updates all values by applying a callback function to each value in the map.

listitem.para: A callable to apply to each value in the map.
The callback should return what the value should be replaced by.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

example.title: Ds\Map::apply example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$map = new \Ds\Map(["a" => 1, "b" => 2, "c" => 3]);
$map->apply(function($key, $value) { return $value * 2; });

print_r($map);
?>

[1] => Ds\Pair Object ( [key] => b [value] => 4 )
[2] => Ds\Pair Object ( [key] => c [value] => 6 )
)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the value for a given key

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the value for a given key, or an optional default value if the key could not be found.

note.para:
Keys of type object are supported.
If an object implements Ds\Hashable, equality will be determined by the object's equals function.
If an object does not implement Ds\Hashable, objects must be references to the same instance to be considered equal.
You can also use array syntax to access values by key, eg. $map["key"].

caution.para: Be careful when using array syntax. Scalar keys will be coerced to integers by the engine. For example, $map["1"] will attempt to access int(1), while $map->get("1") will correctly look up the string key.
See Arrays.

listitem.para: The key to look up.
The optional default value, returned if the key could not be found.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The value mapped to the given key, or the default value if provided and the key could not be found in the map.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: OutOfBoundsException if the key could not be found and a default value was not provided.

example.title: Ds\Map::get example
example.programlisting:
<?php $map = new \Ds\Map(["a" => 1, "b" => 2, "c" => 3]);
var_dump($map->get("a")); // 1 var_dump($map->get("d", 10)); // 10 (default used) ?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

example.title: Ds\Map::get example using array syntax
example.programlisting:
<?php $map = new \Ds\Map(["a" => 1, "b" => 2, "c" => 3]);

example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Creates a new map by intersecting keys with another map

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para:

In other words, returns a copy of the current instance with all keys removed that are not also in the other map.

para.code: A ∩ B = {x : x ∈ A ∧ x ∈ B}

note.para: Values from the current instance will be kept.

listitem.para: The other map, containing the keys to intersect with.

var_dump($a->intersect($b));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sorts the map in-place by key

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sorts the map in-place by key, using an optional comparator function.

listitem.simpara: The comparison function must return an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero if the first argument is considered to be respectively less than, equal to, or greater than the second.

caution.simpara: Returning non-integer values from the comparison function, such as float, will result in an internal cast to int of the callback's return value. So values such as 0.99 and 0.1 will both be cast to an integer value of 0, which will compare such values as equal.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.programlisting:

print_r($map);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen:
Ds\Map Object ( [0] => Ds\Pair Object ( [key] => a [value] => 1 )
[1] => Ds\Pair Object ( [key] => b [value] => 2 )
[2] => Ds\Pair Object ( [key] => c [value] => 3 )
)

example.title: Ds\Map::ksort example using a comparator
example.programlisting:
<?php
$map = new \Ds\Map([1 => "x", 2 => "y", 0 => "z"]);

// Reverse
$map->ksort(function($a, $b) {
    return $b <=> $a;
});

print_r($map);
?>

example.screen:

[1] => Ds\Pair Object ( [key] => 1 [value] => x )
[2] => Ds\Pair Object ( [key] => 0 [value] => z )
)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Associates a key with a value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Associates a key with a value, overwriting a previous association if one exists.

note.para:
Keys of type object are supported.
If an object implements Ds\Hashable, equality will be determined by the object's equals function.
If an object does not implement Ds\Hashable, objects must be references to the same instance to be considered equal.
You can also use array syntax to associate values by key, eg. $map["key"] = $value.

caution.para: Be careful when using array syntax. Scalar keys will be coerced to integers by the engine. For example, $map["1"] will attempt to access int(1), while $map->get("1") will correctly look up the string key.
See Arrays.

listitem.para: The key to associate the value with.
The value to be associated with the key.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

example.programlisting:
<?php
$map = new \Ds\Map();

$map->put("a", 1);
$map->put("b", 2);
$map->put("c", 3);

print_r($map);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen:
Ds\Map Object ( [0] => Ds\Pair Object ( [key] => a [value] => 1 )
[1] => Ds\Pair Object ( [key] => b [value] => 2 )
[2] => Ds\Pair Object ( [key] => c [value] => 3 )
)

example.title: Ds\Map::put example using objects as keys
example.programlisting:
<?php
class HashableObject implements \Ds\Hashable
{
    /**
     * An arbitrary value to use as the hash value. Does not define equality.
     */
    private $value;

    public function __construct($value)
    {
        $this->value = $value;
    }

    public function hash()
    {
        return $this->value;
    }

    public function equals($obj): bool
    {
        return $this->value === $obj->value;
    }
}

$map = new \Ds\Map();

$obj = new \ArrayIterator([]);

// Using the same instance multiple times will overwrite the previous value.
$map->put($obj, 1);
$map->put($obj, 2);

// Using multiple instances of the same object will create new associations.
$map->put(new \stdClass(), 3);
$map->put(new \stdClass(), 4);

// Using multiple instances of equal hashable objects will overwrite previous values.
$map->put(new \HashableObject(1), 5);
$map->put(new \HashableObject(1), 6);
$map->put(new \HashableObject(2), 7);
$map->put(new \HashableObject(2), 8);

var_dump($map);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Reduces the map to a single value using a callback function

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Reduces the map to a single value using a callback function.

listitem.para: The return value of the previous callback, or initial if it's the first iteration.
The key of the current iteration.
The value of the current iteration.
The initial value of the carry value. Can be null.

example.title: Ds\Map::reduce with initial value example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$map = new \Ds\Map(["a" => 1, "b" => 2, "c" => 3]);

$callback = function($carry, $key, $value) {
    return $carry * $value;
};

var_dump($map->reduce($callback, 5));

// Iterations:
//
// $carry = $initial = 5
//
// $carry = $carry * 1 =  5
// $carry = $carry * 2 = 10
// $carry = $carry * 3 = 30
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

example.title: Ds\Map::reduce without an initial value example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$map = new \Ds\Map(["a" => 1, "b" => 2, "c" => 3]);

var_dump($map->reduce(function($carry, $key, $value) {
    return $carry + $value + 5;
}));

// Iterations:
//
// $carry = $initial = null
//
// $carry = $carry + 1 + 5 =  6
// $carry = $carry + 2 + 5 = 13
// $carry = $carry + 3 + 5 = 21
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns a subset of the map defined by a starting index and length

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns a subset of the map defined by a starting index and length.

listitem.para: The index at which the range starts.
If positive, the range will start at that index in the map. If negative, the range will start that far from the end.

If a length is given and is positive, the resulting map will have up to that many pairs in it.
If a length is given and is negative, the range will stop that many pairs from the end.
If the length results in an overflow, only pairs up to the end of the map will be included.
If a length is not provided, the resulting map will contain all pairs between the index and the end of the map.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A subset of the map defined by a starting index and length.

example.title: Ds\Map::slice example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$map = new \Ds\Map(["a" => 1, "b" => 2, "c" => 3, "d" => 4, "e" => 5]);

// Slice from 2 onwards
print_r($map->slice(2)->toArray());

// Slice from 1, for a length of 3
print_r($map->slice(1, 3)->toArray());

// Slice from 1 onwards
print_r($map->slice(1)->toArray());

// Slice from 2 from the end onwards
print_r($map->slice(-2)->toArray());

// Slice from 1 to 1 from the end
print_r($map->slice(1, -1)->toArray());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
