caution.simpara: Returning non-integer values from the comparison function, such as float, will result in an internal cast to int of the callback's return value. So values such as 0.99 and 0.1 will both be cast to an integer value of 0, which will compare such values as equal.

example.title: Ds\Map::sort example using a comparator
example.programlisting:
<?php
$map = new \Ds\Map(["a" => 2, "b" => 3, "c" => 1]);

$map->sort(function($a, $b) {

section.title: Introduction
section.para: A Set is a sequence of unique values. This implementation uses the same hash table as Ds\Map, where values are used as keys and the mapped value is ignored.

simplelist.member: Values can be any type, including objects.
Automatically frees allocated memory when its size drops low enough.
add, remove and contains are all O(1).
Doesn’t support push, pop, insert, shift, or unshift.
get is O(n) if there are deleted values in the buffer before the accessed index, O(1) otherwise.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Adds values to the set

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Adds all given values to the set that haven't already been added.

note.para:
Values of type object are supported.
If an object implements Ds\Hashable, equality will be determined by the object's equals function.
If an object does not implement Ds\Hashable, objects must be references to the same instance to be considered equal.

caution.para: All comparisons are strict (type and value).

listitem.para: Values to add to the set.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

example.title: Ds\Set::add example using integers
example.programlisting:
<?php
$set = new \Ds\Set();

$set->add(1);
$set->add(1);
$set->add(2);
$set->add(3);

// Strict comparison would not treat these the same as int(1)
$set->add("1");
$set->add(true);

var_dump($set);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

example.title: Ds\Set::add example using objects
example.programlisting:
<?php
class HashableObject implements \Ds\Hashable
{
    /**
     * An arbitrary value to use as the hash value. Does not define equality.
     */
    private $value;

    public function __construct($value)
    {
        $this->value = $value;
    }

    public function hash()
    {
        return $this->value;
    }

    public function equals($obj): bool
    {
        return $this->value === $obj->value;
    }
}

$set = new \Ds\Set();

$obj = new \ArrayIterator([]);

// Adding the same instance multiple times will only add the first.
$set->add($obj);
$set->add($obj);

// Adding multiple instances of the same object will add them all.
$set->add(new \stdClass());
$set->add(new \stdClass());

// Adding multiple instances of equal hashable objects will only add the first.
$set->add(new \HashableObject(1));
$set->add(new \HashableObject(1));
$set->add(new \HashableObject(2));
$set->add(new \HashableObject(2));

var_dump($set);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

};

// Iterations:
//
// $carry = $initial = 5
//
// $carry = $carry * 1 =  5
// $carry = $carry * 2 = 10

//
// $carry = $carry + 1 + 5 =  6

A reversed copy of the set.
The current instance is not affected.

example.title: Ds\Set::reversed example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$set = new \Ds\Set(["a", "b", "c"]);

print_r($set->reversed());
print_r($set);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: Ds\Set Object ( [0] => c [1] => b [2] => a ) Ds\Set Object ( [0] => a [1] => b [2] => c )

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns a sub-set of a given range

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Creates a sub-set of a given range.

listitem.para: The index at which the sub-set starts.
If positive, the set will start at that index in the set. If negative, the set will start that far from the end.

If a length is given and is positive, the resulting set will have up to that many values in it.
If the length results in an overflow, only values up to the end of the set will be included.
If a length is given and is negative, the set will stop that many values from the end.
If a length is not provided, the resulting set will contain all values between the index and the end of the set.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A sub-set of the given range.

example.title: Ds\Set::slice example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$set = new \Ds\Set(["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"]);

// Slice from 2 onwards
print_r($set->slice(2));

// Slice from 1, for a length of 3
print_r($set->slice(1, 3));

// Slice from 1 onwards
print_r($set->slice(1));

// Slice from 2 from the end onwards
print_r($set->slice(-2));

// Slice from 1 to 1 from the end
print_r($set->slice(1, -1));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: Ds\Set Object ( [0] => c [1] => d [2] => e ) Ds\Set Object ( [0] => b [1] => c [2] => d ) Ds\Set Object ( [0] => b [1] => c [2] => d [3] => e ) Ds\Set Object ( [0] => d [1] => e ) Ds\Set Object ( [0] => b [1] => c [2] => d )

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sorts the set in-place

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sorts the set in-place, using an optional comparator function.

listitem.simpara: The comparison function must return an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero if the first argument is considered to be respectively less than, equal to, or greater than the second.

caution.simpara: Returning non-integer values from the comparison function, such as float, will result in an internal cast to int of the callback's return value. So values such as 0.99 and 0.1 will both be cast to an integer value of 0, which will compare such values as equal.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

example.title: Ds\Set::sort example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$set = new \Ds\Set([4, 5, 1, 3, 2]);
$set->sort();

print_r($set);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

example.title: Ds\Set::sort example using a comparator
example.programlisting:
<?php
$set = new \Ds\Set([4, 5, 1, 3, 2]);

$set->sort(function($a, $b) {
    return $b <=> $a;
});

print_r($set);
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: A Stack is a “last in, first out” or “LIFO” collection that only allows access to the value at the top of the structure and iterates in that order, destructively.
Uses a Ds\Vector internally.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Allocates enough memory for a required capacity

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Ensures that enough memory is allocated for a required capacity. This removes the need to reallocate the internal buffer as values are added.

listitem.para: The number of values for which capacity should be allocated.

note.para: Capacity will stay the same if this value is less than or equal to the current capacity.

section.title: Introduction
section.para: A PriorityQueue is very similar to a Queue. Values are pushed into the queue with an assigned priority, and the value with the highest priority will always be at the front of the queue.
Implemented using a max heap.

note.para: "First in, first out" ordering is preserved for values with the same priority.
Iterating over a PriorityQueue is destructive, equivalent to successive pop operations until the queue is empty.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Allocates enough memory for a required capacity

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Ensures that enough memory is allocated for a required capacity. This removes the need to reallocate the internal buffer as values are added.

listitem.para: The number of values for which capacity should be allocated.

note.para: Capacity will stay the same if this value is less than or equal to the current capacity.
Capacity will always be rounded up to the nearest power of 2.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

example.programlisting:
<?php
$queue = new \Ds\PriorityQueue();
var_dump($queue->capacity());

$queue->allocate(100);
var_dump($queue->capacity());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refsect1.para: Pushes a value with a given priority into the queue.

listitem.para: The value to push into the queue.
The priority associated with the value.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

example.title: Ds\PriorityQueue::push example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$queue = new \Ds\PriorityQueue();

$queue->push("a",  5);
$queue->push("b", 15);
$queue->push("c", 10);

print_r($queue->pop());
print_r($queue->pop());
print_r($queue->pop());
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Converts the queue to an array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Converts the queue to an array.

note.para: This method is not destructive.
Casting to an array is not supported yet.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array containing all the values in the same order as the queue.

example.title: Ds\PriorityQueue::toArray example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$queue = new \Ds\PriorityQueue();

$queue->push("a",  5);
$queue->push("b", 15);
$queue->push("c", 10);

var_dump($queue->toArray());
?>

preface.title: Introduction
preface.simpara: The var_representation extension provides a compact alternative to var_export that properly escapes control characters.

section.title: Installation
section.para: This PECL extension is not bundled with PHP.

Information for installing this PECL extension may be found in the manual chapter titled Installation of PECL extensions. Additional information such as new releases, downloads, source files, maintainer information, and a CHANGELOG, can be located here: https://pecl.php.net/package/var_representation.
Windows binaries (DLL files) for this PECL extension are available from the PECL website.

appendix.title: Predefined Constants
appendix.simpara: The constants below are defined by this extension, and will only be available when the extension has either been compiled into PHP or dynamically loaded at runtime.

listitem.simpara: var_representation flag indicating that newlines should not be used for whitespace in variable representations.
var_representation flag indicating that strings should be encoded as single quoted strings with unescaped control characters.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns a short, readable, parsable string representation of a variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: var_representation (from the var_representation PECL) returns a string with structured information about the given variable. It is similar to var_export with differences in indentation, string escaping, and array representations.

listitem.para: The variable to generate a representation of.
Bitmask consisting of VAR_REPRESENTATION_SINGLE_LINE, VAR_REPRESENTATION_UNESCAPED. The behaviour of these constants is described on the var_representation constants page.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the variable representation.

example.title: var_representation Examples
example.programlisting:
<?php
$a = [1, 2, ['key' => 'value']];
echo var_representation($a), "\n";
echo var_representation($a, VAR_REPRESENTATION_SINGLE_LINE), "\n";
?>

example.title: Escaping control characters
example.programlisting: <?php echo var_representation("Content-Length: 123\r\n");

example.title: Exporting stdClass
example.programlisting:
<?php
$person = new stdClass;
$person->name = 'ElePHPant ElePHPantsdotter';
$person->website = 'https://php.net/elephpant.php';

echo var_representation($person);

example.title: Exporting classes
example.programlisting:
<?php
class A { public $var; }
$a = new A;
$a->var = 5;
echo var_representation($a);
?>

example.title: Using __set_state()
example.programlisting:
<?php
class A
{
    public $var1;
    public $var2;

    public static function __set_state($an_array)
    {
        $obj = new A;
        $obj->var1 = $an_array['var1'];
        $obj->var2 = $an_array['var2'];
        return $obj;
    }
}

$a = new A;
$a->var1 = 5;
$a->var2 = 'foo';

eval('$b = ' . var_representation($a) . ';'); // $b = \A::__set_state([
                                              //   'var1' => 5,
                                              //   'var2' => 'foo',
                                              // ]);
var_dump($b);
?>

preface.title: Introduction
preface.para: PHP supports libcurl, a library created by Daniel Stenberg, that allows you to connect and communicate to many different types of servers with many different types of protocols. libcurl currently supports the http, https, ftp, gopher, telnet, dict, file, and ldap protocols. libcurl also supports HTTPS certificates, HTTP POST, HTTP PUT, FTP uploading (this can also be done with PHP's ftp extension), HTTP form based upload, proxies, cookies, and user+password authentication.

section.title: Requirements
section.para: In order to use PHP's cURL functions you need to install the libcurl package. PHP requires libcurl version 7.10.5 or later. As of PHP 7.3.0, version 7.15.5 or later is required. As of PHP 8.0.0, version 7.29.0 or later is required. As of PHP 8.4.0, version 7.61.0 or later is required.

section.title: Installation
section.para: To use PHP's cURL support you must also compile PHP --with-curl[=DIR] where DIR is the location of the directory containing the lib and include directories. In the include directory there should be a folder named curl which should contain the easy.h and curl.h files. There should be a file named libcurl.a located in the lib directory.

note.title: Note to Win32 Users
note.simpara: In order to enable this module on a Windows environment, libeay32.dll and ssleay32.dll, or, as of OpenSSL 1.1 libcrypto-*.dll and libssl-*.dll, must be present in your PATH. Also libssh2.dll must be present in your PATH.
You don't need libcurl.dll from the cURL site.

section.title: Runtime Configuration
section.simpara: The behaviour of these functions is affected by settings in php.ini.
section.para:
cURL Configuration Options
Name Default Changeable Changelog
curl.cainfo NULL INI_SYSTEM
For further details and definitions of the INI_* modes, see the .

section.title: Resource Types
section.para: Prior to PHP 8.0.0, this extension defined three resource types: a curl handle, a curl_multi handle, and a curl_share handle.

appendix.title: Predefined Constants
appendix.simpara: The constants below are defined by this extension, and will only be available when the extension has either been compiled into PHP or dynamically loaded at runtime.
appendix.para: Descriptions and uses for these constants are described within the curl_setopt, curl_multi_setopt and curl_getinfo documentation.
