refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the last error on the socket

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: If a Socket instance is passed to this function, the last error which occurred on this particular socket is returned. If socket is null, the error code of the last failed socket function is returned. The latter is particularly helpful for functions like socket_create which don't return a socket on failure and socket_select which can fail for reasons not directly tied to a particular socket. The error code is suitable to be fed to socket_strerror which returns a string describing the given error code.
If no error had occurred, or the error had been cleared with socket_clear_error, the function returns 0.

listitem.para: A Socket instance created with socket_create.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: This function returns a socket error code.

row.entry: socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

example.title: socket_last_error example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$socket = @socket_create(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, SOL_TCP);

if ($socket === false) {
    $errorcode = socket_last_error();
    $errormsg = socket_strerror($errorcode);
    
    die("Couldn't create socket: [$errorcode] $errormsg");
}
?>

note.para: socket_last_error does not clear the error code, use socket_clear_error for this purpose.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Listens for a connection on a socket

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: After the socket socket has been created using socket_create and bound to a name with socket_bind, it may be told to listen for incoming connections on socket.
socket_listen is applicable only to sockets of type SOCK_STREAM or SOCK_SEQPACKET.

listitem.para: A Socket instance created with socket_create or socket_addrinfo_bind

A maximum of backlog incoming connections will be queued for processing. If a connection request arrives with the queue full the client may receive an error with an indication of ECONNREFUSED, or, if the underlying protocol supports retransmission, the request may be ignored so that retries may succeed.

note.para: The maximum number passed to the backlog parameter highly depends on the underlying platform. On Linux, it is silently truncated to SOMAXCONN. On win32, if passed SOMAXCONN, the underlying service provider responsible for the socket will set the backlog to a maximum reasonable value. There is no standard provision to find out the actual backlog value on this platform.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure. The error code can be retrieved with socket_last_error. This code may be passed to socket_strerror to get a textual explanation of the error.

row.entry: socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Reads a maximum of length bytes from a socket

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The function socket_read reads from the Socket instance socket created by the socket_create or socket_accept functions.

listitem.para: A Socket instance created with socket_create or socket_accept.
The maximum number of bytes read is specified by the length parameter. Otherwise you can use \r, \n, or \0 to end reading (depending on the mode parameter, see below).

Optional mode parameter is a named constant:
PHP_BINARY_READ (Default) - use the system recv() function. Safe for reading binary data.
PHP_NORMAL_READ - reading stops at \n or \r.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: socket_read returns the data as a string on success, or false on error (including if the remote host has closed the connection). The error code can be retrieved with socket_last_error. This code may be passed to socket_strerror to get a textual representation of the error.

note.para: socket_read returns a zero length string ("") when there is no more data to read.

row.entry: socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Receives data from a connected socket

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The socket_recv function receives length bytes of data in data from socket. socket_recv can be used to gather data from connected sockets. Additionally, one or more flags can be specified to modify the behaviour of the function.
data is passed by reference, so it must be specified as a variable in the argument list. Data read from socket by socket_recv will be returned in data.

listitem.para: The socket must be a Socket instance previously created by socket_create.
The data received will be fetched to the variable specified with data. If an error occurs, if the connection is reset, or if no data is available, data will be set to null.
Up to length bytes will be fetched from remote host.
The value of flags can be any combination of the following flags, joined with the binary OR (|) operator.

row.entry: Receive data from the beginning of the receive queue without removing it from the queue.
Block until at least length are received. However, if a signal is caught or the remote host disconnects, the function may return less data.
With this flag set, the function returns even if it would normally have blocked.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: socket_recv returns the number of bytes received, or false if there was an error. The actual error code can be retrieved by calling socket_last_error. This error code may be passed to socket_strerror to get a textual explanation of the error.

row.entry: socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

example.title: socket_recv example
example.para: This example is a simple rewrite of the first example from to use socket_recv.
example.programlisting: TCP/IP Connection\n"; /* Get the port for the WWW service. */ $service_port = getservbyname('www', 'tcp'); /* Get the IP address for the target host. */ $address = gethostbyname('www.example.com'); /* Create a TCP/IP socket. */ $socket = socket_create(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, SOL_TCP); if ($socket === false) { echo "socket_create() failed: reason: " . socket_strerror(socket_last_error()) . "\n"; } else { echo "OK.\n"; } echo "Attempting to connect to '$address' on port '$service_port'..."; $result = socket_connect($socket, $address, $service_port); if ($result === false) { echo "socket_connect() failed.\nReason: ($result) " . socket_strerror(socket_last_error($socket)) . "\n"; } else { echo "OK.\n"; } $in = "HEAD / HTTP/1.1\r\n"; $in .= "Host: www.example.com\r\n"; $in .= "Connection: Close\r\n\r\n"; $out = ''; echo "Sending HTTP HEAD request..."; socket_write($socket, $in, strlen($in)); echo "OK.\n"; echo "Reading response:\n\n"; $buf = 'This is my buffer.'; if (false !== ($bytes = socket_recv($socket, $buf, 2048, MSG_WAITALL))) { echo "Read $bytes bytes from socket_recv(). Closing socket..."; } else { echo "socket_recv() failed; reason: " . socket_strerror(socket_last_error($socket)) . "\n"; } socket_close($socket); echo $buf . "\n"; echo "OK.\n\n"; ?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen:
TCP/IP Connection

OK. Attempting to connect to '208.77.188.166' on port '80'...OK. Sending HTTP HEAD request...OK. Reading response: Read 123 bytes from socket_recv(). Closing socket...HTTP/1.1 200 OK Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2009 08:56:36 GMT Server: Apache/2.2.3 (Red Hat) Last-Modified: Tue, 15 Nov 2005 13:24:10 GMT ETag: "b80f4-1b6-80bfd280" Accept-Ranges: bytes Content-Length: 438 Connection: close Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8 OK.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Receives data from a socket whether or not it is connection-oriented

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The socket_recvfrom function receives length bytes of data in data from address on port port (if the socket is not of type AF_UNIX) using socket. socket_recvfrom can be used to gather data from both connected and unconnected sockets. Additionally, one or more flags can be specified to modify the behaviour of the function.

The address and port must be passed by reference. If the socket is not connection-oriented, address will be set to the internet protocol address of the remote host or the path to the UNIX socket. If the socket is connection-oriented, address is null. Additionally, the port will contain the port of the remote host in the case of an unconnected AF_INET or AF_INET6 socket.

note.simpara: This function is binary-safe.

listitem.para: The socket must be a Socket instance previously created by socket_create().
The data received will be fetched to the variable specified with data.
Up to length bytes will be fetched from remote host.
The value of flags can be any combination of the following flags, joined with the binary OR (|) operator.

row.entry: Receive data from the beginning of the receive queue without removing it from the queue.
Block until at least length are received. However, if a signal is caught or the remote host disconnects, the function may return less data.
With this flag set, the function returns even if it would normally have blocked.

listitem.para: If the socket is of the type AF_UNIX type, address is the path to the file. Else, for unconnected sockets, address is the IP address of, the remote host, or null if the socket is connection-oriented.
This argument only applies to AF_INET and AF_INET6 sockets, and specifies the remote port from which the data is received. If the socket is connection-oriented, port will be null.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: socket_recvfrom returns the number of bytes received, or false if there was an error. The actual error code can be retrieved by calling socket_last_error. This error code may be passed to socket_strerror to get a textual explanation of the error.

row.entry: socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

example.title: socket_recvfrom example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$socket = socket_create(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, SOL_UDP);
socket_bind($socket, '127.0.0.1', 1223);

$from = '';
$port = 0;
socket_recvfrom($socket, $buf, 12, 0, $from, $port);

echo "Received $buf from remote address $from and remote port $port" . PHP_EOL;
?>
example.para: This example will initiate a UDP socket on port 1223 of 127.0.0.1 and print at most 12 characters received from a remote host.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Read a message

warning.simpara: This function is currently not documented; only its argument list is available.

row.entry: socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Runs the select() system call on the given arrays of sockets with a specified timeout

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: socket_select accepts arrays of sockets and waits for them to change status. Those coming with BSD sockets background will recognize that those socket arrays are in fact the so-called file descriptor sets. Three independent arrays of sockets are watched.

refsect1.title: Parameters

listitem.para: The sockets listed in the read array will be watched to see if characters become available for reading (more precisely, to see if a read will not block - in particular, a socket is also ready on end-of-file, in which case a socket_read will return a zero length string).
The sockets listed in the write array will be watched to see if a write will not block.
The sockets listed in the except array will be watched for exceptions.

listitem.simpara: The seconds and microseconds together form the timeout parameter. The timeout is an upper bound on the amount of time elapsed before socket_select returns. seconds may be zero, causing socket_select to return immediately. This is useful for polling. If seconds is null (no timeout), socket_select can block indefinitely.
See seconds description.

warning.simpara: On exit, the arrays are modified to indicate which socket actually changed status. The original keys of the arrays are preserved.

refsect1.simpara: The three arrays all have to be passed, but an array that is of no interest can be an empty array or null; at least one of them must be a non-empty array. They are passed by reference and are modified once socket_select returns.

note.para:
Due to a limitation in the current Zend Engine it is not possible to pass a constant modifier like null directly as a parameter to a function which expects this parameter to be passed by reference. Instead use a temporary variable or an expression with the leftmost member being a temporary variable:
Using null with socket_select
<?php $e = NULL; socket_select($r, $w, $e, 0); ?>

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: On success socket_select returns the number of sockets contained in the modified arrays, which may be zero if the timeout expires before anything interesting happens. On error false is returned. The error code can be retrieved with socket_last_error.

example.title: socket_select example
example.programlisting:
<?php
/* Prepare the read array */
$read   = array($socket1, $socket2);
$write  = NULL;
$except = NULL;
$num_changed_sockets = socket_select($read, $write, $except, 0);

if ($num_changed_sockets === false) {
    /* Error handling */
} else if ($num_changed_sockets > 0) {
    /* At least at one of the sockets something interesting happened */
}
?>

note.para:
Be aware that some socket implementations need to be handled very carefully. A few basic rules:
You should always try to use socket_select without timeout. Your program should have nothing to do if there is no data available. Code that depends on timeouts is not usually portable and difficult to debug.
No socket must be added to any set if you do not intend to check its result after the socket_select call, and respond appropriately. After socket_select returns, all sockets in all arrays must be checked. Any socket that is available for writing must be written to, and any socket available for reading must be read from.
When reading from or writing to a socket returned in the arrays, be aware that the full amount of data requested is not necessarily read or written. Be prepared for as little as a single byte.
It's common to most socket implementations that the only exception caught with the except array is out-of-bound data received on a socket.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sends data to a connected socket

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The function socket_send sends length bytes to the socket socket from data.

listitem.para: A Socket instance created with socket_create or socket_accept.
A buffer containing the data that will be sent to the remote host.
The number of bytes that will be sent to the remote host from data.

The value of flags can be any combination of the following flags, joined with the binary OR (|) operator.
Possible values for flags
MSG_OOB
Send OOB (out-of-band) data.
MSG_EOR
Indicate a record mark. The sent data completes the record.
MSG_EOF
Close the sender side of the socket and include an appropriate notification of this at the end of the sent data. The sent data completes the transaction.
MSG_DONTROUTE
Bypass routing, use direct interface.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: socket_send returns the number of bytes sent, or false on error.

row.entry: socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Send a message

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The function socket_sendmsg sends the message described by message through the socket socket, using the sendmsg() system call.

listitem.simpara: A Socket instance created with socket_create, socket_accept or socket_create_pair.

An associative array which may contain the following elements. All of them are optional, and unrecognized keys are silently ignored. In particular there is no flags element when sending; that key only appears in the array filled in by socket_recvmsg.

The address of the remote host, as an array. Its keys are addr and port for AF_INET; addr, port, flowinfo and scope_id for AF_INET6; and path for AF_UNIX. addr accepts an IP address or a host name, which is then resolved. An optional family key selects the address family explicitly; if omitted, the family of socket is used. A family the socket does not support makes the call fail.

A list of buffers holding the data to send, which are sent in order as a single message. Array keys are ignored and the values are converted to string. When this key is missing or empty, no data is sent and the function returns 0.
A list of ancillary data messages. Each is an array with the keys level, type and data. Only the pairs below are supported, and their availability depends on the platform.

row.entry: A non-empty list of Socket instances or stream resources, whose file descriptors are sent to the receiving process.
An array with the keys pid, uid and gid. Named SCM_CREDS or SCM_CREDS2 on some systems.
An array with the keys addr and ifindex.

listitem.para:
The value of flags can be any combination of the following flags, joined with the binary OR (|) operator.
Possible values for flags
MSG_OOB
Send OOB (out-of-band) data.
MSG_EOR
Indicate a record mark. The sent data completes the record.
MSG_DONTWAIT
With this flag set, the function returns even if it would normally have blocked.
MSG_DONTROUTE
Bypass routing, use direct interface.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the number of bytes sent, or false on failure.

row.entry: socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

example.title: Sending a message with socket_sendmsg
example.programlisting:
<?php
$server = socket_create(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, SOL_UDP);
socket_bind($server, '127.0.0.1', 1053);

$client = socket_create(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, SOL_UDP);
$sent = socket_sendmsg($client, [
    'name' => ['addr' => '127.0.0.1', 'port' => 1053],
    'iov'  => ['Hello ', 'world'],
], 0);

echo "sent: $sent\n";

socket_recvfrom($server, $buffer, 64, 0, $from, $port);
echo "received: $buffer\n";
?>

example.title: Passing a file descriptor over a UNIX socket
example.simpara: The control key carries ancillary data. With SCM_RIGHTS, it transfers open file descriptors to the process at the other end of a UNIX socket. This is not available on Windows.
example.programlisting:
<?php
socket_create_pair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 0, $pair);
[$sender, $receiver] = $pair;

$file = fopen(__FILE__, 'r');

socket_sendmsg($sender, [
    // At least one byte of regular data must accompany the ancillary data.
    'iov'     => ['fd'],
    'control' => [
        ['level' => SOL_SOCKET, 'type' => SCM_RIGHTS, 'data' => [$file]],
    ],
], 0);

$message = [
    'buffer_size' => 16,
    'controllen'  => socket_cmsg_space(SOL_SOCKET, SCM_RIGHTS, 1),
];
socket_recvmsg($receiver, $message, 0);

$received = $message['control'][0]['data'][0];
echo "first line: ", fgets($received);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sends a message to a socket, whether it is connected or not

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The function socket_sendto sends length bytes from data through the socket socket to the port at the address address.

listitem.para: A Socket instance created using socket_create.
The sent data will be taken from buffer data.
length bytes from data will be sent.

The value of flags can be any combination of the following flags, joined with the binary OR (|) operator.
Possible values for flags
MSG_OOB
Send OOB (out-of-band) data.
MSG_EOR
Indicate a record mark. The sent data completes the record.
MSG_EOF
Close the sender side of the socket and include an appropriate notification of this at the end of the sent data. The sent data completes the transaction.
MSG_DONTROUTE
Bypass routing, use direct interface.
IP address of the remote host.
port is the remote port number at which the data will be sent.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: socket_sendto returns the number of bytes sent to the remote host, or false if an error occurred.

row.entry: Now throws a ValueError when port is lower than 0 or greater than 65535.
socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

example.title: socket_sendto Example
example.programlisting:
<?php
    $sock = socket_create(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, SOL_UDP);

    $msg = "Ping !";
    $len = strlen($msg);

    socket_sendto($sock, $msg, $len, 0, '127.0.0.1', 1223);
    socket_close($sock);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sets blocking mode on a socket

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The socket_set_block function removes the O_NONBLOCK flag on the socket specified by the socket parameter.
When an operation (e.g. receive, send, connect, accept, ...) is performed on a blocking socket, the script will pause its execution until it receives a signal or it can perform the operation.

listitem.para: A Socket instance created with socket_create or socket_accept.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

example.title: socket_set_block example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$socket = socket_create_listen(1223);
socket_set_block($socket);

socket_accept($socket);
?>
example.para: This example creates a listening socket on all interfaces on port 1223 and sets the socket to O_BLOCK mode. socket_accept will hang until there is a connection to accept.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sets nonblocking mode for file descriptor fd

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The socket_set_nonblock function sets the O_NONBLOCK flag on the socket specified by the socket parameter.

When an operation (e.g. receive, send, connect, accept, ...) is performed on a non-blocking socket, the script will not pause its execution until it receives a signal or it can perform the operation. Rather, if the operation would result in a block, the called function will fail.

listitem.para: A Socket instance created with socket_create or socket_accept.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

example.title: socket_set_nonblock example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$socket = socket_create_listen(1223);
socket_set_nonblock($socket);

socket_accept($socket);
?>
example.para: This example creates a listening socket on all interfaces on port 1223 and sets the socket to O_NONBLOCK mode. socket_accept will immediately fail unless there is a pending connection exactly at this moment.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sets socket options for the socket

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The socket_set_option function sets the option specified by the option parameter, at the specified protocol level, to the value pointed to by the value parameter for the socket.

listitem.para: A Socket instance created with socket_create or socket_accept.

The level parameter specifies the protocol level at which the option resides. For example, to set options at the socket level, a level parameter of SOL_SOCKET would be used. Other levels, such as TCP, can be used by specifying the protocol number of that level. Protocol numbers can be found by using the getprotobyname function.
The available socket options are the same as those for the socket_get_option function.
The option value.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: Now throws an exception when MCAST_LEAVE_GROUP or MCAST_LEAVE_SOURCE_GROUP is used and the value is not a valid object or array, and throws a ValueError when a multicast option is used on a socket that is not of AF_INET or AF_INET6 family.
socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

example.title: socket_set_option example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$socket = socket_create(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, SOL_TCP);

if (!is_resource($socket)) {
    echo 'Unable to create socket: '. socket_strerror(socket_last_error()) . PHP_EOL;
}

if (!socket_set_option($socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, 1)) {
    echo 'Unable to set option on socket: '. socket_strerror(socket_last_error()) . PHP_EOL;
}

if (!socket_bind($socket, '127.0.0.1', 1223)) {
    echo 'Unable to bind socket: '. socket_strerror(socket_last_error()) . PHP_EOL;
}

$rval = socket_get_option($socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR);

if ($rval === false) {
    echo 'Unable to get socket option: '. socket_strerror(socket_last_error()) . PHP_EOL;
} else if ($rval !== 0) {
    echo 'SO_REUSEADDR is set on socket !' . PHP_EOL;
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of socket_set_option

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: socket_set_option.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Shuts down a socket for receiving, sending, or both

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The socket_shutdown function allows you to stop incoming, outgoing or all data (the default) from being sent through the socket

note.para: The associated buffer, or buffers, may or may not be emptied.

listitem.para: A Socket instance created with socket_create.

The value of mode can be one of the following:
possible values for mode
0
Shutdown socket reading
1
Shutdown socket writing
2
Shutdown socket reading and writing

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Return a string describing a socket error

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: socket_strerror takes as its error_code parameter a socket error code as returned by socket_last_error and returns the corresponding explanatory text.

note.para: Although the error messages generated by the socket extension are in English, the system messages retrieved with this function will appear depending on the current locale (LC_MESSAGES).

listitem.para: A valid socket error number, likely produced by socket_last_error.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the error message associated with the error_code parameter.

example.title: socket_strerror example
example.programlisting:
<?php
if (false == ($socket = @socket_create(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, SOL_TCP))) {
   echo "socket_create() failed: reason: " . socket_strerror(socket_last_error()) . "\n";
}

if (false == (@socket_bind($socket, '127.0.0.1', 80))) {
   echo "socket_bind() failed: reason: " . socket_strerror(socket_last_error($socket)) . "\n";
}
?>
example.para: The expected output from the above example (assuming the script is not run with root privileges):

refnamediv.refpurpose: Write to a socket

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The function socket_write writes to the socket from the given data.

listitem.para: The buffer to be written.
The optional parameter length can specify an alternate length of bytes written to the socket. If this length is greater than data's length, it is silently truncated to the length of data.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the number of bytes successfully written to the socket or false on failure. The error code can be retrieved with socket_last_error. This code may be passed to socket_strerror to get a textual explanation of the error.

note.para: It is perfectly valid for socket_write to return zero which means no bytes have been written. Be sure to use the === operator to check for false in case of an error.

row.entry: socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

note.para: socket_write does not necessarily write all bytes from data. It's valid that, depending on the network buffers etc., only a certain amount of data, even one byte, is written despite data being longer. A loop must be used to ensure that the rest of data is transmitted.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Exports the WSAPROTOCOL_INFO Structure

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Exports the WSAPROTOCOL_INFO structure into shared memory and returns an identifier to be used with socket_wsaprotocol_info_import. The exported ID is only valid for the given process_id.

note.simpara: This function is available only on Windows.

listitem.para: A Socket instance.
The ID of the process which will import the socket.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns an identifier to be used for the import, or false on failure

row.entry: socket is a Socket instance now; previously, it was a resource.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Imports a Socket from another Process

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Imports a socket which has formerly been exported from another process.

note.simpara: This function is available only on Windows.

listitem.para: The ID which has been returned by a former call to socket_wsaprotocol_info_export.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a Socket instance on success, or false on failure

row.entry: On success, this function returns a Socket instance now; previously, a resource was returned.

refsect1.para: Releases the shared memory corresponding to the given info_id.

note.simpara: This function is available only on Windows.

section.title: Introduction
section.para: A fully opaque class which replaces Socket resources as of PHP 8.0.0.

section.title: Introduction
section.para: A fully opaque class which replaces AddressInfo resources as of PHP 8.0.0.

preface.title: Introduction
preface.simpara: Bindings to the libssh2 library which provide access to resources (shell, remote exec, tunneling, file transfer) on a remote machine using a secure cryptographic transport.

section.title: Requirements
section.simpara: The OpenSSL and libssh2 libraries are required. Ensure that the development libraries are installed, where a typical package name might be openssl-dev.
Version 1.2 or newer of the libssh2 library is required, although it's possible newer releases of pecl/ssh2 may require newer versions (see the release notes).
The ssh2_auth_agent function will only be available with libssh2 >= 1.2.3.
support for stream_set_timeout to channel streams will only be available with libssh2 >= 1.2.9.

Libssh2 comes in two flavours: gcrypt or openssl. Some Linux distributions build libssh2 with the gcrypt library, some use openssl. Libssh2 has some issues when compiled with gcrypt, please use openssl.

section.title: Installation
section.simpara: Information for installing this PECL extension may be found in the manual chapter titled Installation of PECL extensions. Additional information such as new releases, downloads, source files, maintainer information, and a CHANGELOG, can be located here: https://pecl.php.net/package/ssh2.
Windows binaries (DLL files) for this PECL extension are available from the PECL website.

section.title: Resource Types
section.para:
This extension defines the following resource types:
SSH2 Session SSH2 Listener SSH2 SFTP SSH2 Publickey Subsystem (as of ssh2 0.10)

appendix.title: Predefined Constants
appendix.simpara: The constants below are defined by this extension, and will only be available when the extension has either been compiled into PHP or dynamically loaded at runtime.

listitem.simpara: Flag to ssh2_fingerprint requesting hostkey fingerprint as an MD5 hash.
Flag to ssh2_fingerprint requesting hostkey fingerprint as an SHA1 hash.
Flag to ssh2_fingerprint requesting hostkey fingerprint as a string of hexits.
Flag to ssh2_fingerprint requesting hostkey fingerprint as a raw string of 8-bit characters.
Flag to ssh2_shell specifying that width and height are provided as character sizes.
Flag to ssh2_shell specifying that width and height are provided in pixel units.
Default terminal width requested by ssh2_shell.
Default terminal height requested by ssh2_shell.
Default terminal units requested by ssh2_shell.
Flag to ssh2_fetch_stream requesting STDIO subchannel.
Flag to ssh2_fetch_stream requesting STDERR subchannel.
Default terminal type (e.g. vt102, ansi, xterm, vanilla) requested by ssh2_shell.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Authenticate over SSH using the ssh agent

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Authenticate over SSH using the ssh agent

note.simpara: The ssh2_auth_agent function will only be available when the ssh2 extension is compiled with libssh2 >= 1.2.3.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
Remote user name.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Authenticating with a ssh agent
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);

if (ssh2_auth_agent($connection, 'username')) {
  echo "Authentication Successful!\n";
} else {
  die('Authentication Failed...');
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Authenticate using a public hostkey

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Authenticate using a public hostkey read from a file.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
If privkeyfile is encrypted (which it should be), the passphrase must be provided.
If local_username is omitted, then the value for username will be used for it.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Authentication using a public hostkey
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22, array('hostkey'=>'ssh-rsa'));

if (ssh2_auth_hostbased_file($connection, 'remoteusername', 'myhost.example.com',
                             '/usr/local/etc/hostkey_rsa.pub',
                             '/usr/local/etc/hostkey_rsa', 'secret',
                             'localusername')) {
  echo "Public Key Hostbased Authentication Successful\n";
} else {
  die('Public Key Hostbased Authentication Failed');
}
?>

note.simpara: ssh2_auth_hostbased_file requires libssh2 >= 0.7 and PHP/SSH2 >= 0.7

refnamediv.refpurpose: Authenticate as "none"

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Attempt "none" authentication which usually will (and should) fail. As part of the failure, this function will return an array of accepted authentication methods.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
Remote user name.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the server does accept "none" as an authentication method, or an array of accepted authentication methods on failure.

example.title: Retrieving a list of authentication methods
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);

$auth_methods = ssh2_auth_none($connection, 'user');

if (in_array('password', $auth_methods)) {
  echo "Server supports password based authentication\n";
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Authenticate over SSH using a plain password

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Authenticate over SSH using a plain password. Since version 0.12 this function also supports keyboard_interactive method.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
Remote user name.
Password for username

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Authenticating with a password
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);

if (ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'secret')) {
  echo "Authentication Successful!\n";
} else {
  die('Authentication Failed...');
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Authenticate using a public key in a variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Authenticate using a public key in a variable.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
Name of the user to authenticate as on the remote server.
Public key in OpenSSH's format. It should look something like: ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAA....NX6sqSnHA8= rsa-key-20121110
Private OpenSSH key. It should begin with: -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
If privkey is encrypted (which it should be), the passphrase must be provided.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Authentication using a public key
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22, array('hostkey'=>'ssh-rsa'));
$publicKey = file_get_contents('/home/username/.ssh/id_rsa.pub');
$privateKey = file_get_contents('/home/username/.ssh/id_rsa');

if (ssh2_auth_pubkey($connection, 'username',
                     $publicKey,
                     $privateKey, 'secret')) {
  echo "Public Key Authentication Successful\n";
} else {
  die('Public Key Authentication Failed');
}
?>

note.simpara: The underlying libssh2 library doesn't support partial auths very cleanly. That is, if you need to supply both a public key and a password it will appear as if this function has failed. In this particular case a failure from this call may just mean that auth hasn't been completed yet. You would need to ignore this failure and continue on and call ssh2_auth_password in order to complete authentication.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Authenticate using a public key read from a file

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Authenticate using a public key read from a file.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
Name of the user to authenticate as on the remote server.
The public key file needs to be in OpenSSH's format. It should look something like:
ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAA....NX6sqSnHA8= rsa-key-20121110
If privkeyfile is encrypted (which it should be), the passphrase must be provided.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Authentication using a public key
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22, array('hostkey'=>'ssh-rsa'));

if (ssh2_auth_pubkey_file($connection, 'username',
                          '/home/username/.ssh/id_rsa.pub',
                          '/home/username/.ssh/id_rsa', 'secret')) {
  echo "Public Key Authentication Successful\n";
} else {
  die('Public Key Authentication Failed');
}
?>

note.simpara: The underlying libssh2 library doesn't support partial auths very cleanly. That is, if you need to supply both a public key and a password it will appear as if this function has failed. In this particular case a failure from this call may just mean that auth hasn't been completed yet. You would need to ignore this failure and continue on and call ssh2_auth_password in order to complete authentication.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Connect to an SSH server

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Establish a connection to a remote SSH server.
Once connected, the client should verify the server's hostkey using ssh2_fingerprint, then authenticate using either password or public key.

listitem.simpara: methods may be an associative array with up to four parameters as described below.

table.title: methods may be an associative array with any or all of the following parameters.

row.entry: List of key exchange methods to advertise, comma separated in order of preference.
List of hostkey methods to advertise, comma separated in order of preference.
Associative array containing crypt, compression, and message authentication code (MAC) method preferences for messages sent from client to server.
Associative array containing crypt, compression, and message authentication code (MAC) method preferences for messages sent from server to client.

listitem.simpara: * - Supported Values are dependent on methods supported by underlying library. See libssh2 documentation for additional information.

table.title: client_to_server and server_to_client may be an associative array with any or all of the following parameters.

row.entry: List of crypto methods to advertise, comma separated in order of preference.
rijndael-cbc@lysator.liu.se, aes256-cbc, aes192-cbc, aes128-cbc, 3des-cbc, blowfish-cbc, cast128-cbc, arcfour, and none**
List of compression methods to advertise, comma separated in order of preference.
List of MAC methods to advertise, comma separated in order of preference.
hmac-sha1, hmac-sha1-96, hmac-ripemd160, hmac-ripemd160@openssh.com, and none**

note.title: Crypt and MAC method "none"
note.simpara: For security reasons, none is disabled by the underlying libssh2 library unless explicitly enabled during build time by using the appropriate ./configure options. See documentation for the underlying library for more information.

listitem.para:
callbacks may be an associative array with any or all of the following parameters.
Callbacks parameters
Index Meaning Prototype
ignore
Name of function to call when an SSH2_MSG_IGNORE packet is received
void ignore_cb($message)
debug
Name of function to call when an SSH2_MSG_DEBUG packet is received
void debug_cb($message, $language, $always_display)
macerror
Name of function to call when a packet is received but the message authentication code failed. If the callback returns true, the mismatch will be ignored, otherwise the connection will be terminated.
bool macerror_cb($packet)
disconnect
Name of function to call when an SSH2_MSG_DISCONNECT packet is received
void disconnect_cb($reason, $message, $language)

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a resource on success, or false on error.

example.title: ssh2_connect example
example.simpara: Open a connection forcing 3des-cbc when sending packets, any strength aes cipher when receiving packets, no compression in either direction, and Group1 key exchange.
example.programlisting:
<?php
/* Notify the user if the server terminates the connection */
function my_ssh_disconnect($reason, $message, $language) {
  printf("Server disconnected with reason code [%d] and message: %s\n",
         $reason, $message);
}

$methods = array(
  'kex' => 'diffie-hellman-group1-sha1',
  'client_to_server' => array(
    'crypt' => '3des-cbc',
    'comp' => 'none'),
  'server_to_client' => array(
    'crypt' => 'aes256-cbc,aes192-cbc,aes128-cbc',
    'comp' => 'none'));

$callbacks = array('disconnect' => 'my_ssh_disconnect');

$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22, $methods, $callbacks);
if (!$connection) die('Connection failed');
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Close a connection to a remote SSH server

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Close a connection to a remote SSH server.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Execute a command on a remote server

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Execute a command at the remote end and allocate a channel for it.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
env may be passed as an associative array of name/value pairs to set in the target environment.
Width of the virtual terminal.
Height of the virtual terminal.
width_height_type should be one of SSH2_TERM_UNIT_CHARS or SSH2_TERM_UNIT_PIXELS.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a stream on success or false on failure.

example.title: Executing a command
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');

$stream = ssh2_exec($connection, '/usr/local/bin/php -i');
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Fetch an extended data stream

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Fetches an alternate substream associated with an SSH2 channel stream. The SSH2 protocol currently defines only one substream, STDERR, which has a substream ID of SSH2_STREAM_STDERR (defined as 1).

listitem.simpara: An SSH2 channel stream.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the requested stream resource.

example.title: Opening a shell and retrieving the stderr stream associated with it
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');

$stdio_stream = ssh2_shell($connection);
$stderr_stream = ssh2_fetch_stream($stdio_stream, SSH2_STREAM_STDERR);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Retrieve fingerprint of remote server

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns a server hostkey hash from an active session.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
flags may be either of SSH2_FINGERPRINT_MD5 or SSH2_FINGERPRINT_SHA1 logically ORed with SSH2_FINGERPRINT_HEX or SSH2_FINGERPRINT_RAW.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the hostkey hash as a string.

example.title: Checking the fingerprint against a known value
example.programlisting:
<?php
$known_host = '6F89C2F0A719B30CC38ABDF90755F2E4';

$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);

$fingerprint = ssh2_fingerprint($connection,
               SSH2_FINGERPRINT_MD5 | SSH2_FINGERPRINT_HEX);

if ($fingerprint != $known_host) {
  die("HOSTKEY MISMATCH!\n" .
      "Possible Man-In-The-Middle Attack?");
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Accept a connection created by a listener

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Accepts a connection created by a listener.

warning.simpara: This function is currently not documented; only its argument list is available.

listitem.simpara: An SSH2 Listener resource, obtained from a call to ssh2_forward_listen.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a stream resource, or false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Bind a port on the remote server and listen for connections

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Binds a port on the remote server and listen for connections.

warning.simpara: This function is currently not documented; only its argument list is available.

listitem.simpara: An SSH Session resource, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
The port of the remote server.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns an SSH2 Listener, or false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Configure how often keepalive messages should be sent

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Configures how often keepalive messages are sent on the given session, and whether the server is asked to reply to them.
Keepalive messages are not sent automatically. Once configured, ssh2_keepalive_send must be called to actually send a keepalive message.

note.simpara: This function is only available when the extension is built against a libssh2 version providing keepalive support.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
Whether the server is requested to reply to keepalive messages. Requesting a reply makes an unresponsive server detectable, at the cost of some extra traffic.

The number of seconds that may pass without any traffic before a keepalive message should be sent. A value of 0 disables keepalive messages, and a value of 1 is treated as 2 by the underlying library.
Accepted values range from 0 to 4294967295.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: An E_WARNING is emitted when interval is outside the accepted range, in which case the keepalive configuration is left unchanged.

example.title: Sending keepalive messages
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');

// Ask the server to reply, after 30 seconds without any traffic
ssh2_keepalive_config($connection, true, 30);

// Keepalive messages are only sent when this function is called
ssh2_keepalive_send($connection);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Send a keepalive message

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sends a keepalive message on the given session, according to the configuration set with ssh2_keepalive_config.

note.simpara: This function is only available when the extension is built against a libssh2 version providing keepalive support.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the number of seconds that may pass before another keepalive message must be sent, or false on failure. 0 is returned when keepalive messages are disabled.
Since 0 and false are both falsy, the === operator has to be used to tell them apart.

example.title: Sending a keepalive message
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');
ssh2_keepalive_config($connection, true, 30);

$seconds = ssh2_keepalive_send($connection);

if ($seconds === false) {
    echo "The keepalive message could not be sent", PHP_EOL;
} elseif ($seconds === 0) {
    echo "Keepalive messages are disabled", PHP_EOL;
} else {
    echo "Next keepalive message due in $seconds seconds", PHP_EOL;
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Return list of negotiated methods

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns list of negotiated methods.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.

example.title: Determining what methods were negotiated
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
$methods = ssh2_methods_negotiated($connection);

echo "Encryption keys were negotiated using: {$methods['kex']}\n";
echo "Server identified using an {$methods['hostkey']} with ";
echo "fingerprint: " . ssh2_fingerprint($connection) . "\n";

echo "Client to Server packets will use methods:\n";
echo "\tCrypt: {$methods['client_to_server']['crypt']}\n";
echo "\tComp: {$methods['client_to_server']['comp']}\n";
echo "\tMAC: {$methods['client_to_server']['mac']}\n";

echo "Server to Client packets will use methods:\n";
echo "\tCrypt: {$methods['server_to_client']['crypt']}\n";
echo "\tComp: {$methods['server_to_client']['comp']}\n";
echo "\tMAC: {$methods['server_to_client']['mac']}\n";

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Poll the channels/listeners/streams for events

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Polls the channels/listeners/streams for events, and returns the number of descriptors which returned non-zero revents.

warning.simpara: This function is currently not documented; only its argument list is available.

listitem.simpara: An indexed array of subarrays with the keys 'resource' and 'events'. The value of the resource is a (channel) stream or an SSH2 Listener resource. The value of the event are SSH2_POLL* flags bitwise ORed together. Each subarray will be populated with an 'revents' element on return, whose values are SSH2_POLL* flags bitwise ORed together of the events that occurred.
The timeout in seconds.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the number of descriptors which returned non-zero revents.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Add an authorized publickey

note.simpara: The public key subsystem is used for managing public keys on a server to which the client is already authenticated. To authenticate to a remote system using public key authentication, use the ssh2_auth_pubkey_file function instead.

listitem.simpara: Publickey Subsystem resource created by ssh2_publickey_init.
Publickey algorithm (e.g.): ssh-dss, ssh-rsa
Publickey blob as raw binary data
If the specified key already exists, should it be overwritten?

Associative array of attributes to assign to this public key. Refer to ietf-secsh-publickey-subsystem for a list of supported attributes. To mark an attribute as mandatory, precede its name with an asterisk. If the server is unable to support an attribute marked mandatory, it will abort the add process.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Adding a publickey with ssh2_publickey_add
example.programlisting:
<?php
$ssh2 = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($ssh2, 'jdoe', 'password');
$pkey = ssh2_publickey_init($ssh2);

$keyblob = base64_decode('
AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAABIwAAAIEA5HVt6VqSGd5PTrLRdjNONxXH1tVFGn0
Bd26BF0aCP9qyJRlvdJ3j4WBeX4ZmrveGrjMgkseSYc4xZ26sDHwfL351xj
zaLpipu\BGRrw17mWVBhuCExo476ri5tQFzbTc54VEHYckxQ16CjSTibI5X
69GmnYC9PNqEYq/1TP+HF10=');

ssh2_publickey_add($pkey, 'ssh-rsa', $keyblob, false, array('comment'=>"John's Key"));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Initialize Publickey subsystem

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Request the Publickey subsystem from an already connected SSH2 server.

The publickey subsystem allows an already connected and authenticated client to manage the list of authorized public keys stored on the target server in an implementation agnostic manner. If the remote server does not support the publickey subsystem, the ssh2_publickey_init function will return false.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns an SSH2 Publickey Subsystem resource for use with all other ssh2_publickey_*() methods or false on failure.

note.simpara: The public key subsystem is used for managing public keys on a server to which the client is already authenticated. To authenticate to a remote system using public key authentication, use the ssh2_auth_pubkey_file function instead.

refnamediv.refpurpose: List currently authorized publickeys

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: List currently authorized publickeys.

listitem.simpara: Publickey Subsystem resource

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a numerically indexed array of keys, each of which is an associative array containing: name, blob, and attrs elements.

row.entry: Name of algorithm used by this publickey, for example: ssh-dss or ssh-rsa.
Publickey blob as raw binary data.
Attributes assigned to this publickey. The most common attribute, and the only one supported by publickey version 1 servers, is comment, which may be any freeform string.

example.title: Listing authorized keys with ssh2_publickey_list
example.programlisting:
<?php
$ssh2 = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($ssh2, 'jdoe', 'secret');
$pkey = ssh2_publickey_init($ssh2);

$list = ssh2_publickey_list($pkey);

foreach($list as $key) {
  echo "Key: {$key['name']}\n";
  echo "Blob: " . chunk_split(base64_encode($key['blob']), 40, "\n") . "\n";
  echo "Comment: {$key['attrs']['comment']}\n\n";
}
?>

note.simpara: The public key subsystem is used for managing public keys on a server to which the client is already authenticated. To authenticate to a remote system using public key authentication, use the ssh2_auth_pubkey_file function instead.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Remove an authorized publickey

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Removes an authorized publickey.

listitem.simpara: Publickey Subsystem Resource
Publickey algorithm (e.g.): ssh-dss, ssh-rsa
Publickey blob as raw binary data

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

note.simpara: The public key subsystem is used for managing public keys on a server to which the client is already authenticated. To authenticate to a remote system using public key authentication, use the ssh2_auth_pubkey_file function instead.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Request a file via SCP

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Copy a file from the remote server to the local filesystem using the SCP protocol.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
Path to the remote file.
Path to the local file.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Downloading a file via SCP
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');

ssh2_scp_recv($connection, '/remote/filename', '/local/filename');
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Send a file via SCP

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Copy a file from the local filesystem to the remote server using the SCP protocol.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
Path to the local file.
Path to the remote file.
The file will be created with the mode specified by create_mode.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Uploading a file via SCP
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');

ssh2_scp_send($connection, '/local/filename', '/remote/filename', 0644);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Send EOF to stream

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sends an EOF to the stream; this is typically used to close standard input, while keeping output and error alive. For example, one can send a remote process some data over standard input, close it to start processing, and still be able to read out the results without creating additional files.

listitem.simpara: An SSH stream; can be acquired through functions like ssh2_fetch_stream or ssh2_connect.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Send a signal to a remote process

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sends a signal to the process running at the remote end of the given channel.

note.simpara: This function is only available when the extension is built against libssh2 >= 1.9.0.

listitem.simpara: An SSH channel stream, as returned by ssh2_exec or ssh2_shell.
The name of the signal to send, without the SIG prefix, as defined by the SSH connection protocol (RFC 4254); for example TERM, KILL or INT.
The value is forwarded to the server as is; it is not validated against the names listed by the protocol.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: An E_WARNING is emitted when channel is not an SSH channel stream, and when the signal could not be sent.

example.title: Interrupting a remote command
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');

$stream = ssh2_exec($connection, 'trap "echo interrupted" INT; sleep 60');

ssh2_send_signal($stream, 'INT');

stream_set_blocking($stream, true);
echo stream_get_contents($stream);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set the timeout for blocking operations on a session

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sets how long a blocking operation on the given session may wait before it is considered to have timed out.
When the resulting timeout is 0, which is the default, no timeout is applied and blocking operations may wait indefinitely.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
The timeout, in seconds.
An additional number of microseconds added to the timeout. The underlying library only supports millisecond precision, so this value is rounded up to the next whole millisecond.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Limiting how long blocking operations may wait
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);

// Give up on blocking operations after 5.5 seconds
ssh2_set_timeout($connection, 5, 500000);

ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Initialize SFTP subsystem

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Request the SFTP subsystem from an already connected SSH2 server.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: This method returns an SSH2 SFTP resource for use with all other ssh2_sftp_*() methods and the ssh2.sftp:// fopen wrapper, or false on failure.

example.title: Opening a file via SFTP
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');

$sftp = ssh2_sftp($connection);

$stream = fopen('ssh2.sftp://' . intval($sftp) . '/path/to/file', 'r');
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Changes file mode

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Attempts to change the mode of the specified file to that given in mode.

listitem.simpara: An SSH2 SFTP resource opened by ssh2_sftp.
Path to the file.
Permissions on the file. See the chmod for more details on this parameter.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Changing the mode of a file on a remote server
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');
$sftp = ssh2_sftp($connection);

ssh2_sftp_chmod($sftp, '/somedir/somefile', 0755);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Stat a symbolic link

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Stats a symbolic link on the remote filesystem without following the link.
This function is similar to using the lstat function with the ssh2.sftp:// wrapper and returns the same values.

listitem.simpara: An SSH2 SFTP resource opened by ssh2_sftp.
Path to the remote symbolic link.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns an array of statistics for the given symbolic link on success or false on failure. See the documentation for stat for details on the values which may be returned.

example.title: Stating a symbolic link via SFTP
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');

$sftp = ssh2_sftp($connection);
$statinfo = ssh2_sftp_lstat($sftp, '/path/to/symlink');

$filesize = $statinfo['size'];
$group = $statinfo['gid'];
$owner = $statinfo['uid'];
$atime = $statinfo['atime'];
$mtime = $statinfo['mtime'];
$mode = $statinfo['mode'];
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Create a directory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Creates a directory on the remote file server with permissions set to mode.
This function is similar to using mkdir with the ssh2.sftp:// wrapper.

listitem.simpara: An SSH2 SFTP resource opened by ssh2_sftp.
Path of the new directory.
Permissions on the new directory. The actual mode is affected by the current umask.
If recursive is true any parent directories required for dirname will be automatically created as well.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Creating a directory on a remote server
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');
$sftp = ssh2_sftp($connection);

ssh2_sftp_mkdir($sftp, '/home/username/newdir');
/* Or:  mkdir("ssh2.sftp://$sftp/home/username/newdir"); */
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Return the target of a symbolic link

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns the target of a symbolic link.

listitem.simpara: An SSH2 SFTP resource opened by ssh2_sftp.
Path of the symbolic link.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the target of the symbolic link or false on failure.

example.title: Reading a symbolic link
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');
$sftp = ssh2_sftp($connection);

$target = ssh2_sftp_readlink($sftp, '/tmp/mysql.sock');
/* $target is now (e.g.): '/var/run/mysql.sock' */
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Resolve the realpath of a provided path string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Translates filename into the effective real path on the remote filesystem.

listitem.simpara: An SSH2 SFTP resource opened by ssh2_sftp.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the real path as a string or false on failure.

example.title: Resolving a pathname
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');
$sftp = ssh2_sftp($connection);

$realpath = ssh2_sftp_realpath($sftp, '/home/username/../../../..//./usr/../etc/passwd');
/* $realpath is now: '/etc/passwd' */
?>

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Renames a file on the remote filesystem.

listitem.simpara: An SSH2 SFTP resource opened by ssh2_sftp.

$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);

example.title: Creating a symbolic link

<?php

refnamediv.refpurpose: Request an interactive shell

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Open a shell at the remote end and allocate a stream for it.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.
termtype should correspond to one of the entries in the target system's /etc/termcap file.
env may be passed as an associative array of name/value pairs to set in the target environment.
Width of the virtual terminal.
Height of the virtual terminal.
width_height_type should be one of SSH2_TERM_UNIT_CHARS or SSH2_TERM_UNIT_PIXELS.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a stream resource on success, or false on failure.

example.title: Requesting an interactive shell
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');

$stream = ssh2_shell($connection, 'vt102', null, 80, 24, SSH2_TERM_UNIT_CHARS);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Change the dimensions of a channel's pseudo-terminal

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Requests that the pseudo-terminal (PTY) attached to the given channel be resized to the given dimensions.

note.simpara: The extension declares only the first three parameters, under the name session for channel. As a result, width_px and height_px can only be passed positionally.

listitem.simpara: An SSH channel stream, as returned by ssh2_exec or ssh2_shell.
The width of the terminal, in characters.
The height of the terminal, in characters.
The width of the terminal in pixels, or 0 to leave the pixel dimensions unspecified.
The height of the terminal in pixels, or 0 to leave the pixel dimensions unspecified.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true, or false when channel is not an SSH channel stream.
The outcome of the resize request itself is not reported: true is returned even when the remote end does not honour it.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: An E_WARNING is emitted when channel is not an SSH channel stream.

example.title: Resizing the pseudo-terminal of a shell
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_password($connection, 'username', 'password');

$shell = ssh2_shell($connection, 'xterm', null, 80, 24);

// Tell the remote end the terminal is now 132 columns by 43 rows
ssh2_shell_resize($shell, 132, 43);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Open a tunnel through a remote server

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Open a socket stream to an arbitrary host/port by way of the currently connected SSH server.

listitem.simpara: An SSH connection link identifier, obtained from a call to ssh2_connect.

example.title: Opening a tunnel to an arbitrary host
example.programlisting:
<?php
$connection = ssh2_connect('shell.example.com', 22);
ssh2_auth_pubkey_file($connection, 'username', 'id_dsa.pub', 'id_dsa');

$tunnel = ssh2_tunnel($connection, '10.0.0.101', 12345);
?>

preface.title: Introduction
preface.simpara: This extension allows php applications to communicate with any Stomp compliant Message Brokers through easy object-oriented and procedural interfaces. Stomp official site

section.title: Requirements
section.simpara: The OpenSSL package >= 0.9.6 and the openssl extension may also be required to use stomp over SSL.

section.title: Installation
section.simpara: Information for installing this PECL extension may be found in the manual chapter titled Installation of PECL extensions. Additional information such as new releases, downloads, source files, maintainer information, and a CHANGELOG, can be located here: https://pecl.php.net/package/stomp

section.title: Runtime Configuration
section.simpara: The behaviour of these functions is affected by settings in php.ini.
Here's a short explanation of the configuration directives.

listitem.simpara: The default broker URI to use when connecting to the message broker if no other URI is specified.
The seconds part of the default connection timeout.
The microseconds part of the default connection timeout.
The seconds part of the default reading timeout.
The microseconds part of the default reading timeout.

section.title: Resource Types
section.simpara: There is only one resource type used in the stomp extension - it's the link identifier for a stomp connection.

example.title: Object-oriented style
example.programlisting:
<?php

$queue  = '/queue/foo';
$msg    = 'bar';

/* connection */
try {
    $stomp = new Stomp('tcp://localhost:61613');
} catch(StompException $e) {
    die('Connection failed: ' . $e->getMessage());
}

/* send a message to the queue 'foo' */
$stomp->send($queue, $msg);

/* subscribe to messages from the queue 'foo' */
$stomp->subscribe($queue);

/* read a frame */
$frame = $stomp->readFrame();

if ($frame->body === $msg) {
    var_dump($frame);

    /* acknowledge that the frame was received */
    $stomp->ack($frame);
}

/* close connection */
unset($stomp);

?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: object(StompFrame)#2 (3) { ["command"]=> string(7) "MESSAGE" ["headers"]=> array(5) { ["message-id"]=> string(41) "ID:php.net-55293-1257226743606-4:2:-1:1:1" ["destination"]=> string(10) "/queue/foo" ["timestamp"]=> string(13) "1257226805828" ["expires"]=> string(1) "0" ["priority"]=> string(1) "0" } ["body"]=> string(3) "bar" }

example.title: Procedural style
example.programlisting:
<?php

$queue  = '/queue/foo';
$msg    = 'bar';

/* connection */
$link = stomp_connect('ssl://localhost:61612');

/* check connection */
if (!$link) {
    die('Connection failed: ' . stomp_connect_error());
}

/* begin a transaction */
stomp_begin($link, 't1');

/* send a message to the queue 'foo' */
stomp_send($link, $queue, $msg, array('transaction' => 't1'));

/* commit a transaction */
stomp_commit($link, 't1');

/* subscribe to messages from the queue 'foo' */
stomp_subscribe($link, $queue);

/* read a frame */
$frame = stomp_read_frame($link);

if ($frame['body'] === $msg) {
    var_dump($frame);

    /* acknowledge that the frame was received */
    stomp_ack($link, $frame['headers']['message-id']);
}

/* close connection */
stomp_close($link);

?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: array(3) { ["command"]=> string(7) "MESSAGE" ["body"]=> string(3) "bar" ["headers"]=> array(6) { ["transaction"]=> string(2) "t1" ["message-id"]=> string(41) "ID:php.net-55293-1257226743606-4:3:-1:1:1" ["destination"]=> string(10) "/queue/foo" ["timestamp"]=> string(13) "1257227037059" ["expires"]=> string(1) "0" ["priority"]=> string(1) "0" } }

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Represents a connection between PHP and a Stomp compliant Message Broker.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Rolls back a transaction in progress

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Object-oriented style (method):
Procedural style:
Rolls back a transaction in progress.

listitem.simpara: Procedural style only: The stomp link identifier returned by stomp_connect.
The transaction to abort.
Associative array containing the additional headers (example: receipt).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Object-oriented style
example.programlisting:
<?php

/* connection */
try {
    $stomp = new Stomp('tcp://localhost:61613');
} catch(StompException $e) {
    die('Connection failed: ' . $e->getMessage());
}

/* begin a transaction */
$stomp->begin('t1');

/* send a message to the queue */
$stomp->send('/queue/foo', 'bar', array('transaction' => 't1'));

/* rollback */
$stomp->abort('t1');

/* close connection */
unset($stomp);
?>

example.title: Procedural style
example.programlisting:
<?php

/* connection */
$link = stomp_connect('tcp://localhost:61613');

/* check connection */
if (!$link) {
    die('Connection failed: ' . stomp_connect_error());
}

/* begin a transaction */
stomp_begin($link, 't1');

/* send a message to the queue 'foo' */
stomp_send($link, '/queue/foo', 'bar', array('transaction' => 't1'));

/* rollback */
stomp_abort($link, 't1');

/* close connection */
stomp_close($link);

?>

tip.simpara: Stomp is inherently asynchronous. Synchronous communication can be implemented adding a receipt header. This will cause methods to not return anything until the server has acknowledged receipt of the message or until read timeout was reached.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Acknowledges consumption of a message

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Object-oriented style (method):
Procedural style:
Acknowledges consumption of a message from a subscription using client acknowledgment.

listitem.simpara: Procedural style only: The stomp link identifier returned by stomp_connect.
The message/messageId to be acknowledged.
Associative array containing the additional headers (example: receipt).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

example.title: Object-oriented style
example.programlisting:
<?php

$queue  = '/queue/foo';
$msg    = 'bar';

/* connection */
try {
    $stomp = new Stomp('tcp://localhost:61613');
} catch(StompException $e) {
    die('Connection failed: ' . $e->getMessage());
}

/* send a message to the queue 'foo' */
$stomp->send($queue, $msg);

/* subscribe to messages from the queue 'foo' */
$stomp->subscribe($queue);

/* read a frame */
$frame = $stomp->readFrame();

if ($frame->body === $msg) {
    /* acknowledge that the frame was received */
    $stomp->ack($frame);
}

/* remove the subscription */
$stomp->unsubscribe($queue);

/* close connection */
unset($stomp);

?>

example.title: Procedural style
example.programlisting:
<?php

$queue  = '/queue/foo';
$msg    = 'bar';

/* connection */
$link = stomp_connect('ssl://localhost:61612');

/* check connection */
if (!$link) {
    die('Connection failed: ' . stomp_connect_error());
}

/* begin a transaction */
stomp_begin($link, 't1');

/* send a message to the queue 'foo' */
stomp_send($link, $queue, $msg, array('transaction' => 't1'));

/* commit a transaction */
stomp_commit($link, 't1');

/* subscribe to messages from the queue 'foo' */
stomp_subscribe($link, $queue);

/* read a frame */
$frame = stomp_read_frame($link);

if ($frame['body'] === $msg) {
    /* acknowledge that the frame was received */
    stomp_ack($link, $frame['headers']['message-id']);
}

/* remove the subscription */
stomp_unsubscribe($link, $queue);

/* close connection */
stomp_close($link);

?>

note.simpara: A transaction header may be specified, indicating that the message acknowledgment should be part of the named transaction.

tip.simpara: Stomp is inherently asynchronous. Synchronous communication can be implemented adding a receipt header. This will cause methods to not return anything until the server has acknowledged receipt of the message or until read timeout was reached.

preface.simpara: LibSVM is an efficient solver for SVM classification and regression problems. The svm extension wraps this in a PHP interface for easy use in PHP scripts.

section.title: Requirements
section.simpara: Libsvm itself is required, and is available through some package management - libsvm-devel for RPM based system or libsvm-dev for Debian based ones. Alternatively it is available direct from the website. If installing from the official website then some steps will need to be taken as the package does not install automatically. For example, assuming the latest version is 3.1:
section.screen: wget http://www.csie.ntu.edu.tw/~cjlin/cgi-bin/libsvm.cgi?+http://www.csie.ntu.edu.tw/~cjlin/libsvm+tar.gz tar xvzf libsvm-3.1.tar.gz cd libsvm-3.1 make lib cp libsvm.so.1 /usr/lib ln -s libsvm.so.1 libsvm.so ldconfig ldconfig --print | grep libsvm
section.simpara: This last step should show libsvm is installed.

section.title: Installation
section.simpara: Information for installing this PECL extension may be found in the manual chapter titled Installation of PECL extensions. Additional information such as new releases, downloads, source files, maintainer information, and a CHANGELOG, can be located here: https://pecl.php.net/package/svm

chapter.title: Examples
chapter.simpara: The basic process is to define parameters, supply training data to generate a model on, then make predictions based on the model. There are a default set of parameters that should get some results with most any input, so we'll start by looking at the data.

Data is supplied in either a file, a stream, or as an array. If supplied in a file or a stream, it must contain one line per training example, which must be formatted as an integer class (usually 1 and -1) followed by a series of feature/value pairs, in increasing feature order. The features are integers, the values floats, usually scaled 0-1. For example:

In a document classification problem, say a spam checker, each line would represent a document. There would be two classes, -1 for spam, 1 for ham. Each feature would represent some word, and the value would represent that importance of that word to the document (perhaps the frequency count, with the total scaled to unit length). Features that were 0 (e.g. the word did not appear in the document at all) would simply not be included.
In array mode, the data must be passed as an array of arrays. Each sub-array must have the class as the first element, then key => value sets for the feature values pairs.
This data is passed to the SVM class's train function, which will return an SVM model is successful.

Once a model has been generated, it can be used to make predictions about previously unseen data. This can be passed as an array to the model's predict function, in the same format as before, but without the label. The response will be the class.
Models can be saved and restored as required, using the save and load functions, which both take a file location.

example.title: Train from array
example.programlisting:
<?php
$data = array(
    array(-1, 1 => 0.43, 3 => 0.12, 9284 => 0.2),
    array(1, 1 => 0.22, 5 => 0.01, 94 => 0.11),
);

$svm = new SVM();
$model = $svm->train($data);

$data = array(1 => 0.43, 3 => 0.12, 9284 => 0.2);
$result = $model->predict($data);
var_dump($result);
$model->save('model.svm');
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

example.title: Train from a file
example.programlisting:
<?php
$svm = new SVM();
$model = $svm->train("traindata.txt");
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Test training params on subsets of the training data

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Crossvalidate can be used to test the effectiveness of the current parameter set on a subset of the training data. Given a problem set and a n "folds", it separates the problem set into n subsets, and the repeatedly trains on one subset and tests on another. While the accuracy will generally be lower than a SVM trained on the entire data set, the accuracy score returned should be relatively useful, so it can be used to test different training parameters.

listitem.simpara: The problem data. This can either be in the form of an array, the URL of an SVMLight formatted file, or a stream to an opened SVMLight formatted datasource.
The number of sets the data should be divided into and cross tested. A higher number means smaller training sets and less reliability. 5 is a good number to start with.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The correct percentage, expressed as a floating point number from 0-1. In the case of NU_SVC or EPSILON_SVR kernels the mean squared error will returned instead.

refsect1.title: Description
