( 1 === 1 ) ? print 'true' : print 'false';
print PHP_EOL;
?>

note.title: Using with parentheses

note.simpara: Because this is a language construct and not a function, it cannot be called using variable functions, or named arguments.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Output a formatted string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Produces output according to format.

listitem.simpara: The format string is composed of zero or more directives: ordinary characters (excluding %) that are copied directly to the result and conversion specifications, each of which results in fetching its own parameter.
A conversion specification follows this prototype: %[argnum$][flags][width][.precision]specifier.

formalpara.title: Argnum
formalpara.para: An integer followed by a dollar sign $, to specify which number argument to treat in the conversion.

row.entry: Left-justify within the given field width; Right justification is the default
Prefix positive numbers with a plus sign +; Default only negative are prefixed with a negative sign.
Pads the result with spaces. This is the default.
Only left-pads numbers with zeros. With s specifiers this can also right-pad with zeros.
Pads the result with the character (char).

formalpara.title: Width
formalpara.para: Either an integer that says how many characters (minimum) this conversion should result in, or *. If * is used, then the width is supplied as an additional integer value preceding the one formatted by the specifier.

formalpara.title: Precision
formalpara.para:
A period . optionally followed by either an integer or *, whose meaning depends on the specifier:
For e, E, f and F specifiers: this is the number of digits to be printed after the decimal point (by default, this is 6).
For g, G, h and H specifiers: this is the maximum number of significant digits to be printed.
For s specifier: it acts as a cutoff point, setting a maximum character limit to the string.
If the period is specified without an explicit value for precision, 0 is assumed. If * is used, the precision is supplied as an additional integer value preceding the one formatted by the specifier.

row.entry: A literal percent character. No argument is required.
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as a binary number.
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as the character with that ASCII.
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as a (signed) decimal number.
The argument is treated as scientific notation (e.g. 1.2e+2).
Like the e specifier but uses uppercase letter (e.g. 1.2E+2).
The argument is treated as a float and presented as a floating-point number (locale aware).
The argument is treated as a float and presented as a floating-point number (non-locale aware).

entry.simpara: General format.
Let P equal the precision if nonzero, 6 if the precision is omitted, or 1 if the precision is zero. Then, if a conversion with style E would have an exponent of X:
If P > X ≥ −4, the conversion is with style f and precision P − (X + 1). Otherwise, the conversion is with style e and precision P − 1.

row.entry: Like the g specifier but uses E and f.
Like the g specifier but uses F. Available as of PHP 8.0.0.
Like the g specifier but uses E and F. Available as of PHP 8.0.0.
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as an octal number.
The argument is treated and presented as a string.
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as an unsigned decimal number.
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as a hexadecimal number (with lowercase letters).
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as a hexadecimal number (with uppercase letters).

warning.simpara: The c type specifier ignores padding and width.
Attempting to use a combination of the string and width specifiers with character sets that require more than one byte per character may result in unexpected results.

listitem.para:
Variables will be co-erced to a suitable type for the specifier:
Type Handling
Type Specifiers
string s
int
d, u, c, o, x, X, b
float
e, E, f, F, g, G, h, H

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the length of the outputted string.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: As of PHP 8.0.0, a ValueError is thrown if the number of arguments is zero. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, a E_WARNING was emitted instead.
As of PHP 8.0.0, a ValueError is thrown if [width] is less than zero or bigger than PHP_INT_MAX. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, a E_WARNING was emitted instead.
As of PHP 8.0.0, a ValueError is thrown if [precision] is less than zero or bigger than PHP_INT_MAX. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, a E_WARNING was emitted instead.
As of PHP 8.0.0, a ArgumentCountError is thrown when less arguments are given than required. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, false was returned and a E_WARNING emitted instead.

row.entry: This function no longer returns false on failure.
Throw a ValueError if the number of arguments is zero; previously this function emitted a E_WARNING instead.
Throw a ValueError if [width] is less than zero or bigger than PHP_INT_MAX; previously this function emitted a E_WARNING instead.
Throw a ValueError if [precision] is less than zero or bigger than PHP_INT_MAX; previously this function emitted a E_WARNING instead.
Throw a ArgumentCountError when less arguments are given than required; previously this function emitted a E_WARNING instead.

example.title: printf: various examples
example.programlisting:
<?php $n = 43951789; $u = -43951789; $c = 65; // ASCII 65 is 'A'
// notice the double %%, this prints a literal '%' character printf("%%b = '%b'
", $n); // binary representation printf("%%c = '%c'
", $c); // print the ascii character, same as chr() function printf("%%d = '%d'
", $n); // standard integer representation printf("%%e = '%e'
", $n); // scientific notation printf("%%u = '%u'
", $n); // unsigned integer representation of a positive integer printf("%%u = '%u'
", $u); // unsigned integer representation of a negative integer printf("%%f = '%f'
", $n); // floating point representation printf("%%o = '%o'
", $n); // octal representation printf("%%s = '%s'
", $n); // string representation printf("%%x = '%x'
", $n); // hexadecimal representation (lower-case) printf("%%X = '%X'
", $n); // hexadecimal representation (upper-case)
printf("%%+d = '%+d'
", $n); // sign specifier on a positive integer printf("%%+d = '%+d'
", $u); // sign specifier on a negative integer ?>

example.title: printf: string specifiers
example.programlisting:
<?php $s = 'monkey'; $t = 'many monkeys';
printf("[%s]
", $s); // standard string output printf("[%10s]
", $s); // right-justification with spaces printf("[%-10s]
", $s); // left-justification with spaces printf("[%010s]
", $s); // zero-padding works on strings too printf("[%'#10s]
", $s); // use the custom padding character '#' printf("[%'#*s]
", 10, $s); // Provide the padding width as an additional argument printf("[%10.9s]
", $t); // right-justification but with a cutoff of 9 characters printf("[%-10.9s]
", $t); // left-justification but with a cutoff of 9 characters ?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Convert a quoted-printable string to an 8 bit string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function returns an 8-bit binary string corresponding to the decoded quoted printable string (according to RFC2045, section 6.7, not RFC2821, section 4.5.2, so additional periods are not stripped from the beginning of a line).
refsect1.para: This function is similar to imap_qprint, except this one does not require the IMAP module to work.

listitem.para: The input string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the 8-bit binary string.

example.title: quoted_printable_decode example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$encoded = quoted_printable_encode('Möchten Sie ein paar Äpfel?');

var_dump($encoded);
var_dump(quoted_printable_decode($encoded));
?>
example.screen: string(37) "M=C3=B6chten Sie ein paar =C3=84pfel?" string(29) "Möchten Sie ein paar Äpfel?"

refnamediv.refpurpose: Convert a 8 bit string to a quoted-printable string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns a quoted printable string created according to RFC2045, section 6.7.
This function is similar to imap_8bit, except this one does not require the IMAP module to work.

listitem.para: The input string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the encoded string.

example.title: quoted_printable_encode example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$encoded = quoted_printable_encode('Möchten Sie ein paar Äpfel?');

var_dump($encoded);
var_dump(quoted_printable_decode($encoded));
?>
example.screen: string(37) "M=C3=B6chten Sie ein paar =C3=84pfel?" string(29) "Möchten Sie ein paar Äpfel?"

refnamediv.refpurpose: Quote meta characters

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns a version of str with a backslash character (\) before every character that is among these: . \ + * ? [ ^ ] ( $ )

listitem.para: The input string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the string with meta characters quoted, or false if an empty string is given as string.

example.title: quotemeta example
example.programlisting:
<?php

var_dump(quotemeta('PHP is a popular scripting language. Fast, flexible, and pragmatic.'));
?>
example.screen: string(69) "PHP is a popular scripting language\. Fast, flexible, and pragmatic\."

note.simpara: This function is binary-safe.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Strip whitespace (or other characters) from the end of a string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function returns a string with whitespace (or other characters) stripped from the end of string.
Without the second parameter, rtrim will strip these characters:

listitem.simpara: " ": ASCII SP character 0x20, an ordinary space.
"\t": ASCII HT character 0x09, a tab.
"\n": ASCII LF character 0x0A, a new line (line feed).
"\r": ASCII CR character 0x0D, a carriage return.
"\0": ASCII NUL character 0x00, the NUL-byte.
"\v": ASCII VT character 0x0B, a vertical tab.
The input string.

Optionally, the stripped characters can also be specified using the characters parameter. Simply list all characters that need to be stripped. With .. it is possible to specify an incrementing range of characters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns the modified string.

example.title: Usage example of rtrim
example.programlisting:
<?php

$text = "\t\tThese are a few words :) ...  ";
$binary = "\x09Example string\x0A";
$hello  = "Hello World";
var_dump($text, $binary, $hello);

print "\n";

$trimmed = rtrim($text);
var_dump($trimmed);

$trimmed = rtrim($text, " \t.");
var_dump($trimmed);

$trimmed = rtrim($hello, "Hdle");
var_dump($trimmed);

// trim the ASCII control characters at the end of $binary
// (from 0 to 31 inclusive)
$clean = rtrim($binary, "\x00..\x1F");
var_dump($clean);

?>
example.screen:
string(32) " These are a few words :) ... " string(16) " Example string " string(11) "Hello World"
string(30) " These are a few words :) ..." string(26) " These are a few words :)" string(9) "Hello Wor" string(15) " Example string"

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set locale information

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Alternative signature (not supported with named arguments):
refsect1.para: Sets locale information.

warning.simpara: The locale information is maintained per process, not per thread. If you are running PHP on a multithreaded server API, you may experience sudden changes in locale settings while a script is running, though the script itself never called setlocale. This happens due to other scripts running in different threads of the same process at the same time, changing the process-wide locale using setlocale. On Windows, locale information is maintained per thread as of PHP 7.0.5.

listitem.para:
category is a named constant specifying the category of the functions affected by the locale setting:
LC_ALL for all of the below
LC_COLLATE for string comparison, see strcoll
LC_CTYPE for character classification and conversion, for example ctype_alpha
LC_MONETARY for localeconv
LC_NUMERIC for decimal separator (See also localeconv)
LC_TIME for date and time formatting with strftime
LC_MESSAGES for system responses (available if PHP was compiled with libintl)
If locales is the empty string "" or is null, the locale names will be set from the values of environment variables with the same names as the above categories, or from "LANG".
If locales is "0", the locale setting is not affected, only the current setting is returned.

If locales is followed by additional parameters then each parameter is tried to be set as new locale until success. This is useful if a locale is known under different names on different systems or for providing a fallback for a possibly not available locale.
Optional string parameters to try as locale settings until success.

Each array element is tried to be set as new locale until success. This is useful if a locale is known under different names on different systems or for providing a fallback for a possibly not available locale.

note.para: On Windows, setlocale(LC_ALL, '') sets the locale names from the system's regional/language settings (accessible via Control Panel).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the new current locale, or false if the locale functionality is not implemented on your platform, the specified locale does not exist or the category name is invalid.
An invalid category name also causes a warning message. Category/locale names can be found in RFC 1766 and ISO 639. Different systems have different naming schemes for locales.

note.para: The return value of setlocale depends on the system that PHP is running. It returns exactly what the system setlocale function returns.

row.entry: Passing an integer 0 as the locales argument is no longer supported and now throws a TypeError.

example.title: setlocale Examples
example.programlisting:
<?php
/* Set locale to Dutch */
setlocale(LC_ALL, 'nl_NL');

/* Output: vrijdag 22 december 1978 */
echo strftime("%A %e %B %Y", mktime(0, 0, 0, 12, 22, 1978));

/* try different possible locale names for german */
$loc_de = setlocale(LC_ALL, 'de_DE@euro', 'de_DE', 'de', 'ge');
echo "Preferred locale for german on this system is '$loc_de'";
?>

example.title: setlocale Retrieve current setting
example.programlisting:
<?php
/* Retrieve current setting */
$current = setlocale(LC_ALL, null);

echo "Current locale '$current'";
?>

example.title: setlocale Examples for Windows
example.programlisting:
<?php
/* Set locale to Dutch */
setlocale(LC_ALL, 'nld_nld');

/* Output: vrijdag 22 december 1978 */
echo strftime("%A %d %B %Y", mktime(0, 0, 0, 12, 22, 1978));

/* try different possible locale names for german */
$loc_de = setlocale(LC_ALL, 'de_DE@euro', 'de_DE', 'deu_deu');
echo "Preferred locale for german on this system is '$loc_de'";
?>

tip.para: Windows users will find useful information about locales strings at Microsoft's MSDN website. Supported language strings can be found in the language strings documentation and supported country/region strings in the country/region strings documentation.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Calculate the sha1 hash of a string

warning.simpara: It is not recommended to use this function to secure passwords, due to the fast nature of this hashing algorithm. See the Password Hashing FAQ for details and best practices.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Calculates the sha1 hash of string using the US Secure Hash Algorithm 1.

listitem.para: The input string.
If the optional binary is set to true, then the sha1 digest is instead returned in raw binary format with a length of 20, otherwise the returned value is a 40-character hexadecimal number.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the sha1 hash as a string.

example.title: A sha1 example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$str = 'apple';

if (sha1($str) === 'd0be2dc421be4fcd0172e5afceea3970e2f3d940') {
    echo "Would you like a green or red apple?";
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Calculate the sha1 hash of a file

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Calculates the sha1 hash of the file specified by filename using the US Secure Hash Algorithm 1, and returns that hash. The hash is a 40-character hexadecimal number.

listitem.para: The filename of the file to hash.
When true, returns the digest in raw binary format with a length of 20.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a string on success, false otherwise.

example.title: sha1_file example
example.programlisting:
<?php
foreach (glob('/examples/*.xml') as $ent)
{
    if (is_dir($ent)) {
        continue;
    }

    echo $ent . ' (SHA1: ' . sha1_file($ent) . ')', PHP_EOL;
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Calculate the similarity between two strings

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This calculates the similarity between two strings as described in Programming Classics: Implementing the World's Best Algorithms by Oliver (ISBN 0-131-00413-1). Note that this implementation does not use a stack as in Oliver's pseudo code, but recursive calls which may or may not speed up the whole process. Note also that the complexity of this algorithm is O(N**3) where N is the length of the longest string.

listitem.para: The first string.
The second string.

note.para: Swapping the string1 and string2 may yield a different result; see the example below.

listitem.para: By passing a reference as third argument, similar_text will calculate the similarity in percent, by dividing the result of similar_text by the average of the lengths of the given strings times 100.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the number of matching chars in both strings.

The number of matching characters is calculated by finding the longest first common substring, and then doing this for the prefixes and the suffixes, recursively. The lengths of all found common substrings are added.

example.title: similar_text argument swapping example
example.para: This example shows that swapping the string1 and string2 argument may yield different results.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$sim = similar_text('bafoobar', 'barfoo', $perc);
echo "similarity: $sim ($perc %)\n";
$sim = similar_text('barfoo', 'bafoobar', $perc);
echo "similarity: $sim ($perc %)\n";
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Calculate the soundex key of a string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Calculates the soundex key of string.

Soundex keys have the property that words pronounced similarly produce the same soundex key, and can thus be used to simplify searches in databases where you know the pronunciation but not the spelling.
This particular soundex function is one described by Donald Knuth in "The Art Of Computer Programming, vol. 3: Sorting And Searching", Addison-Wesley (1973), pp. 391-392.

listitem.para: The input string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the soundex key as a string with four characters. If at least one letter is contained in string, the returned string starts with a letter. Otherwise "0000" is returned.

row.entry: Prior to this version, calling the function with an empty string returned false for no particular reason.

example.title: Soundex Examples
example.programlisting:
<?php echo soundex("Euler"), PHP_EOL, soundex("Ellery"), PHP_EOL;
soundex("Euler") == soundex("Ellery"); // E460 soundex("Gauss") == soundex("Ghosh"); // G200 soundex("Hilbert") == soundex("Heilbronn"); // H416 soundex("Knuth") == soundex("Kant"); // K530 soundex("Lloyd") == soundex("Ladd"); // L300 soundex("Lukasiewicz") == soundex("Lissajous"); // L222 ?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Return a formatted string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns a string produced according to the formatting string format.

listitem.simpara: The format string is composed of zero or more directives: ordinary characters (excluding %) that are copied directly to the result and conversion specifications, each of which results in fetching its own parameter.
A conversion specification follows this prototype: %[argnum$][flags][width][.precision]specifier.

formalpara.title: Argnum
formalpara.para: An integer followed by a dollar sign $, to specify which number argument to treat in the conversion.

row.entry: Left-justify within the given field width; Right justification is the default
Prefix positive numbers with a plus sign +; Default only negative are prefixed with a negative sign.
Pads the result with spaces. This is the default.
Only left-pads numbers with zeros. With s specifiers this can also right-pad with zeros.
Pads the result with the character (char).

formalpara.title: Width
formalpara.para: Either an integer that says how many characters (minimum) this conversion should result in, or *. If * is used, then the width is supplied as an additional integer value preceding the one formatted by the specifier.

formalpara.title: Precision
formalpara.para:
A period . optionally followed by either an integer or *, whose meaning depends on the specifier:
For e, E, f and F specifiers: this is the number of digits to be printed after the decimal point (by default, this is 6).
For g, G, h and H specifiers: this is the maximum number of significant digits to be printed.
For s specifier: it acts as a cutoff point, setting a maximum character limit to the string.
If the period is specified without an explicit value for precision, 0 is assumed. If * is used, the precision is supplied as an additional integer value preceding the one formatted by the specifier.

row.entry: A literal percent character. No argument is required.
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as a binary number.
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as the character with that ASCII.
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as a (signed) decimal number.
The argument is treated as scientific notation (e.g. 1.2e+2).
Like the e specifier but uses uppercase letter (e.g. 1.2E+2).
The argument is treated as a float and presented as a floating-point number (locale aware).
The argument is treated as a float and presented as a floating-point number (non-locale aware).

entry.simpara: General format.
Let P equal the precision if nonzero, 6 if the precision is omitted, or 1 if the precision is zero. Then, if a conversion with style E would have an exponent of X:
If P > X ≥ −4, the conversion is with style f and precision P − (X + 1). Otherwise, the conversion is with style e and precision P − 1.

row.entry: Like the g specifier but uses E and f.
Like the g specifier but uses F. Available as of PHP 8.0.0.
Like the g specifier but uses E and F. Available as of PHP 8.0.0.
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as an octal number.
The argument is treated and presented as a string.
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as an unsigned decimal number.
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as a hexadecimal number (with lowercase letters).
The argument is treated as an integer and presented as a hexadecimal number (with uppercase letters).

warning.simpara: The c type specifier ignores padding and width.
Attempting to use a combination of the string and width specifiers with character sets that require more than one byte per character may result in unexpected results.

listitem.para:
Variables will be co-erced to a suitable type for the specifier:
Type Handling
Type Specifiers
string s
int
d, u, c, o, x, X, b
float
e, E, f, F, g, G, h, H

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a string produced according to the formatting string format.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: As of PHP 8.0.0, a ValueError is thrown if the number of arguments is zero. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, a E_WARNING was emitted instead.
As of PHP 8.0.0, a ValueError is thrown if [width] is less than zero or bigger than PHP_INT_MAX. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, a E_WARNING was emitted instead.
As of PHP 8.0.0, a ValueError is thrown if [precision] is less than zero or bigger than PHP_INT_MAX. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, a E_WARNING was emitted instead.
As of PHP 8.0.0, a ArgumentCountError is thrown when less arguments are given than required. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, false was returned and a E_WARNING emitted instead.

row.entry: This function no longer returns false on failure.
Throw a ValueError if the number of arguments is zero; previously this function emitted a E_WARNING instead.
Throw a ValueError if [width] is less than zero or bigger than PHP_INT_MAX; previously this function emitted a E_WARNING instead.
Throw a ValueError if [precision] is less than zero or bigger than PHP_INT_MAX; previously this function emitted a E_WARNING instead.
Throw a ArgumentCountError when less arguments are given than required; previously this function emitted a E_WARNING instead.

refsect1.title: Examples

example.title: Argument swapping
example.para: The format string supports argument numbering/swapping.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$num = 5;
$location = 'tree';

$format = 'There are %d monkeys in the %s';
echo sprintf($format, $num, $location);
?>
example.screen: There are 5 monkeys in the tree

refsect1.para: However imagine we are creating a format string in a separate file, commonly because we would like to internationalize it and we rewrite it as:

example.title: Wrong Argument Order
example.para: The format string supports argument numbering/swapping.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$num = 5;
$location = 'tree';

$format = 'The %s contains %d monkeys';
echo sprintf($format, $num, $location);
?>

refsect1.para: We now have a problem. The order of the placeholders in the format string does not match the order of the arguments in the code. We would like to leave the code as is and simply indicate in the format string which arguments the placeholders refer to. We would write the format string like this instead:

example.title: Use Order Placeholder
example.programlisting:
<?php
$num = 5;
$location = 'tree';

$format = 'The %2$s contains %1$d monkeys';
echo sprintf($format, $num, $location);
?>

refsect1.para: An added benefit is that placeholders can be repeated without adding more arguments in the code.

example.title: Repeated Placeholder
example.programlisting:
<?php
$num = 5;
$location = 'tree';

$format = 'The %2$s contains %1$d monkeys.
           That\'s a nice %2$s full of %1$d monkeys.';
echo sprintf($format, $num, $location);
?>

refsect1.para: When using argument swapping, the n$ position specifier must come immediately after the percent sign (%), before any other specifiers, as shown below.

example.title: Specifying padding character
example.programlisting:
<?php
echo sprintf("%'.9d\n", 123);
echo sprintf("%'.09d\n", 123);
?>

example.title: Position specifier with other specifiers
example.programlisting:
<?php
$num = 5;
$location = 'tree';

$format = 'The %2$s contains %1$04d monkeys';
echo sprintf($format, $num, $location);
?>

example.title: sprintf: zero-padded integers
example.programlisting:
<?php
$year = 2005;
$month = 5;
$day = 6;

$isodate = sprintf("%04d-%02d-%02d", $year, $month, $day);
echo $isodate, PHP_EOL;
?>

example.title: sprintf: formatting currency
example.programlisting:
<?php
$money1 = 68.75;
$money2 = 54.35;
$money = $money1 + $money2;
echo $money, PHP_EOL;

$formatted = sprintf("%01.2f", $money);
echo $formatted, PHP_EOL;
?>

example.title: sprintf: scientific notation
example.programlisting:
<?php
$number = 362525200;

echo sprintf("%.3e", $number), PHP_EOL;
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Parses input from a string according to a format

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The function sscanf is the input analog of printf. sscanf reads from the string string and interprets it according to the specified format.
Any whitespace in the format string matches any whitespace in the input string. This means that even a tab (\t) in the format string can match a single space character in the input string.

listitem.simpara: The input string being parsed.

listitem.para:
The interpreted format for string, which is described in the documentation for sprintf with following differences:
Function is not locale-aware.
F, g, G and b are not supported.
D stands for decimal number.
i stands for integer with base detection.
n stands for number of characters processed so far.
s stops reading at any whitespace character.
* instead of argnum$ suppresses the assignment of this conversion specification.

listitem.simpara: Optionally pass in variables by reference that will contain the parsed values.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: If only two parameters were passed to this function, the values parsed will be returned as an array. Otherwise, if optional parameters are passed, the function will return the number of assigned values. The optional parameters must be passed by reference.
If there are more substrings expected in the format than there are available within string, null will be returned.
When optional parameters are used and the end of the input string is reached before any value has been parsed, -1 is returned.

refsect1.title: Examples

example.title: sscanf Example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// getting the serial number
list($serial) = sscanf("SN/2350001", "SN/%d");
// and the date of manufacturing
$mandate = "January 01 2000";
list($month, $day, $year) = sscanf($mandate, "%s %d %d");
echo "Item $serial was manufactured on: $year-" . substr($month, 0, 3) . "-$day\n";
?>

refsect1.simpara: If optional parameters are passed, the function will return the number of assigned values.

example.title: sscanf - using optional parameters
example.programlisting:
<?php
// get author info and generate DocBook entry
$auth = "24\tLewis Carroll";
$n = sscanf($auth, "%d\t%s %s", $id, $first, $last);
echo "<author id='$id'>
    <firstname>$first</firstname>
    <surname>$last</surname>
</author>\n";
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Determine if a string contains a given substring

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Performs a case-sensitive check indicating if needle is contained in haystack.

listitem.para: The string to search in.
The substring to search for in the haystack.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if needle is in haystack, false otherwise.

example.title: Using the empty string ''
example.programlisting:
<?php
if (str_contains('abc', '')) {
    echo "Checking the existence of the empty string will always return true";
}
?>
example.screen: Checking the existence of the empty string will always return true

example.title: Showing case-sensitivity
example.programlisting:
<?php
$string = 'The lazy fox jumped over the fence';

if (str_contains($string, 'lazy')) {
    echo "The string 'lazy' was found in the string\n";
}

if (str_contains($string, 'Lazy')) {
    echo 'The string "Lazy" was found in the string';
} else {
    echo '"Lazy" was not found because the case does not match';
}

?>
example.screen: The string 'lazy' was found in the string "Lazy" was not found because the case does not match

note.simpara: This function is binary-safe.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Decrement an alphanumeric string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the decremented alphanumeric ASCII string.

listitem.para: The input string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the decremented alphanumeric ASCII string.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: A ValueError is thrown if string is empty.
A ValueError is thrown if string is not an alphanumeric ASCII string.
A ValueError is thrown if string cannot be decremented. For example, "A" or "0".

example.title: Basic str_decrement example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$str = 'ABC';
var_dump(str_decrement($str));
?>

example.title: str_decrement example with a carry
example.programlisting:
<?php
$str = 'ZA';
var_dump(str_decrement($str));

$str = 'AA';
var_dump(str_decrement($str));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks if a string ends with a given substring

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Performs a case-sensitive check indicating if haystack ends with needle.

listitem.para: The string to search in.
The substring to search for in the haystack.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if haystack ends with needle, false otherwise.

example.title: Using the empty string ''
example.programlisting:
<?php
if (str_ends_with('abc', '')) {
    echo "All strings end with the empty string";
}
?>
example.screen: All strings end with the empty string

example.title: Showing case-sensitivity
example.programlisting:
<?php
$string = 'The lazy fox jumped over the fence';

if (str_ends_with($string, 'fence')) {
    echo "The string ends with 'fence'\n";
}

if (str_ends_with($string, 'Fence')) {
    echo 'The string ends with "Fence"';
} else {
    echo '"Fence" was not found because the case does not match';
}

?>
example.screen: The string ends with 'fence' "Fence" was not found because the case does not match

note.simpara: This function is binary-safe.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Parse a CSV string into an array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Parses a string input for fields in CSV format and returns an array containing the fields read.

note.simpara: The locale settings are taken into account by this function. For example, data encoded in certain one-byte encodings may be parsed incorrectly if LC_CTYPE is en_US.UTF-8.

listitem.para: The string to parse.
The separator parameter sets the field separator. It must be a single byte character.
The enclosure parameter sets the field enclosure character. It must be a single byte character.
The escape parameter sets the escape character. It must be a single byte character or the empty string. The empty string ("") disables the proprietary escape mechanism.

warning.simpara: In the input stream, the enclosure character can always be escaped by doubling it inside a quoted string, resulting in a single enclosure character in the parsed result. The escape character works differently: If a sequence of escape and enclosure characters appear in the input, both characters will be present in the parsed result. So for the default parameters, a CSV line like "a""b","c\"d" will have the fields parsed as a"b and c\"d, respectively.
As of PHP 8.4.0, depending on the default value of escape is deprecated. It needs to be provided explicitly either positionally or by the use of named arguments.

When escape is set to anything other than an empty string ("") it can result in CSV that is not compliant with RFC 4180 or unable to survive a roundtrip through the PHP CSV functions. The default for escape is "\\" so it is recommended to set it to the empty string explicitly. The default value will change in a future version of PHP, no earlier than PHP 9.0.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns an indexed array containing the fields read.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Throws a ValueError if separator or enclosure is not one byte long.
Throws a ValueError if escape is not one byte long or the empty string.

row.entry: Relying on the default value of escape is now deprecated.
Now throws a ValueError if separator, enclosure, or escape is invalid. This mimics the behavior of fgetcsv and fputcsv.
An empty string is returned instead of a string with a single null byte for the last field if it contains only an unterminated enclosure.
The escape parameter now interprets an empty string as signal to disable the proprietary escape mechanism. Formerly, an empty string was treated like the default parameter value.

example.title: str_getcsv example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$string = 'PHP,Java,Python,Kotlin,Swift';
$data = str_getcsv($string, escape: '\\');

var_dump($data);
?>
example.screen: array(5) { [0]=> string(3) "PHP" [1]=> string(4) "Java" [2]=> string(6) "Python" [3]=> string(6) "Kotlin" [4]=> string(5) "Swift" }

example.title: str_getcsv example with an empty string

caution.simpara: On an empty string this function returns the value [null] instead of an empty array.

example.programlisting:
<?php

$string = '';
$data = str_getcsv($string, escape: '\\');

var_dump($data);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Increment an alphanumeric string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the incremented alphanumeric ASCII string.

listitem.para: The input string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the incremented alphanumeric ASCII string.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: A ValueError is thrown if string is empty.
A ValueError is thrown if string is not an alphanumeric ASCII string.

example.title: Basic str_increment example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$str = 'ABC';
var_dump(str_increment($str));
?>

example.title: str_increment example with a carry
example.programlisting:
<?php
$str = 'DZ';
var_dump(str_increment($str));

$str = 'ZZ';
var_dump(str_increment($str));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Case-insensitive version of str_replace

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function returns a string or an array with all occurrences of search in subject (ignoring case) replaced with the given replace value.
To replace text based on a pattern rather than a fixed string, use preg_replace with the i pattern modifier.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.para: If search and replace are arrays, then str_ireplace takes a value from each array and uses them to search and replace on subject. If replace has fewer values than search, then an empty string is used for the rest of replacement values. If search is an array and replace is a string, then this replacement string is used for every value of search. The converse would not make sense, though.
If search or replace are arrays, their elements are processed first to last.

listitem.para: The value being searched for, otherwise known as the needle. An array may be used to designate multiple needles.
The replacement value that replaces found search values. An array may be used to designate multiple replacements.
The string or array being searched and replaced on, otherwise known as the haystack.
If subject is an array, then the search and replace is performed with every entry of subject, and the return value is an array as well.
If passed, this will be set to the number of replacements performed.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a string or an array of replacements.

row.entry: Case folding no longer depends on the locale set with setlocale. Only ASCII case folding will be done. Non-ASCII bytes will be compared by their byte value.

example.title: str_ireplace example
example.programlisting: <?php $bodytag = str_ireplace("%body%", "black", "<body text=%BODY%>"); echo $bodytag; // <body text=black> ?>

note.simpara: This function is binary-safe.

caution.title: Replacement order gotcha
caution.para: Because str_ireplace replaces left to right, it might replace a previously inserted value when doing multiple replacements. Example #2 in the str_replace documentation demonstrates how this may affect you in practice.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Pad a string to a certain length with another string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function returns the string string padded on the left, the right, or both sides to the specified padding length. If the optional argument pad_string is not supplied, the string is padded with spaces, otherwise it is padded with characters from pad_string up to the limit.

listitem.para: The input string.
The desired length of the final padded string. If the value of length is negative, less than, or equal to the length of the input string, no padding takes place, and string will be returned.

note.para: The pad_string may be truncated if the required number of padding characters can't be evenly divided by the pad_string's length.

listitem.para: Optional argument pad_type can be STR_PAD_RIGHT, STR_PAD_LEFT, or STR_PAD_BOTH. If pad_type is not specified it is assumed to be STR_PAD_RIGHT.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the padded string.

example.title: str_pad example
example.programlisting: <?php $input = "Alien"; echo str_pad($input, 10), PHP_EOL; // produces "Alien " echo str_pad($input, 10, "-=", STR_PAD_LEFT), PHP_EOL; // produces "-=-=-Alien" echo str_pad($input, 10, "_", STR_PAD_BOTH), PHP_EOL; // produces "__Alien___" echo str_pad($input, 6, "___"), PHP_EOL; // produces "Alien_" echo str_pad($input, 3, "*"), PHP_EOL; // produces "Alien" ?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Repeat a string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns string repeated times times.

listitem.para: The string to be repeated.

listitem.simpara: Number of times the string string should be repeated.
listitem.para: times has to be greater than or equal to 0. If the times is set to 0, the function will return an empty string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the repeated string.

example.title: str_repeat example
example.programlisting:
<?php
echo str_repeat("-=", 10);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Replace all occurrences of the search string with the replacement string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function returns a string or an array with all occurrences of search in subject replaced with the given replace value.
To replace text based on a pattern rather than a fixed string, use preg_replace.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.para: If search and replace are arrays, then str_replace takes a value from each array and uses them to search and replace on subject. If replace has fewer values than search, then an empty string is used for the rest of replacement values. If search is an array and replace is a string, then this replacement string is used for every value of search. The converse would not make sense, though.
If search or replace are arrays, their elements are processed first to last.

listitem.para: The value being searched for, otherwise known as the needle. An array may be used to designate multiple needles.
The replacement value that replaces found search values. An array may be used to designate multiple replacements.
The string or array being searched and replaced on, otherwise known as the haystack.
If subject is an array, then the search and replace is performed with every entry of subject, and the return value is an array as well.
If passed, this will be set to the number of replacements performed.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: This function returns a string or an array with the replaced values.

example.title: Basic str_replace examples
example.programlisting:
<?php
// Provides: <body text='black'>
$bodytag = str_replace("%body%", "black", "<body text='%body%'>");
echo $bodytag, PHP_EOL;

// Provides: Hll Wrld f PHP
$vowels = array("a", "e", "i", "o", "u", "A", "E", "I", "O", "U");
$onlyconsonants = str_replace($vowels, "", "Hello World of PHP");
echo $onlyconsonants, PHP_EOL;

// Provides: You should eat pizza, beer, and ice cream every day
$phrase  = "You should eat fruits, vegetables, and fiber every day.";
$healthy = array("fruits", "vegetables", "fiber");
$yummy   = array("pizza", "beer", "ice cream");

$newphrase = str_replace($healthy, $yummy, $phrase);
echo $newphrase, PHP_EOL;

// Provides: 2
$str = str_replace("ll", "", "good golly miss molly!", $count);
echo $count, PHP_EOL;
?>

example.title: Examples of potential str_replace gotchas
example.programlisting: '; // Processes \r\n's first so they aren't converted twice. $newstr = str_replace($order, $replace, $str); echo $newstr, PHP_EOL; // Outputs F because A is replaced with B, then B is replaced with C, and so on... // Finally E is replaced with F, because of left to right replacements. $search = array('A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E'); $replace = array('B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'); $subject = 'A'; echo str_replace($search, $replace, $subject), PHP_EOL; // Outputs: apearpearle pear // For the same reason mentioned above $letters = array('a', 'p'); $fruit = array('apple', 'pear'); $text = 'a p'; $output = str_replace($letters, $fruit, $text); echo $output, PHP_EOL; ?>

note.simpara: This function is binary-safe.

caution.title: Replacement order gotcha
caution.para: Because str_replace replaces left to right, it might replace a previously inserted value when doing multiple replacements. See also the examples in this document.

note.para: This function is case-sensitive. Use str_ireplace for case-insensitive replace.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Perform the rot13 transform on a string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Performs the ROT13 encoding on the string argument and returns the resulting string.

The ROT13 encoding simply shifts every letter by 13 places in the alphabet while leaving non-alpha characters untouched. Encoding and decoding are done by the same function, passing an encoded string as argument will return the original version.

listitem.para: The input string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the ROT13 version of the given string.

example.title: str_rot13 example
example.programlisting:
<?php
echo str_rot13('PHP 4.3.0'); // CUC 4.3.0
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Randomly shuffles a string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: str_shuffle shuffles a string. One permutation of all possible is created.

caution.simpara: This function does not generate cryptographically secure values, and must not be used for cryptographic purposes, or purposes that require returned values to be unguessable.

If cryptographically secure randomness is required, the Random\Randomizer may be used with the Random\Engine\Secure engine. For simple use cases, the random_int and random_bytes functions provide a convenient and secure API that is backed by the operating system’s CSPRNG.

This function uses the global Mt19937 (“Mersenne Twister”) instance as the source of randomness and thus shares its state with all other functions using the global Mt19937. Using any of these functions advances the sequence for all the other functions, regardless of scope.
Generating repeatable sequences by seeding mt_srand or srand with a known value will also yield repeatable output from this function.
Prefer using Random\Randomizer methods in all newly written code.

listitem.para: The input string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the shuffled string.

row.entry: The internal randomization algorithm has been changed to use the Mersenne Twister Random Number Generator instead of the libc rand function.

example.title: str_shuffle example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$str = 'abcdef';
$shuffled = str_shuffle($str);

// This will echo something like: bfdaec
echo $shuffled;
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Convert a string to an array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Converts a string to an array.

listitem.para: The input string.
Maximum length of the chunk.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: If the optional length parameter is specified, the returned array will be broken down into chunks with each being length in length, except the final chunk which may be shorter if the string does not divide evenly. The default length is 1, meaning every chunk will be one byte in size.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: If length is less than 1, a ValueError will be thrown.

row.entry: If string is empty an empty array is now returned. Previously an array containing a single empty string was returned.
If length is less than 1, a ValueError will be thrown now; previously, an error of level E_WARNING has been raised instead, and the function returned false.

example.title: Example uses of str_split
example.programlisting:
<?php

$str = "Hello Friend";

$arr1 = str_split($str);
$arr2 = str_split($str, 3);

print_r($arr1);
print_r($arr2);

?>

note.para: str_split will split into bytes, rather than characters when dealing with a multi-byte encoded string. mb_str_split can be used to split the string into code points. grapheme_str_split can be used to split the string into grapheme clusters.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks if a string starts with a given substring

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Performs a case-sensitive check indicating if haystack begins with needle.

listitem.para: The string to search in.
The substring to search for in the haystack.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if haystack begins with needle, false otherwise.

example.title: Using the empty string ''
example.programlisting:
<?php
if (str_starts_with('abc', '')) {
    echo "All strings start with the empty string";
}
?>
example.screen: All strings start with the empty string

example.title: Showing case-sensitivity
example.programlisting:
<?php
$string = 'The lazy fox jumped over the fence';

if (str_starts_with($string, 'The')) {
    echo "The string starts with 'The'\n";
}

if (str_starts_with($string, 'the')) {
    echo 'The string starts with "the"';
} else {
    echo '"the" was not found because the case does not match';
}

?>
example.screen: The string starts with 'The' "the" was not found because the case does not match

note.simpara: This function is binary-safe.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Return information about words used in a string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Counts the number of words inside string. If the optional format is not specified, then the return value will be an integer representing the number of words found. In the event the format is specified, the return value will be an array, content of which is dependent on the format. The possible value for the format and the resultant outputs are listed below.

For the purpose of this function, 'word' is defined as a locale dependent string containing alphabetic characters, which also may contain, but not start with "'" and "-" characters. Note that multibyte locales are not supported.

listitem.para: The string

Specify the return value of this function. The current supported values are:
0 - returns the number of words found
1 - returns an array containing all the words found inside the string
2 - returns an associative array, where the key is the numeric position of the word inside the string and the value is the actual word itself
A list of additional characters which will be considered as 'word'

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns an array or an integer, depending on the format chosen.

example.title: A str_word_count example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$str = "Hello fri3nd, you're
       looking          good today!";

print_r(str_word_count($str, 1));
print_r(str_word_count($str, 2));
print_r(str_word_count($str, 1, 'àáãç3'));

echo str_word_count($str);

?>
example.screen: Array ( [0] => Hello [1] => fri [2] => nd [3] => you're [4] => looking [5] => good [6] => today ) Array ( [0] => Hello [6] => fri [10] => nd [14] => you're [28] => looking [45] => good [50] => today ) Array ( [0] => Hello [1] => fri3nd [2] => you're [3] => looking [4] => good [5] => today ) 7

refnamediv.refpurpose: Binary safe case-insensitive string comparison

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Binary safe case-insensitive string comparison. The comparison is not locale aware; only ASCII letters are compared in a case-insensitive way.

listitem.para: The first string
The second string

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a value less than 0 if string1 is less than string2; a value greater than 0 if string1 is greater than string2, and 0 if they are equal. No particular meaning can be reliably inferred from the value aside from its sign.

row.entry: This function is no longer guaranteed to return strlen($string1) - strlen($string2) when string lengths are not equal, but may now return -1 or 1 instead.

example.title: strcasecmp example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$var1 = "Hello";
$var2 = "hello";
if (strcasecmp($var1, $var2) == 0) {
    echo '$var1 is equal to $var2 in a case-insensitive string comparison';
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of strstr

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: strstr.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Binary safe string comparison

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Note that this comparison is case sensitive. For case-insensitive comparison, see strcasecmp.
Note that this comparison is not locale aware. For locale aware comparison see strcoll or Collator::compare

listitem.para: The first string.
The second string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a value less than 0 if string1 is less than string2; a value greater than 0 if string1 is greater than string2, and 0 if they are equal. No particular meaning can be reliably inferred from the value aside from its sign.

row.entry: This function is no longer guaranteed to return strlen($string1) - strlen($string2) when string lengths are not equal, but may now return -1 or 1 instead.

example.title: strcmp example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$var1 = "Hello";
$var2 = "hello";
if (strcmp($var1, $var2) !== 0) {
    echo '$var1 is not equal to $var2 in a case sensitive string comparison';
}
?>

listitem.simpara: Full string comparison
Partial string comparison
Similar / other string comparison

refnamediv.refpurpose: Locale based string comparison

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Note that this comparison is case sensitive, and unlike strcmp this function is not binary safe.
strcoll uses the current locale for doing the comparisons. If the current locale is C or POSIX, this function is equivalent to strcmp.

listitem.para: The first string.
The second string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns < 0 if string1 is less than string2; > 0 if string1 is greater than string2, and 0 if they are equal.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Find length of initial segment not matching mask

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the length of the initial segment of string which does not contain any of the characters in characters.

If offset and length are omitted, then all of string will be examined. If they are included, then the effect will be the same as calling strcspn(substr($string, $offset, $length), $characters) (see for more information).

listitem.para: The string to examine.
The string containing every disallowed character.
The position in string to start searching.

If offset is given and is non-negative, then strcspn will begin examining string at the offset'th position. For instance, in the string 'abcdef', the character at position 0 is 'a', the character at position 2 is 'c', and so forth.
If offset is given and is negative, then strcspn will begin examining string at the offset'th position from the end of string.
The length of the segment from string to examine.
If length is given and is non-negative, then string will be examined for length characters after the starting position.
If length is given and is negative, then string will be examined from the starting position up to length characters from the end of string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the length of the initial segment of string which consists entirely of characters not in characters.

note.para: When a offset parameter is set, the returned length is counted starting from this position, not from the beginning of string.

entry.simpara: Prior to PHP 8.4.0, when characters was the empty string, the search would incorrectly stop at the first null byte in string.

example.title: strcspn example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$a = strcspn('banana', 'a');
$b = strcspn('banana', 'abcd');
$c = strcspn('banana', 'z');
$d = strcspn('abcdhelloabcd', 'a', -9);
$e = strcspn('abcdhelloabcd', 'a', -9, -5);

var_dump($a);
var_dump($b);
var_dump($c);
var_dump($d);
var_dump($e);
?>

note.simpara: This function is binary-safe.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Strip HTML and PHP tags from a string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function tries to return a string with all NULL bytes, HTML and PHP tags stripped from a given string. It uses the same tag stripping state machine as the fgetss function.

listitem.para: The input string.

You can use the optional second parameter to specify tags which should not be stripped. These are either given as string, or as of PHP 7.4.0, as array. Refer to the example below regarding the format of this parameter.

note.para: HTML comments and PHP tags are also stripped. This is hardcoded and can not be changed with allowed_tags.

Self-closing XHTML tags are ignored and only non-self-closing tags should be used in allowed_tags. For example, to allow both
and
, you should use:

informalexample.programlisting: '); ?>

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the stripped string.

row.entry: The allowed_tags now alternatively accepts an array.

example.title: strip_tags example
example.programlisting:
Test paragraph.

Other text'; echo strip_tags($text); echo "\n"; // Allow

and echo strip_tags($text, '

'); // as of PHP 7.4.0 the line above can be written as: // echo strip_tags($text, ['p', 'a']); ?>
example.screen:
Test paragraph. Other text

Test paragraph.

Other text

warning.para: This function should not be used to try to prevent XSS attacks. Use more appropriate functions like htmlspecialchars or other means depending on the context of the output.
Because strip_tags does not actually validate the HTML, partial or broken tags can result in the removal of more text/data than expected.

This function does not modify any attributes on the tags that you allow using allowed_tags, including the style and onmouseover attributes that a mischievous user may abuse when posting text that will be shown to other users.

note.para: Tag names within the input HTML that are greater than 1023 bytes in length will be treated as though they are invalid, regardless of the allowed_tags parameter.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Un-quote string quoted with addcslashes

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns a string with backslashes stripped off. Recognizes C-like \n, \r ..., octal and hexadecimal representation.

listitem.para: The string to be unescaped.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the unescaped string.

example.title: stripcslashes example
example.programlisting:
<?php
var_dump(stripcslashes('I\'d have a coffee.\nNot a problem.') === "I'd have a coffee. Not a problem."); // true ?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Find the position of the first occurrence of a case-insensitive substring in a string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Find the numeric position of the first occurrence of needle in the haystack string.
refsect1.simpara: Unlike strpos, stripos is case-insensitive.

listitem.para: The string to search in.
The string to search for.
listitem.simpara: Prior to PHP 8.0.0, if needle is not a string, it is converted to an integer and applied as the ordinal value of a character. This behavior is deprecated as of PHP 7.3.0, and relying on it is highly discouraged. Depending on the intended behavior, the needle should either be explicitly cast to string, or an explicit call to chr should be performed.

listitem.para: If specified, search will start this number of characters counted from the beginning of the string. If the offset is negative, the search will start this number of characters counted from the end of the string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the position of where the needle exists relative to the beginning of the haystack string (independent of offset). Also note that string positions start at 0, and not 1.
Returns false if the needle was not found.

warning.simpara: This function may return Boolean false, but may also return a non-Boolean value which evaluates to false. Please read the section on Booleans for more information. Use the === operator for testing the return value of this function.

listitem.simpara: If offset is greater than the length of haystack, a ValueError will be thrown.

row.entry: Case folding no longer depends on the locale set with setlocale. Only ASCII case folding will be done. Non-ASCII bytes will be compared by their byte value.
needle now accepts an empty string.
Passing an int as needle is no longer supported.
Passing an int as needle has been deprecated.
Support for negative offsets has been added.

example.title: stripos examples
example.programlisting:
<?php
$findme    = 'a';
$mystring1 = 'xyz';
$mystring2 = 'ABC';

$pos1 = stripos($mystring1, $findme);
$pos2 = stripos($mystring2, $findme);

// Nope, 'a' is certainly not in 'xyz'
if ($pos1 === false) {
    echo "The string '$findme' was not found in the string '$mystring1'", PHP_EOL;
}

// Note our use of !==.  Simply != would not work as expected
// because the position of 'a' is the 0th (first) character.
if ($pos2 !== false) {
    echo "We found '$findme' in '$mystring2' at position $pos2", PHP_EOL;
}
?>

note.simpara: This function is binary-safe.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Un-quotes a quoted string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Un-quotes a quoted string.
stripslashes can be used if you aren't inserting this data into a place (such as a database) that requires escaping. For example, if you're simply outputting data straight from an HTML form.

listitem.para: The input string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a string with backslashes stripped off. (\' becomes ' and so on.) Double backslashes (\\) are made into a single backslash (\).

example.title: A stripslashes example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$str = "Is your name O\'reilly?";

// Outputs: Is your name O'reilly?
echo stripslashes($str);
?>

note.para: stripslashes is not recursive. If you want to apply this function to a multi-dimensional array, you need to use a recursive function.

example.title: Using stripslashes on an array
example.programlisting:
<?php
function stripslashes_deep($value)
{
    $value = is_array($value) ?
                array_map('stripslashes_deep', $value) :
                stripslashes($value);

    return $value;
}

// Example
$array = array("f\\'oo", "b\\'ar", array("fo\\'o", "b\\'ar"));
$array = stripslashes_deep($array);

// Output
print_r($array);
?>
example.screen:
Array ( [0] => f'oo [1] => b'ar [2] => Array ( [0] => fo'o [1] => b'ar )
)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Case-insensitive strstr

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns all of haystack starting from and including the first occurrence of needle to the end.

refsect1.title: Parameters

listitem.para: The string to search in
The string to search for.
listitem.simpara: Prior to PHP 8.0.0, if needle is not a string, it is converted to an integer and applied as the ordinal value of a character. This behavior is deprecated as of PHP 7.3.0, and relying on it is highly discouraged. Depending on the intended behavior, the needle should either be explicitly cast to string, or an explicit call to chr should be performed.

listitem.para: If true, stristr returns the part of the haystack before the first occurrence of the needle (excluding needle).

refsect1.para: needle and haystack are examined in a case-insensitive manner.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the matched substring. If needle is not found, returns false.

row.entry: Case folding no longer depends on the locale set with setlocale. Only ASCII case folding will be done. Non-ASCII bytes will be compared by their byte value.
needle now accepts an empty string.
Passing an int as needle is no longer supported.
Passing an int as needle has been deprecated.

example.title: stristr example
example.programlisting: <?php $email = 'USER@EXAMPLE.com'; echo stristr($email, 'e'), PHP_EOL; // outputs ER@EXAMPLE.com echo stristr($email, 'e', true), PHP_EOL; // outputs US ?>

example.title: Testing if a string is found or not
example.programlisting:
<?php
  $string = 'Hello World!';
  if (stristr($string, 'earth') === FALSE) {
    echo '"earth" not found in string';
  }
// outputs: "earth" not found in string
?>

note.simpara: This function is binary-safe.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get string length

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the length of the given string.

listitem.para: The string being measured for length.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The length of the string in bytes.

example.title: A strlen example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$str = 'abcdef';
echo strlen($str), PHP_EOL; // 6

$str = ' ab cd ';
echo strlen($str), PHP_EOL; // 7
?>

note.para: strlen returns the number of bytes rather than the number of characters in a string.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Case insensitive string comparisons using a "natural order" algorithm

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function implements a comparison algorithm that orders alphanumeric strings in the way a human being would. The behaviour of this function is similar to strnatcmp, except that the comparison is not case sensitive. For more information see: Martin Pool's Natural Order String Comparison page.

listitem.para: The first string.
The second string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a value less than 0 if string1 is less than string2; a value greater than 0 if string1 is greater than string2, and 0 if they are equal. No particular meaning can be reliably inferred from the value aside from its sign.

row.entry: This function is no longer guaranteed to return strlen($string1) - strlen($string2) when string lengths are not equal, but may now return -1 or 1 instead.

example.title: strnatcasecmp example
example.programlisting:
<?php

var_dump(strnatcasecmp('Apple', 'Banana'));
var_dump(strnatcasecmp('Banana', 'Apple'));
var_dump(strnatcasecmp('apple', 'Apple'));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: String comparisons using a "natural order" algorithm

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function implements a comparison algorithm that orders alphanumeric strings in the way a human being would, this is described as a "natural ordering". Note that this comparison is case sensitive.

listitem.para: The first string.
The second string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a value less than 0 if string1 is less than string2; a value greater than 0 if string1 is greater than string2, and 0 if they are equal. No particular meaning can be reliably inferred from the value aside from its sign.

row.entry: This function is no longer guaranteed to return strlen($string1) - strlen($string2) when string lengths are not equal, but may now return -1 or 1 instead.

refsect1.title: Examples
refsect1.para:
An example of the difference between this algorithm and the regular computer string sorting algorithms (used in strcmp) can be seen below:
strcmp
<?php $arr1 = $arr2 = array("img12.png", "img10.png", "img2.png", "img1.png"); echo "Standard string comparison\n"; usort($arr1, "strcmp"); print_r($arr1); echo "\nNatural order string comparison\n"; usort($arr2, "strnatcmp"); print_r($arr2); ?>
The above example will output:
Standard string comparison Array ( [0] => img1.png [1] => img10.png [2] => img12.png [3] => img2.png )
Natural order string comparison Array ( [0] => img1.png [1] => img2.png [2] => img10.png [3] => img12.png )
For more information see: Martin Pool's Natural Order String Comparison page.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Binary safe case-insensitive string comparison of the first n characters

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function is similar to strcasecmp, with the difference that you can specify the (upper limit of the) number of characters from each string to be used in the comparison.

listitem.para: The first string.
The second string.
The length of strings to be used in the comparison.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a value less than 0 if string1 is less than string2; a value greater than 0 if string1 is greater than string2, and 0 if they are equal. No particular meaning can be reliably inferred from the value aside from its sign.

row.entry: This function is no longer guaranteed to return strlen($string1) - strlen($string2) when string lengths are not equal, but may now return -1 or 1 instead.

example.title: strncasecmp example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$var1 = 'Hello John';
$var2 = 'hello Doe';
if (strncasecmp($var1, $var2, 5) === 0) {
    echo 'First 5 characters of $var1 and $var2 are equal in a case-insensitive string comparison';
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Binary safe string comparison of the first n characters

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function is similar to strcmp, with the difference that you can specify the (upper limit of the) number of characters from each string to be used in the comparison.
Note that this comparison is case sensitive.

listitem.para: The first string.
The second string.
Number of characters to use in the comparison.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a value less than 0 if string1 is less than string2; a value greater than 0 if string1 is greater than string2, and 0 if they are equal. No particular meaning can be reliably inferred from the value aside from its sign.

row.entry: This function is no longer guaranteed to return strlen($string1) - strlen($string2) when string lengths are not equal, but may now return -1 or 1 instead.

example.title: strncmp example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$var1 = 'Hello John';
$var2 = 'Hello Doe';
if (strncmp($var1, $var2, 5) === 0) {
    echo 'First 5 characters of $var1 and $var2 are equal in a case-sensitive string comparison';
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Search a string for any of a set of characters

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: strpbrk searches the string string for any of the characters in characters.

listitem.para: The string where characters is looked for.
This parameter is case sensitive.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a string starting from the character found, or false if it is not found.

example.title: strpbrk example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$text = 'This is a Simple text.';

// this echoes "is is a Simple text." because 'i' is matched first
echo strpbrk($text, 'mi'), PHP_EOL;

// this echoes "Simple text." because chars are case sensitive
echo strpbrk($text, 'S'), PHP_EOL;
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Find the position of the first occurrence of a substring in a string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Find the numeric position of the first occurrence of needle in the haystack string.

listitem.para: The string to search in.

listitem.simpara: The string to search for.
Passing an empty string as needle matches at every position. strpos returns offset when it is specified, or 0 otherwise.

Prior to PHP 8.0.0, if needle is not a string, it is converted to an integer and applied as the ordinal value of a character. This behavior is deprecated as of PHP 7.3.0, and relying on it is highly discouraged. Depending on the intended behavior, the needle should either be explicitly cast to string, or an explicit call to chr should be performed.

listitem.para: If specified, search will start this number of characters counted from the beginning of the string. If the offset is negative, the search will start this number of characters counted from the end of the string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the position of where the needle exists relative to the beginning of the haystack string (independent of offset). Also note that string positions start at 0, and not 1.
Returns false if the needle was not found.

warning.simpara: This function may return Boolean false, but may also return a non-Boolean value which evaluates to false. Please read the section on Booleans for more information. Use the === operator for testing the return value of this function.

listitem.simpara: If offset is greater than the length of haystack, a ValueError will be thrown.

row.entry: needle now accepts an empty string.
Passing an int as needle is no longer supported.
Passing an int as needle has been deprecated.
Support for negative offsets has been added.

example.title: Using ===
example.programlisting:
<?php
$mystring = 'abc';
$findme   = 'a';
$pos = strpos($mystring, $findme);

// Note our use of ===.  Simply == would not work as expected
// because the position of 'a' was the 0th (first) character.
if ($pos === false) {
    echo "The string '$findme' was not found in the string '$mystring'";
} else {
    echo "The string '$findme' was found in the string '$mystring'";
    echo " and exists at position $pos";
}
?>

example.title: Using !==
example.programlisting:
<?php
$mystring = 'abc';
$findme   = 'a';
$pos = strpos($mystring, $findme);

// The !== operator can also be used.  Using != would not work as expected
// because the position of 'a' is 0. The statement (0 != false) evaluates
// to false.
if ($pos !== false) {
     echo "The string '$findme' was found in the string '$mystring'";
         echo " and exists at position $pos";
} else {
     echo "The string '$findme' was not found in the string '$mystring'";
}
?>

example.title: Using an offset
example.programlisting:
<?php
// We can search for the character, ignoring anything before the offset
$newstring = 'abcdef abcdef';
$pos = strpos($newstring, 'a', 1); // $pos = 7, not 0

echo $pos, PHP_EOL;
?>

note.simpara: This function is binary-safe.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Find the last occurrence of a character in a string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function returns the portion of haystack which starts at the last occurrence of needle and goes until the end of haystack.

listitem.para: The string to search in
If needle contains more than one character, only the first is used. This behavior is different from that of strstr.
listitem.simpara: Prior to PHP 8.0.0, if needle is not a string, it is converted to an integer and applied as the ordinal value of a character. This behavior is deprecated as of PHP 7.3.0, and relying on it is highly discouraged. Depending on the intended behavior, the needle should either be explicitly cast to string, or an explicit call to chr should be performed.

listitem.para: If true, strrchr returns the part of the haystack before the last occurrence of the needle (excluding the needle).

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: This function returns the portion of string, or false if needle is not found.

row.entry: needle now accepts an empty string.
Passing an int as needle is no longer supported.
Passing an int as needle has been deprecated.

example.title: strrchr example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$ext = strrchr('somefile.txt', '.');
echo "file extension: $ext \n";
$ext = $ext ? strtolower(substr($ext, 1)) : '';
echo "file extension: $ext";
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

note.simpara: This function is binary-safe.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Reverse a string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns string, reversed.

listitem.para: The string to be reversed.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the reversed string.

example.title: Reversing a string with strrev
example.programlisting: <?php echo strrev("Hello world!"); // outputs "!dlrow olleH" ?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Find the position of the last occurrence of a case-insensitive substring in a string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Find the numeric position of the last occurrence of needle in the haystack string.
refsect1.simpara: Unlike strrpos, strripos is case-insensitive.

listitem.para: The string to search in.
The string to search for.
listitem.simpara: Prior to PHP 8.0.0, if needle is not a string, it is converted to an integer and applied as the ordinal value of a character. This behavior is deprecated as of PHP 7.3.0, and relying on it is highly discouraged. Depending on the intended behavior, the needle should either be explicitly cast to string, or an explicit call to chr should be performed.

listitem.para: If zero or positive, the search is performed left to right skipping the first offset bytes of the haystack.

If negative, the search is performed right to left skipping the last offset bytes of the haystack and searching for the first occurrence of needle.
This is effectively looking for the last occurrence of needle before the last offset bytes.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para:
Returns the position where the needle exists relative to the beginning of the haystack string (independent of search direction or offset).
String positions start at 0, and not 1.
Returns false if the needle was not found.

warning.simpara: This function may return Boolean false, but may also return a non-Boolean value which evaluates to false. Please read the section on Booleans for more information. Use the === operator for testing the return value of this function.

listitem.simpara: If offset is greater than the length of haystack, a ValueError will be thrown.

row.entry: Case folding no longer depends on the locale set with setlocale. Only ASCII case folding will be done. Non-ASCII bytes will be compared by their byte value.
needle now accepts an empty string.
Passing an int as needle is no longer supported.
Passing an int as needle has been deprecated.

example.title: A simple strripos example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$haystack = 'ababcd';
$needle   = 'aB';

$pos      = strripos($haystack, $needle);

if ($pos === false) {
    echo "Sorry, we did not find `$needle` in `$haystack`";
} else {
    echo "Congratulations!\n";
    echo "We found the last `$needle` in `$haystack` at position `$pos`";
}

?>
example.screen: Congratulations! We found the last `aB` in `ababcd` at position `2`

refnamediv.refpurpose: Find the position of the last occurrence of a substring in a string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Find the numeric position of the last occurrence of needle in the haystack string.

listitem.para: The string to search in.
The string to search for.
listitem.simpara: Prior to PHP 8.0.0, if needle is not a string, it is converted to an integer and applied as the ordinal value of a character. This behavior is deprecated as of PHP 7.3.0, and relying on it is highly discouraged. Depending on the intended behavior, the needle should either be explicitly cast to string, or an explicit call to chr should be performed.

listitem.para: If zero or positive, the search is performed left to right skipping the first offset bytes of the haystack.

If negative, the search starts offset bytes from the right instead of from the beginning of haystack. The search is performed right to left, searching for the first occurrence of needle from the selected byte.
This is effectively looking for the last occurrence of needle at or before the last offset bytes.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para:
Returns the position where the needle exists relative to the beginning of the haystack string (independent of search direction or offset).
String positions start at 0, and not 1.
Returns false if the needle was not found.

warning.simpara: This function may return Boolean false, but may also return a non-Boolean value which evaluates to false. Please read the section on Booleans for more information. Use the === operator for testing the return value of this function.

listitem.simpara: If offset is greater than the length of haystack, a ValueError will be thrown.

row.entry: needle now accepts an empty string.
Passing an int as needle is no longer supported.
Passing an int as needle has been deprecated.

example.title: Checking if a needle is in the haystack
example.para: It is easy to mistake the return values for "character found at position 0" and "character not found". Here's how to detect the difference:
example.programlisting:
<?php
$mystring = 'Elephpant';

$pos = strrpos($mystring, "b");
if ($pos === false) { // note: three equal signs
    // not found...
}

?>

example.title: Searching with offsets
example.programlisting:
<?php
$foo = "0123456789a123456789b123456789c";

// Looking for '0' from the 0th byte (from the beginning)
