note.para: If needle is a string, the comparison is done in a case-sensitive manner.

listitem.para: The array.
If the third parameter strict is set to true then the in_array function will also check the types of the needle in the haystack.

note.simpara: Prior to PHP 8.0.0, a non-numeric string needle would loosely match a haystack value of 0, and vice versa. As of PHP 8.0.0, the number is converted to a string and the two are compared as strings, so only a numeric string of the same value still matches.

Non-strict mode nonetheless uses loose comparison, so values of different types can still compare as equal: true matches any truthy string, and false matches both "" and "0". Unless the types of all values involved are known with certainty, always pass strict to force an identity comparison.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if needle is found in the array, false otherwise.

example.title: in_array example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$os = array("Mac", "NT", "Irix", "Linux");
if (in_array("Irix", $os)) {
    echo "Got Irix";
}
if (in_array("mac", $os)) {
    echo "Got mac";
}
?>
example.para: The second condition fails because in_array is case-sensitive, so the program above will display:

example.title: in_array with strict example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$a = array('1.10', 12.4, 1.13);

if (in_array('12.4', $a, true)) {
    echo "'12.4' found with strict check\n";
}

if (in_array(1.13, $a, true)) {
    echo "1.13 found with strict check\n";
}
?>

example.title: in_array with an array as needle
example.programlisting:
<?php
$a = array(array('p', 'h'), array('p', 'r'), 'o');

if (in_array(array('p', 'h'), $a)) {
    echo "'ph' was found\n";
}

if (in_array(array('f', 'i'), $a)) {
    echo "'fi' was found\n";
}

if (in_array('o', $a)) {
    echo "'o' was found\n";
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Fetch a key from an array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: key returns the index element of the current array position.

listitem.para: The array.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The key function simply returns the key of the array element that's currently being pointed to by the internal pointer. It does not move the pointer in any way. If the internal pointer points beyond the end of the elements list or the array is empty, key returns null.

row.entry: Calling this function on objects is deprecated. Either convert the object to an array using get_mangled_object_vars first, or use the methods provided by a class that implements Iterator, such as ArrayIterator, instead.
Instances of SPL classes are now treated like empty objects that have no properties instead of calling the Iterator method with the same name as this function.

example.title: key example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$array = array(
    'fruit1' => 'apple',
    'fruit2' => 'orange',
    'fruit3' => 'grape',
    'fruit4' => 'apple',
    'fruit5' => 'apple');

// this cycle echoes all associative array
// key where value equals "apple"
while ($fruit_name = current($array)) {
    if ($fruit_name == 'apple') {
        echo key($array), "\n";
    }
    next($array);
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of array_key_exists

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: array_key_exists.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sort an array by key in descending order

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sorts array in place by keys in descending order.

note.simpara: If two members compare as equal, they retain their original order. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, their relative order in the sorted array was undefined.
Resets array's internal pointer to the first element.

listitem.para: The input array.

listitem.simpara: The optional second parameter flags may be used to modify the sorting behavior using these values:
listitem.para:
Sorting type flags:
SORT_REGULAR - compare items normally; the details are described in the comparison operators section
SORT_NUMERIC - compare items numerically
SORT_STRING - compare items as strings
SORT_LOCALE_STRING - compare items as strings, based on the current locale. It uses the locale, which can be changed using setlocale
SORT_NATURAL - compare items as strings using "natural ordering" like natsort
SORT_FLAG_CASE - can be combined (bitwise OR) with SORT_STRING or SORT_NATURAL to sort strings case-insensitively

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Always returns true.

row.entry: The return type is true now; previously, it was bool.
This function now does numeric string comparison under SORT_REGULAR using the standard PHP 8 rules.

example.title: krsort example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$fruits = array("d"=>"lemon", "a"=>"orange", "b"=>"banana", "c"=>"apple");
krsort($fruits);
foreach ($fruits as $key => $val) {
    echo "$key = $val\n";
}
?>
example.screen: d = lemon c = apple b = banana a = orange

simplelist.member: The comparison of array sorting functions

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sort an array by key in ascending order

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sorts array in place by keys in ascending order.

note.simpara: If two members compare as equal, they retain their original order. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, their relative order in the sorted array was undefined.
Resets array's internal pointer to the first element.

listitem.para: The input array.

listitem.simpara: The optional second parameter flags may be used to modify the sorting behavior using these values:
listitem.para:
Sorting type flags:
SORT_REGULAR - compare items normally; the details are described in the comparison operators section
SORT_NUMERIC - compare items numerically
SORT_STRING - compare items as strings
SORT_LOCALE_STRING - compare items as strings, based on the current locale. It uses the locale, which can be changed using setlocale
SORT_NATURAL - compare items as strings using "natural ordering" like natsort
SORT_FLAG_CASE - can be combined (bitwise OR) with SORT_STRING or SORT_NATURAL to sort strings case-insensitively

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Always returns true.

row.entry: The return type is true now; previously, it was bool.
This function now does numeric string comparison under SORT_REGULAR using the standard PHP 8 rules.

example.title: ksort example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$fruits = array("d"=>"lemon", "a"=>"orange", "b"=>"banana", "c"=>"apple");
ksort($fruits);
foreach ($fruits as $key => $val) {
    echo "$key = $val\n";
}
?>
example.screen: a = orange b = banana c = apple d = lemon

example.title: ksort with int keys
example.programlisting:
<?php
$a = [0 => 'First', 2 => 'Last', 1 => 'Middle'];
var_dump($a);
ksort($a);
var_dump($a);
?>
example.screen: array(3) { [0]=> string(5) "First" [2]=> string(4) "Last" [1]=> string(6) "Middle" } array(3) { [0]=> string(5) "First" [1]=> string(6) "Middle" [2]=> string(4) "Last" }

simplelist.member: The comparison of array sorting functions

refnamediv.refpurpose: Assign variables as if they were an array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Like array, this is not really a function, but a language construct. list is used to assign a list of variables in one operation. Only arrays and objects that implement ArrayAccess can be unpacked. list expressions can not be completely empty.

note.para: Before PHP 7.1.0, list only worked on numerical arrays and assumes the numerical indices start at 0.

refsect1.para: As of PHP 7.1.0, list can also contain explicit keys, allowing for the destructuring of arrays with non-integer or non-sequential keys. For more details on array destructuring, see the array destructuring section.

note.para: Attempting to access an array key which has not been defined is the same as accessing any other undefined variable: an E_WARNING-level error message (E_NOTICE-level prior to PHP 8.0.0) will be issued, and the result will be null.
Attempting to unpack a scalar assigns null to all variables. Attempting to unpack an object that does not implement ArrayAccess is a fatal error.

listitem.para: A variable.
Further variables.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the assigned array.

row.entry: Destructuring a non-array value (other than null) now emits an E_WARNING.
Support for reference assignments in array destructuring was added.
It is now possible to specify keys in list. This enables destructuring of arrays with non-integer or non-sequential keys.

refsect1.title: Examples

example.title: list examples
example.programlisting:
<?php

$info = array('coffee', 'brown', 'caffeine');

// Listing all the variables
list($drink, $color, $power) = $info;
echo "$drink is $color and $power makes it special.\n";

// Listing some of them
list($drink, , $power) = $info;
echo "$drink has $power.\n";

// Or let's skip to only the third one
list( , , $power) = $info;
echo "I need $power!\n";

// list() doesn't work with strings
list($bar) = "abcde";
var_dump($bar); // NULL
?>

example.title: An example use of list
example.programlisting:
<?php
$result = $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM employees");
while (list($id, $name) = $result->fetch(PDO::FETCH_NUM)) {
    echo "id: $id, name: $name\n";
}
?>

example.title: Using nested list
example.programlisting:
<?php

list($a, list($b, $c)) = array(1, array(2, 3));

var_dump($a, $b, $c);

?>

refsect1.para: The order in which the indices of the array to be consumed by list are defined is irrelevant.

example.title: list and order of index definitions
example.programlisting:
<?php
$foo = array(2 => 'a', 'foo' => 'b', 0 => 'c');
$foo[1] = 'd';
list($x, $y, $z) = $foo;
var_dump($foo, $x, $y, $z);
example.para: Gives the following output (note the order of the elements compared in which order they were written in the list syntax):
example.screen: array(4) { [2]=> string(1) "a" ["foo"]=> string(1) "b" [0]=> string(1) "c" [1]=> string(1) "d" } string(1) "c" string(1) "d" string(1) "a"

example.title: list with keys
example.simpara: As of PHP 7.1.0 list can now also contain explicit keys, which can be given as arbitrary expressions. Mixing of integer and string keys is allowed; however, elements with and without keys cannot be mixed.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$data = [
    ["id" => 1, "name" => 'Tom'],
    ["id" => 2, "name" => 'Fred'],
];
foreach ($data as ["id" => $id, "name" => $name]) {
    echo "id: $id, name: $name\n";
}
echo PHP_EOL;
list(1 => $second, 3 => $fourth) = [1, 2, 3, 4];
echo "$second, $fourth\n";
example.screen:
id: 1, name: Tom id: 2, name: Fred
2, 4

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sort an array using a case insensitive "natural order" algorithm

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: natcasesort is a case insensitive version of natsort.
This function implements a sort algorithm that orders alphanumeric strings in the way a human being would while maintaining key/value associations. This is described as a "natural ordering".

note.simpara: If two members compare as equal, they retain their original order. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, their relative order in the sorted array was undefined.
Resets array's internal pointer to the first element.

listitem.para: The input array.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Always returns true.

row.entry: The return type is true now; previously, it was bool.

example.title: natcasesort example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$array1 = $array2 = array('IMG0.png', 'img12.png', 'img10.png', 'img2.png', 'img1.png', 'IMG3.png');

sort($array1);
echo "Standard sorting\n";
print_r($array1);

natcasesort($array2);
echo "\nNatural order sorting (case-insensitive)\n";
print_r($array2);
?>
example.screen:
Standard sorting Array ( [0] => IMG0.png [1] => IMG3.png [2] => img1.png [3] => img10.png [4] => img12.png [5] => img2.png )
Natural order sorting (case-insensitive) Array ( [0] => IMG0.png [4] => img1.png [3] => img2.png [5] => IMG3.png [2] => img10.png [1] => img12.png )
example.para: For more information see: Martin Pool's Natural Order String Comparison page.

simplelist.member: The comparison of array sorting functions

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sort an array using a "natural order" algorithm

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function implements a sort algorithm that orders alphanumeric strings in the way a human being would while maintaining key/value associations. This is described as a "natural ordering". An example of the difference between this algorithm and the regular computer string sorting algorithms (used in sort) can be seen in the example below.

note.simpara: If two members compare as equal, they retain their original order. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, their relative order in the sorted array was undefined.
Resets array's internal pointer to the first element.

listitem.para: The input array.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Always returns true.

row.entry: The return type is true now; previously, it was bool.

example.title: natsort examples demonstrating basic usage
example.programlisting:
<?php
$array1 = $array2 = array("img12.png", "img10.png", "img2.png", "img1.png");

asort($array1);
echo "Standard sorting\n";
print_r($array1);

natsort($array2);
echo "\nNatural order sorting\n";
print_r($array2);
?>
example.screen:
Standard sorting Array ( [3] => img1.png [1] => img10.png [0] => img12.png [2] => img2.png )
Natural order sorting Array ( [3] => img1.png [2] => img2.png [1] => img10.png [0] => img12.png )
example.para: For more information see: Martin Pool's Natural Order String Comparison page.

example.title: natsort examples demonstrating potential gotchas
example.programlisting:
<?php
echo "Negative numbers\n";
$negative = array('-5','3','-2','0','-1000','9','1');
print_r($negative);
natsort($negative);
print_r($negative);

echo "Zero padding\n";
$zeros = array('09', '8', '10', '009', '011', '0'); 
print_r($zeros);
natsort($zeros);
print_r($zeros);
?>

simplelist.member: The comparison of array sorting functions

refnamediv.refpurpose: Advance the internal pointer of an array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: next behaves like current, with one difference. It advances the internal array pointer one place forward before returning the element value. That means it returns the next array value and advances the internal array pointer by one.

listitem.para: The array being affected.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the array value in the next place that's pointed to by the internal array pointer, or false if there are no more elements.

warning.simpara: This function may return Boolean false, but may also return a non-Boolean value which evaluates to false. Please read the section on Booleans for more information. Use the === operator for testing the return value of this function.

row.entry: Calling this function on objects is deprecated. Either convert the object to an array using get_mangled_object_vars first, or use the methods provided by a class that implements Iterator, such as ArrayIterator, instead.
Instances of SPL classes are now treated like empty objects that have no properties instead of calling the Iterator method with the same name as this function.

example.title: Example use of next and friends
example.programlisting:
<?php
$transport = array('foot', 'bike', 'car', 'plane');
echo $mode = current($transport), PHP_EOL; // $mode = 'foot';
echo $mode = next($transport), PHP_EOL;    // $mode = 'bike';
echo $mode = next($transport), PHP_EOL;    // $mode = 'car';
echo $mode = prev($transport), PHP_EOL;    // $mode = 'bike';
echo $mode = end($transport), PHP_EOL;     // $mode = 'plane';
?>

note.simpara: The end of an array is indistinguishable from a bool false element. To properly traverse an array which may contain false elements, see the foreach function.
To still use next and properly check if the end of the array has been reached, verify that the key is null.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of current

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: current

refnamediv.refpurpose: Rewind the internal array pointer

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Rewind the internal array pointer.
prev behaves just like next, except it rewinds the internal array pointer one place instead of advancing it.

listitem.para: The input array.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the array value in the previous place that's pointed to by the internal array pointer, or false if there are no more elements.

warning.simpara: This function may return Boolean false, but may also return a non-Boolean value which evaluates to false. Please read the section on Booleans for more information. Use the === operator for testing the return value of this function.

row.entry: Calling this function on objects is deprecated. Either convert the object to an array using get_mangled_object_vars first, or use the methods provided by a class that implements Iterator, such as ArrayIterator, instead.
Instances of SPL classes are now treated like empty objects that have no properties instead of calling the Iterator method with the same name as this function.

example.title: Example use of prev and friends
example.programlisting:
<?php
$transport = array('foot', 'bike', 'car', 'plane');
echo $mode = current($transport), PHP_EOL; // $mode = 'foot';
echo $mode = next($transport), PHP_EOL;    // $mode = 'bike';
echo $mode = next($transport), PHP_EOL;    // $mode = 'car';
echo $mode = prev($transport), PHP_EOL;    // $mode = 'bike';
echo $mode = end($transport), PHP_EOL;     // $mode = 'plane';
?>

note.simpara: The beginning of an array is indistinguishable from a bool false element. To make the distinction, check that the key of the prev element is not null.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Create an array containing a range of elements

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Create an array containing a range of elements.
If both start and end are strings, and step is int the produced array will be a sequence of bytes. Otherwise, the produced array will be a sequence of numbers.
The sequence is increasing if start is less than equal to end. Otherwise, the sequence is decreasing.

listitem.para: First value of the sequence.
Last possible value of the sequence.
step indicates by how much is the produced sequence progressed between values of the sequence.
step may be negative for decreasing sequences.
If step is a float without a fractional part, it is interpreted as int.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a sequence of elements as an array with the first element being start going up to end, with each value of the sequence being step values apart.
The last element of the returned array is either end or the previous element of the sequence, depending on the value of step.
If both start and end are strings, and step is int the produced array will be a sequence of bytes, generally latin ASCII characters.
If at least one of start, end, or step is float the produced array will be a sequence of float.
Otherwise, the produced array will be a sequence of int.

listitem.simpara: If step is 0, a ValueError is thrown.
If start, end, or step is not is_finite, a ValueError is thrown.
If step is negative, but the produced range is increasing (i.e. $start <= $end), a ValueError is thrown.
If start or end is the empty string '', an E_WARNING is emitted and the empty string will be interpreted as 0.
If start or end is a non-numeric string with more than one byte, an E_WARNING is emitted.
If start or end is a string that is implicitly cast to an int because the other boundary value is a number, an E_WARNING is emitted.
If step is a float, and start and end are non-numeric string, an E_WARNING is emitted.

row.entry: If both start and end are strings then range will now always produce an array of bytes. Previously if one of the boundary values was a numeric string, then the other boundary value was implicitly cast to int.
An E_WARNING is now emitted if start or end is a string that is implicitly cast to int because the other boundary value is a number.
An E_WARNING is now emitted if start or end is a non-numeric string with more than one byte.
An E_WARNING is now emitted if start or end is the empty string.
If step is a float with no fractional part, it will be interpreted as an int.
A ValueError is now thrown if step is negative when producing an increasing range.
A ValueError is now thrown if step is not finite.
A TypeError is now thrown if start or end is an array, object, or resource. Previously they were implicitly cast to int.

example.title: range examples
example.programlisting:
<?php
echo implode(', ', range(0, 12)), PHP_EOL;

echo implode(', ', range(0, 100, 10)), PHP_EOL;

echo implode(', ', range('a', 'i')), PHP_EOL;

echo implode(', ', range('c', 'a')), PHP_EOL;

echo implode(', ', range('A', 'z')), PHP_EOL;
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set the internal pointer of an array to its first element

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: reset rewinds array's internal pointer to the first element and returns the value of the first array element.

listitem.para: The input array.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the value of the first array element, or false if the array is empty.

warning.simpara: This function may return Boolean false, but may also return a non-Boolean value which evaluates to false. Please read the section on Booleans for more information. Use the === operator for testing the return value of this function.

row.entry: Calling this function on objects is deprecated. Either convert the object to an array using get_mangled_object_vars first, or use the methods provided by a class that implements Iterator, such as ArrayIterator, instead.
Instances of SPL classes are now treated like empty objects that have no properties instead of calling the Iterator method with the same name as this function.

example.title: reset example
example.programlisting:
\n"; // "step one" // skip two steps next($array); next($array); echo current($array) . "
\n"; // "step three" // reset pointer, start again on step one reset($array); echo current($array) . "
\n"; // "step one" ?>

note.simpara: The return value for an empty array is indistinguishable from the return value in case of an array which has a bool false first element. To properly check the value of the first element of an array which may contain false elements, first check the count of the array, or check that key is not null, after calling reset.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sort an array in descending order

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sorts array in place by values in descending order.

note.simpara: If two members compare as equal, they retain their original order. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, their relative order in the sorted array was undefined.
This function assigns new keys to the elements in array. It will remove any existing keys that may have been assigned, rather than just reordering the keys.
Resets array's internal pointer to the first element.

listitem.para: The input array.

listitem.simpara: The optional second parameter flags may be used to modify the sorting behavior using these values:
listitem.para:
Sorting type flags:
SORT_REGULAR - compare items normally; the details are described in the comparison operators section
SORT_NUMERIC - compare items numerically
SORT_STRING - compare items as strings
SORT_LOCALE_STRING - compare items as strings, based on the current locale. It uses the locale, which can be changed using setlocale
SORT_NATURAL - compare items as strings using "natural ordering" like natsort
SORT_FLAG_CASE - can be combined (bitwise OR) with SORT_STRING or SORT_NATURAL to sort strings case-insensitively

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Always returns true.

row.entry: The return type is true now; previously, it was bool.

example.title: rsort example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$fruits = array("lemon", "orange", "banana", "apple");
rsort($fruits);
foreach ($fruits as $key => $val) {
    echo "$key = $val\n";
}
?>
example.para: The fruits have been sorted in reverse alphabetical order.

simplelist.member: The comparison of array sorting functions

refnamediv.refpurpose: Shuffle an array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function shuffles (randomizes the order of the elements in) an array.

caution.simpara: This function does not generate cryptographically secure values, and must not be used for cryptographic purposes, or purposes that require returned values to be unguessable.

If cryptographically secure randomness is required, the Random\Randomizer may be used with the Random\Engine\Secure engine. For simple use cases, the random_int and random_bytes functions provide a convenient and secure API that is backed by the operating system’s CSPRNG.

This function uses the global Mt19937 (“Mersenne Twister”) instance as the source of randomness and thus shares its state with all other functions using the global Mt19937. Using any of these functions advances the sequence for all the other functions, regardless of scope.
Generating repeatable sequences by seeding mt_srand or srand with a known value will also yield repeatable output from this function.
Prefer using Random\Randomizer methods in all newly written code.

listitem.para: The array.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Always returns true.

row.entry: The internal randomization algorithm has been changed to use the Mersenne Twister Random Number Generator instead of the libc rand function.

example.title: shuffle example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$numbers = range(1, 20);
shuffle($numbers);
foreach ($numbers as $number) {
    echo "$number ";
}
?>

note.simpara: This function assigns new keys to the elements in array. It will remove any existing keys that may have been assigned, rather than just reordering the keys.
Resets array's internal pointer to the first element.

simplelist.member: The comparison of array sorting functions

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of count

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: count.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sort an array in ascending order

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sorts array in place by values in ascending order.

note.simpara: If two members compare as equal, they retain their original order. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, their relative order in the sorted array was undefined.
This function assigns new keys to the elements in array. It will remove any existing keys that may have been assigned, rather than just reordering the keys.
Resets array's internal pointer to the first element.

listitem.para: The input array.

listitem.simpara: The optional second parameter flags may be used to modify the sorting behavior using these values:
listitem.para:
Sorting type flags:
SORT_REGULAR - compare items normally; the details are described in the comparison operators section
SORT_NUMERIC - compare items numerically
SORT_STRING - compare items as strings
SORT_LOCALE_STRING - compare items as strings, based on the current locale. It uses the locale, which can be changed using setlocale
SORT_NATURAL - compare items as strings using "natural ordering" like natsort
SORT_FLAG_CASE - can be combined (bitwise OR) with SORT_STRING or SORT_NATURAL to sort strings case-insensitively

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Always returns true.

row.entry: The return type is true now; previously, it was bool.

refsect1.title: Examples

example.title: sort example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$fruits = array("lemon", "orange", "banana", "apple");
sort($fruits);
foreach ($fruits as $key => $val) {
    echo "fruits[" . $key . "] = " . $val . "\n";
}

?>
example.screen: fruits[0] = apple fruits[1] = banana fruits[2] = lemon fruits[3] = orange

refsect1.para: The fruits have been sorted in alphabetical order.

example.title: sort example using case-insensitive natural ordering
example.programlisting:
<?php

$fruits = array(
    "Orange1", "orange2", "Orange3", "orange20"
);
sort($fruits, SORT_NATURAL | SORT_FLAG_CASE);
foreach ($fruits as $key => $val) {
    echo "fruits[" . $key . "] = " . $val . "\n";
}

?>
example.screen: fruits[0] = Orange1 fruits[1] = orange2 fruits[2] = Orange3 fruits[3] = orange20

refsect1.para: The fruits have been sorted like natcasesort.

note.simpara: Like most PHP sorting functions, sort uses an implementation of Quicksort. The pivot is chosen in the middle of the partition resulting in an optimal time for already sorted arrays. This is however an implementation detail you shouldn't rely on.

warning.simpara: Be careful when sorting arrays with mixed types values because sort can produce unexpected results, if flags is SORT_REGULAR.

simplelist.member: The comparison of array sorting functions

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sort an array with a user-defined comparison function and maintain index association

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sorts array in place such that its keys maintain their correlation with the values they are associated with, using a user-defined comparison function.
This is used mainly when sorting associative arrays where the actual element order is significant.

note.simpara: If two members compare as equal, they retain their original order. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, their relative order in the sorted array was undefined.
Resets array's internal pointer to the first element.

listitem.para: The input array.

listitem.simpara: The comparison function must return an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero if the first argument is considered to be respectively less than, equal to, or greater than the second.

caution.simpara: Returning non-integer values from the comparison function, such as float, will result in an internal cast to int of the callback's return value. So values such as 0.99 and 0.1 will both be cast to an integer value of 0, which will compare such values as equal.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Always returns true.

row.entry: The return type is true now; previously, it was bool.
If callback expects a parameter to be passed by reference, this function will now emit an E_WARNING.

example.title: Basic uasort example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// Comparison function
function cmp($a, $b) {
    if ($a == $b) {
        return 0;
    }
    return ($a < $b) ? -1 : 1;
}

// Array to be sorted
$array = array('a' => 4, 'b' => 8, 'c' => -1, 'd' => -9, 'e' => 2, 'f' => 5, 'g' => 3, 'h' => -4);
print_r($array);

// Sort and print the resulting array
uasort($array, 'cmp');
print_r($array);
?>

simplelist.member: The comparison of array sorting functions

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sort an array by keys using a user-defined comparison function

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sorts array in place by keys using a user-supplied comparison function to determine the order.

note.simpara: If two members compare as equal, they retain their original order. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, their relative order in the sorted array was undefined.
Resets array's internal pointer to the first element.

listitem.para: The input array.

listitem.simpara: The comparison function must return an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero if the first argument is considered to be respectively less than, equal to, or greater than the second.

caution.simpara: Returning non-integer values from the comparison function, such as float, will result in an internal cast to int of the callback's return value. So values such as 0.99 and 0.1 will both be cast to an integer value of 0, which will compare such values as equal.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Always returns true.

row.entry: The return type is true now; previously, it was bool.
If callback expects a parameter to be passed by reference, this function will now emit an E_WARNING.

example.title: uksort example
example.programlisting:
<?php
function cmp($a, $b)
{
    $a = preg_replace('@^(a|an|the) @', '', $a);
    $b = preg_replace('@^(a|an|the) @', '', $b);
    return strcasecmp($a, $b);
}

$a = array("John" => 1, "the Earth" => 2, "an apple" => 3, "a banana" => 4);

uksort($a, "cmp");

foreach ($a as $key => $value) {
    echo "$key: $value\n";
}
?>
example.screen: an apple: 3 a banana: 4 the Earth: 2 John: 1

simplelist.member: The comparison of array sorting functions

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sort an array by values using a user-defined comparison function

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sorts array in place by values using a user-supplied comparison function to determine the order.

note.simpara: If two members compare as equal, they retain their original order. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, their relative order in the sorted array was undefined.
This function assigns new keys to the elements in array. It will remove any existing keys that may have been assigned, rather than just reordering the keys.

listitem.para: The input array.

listitem.simpara: The comparison function must return an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero if the first argument is considered to be respectively less than, equal to, or greater than the second.

caution.simpara: Returning non-integer values from the comparison function, such as float, will result in an internal cast to int of the callback's return value. So values such as 0.99 and 0.1 will both be cast to an integer value of 0, which will compare such values as equal.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Always returns true.

row.entry: The return type is true now; previously, it was bool.
If callback expects a parameter to be passed by reference, this function will now emit an E_WARNING.

example.title: usort example
example.programlisting:
<?php
function cmp($a, $b)
{
    if ($a == $b) {
        return 0;
    }
    return ($a < $b) ? -1 : 1;
}

$a = array(3, 2, 5, 6, 1);

usort($a, "cmp");

foreach ($a as $key => $value) {
    echo "$key: $value\n";
}
?>
example.para: The spaceship operator may be used to simplify the internal comparison even further.
example.programlisting:
<?php
function cmp($a, $b)
{
    return $a <=> $b;
}

$a = array(3, 2, 5, 6, 1);

usort($a, "cmp");

foreach ($a as $key => $value) {
    echo "$key: $value\n";
}
?>

note.para: Obviously in this trivial case the sort function would be more appropriate.

example.title: usort example using multi-dimensional array
example.programlisting:
<?php
function cmp($a, $b)
{
    return strcmp($a["fruit"], $b["fruit"]);
}

$fruits[0]["fruit"] = "lemons";
$fruits[1]["fruit"] = "apples";
$fruits[2]["fruit"] = "grapes";

usort($fruits, "cmp");

foreach ($fruits as $key => $value) {
    echo "\$fruits[$key]: " . $value["fruit"] . "\n";
}
?>
example.para: When sorting a multi-dimensional array, $a and $b contain references to the first index of the array.

example.title: usort example using a member function of an object
example.programlisting:
<?php
class TestObj {
    public string $name;

    function __construct($name)
    {
        $this->name = $name;
    }

    /* This is the static comparing function: */
    static function cmp_obj($a, $b)
    {
        return strtolower($a->name) <=> strtolower($b->name);
    }
}

$a[] = new TestObj("c");
$a[] = new TestObj("b");
$a[] = new TestObj("d");

usort($a, [TestObj::class, "cmp_obj"]);

foreach ($a as $item) {
    echo $item->name . "\n";
}
?>

example.title: usort example using a closure to sort a multi-dimensional array
example.programlisting:
<?php
$array[0] = array('key_a' => 'z', 'key_b' => 'c');
$array[1] = array('key_a' => 'x', 'key_b' => 'b');
$array[2] = array('key_a' => 'y', 'key_b' => 'a');

function build_sorter($key) {
    return function ($a, $b) use ($key) {
        return strnatcmp($a[$key], $b[$key]);
    };
}

usort($array, build_sorter('key_b'));

foreach ($array as $item) {
    echo $item['key_a'] . ', ' . $item['key_b'] . "\n";
}
?>
example.screen: y, a x, b z, c

example.title: usort example using the spaceship operator
example.para: The spaceship operator allows for straightforward comparison of compound values across multiple axes. The following example will sort $people by last name, then by first name if the last name matches.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$people[0] = ['first' => 'Adam', 'last' => 'West'];
$people[1] = ['first' => 'Alec', 'last' => 'Baldwin'];
$people[2] = ['first' => 'Adam', 'last' => 'Baldwin'];

function sorter(array $a, array $b) {
    return [$a['last'], $a['first']] <=> [$b['last'], $b['first']];
}

usort($people, 'sorter');

foreach ($people as $person) {
    print $person['last'] . ', ' . $person['first'] . PHP_EOL;
}
?>
example.screen: Baldwin, Adam Baldwin, Alec West, Adam
