preface.title: Introduction
preface.para: PHP comes with a complete reflection API that adds the ability to introspect classes, interfaces, functions, methods and extensions. Additionally, the reflection API offers ways to retrieve doc comments for functions, classes and methods.

Please note that certain parts of the internal API are missing the necessary code to work with the Reflection extension. E.g., an internal PHP class might be missing reflection data for properties. These few cases are considered bugs, however, so they should be discovered and fixed.

chapter.title: Examples
chapter.para: Many examples exist within the Reflection documentation, typically within the __construct documentation for each class.

example.title: Reflection Example from Shell (a Terminal)
example.programlisting: $ php --rf strlen $ php --rc finfo $ php --re json $ php --ri dom
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

chapter.title: Extending
chapter.para: If you want to create specialized versions of the built-in classes (say, for creating colorized HTML when being exported, having easy-access member variables instead of methods or having utility methods), you may go ahead and extend them.

example.title: Extending the built-in classes
example.programlisting:
<?php
/**
 * My Reflection_Method class
 */
class My_Reflection_Method extends ReflectionMethod
{
    public $visibility = array();

    public function __construct($o, $m)
    {
        parent::__construct($o, $m);
        $this->visibility = Reflection::getModifierNames($this->getModifiers());
    }
}

/**
 * Demo class #1
 *
 */
class T {
    protected function x() {}
}

/**
 * Demo class #2
 *
 */
class U extends T {
    function x() {}
}

// Print out information
var_dump(new My_Reflection_Method('U', 'x'));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

caution.para: If you're overwriting the constructor, remember to call the parent's constructor before any code you insert. Failing to do so will result in the following: Fatal error: Internal error: Failed to retrieve the reflection object

section.title: Introduction
section.para: The reflection class.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Exports

warning.simpara: This function has been DEPRECATED as of PHP 7.4.0, and REMOVED as of PHP 8.0.0. Relying on this function is highly discouraged.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Exports a reflection.

warning.simpara: This function is currently not documented; only its argument list is available.

listitem.para: The reflection to export.
Setting to true will return the export, as opposed to emitting it. Setting to false (the default) will do the opposite.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: If the return parameter is set to true, then the export is returned as a string, otherwise null is returned.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets modifier names

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets modifier names.

listitem.para: Bitfield of the modifiers to get.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array of modifier names.

example.title: Reflection::getModifierNames example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Testing
{
    final public static function foo()
    {
        return;
    }

    public function bar()
    {
        return;
    }
}

$foo = new ReflectionMethod('Testing', 'foo');

echo "Modifiers for method foo():\n";
echo $foo->getModifiers() . "\n";
echo implode(' ', Reflection::getModifierNames($foo->getModifiers())) . "\n";

$bar = new ReflectionMethod('Testing', 'bar');

echo "Modifiers for method bar():\n";
echo $bar->getModifiers() . "\n";
echo implode(' ', Reflection::getModifierNames($bar->getModifiers()));
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: Modifiers for method foo(): 261 final public static Modifiers for method bar(): 65792 public

section.title: Introduction
section.para: The ReflectionClass class reports information about a class.

listitem.para: Name of the class. Read-only, throws ReflectionException in attempt to write.
Indicates the class is abstract because it has some abstract methods.
Indicates the class is abstract because of its definition.
Indicates the class is final.
Indicates the class is readonly.

listitem.simpara: Indicates that serialize should not trigger initialization of a lazy object.
Indicates an object destructor should not be called when resetting it as lazy.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Exports a reflected class.

listitem.para: The reflection to export.
Setting to true will return the export, as opposed to emitting it. Setting to false (the default) will do the opposite.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: If the return parameter is set to true, then the export is returned as a string, otherwise null is returned.

example.programlisting:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets Attributes

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns all attributes declared on this class as an array of ReflectionAttribute.

listitem.simpara: Filter the results to include only ReflectionAttribute instances for attributes matching this class name.
Flags for determining how to filter the results, if name is provided.
Default is 0 which will only return results for attributes that are of the class name.
The only other option available, is to use ReflectionAttribute::IS_INSTANCEOF, which will instead use instanceof for filtering.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Array of attributes, as a ReflectionAttribute object.

example.title: Basic usage
example.programlisting:
<?php
#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red {
}

#[Fruit]
#[Red]
class Apple {
}

$class = new ReflectionClass('Apple');
$attributes = $class->getAttributes();
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

example.title: Filtering results by class name
example.programlisting:
<?php
#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red {
}

#[Fruit]
#[Red]
class Apple {
}

$class = new ReflectionClass('Apple');
$attributes = $class->getAttributes('Fruit');
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

example.title: Filtering results by class name, with inheritance
example.programlisting:
<?php
interface Color {
}

#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red implements Color {
}

#[Fruit]
#[Red]
class Apple {
}

$class = new ReflectionClass('Apple');
$attributes = $class->getAttributes(Color::class, ReflectionAttribute::IS_INSTANCEOF);
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets defined constant

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets the defined constant.

listitem.para: The name of the class constant to get.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Value of the constant with the name name. Returns false if the constant was not found in the class.

row.entry: Calling ReflectionClass::getConstant for constants that do not exist has been deprecated.

example.title: Usage of ReflectionClass::getConstant
example.programlisting:
<?php

class Example {
    const C1 = false;
    const C2 = 'I am a constant';
}

$reflection = new ReflectionClass('Example');

var_dump($reflection->getConstant('C1'));
var_dump($reflection->getConstant('C2'));
var_dump($reflection->getConstant('C3'));
?>
example.screen: bool(false) string(15) "I am a constant" bool(false)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets constants

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets all defined constants from a class, regardless of their visibility.

listitem.para: The optional filter, for filtering desired constant visibilities. It's configured using the ReflectionClassConstant constants, and defaults to all constant visibilities.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array of constants, where the keys hold the name and the values the value of the constants.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets the constructor of the class

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets the constructor of the reflected class.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A ReflectionMethod object reflecting the class' constructor, or null if the class has no constructor.

example.title: Basic usage of ReflectionClass::getConstructor
example.programlisting:
<?php
$class = new ReflectionClass('ReflectionClass');
$constructor = $class->getConstructor();
var_dump($constructor);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets default properties

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets default properties from a class (including inherited properties).

note.para: This method only works for static properties when used on internal classes. The default value of a static class property can not be tracked when using this method on user defined classes.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array of default properties, with the key being the name of the property and the value being the default value of the property or null if the property doesn't have a default value. The function does not distinguish between static and non static properties and does not take visibility modifiers into account.

example.title: ReflectionClass::getDefaultProperties example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Bar {
    protected $inheritedProperty = 'inheritedDefault';
}

class Foo extends Bar {
    public $property = 'propertyDefault';
    private $privateProperty = 'privatePropertyDefault';
    public static $staticProperty = 'staticProperty';
    public $defaultlessProperty;
}

$reflectionClass = new ReflectionClass('Foo');
var_dump($reflectionClass->getDefaultProperties());
?>
example.screen: array(5) { ["staticProperty"]=> string(14) "staticProperty" ["property"]=> string(15) "propertyDefault" ["privateProperty"]=> string(22) "privatePropertyDefault" ["defaultlessProperty"]=> NULL ["inheritedProperty"]=> string(16) "inheritedDefault" }

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets doc comments

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets doc comments from a class. Doc comments start with /**, followed by whitespace. If there are multiple doc comments above the class definition, the one closest to the class will be taken.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The doc comment if it exists, otherwise false.

example.title: ReflectionClass::getDocComment example
example.programlisting:
<?php
/**

 * @param  foo bar
 * @return baz
 */
class TestClass { }

$rc = new ReflectionClass('TestClass');
var_dump($rc->getDocComment());
?>
example.screen: string(60) "/** * A test class * * @param foo bar * @return baz */"

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets an array of methods

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets an array of methods for the class.

listitem.para: Filter the results to include only methods with certain attributes. Defaults to no filtering.

Any bitwise disjunction of ReflectionMethod::IS_STATIC, ReflectionMethod::IS_PUBLIC, ReflectionMethod::IS_PROTECTED, ReflectionMethod::IS_PRIVATE, ReflectionMethod::IS_ABSTRACT, ReflectionMethod::IS_FINAL, so that all methods with any of the given attributes will be returned.

note.simpara: Note that other bitwise operations, for instance ~ will not work as expected. In other words, it is not possible to retrieve all non-static methods, for example.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array of ReflectionMethod objects reflecting each method.

example.title: Basic usage of ReflectionClass::getMethods
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Apple {
    public function firstMethod() { }
    final protected function secondMethod() { }
    private static function thirdMethod() { }
}

$class = new ReflectionClass('Apple');
$methods = $class->getMethods();
var_dump($methods);
?>

example.title: Filtering results from ReflectionClass::getMethods
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Apple {
    public function firstMethod() { }
    final protected function secondMethod() { }
    private static function thirdMethod() { }
}

$class = new ReflectionClass('Apple');
$methods = $class->getMethods(ReflectionMethod::IS_STATIC | ReflectionMethod::IS_FINAL);
var_dump($methods);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets properties

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Retrieves reflected properties.

listitem.para: The optional filter, for filtering desired property types. It's configured using the ReflectionProperty constants, and defaults to all property types.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array of ReflectionProperty objects.

example.title: ReflectionClass::getProperties filtering example
example.para: This example demonstrates usage of the optional filter parameter, where it essentially skips private properties.
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Foo {
    public    $foo  = 1;
    protected $bar  = 2;
    private   $baz  = 3;
}

$foo = new Foo();

$reflect = new ReflectionClass($foo);
$props   = $reflect->getProperties(ReflectionProperty::IS_PUBLIC | ReflectionProperty::IS_PROTECTED);

foreach ($props as $prop) {
    print $prop->getName() . "\n";
}

var_dump($props);

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks if method is defined

refsect1.para: Checks whether a specific method is defined in a class.

listitem.para: Name of the method being checked for.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: true if it has the method, otherwise false

example.title: ReflectionClass::hasMethod example
example.programlisting:
<?php
Class C {
    public function publicFoo() {
        return true;
    }

    protected function protectedFoo() {
        return true;
    }

    private function privateFoo() {
        return true;
    }

    static function staticFoo() {
        return true;
    }
}

$rc = new ReflectionClass("C");

var_dump($rc->hasMethod('publicFoo'));

var_dump($rc->hasMethod('protectedFoo'));

var_dump($rc->hasMethod('privateFoo'));

var_dump($rc->hasMethod('staticFoo'));

// C should not have method bar
var_dump($rc->hasMethod('bar'));

// Method names are case insensitive
var_dump($rc->hasMethod('PUBLICfOO'));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Forces initialization of a lazy object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Forces initialization of the specified object. This method has no effect if the object is not lazy or has already been initialized. Otherwise, initialization proceeds as described in the Initialization Sequence.

note.simpara: In most cases, calling this method is unnecessary, as lazy objects initialize themselves automatically when their state is observed or modified.

listitem.simpara: The object to initialize.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: If object is a lazy proxy, returns its real instance. Otherwise, returns object itself.

example.title: Basic usage
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Example
{
    public function __construct(public int $prop) {
    }
}

$reflector = new ReflectionClass(Example::class);

$object = $reflector->newLazyGhost(function ($object) {
    echo "Initializer called\n";
    $object->__construct(1);
});

var_dump($object);

$reflector->initializeLazyObject($object);

var_dump($object);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks if the class is instantiable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks if the class is instantiable.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the class is instantiable or false otherwise.

example.title: ReflectionClass::isInstantiable example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class C { }

interface iface {
    function f1();
}

class ifaceImpl implements iface {
    function f1() {}
}

abstract class abstractClass {
    function f1() { }
    abstract function f2();
}

class D extends abstractClass {
    function f2() { }
}

trait T {
    function f1() {}
}

class privateConstructor {
    private function __construct() { }
}

$classes = array(
    "C",
    "iface",
    "ifaceImpl",
    "abstractClass",
    "D",
    "T",
    "privateConstructor",
);

foreach($classes  as $class ) {
    $reflectionClass = new ReflectionClass($class);
    echo "Is $class instantiable?  ";
    var_dump($reflectionClass->isInstantiable()); 
}

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks if class is defined internally by an extension, or the core

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks if the class is defined internally by an extension, or the core, as opposed to user-defined.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the class is defined internally by an extension or core, or false otherwise.

example.title: Basic usage of ReflectionClass::isInternal
example.programlisting:
<?php
$internalclass = new ReflectionClass('ReflectionClass');

class Apple {}
$userclass = new ReflectionClass('Apple');

var_dump($internalclass->isInternal());
var_dump($userclass->isInternal());
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Check whether this class is iterable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Check whether this class is iterable (i.e. can be used inside foreach).

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the class is iterable or false otherwise.

example.title: Basic ReflectionClass::isIterable Usage
example.programlisting:
<?php

class IteratorClass implements Iterator
{
    public function __construct() {}

    public function key(): mixed {}

    public function current(): mixed {}

    public function next(): void {}

    public function valid(): bool {}

    public function rewind(): void {}
}

class DerivedClass extends IteratorClass {}

class NonIterator {}

function dump_iterable($class)
{
    $reflection = new ReflectionClass($class);
    var_dump($reflection->isIterable());
}

$classes = ["ArrayObject", "IteratorClass", "DerivedClass", "NonIterator",];

foreach ($classes as $class) {
    echo "Is $class iterable? ";
    dump_iterable($class);
}
?>
example.screen: Is ArrayObject iterable? bool(true) Is IteratorClass iterable? bool(true) Is DerivedClass iterable? bool(true) Is NonIterator iterable? bool(false)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks if an object is lazy and uninitialized

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Checks if an object is lazy and uninitialized.

listitem.simpara: The object to check.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if object is an uninitialized lazy object, false otherwise.

example.title: Basic usage
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Example
{
    public function __construct(public int $prop) {
    }
}

$reflector = new ReflectionClass(Example::class);

$object = $reflector->newLazyGhost(function ($object) {
    echo "Initializer called\n";
    $object->__construct(1);
});

var_dump($reflector->isUninitializedLazyObject($object));

var_dump($object->prop);

var_dump($reflector->isUninitializedLazyObject($object));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks if user defined

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks whether the class is user-defined, as opposed to internal.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Marks a lazy object as initialized without calling the initializer or factory

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Marks a lazy object as initialized without calling the initializer or factory. This has no effect if object is not lazy or is already initialized.

The effect of calling this method is the same as described for Ghost Objects (regardless of the laziness strategy of object) in initialization sequence, except that the initializer is not called. After that, the object is indistinguishable from an object that was never lazy and was created with ReflectionClass::newInstanceWithoutConstructor, except for the value of properties that were already initialized with ReflectionProperty::setRawValueWithoutLazyInitialization or ReflectionProperty::skipLazyInitialization.

listitem.simpara: The object to mark as initialized.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns object.

example.title: Marking an uninitialized lazy object as initialized
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Example
{
    public string $prop1;
    public string $prop2;
    public string $prop3 = 'default value';
}

$reflector = new ReflectionClass(Example::class);

$object = $reflector->newLazyGhost(function ($object) {
    echo "Initializer called\n";
    $object->prop1 = 'initialized';
});

$reflector->getProperty('prop1')
          ->setRawValueWithoutLazyInitialization($object, 'prop1 value');

var_dump($object);

$reflector->markLazyObjectAsInitialized($object);

var_dump($object);
?>
example.screen: lazy ghost object(Example)#3 (1) { ["prop1"]=> string(11) "prop1 value" ["prop2"]=> uninitialized(string) ["prop3"]=> uninitialized(string) } object(Example)#3 (2) { ["prop1"]=> string(11) "prop1 value" ["prop2"]=> uninitialized(string) ["prop3"]=> string(13) "default value" }

example.title: Marking an initialized object as initialized
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Example
{
    public string $prop1;
    public string $prop2;
    public string $prop3 = 'default value';
}

$reflector = new ReflectionClass(Example::class);

$object = $reflector->newLazyGhost(function ($object) {
    echo "Initializer called\n";
    $object->prop1 = 'initialized';
});

$reflector->getProperty('prop1')
          ->setRawValueWithoutLazyInitialization($object, 'prop1 value');

var_dump($object->prop3);
var_dump($object);

$reflector->markLazyObjectAsInitialized($object);

var_dump($object);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Creates a new class instance from given arguments

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Creates a new instance of the class. The given arguments are passed to the class constructor.

listitem.para: Accepts a variable number of arguments which are passed to the class constructor, much like call_user_func.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: A ReflectionException if the class constructor is not public.
A ReflectionException if the class does not have a constructor and the args parameter contains one or more parameters.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Creates a new class instance from given arguments

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Creates a new instance of the class, the given arguments are passed to the class constructor.

listitem.simpara: The parameters to be passed to the class constructor as an array.
If the keys of args are all numeric, the keys are ignored and each element is passed to the constructor as a positional argument, in order.
If any keys of args are strings, those elements are passed to the constructor as named arguments, with the name given by the key.
An Error is thrown if a numeric key in args appears after a string key, or if a string key does not match the name of any constructor parameter.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a new instance of the class, or null on failure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: A ReflectionException if the class constructor is not public.
A ReflectionException if the class does not have a constructor and the args parameter contains one or more parameters.

row.entry: args keys will now be interpreted as parameter names, instead of being silently ignored.

example.title: Basic usage of ReflectionClass::newInstanceArgs
example.programlisting:
<?php
$class = new ReflectionClass('ReflectionFunction');
$instance = $class->newInstanceArgs(array('substr'));
var_dump($instance);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Creates a new class instance without invoking the constructor

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Creates a new instance of the class without invoking the constructor.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: A ReflectionException if the class is an internal class that cannot be instantiated without invoking the constructor. This exception is limited only to internal classes that are final.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Creates a new lazy ghost instance

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Creates a new lazy ghost instance of the class, attaching the initializer to it. The constructor is not called, and properties are not set to their default value. However, the object will be automatically initialized by invoking the initializer the first time its state is observed or modified. See Initialization Triggers and Initialization Sequence.

listitem.simpara: The initializer is a callback with the following signature:
The object being initialized. At this point, the object is no longer marked as lazy, and accessing it does not trigger initialization again.
The initializer function must return null or no value.

listitem.para:
options can be a combination of the following flags:
ReflectionClass::SKIP_INITIALIZATION_ON_SERIALIZE
By default, serializing a lazy object triggers its initialization. Setting this flag prevents initialization, allowing lazy objects to be serialized without being initialized.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a lazy ghost instance. If the object has no properties, or if all its properties are static or virtual, a normal (non-lazy) instance is returned. See also Lifecycle of Lazy Objects.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: An Error if the class is internal or extends an internal class except stdClass.

example.title: Basic usage
example.programlisting:
<?php

class Example {
    public function __construct(public int $prop) {
        echo __METHOD__, "\n";
    }
}

$reflector = new ReflectionClass(Example::class);
$object = $reflector->newLazyGhost(function (Example $object) {
     $object->__construct(1);
});

var_dump($object);
var_dump($object instanceof Example);

// Triggers initialization, and fetches the property after that
var_dump($object->prop);

?>
example.screen: lazy ghost object(Example)#3 (0) { ["prop"]=> uninitialized(int) } bool(true) Example::__construct int(1)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Creates a new lazy proxy instance

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Creates a new lazy proxy instance of the class, attaching the factory function to it. The constructor is not called, and properties are not set to their default values. When an attempt is made to observe or modify the proxy's state for the first time, the factory function is called to provide a real instance, which is then attached to the proxy. After this, all subsequent interactions with the proxy are forwarded to the real instance. See Initialization Triggers and Initialization Sequence.

listitem.simpara: The factory is a callback with the following signature:
The object being initialized. At this point, the object is no longer marked as lazy, and accessing it does not trigger initialization again.

The factory function must return an object, referred to as the real instance, which is then attached to the proxy. This real instance must not be lazy and must not be the proxy itself. If the real instance does not have the same class as the proxy, the proxy's class must be a subclass of the real instance's class, without additional properties, and must not override the __destruct or __clone methods.

listitem.para:
options can be a combination of the following flags:
ReflectionClass::SKIP_INITIALIZATION_ON_SERIALIZE
By default, serializing a lazy object triggers its initialization. Setting this flag prevents initialization, allowing lazy objects to be serialized without being initialized.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a lazy proxy instance. If the object has no properties, or if all its properties are static or virtual, a normal (non-lazy) instance is returned. See also Lifecycle of Lazy Objects.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: An Error if the class is internal or extends an internal class except stdClass.

example.title: Basic usage
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Example {
    public function __construct(public int $prop) {
        echo __METHOD__, "\n";
    }
}

$reflector = new ReflectionClass(Example::class);
$object = $reflector->newLazyProxy(function (Example $object) {
     $realInstance = new Example(1);
     return $realInstance;
});

var_dump($object);
var_dump($object instanceof Example);

// Triggers initialization, and forwards the property fetch to the real instance
var_dump($object->prop);

var_dump($object);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Resets an object and marks it as lazy

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Resets an existing object and marks it as lazy.

The object's destructor is called (if one exists) unless the ReflectionClass::SKIP_DESTRUCTOR flag is specified. In the special case where the object is an initialized proxy, the real instance is detached from the proxy. If the real instance is no longer referenced elsewhere, its destructor is called regardless of the SKIP_DESTRUCTOR flag.

Dynamic properties are removed, and the value of properties declared on the class is discarded as though unset was called, and marked as lazy. This implies that if the object is an instance of a subclass with additional properties, these properties are not modified and not made lazy. Readonly properties are also not modified and not made lazy if they are final or the class itself is final.
If no properties were marked lazy, the object is not marked as lazy. See also Lazy Objects Lifecycle.
Otherwise, after calling this method, the behavior of the object is the same as an object created by ReflectionClass::newLazyGhost (except for subclass and readonly properties, as described above).

The object is not replaced by another one, and its identity remains unchanged. Functionality such as spl_object_id, spl_object_hash, SplObjectStorage, WeakMap, WeakReference, or the identity operator (===) are unaffected.

listitem.simpara: A non-lazy object, or an initialized lazy object.
An initializer callback with the same signature and purpose as in ReflectionClass::newLazyGhost.

listitem.para:
options can be a combination of the following flags:
ReflectionClass::SKIP_INITIALIZATION_ON_SERIALIZE
By default, serializing a lazy object triggers its initialization. Setting this flag prevents initialization, allowing lazy objects to be serialized without being initialized.
ReflectionClass::SKIP_DESTRUCTOR
By default, the object destructor is called (if any) before making it lazy. This provides safety regarding any preexisting state in the object. This flag disables that behavior, allowing objects to be reset as lazy without calling the destructor.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: A ReflectionException if the object is lazy and non-initialized.
An Error if the object is being initialized, or if the object properties are being iterated with foreach.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Resets an object and marks it as lazy

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The behavior of this method is the same as ReflectionClass::resetAsLazyGhost except that it uses the proxy strategy.

The object itself becomes the proxy. Similarly to ReflectionClass::resetAsLazyGhost, the object is not replaced by an other one, and its identity does not change, even after initialization. The proxy and the real instance are distinct objects, with distinct identities.

listitem.simpara: A non-lazy object, or an initialized lazy object.
An factory callback with the same signature and purpose as in ReflectionClass::newLazyProxy.

listitem.para:
options can be a combination of the following flags:
ReflectionClass::SKIP_INITIALIZATION_ON_SERIALIZE
By default, serializing a lazy object triggers its initialization. Setting this flag prevents initialization, allowing lazy objects to be serialized without being initialized.
ReflectionClass::SKIP_DESTRUCTOR
By default, the object destructor is called (if any) before making it lazy. This provides safety regarding any preexisting state in the object. This flag disables that behavior, allowing objects to be reset as lazy without calling the destructor.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: A ReflectionException if the object is lazy and non-initialized.
An Error if the object is being initialized, or if the object properties are being iterated with foreach.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sets static property value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sets the value of a static property on this class, regardless of the property's visibility.
ReflectionProperty::setValue can also be used to set the value of static properties.

listitem.para: Property name.
New property value.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

row.entry: ReflectionClass::setStaticPropertyValue can now set private and protected static properties. Previously, a ReflectionException was thrown.

section.title: Introduction
section.para: The ReflectionClassConstant class reports information about a class constant.

listitem.para: Name of the class constant. Read-only, throws ReflectionException in attempt to write.
Name of the class where the class constant is defined. Read-only, throws ReflectionException in attempt to write.
Indicates public constants. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, the value was 256.
Indicates protected constants. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, the value was 512.
Indicates private constants. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, the value was 1024.
Indicates final constants. Available as of PHP 8.1.0.

note.para: The values of these constants may change between PHP versions. It is recommended to always use the constants and not rely on the values directly.

row.entry: The class constants are now typed.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Constructs a ReflectionClassConstant

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Constructs a new ReflectionClassConstant object.

listitem.para: Either a string containing the name of the class to reflect, or an object.
The name of the class constant.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: Throws an Exception in case the given class constant does not exist.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Export

warning.simpara: This function has been DEPRECATED as of PHP 7.4.0, and REMOVED as of PHP 8.0.0. Relying on this function is highly discouraged.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Exports a reflection.

warning.simpara: This function is currently not documented; only its argument list is available.

listitem.para: The reflection to export.
The class constant name.
Setting to true will return the export, as opposed to emitting it. Setting to false (the default) will do the opposite.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets Attributes

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns all attributes declared on this class constant as an array of ReflectionAttribute.

listitem.simpara: Filter the results to include only ReflectionAttribute instances for attributes matching this class name.
Flags for determining how to filter the results, if name is provided.
Default is 0 which will only return results for attributes that are of the class name.
The only other option available, is to use ReflectionAttribute::IS_INSTANCEOF, which will instead use instanceof for filtering.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Array of attributes, as a ReflectionAttribute object.

example.title: Basic usage
example.programlisting:
<?php
#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red {
}

class Basket {
    #[Fruit]
    #[Red]
    public const APPLE = 'apple';
}

$classConstant = new ReflectionClassConstant('Basket', 'APPLE');
$attributes = $classConstant->getAttributes();
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

example.title: Filtering results by class name
example.programlisting:
<?php
#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red {
}

class Basket {
    #[Fruit]
    #[Red]
    public const APPLE = 'apple';
}

$classConstant = new ReflectionClassConstant('Basket', 'APPLE');
$attributes = $classConstant->getAttributes('Fruit');
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

example.title: Filtering results by class name, with inheritance
example.programlisting:
<?php
interface Color {
}

#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red implements Color {
}

class Basket {
    #[Fruit]
    #[Red]
    public const APPLE = 'apple';
}

$classConstant = new ReflectionClassConstant('Basket', 'APPLE');
$attributes = $classConstant->getAttributes('Color', ReflectionAttribute::IS_INSTANCEOF);
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks if class constant is an Enum case

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks if the class constant is an Enum case.

refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: true if the class constant is an Enum case; false otherwise.

example.title: ReflectionClassConstant::isEnumCase example
example.para: Distinguish between Enum cases and regular class constants.
example.programlisting:
<?php
enum Status
{
    const BORING_CONSTANT = 'test';
    const ENUM_VALUE = Status::PUBLISHED;

    case DRAFT;
    case PUBLISHED;
    case ARCHIVED;
}

$reflection = new ReflectionEnum(Status::class);
foreach ($reflection->getReflectionConstants() as $constant) {
    echo "{$constant->name} is ",
        $constant->isEnumCase() ? "an enum case" : "a regular class constant",
        PHP_EOL;
}
?>
example.screen: BORING_CONSTANT is a regular class constant ENUM_VALUE is a regular class constant DRAFT is an enum case PUBLISHED is an enum case ARCHIVED is an enum case

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets Attributes

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns all attributes declared on this global constant as an array of ReflectionAttribute.

listitem.simpara: Filter the results to include only ReflectionAttribute instances for attributes matching this class name.
Flags for determining how to filter the results, if name is provided.
Default is 0 which will only return results for attributes that are of the class name.
The only other option available, is to use ReflectionAttribute::IS_INSTANCEOF, which will instead use instanceof for filtering.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Array of attributes, as ReflectionAttribute objects.

example.title: Basic usage
example.programlisting:
<?php
#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red {
}

#[Fruit]
#[Red]
const APPLE = 'apple';

$constant = new ReflectionConstant('APPLE');
$attributes = $constant->getAttributes();
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.para: The ReflectionEnum class reports information about an Enum.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Instantiates a ReflectionEnum object

listitem.para: An enum instance or a name.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets the backing type of an Enum, if any

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: If the enumeration is a Backed Enum, this method will return an instance of ReflectionType for the backing type of the Enum. If it is not a Backed Enum, it will return null.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: An instance of ReflectionNamedType, or null if the Enum has no backing type.

row.entry: The return type is now declared as ?ReflectionNamedType. Previously, ?ReflectionType was declared.

example.title: ReflectionEnum::getBackingType example
example.programlisting:
<?php
enum Suit: string
{
    case Hearts = 'H';
    case Diamonds = 'D';
    case Clubs = 'C';
    case Spades = 'S';
}

$rEnum = new ReflectionEnum(Suit::class);

$rBackingType = $rEnum->getBackingType();

var_dump((string) $rBackingType);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns a specific case of an Enum

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the reflection object for a specific Enum case by name. If the requested case is not defined, a ReflectionException is thrown.

listitem.para: The name of the case to retrieve.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An instance of ReflectionEnumUnitCase or ReflectionEnumBackedCase, as appropriate.

example.title: ReflectionEnum::getCase example
example.programlisting:
<?php
enum Suit
{
    case Hearts;
    case Diamonds;
    case Clubs;
    case Spades;
}

$rEnum = new ReflectionEnum(Suit::class);

$rCase = $rEnum->getCase('Clubs');

var_dump($rCase->getValue());
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns a list of all cases on an Enum

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: An Enum may contain zero or more cases. This method retrieves all defined cases, in lexical order (that is, the order they appear in the source code).

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: An array of Enum reflection objects, one for each case in the Enum. For a Unit Enum, they will all be instances of ReflectionEnumUnitCase. For a Backed Enum, they will all be instances of ReflectionEnumBackedCase.

example.title: ReflectionEnum::getCases example
example.programlisting:
<?php
enum Suit
{
    case Hearts;
    case Diamonds;
    case Clubs;
    case Spades;
}

$rEnum = new ReflectionEnum(Suit::class);

$cases = $rEnum->getCases();

foreach ($cases as $rCase) {
    var_dump($rCase->getValue());
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks for a case on an Enum

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Determines if a given case is defined on an Enum.

listitem.para: The case to check for.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: true if the case is defined, false if not.

example.title: ReflectionEnum::hasCase example
example.programlisting:
<?php
enum Suit
{
    case Hearts;
    case Diamonds;
    case Clubs;
    case Spades;
}

$rEnum = new ReflectionEnum(Suit::class);

var_dump($rEnum->hasCase('Hearts'));
var_dump($rEnum->hasCase('Horseshoes'));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Determines if an Enum is a Backed Enum

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: A Backed Enum is one that has a native backing scalar equivalent, either a string or an int. Not all Enums are backed.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: true if the Enum has a backing scalar, false if not.

example.title: ReflectionEnum::isBacked example
example.programlisting:
<?php
enum Suit
{
    case Hearts;
    case Diamonds;
    case Clubs;
    case Spades;
}

enum BackedSuit: string
{
    case Hearts = 'H';
    case Diamonds = 'D';
    case Clubs = 'C';
    case Spades = 'S';
}

var_dump((new ReflectionEnum(Suit::class))->isBacked());
var_dump((new ReflectionEnum(BackedSuit::class))->isBacked());
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.para: The ReflectionFunction class reports information about a function.

listitem.para: Indicates deprecated functions.

row.entry: The class constants are now typed.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Constructs a ReflectionFunction object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Constructs a ReflectionFunction object.

listitem.para: The name of the function to reflect or a closure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: A ReflectionException if the function parameter does not contain a valid function.

example.title: ReflectionFunction::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php
/**
 * A simple counter
 *
 * @return    int
 */
function counter1()
{
    static $c = 0;
    return ++$c;
}

/**
 * Another simple counter
 *
 * @return    int
 */
$counter2 = function()
{
    static $d = 0;
    return ++$d;

};

function dumpReflectionFunction($func)
{
    // Print out basic information
    printf(
        "\n\n===> The %s function '%s'\n".
        "     declared in %s\n".
        "     lines %d to %d\n",
        $func->isInternal() ? 'internal' : 'user-defined',
        $func->getName(),
        $func->getFileName(),
        $func->getStartLine(),
        $func->getEndline()
    );

    // Print documentation comment
    printf("---> Documentation:\n %s\n", var_export($func->getDocComment(), true));

    // Print static variables if existent
    if ($statics = $func->getStaticVariables())
    {
        printf("---> Static variables: %s\n", var_export($statics, true));
    }
}

// Create an instance of the ReflectionFunction class
dumpReflectionFunction(new ReflectionFunction('counter1'));
dumpReflectionFunction(new ReflectionFunction($counter2));
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen:
===> The user-defined function 'counter1' declared in Z:\reflectcounter.php lines 7 to 11 ---> Documentation: '/** * A simple counter * * @return int */' ---> Static variables: array ( 'c' => 0, )
===> The user-defined function '{closure}' declared in Z:\reflectcounter.php lines 18 to 23 ---> Documentation: '/** * Another simple counter * * @return int */' ---> Static variables: array ( 'd' => 0, )

refnamediv.refpurpose: Invokes function

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Invokes a reflected function.

listitem.para: The passed in argument list. It accepts a variable number of arguments which are passed to the function much like call_user_func is.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the result of the invoked function call.

example.title: ReflectionFunction::invoke example
example.programlisting:
<?php
function title($title, $name)
{
    return sprintf("%s. %s\r\n", $title, $name);
}

$function = new ReflectionFunction('title');

echo $function->invoke('Dr', 'Phil');
?>

note.para: ReflectionFunction::invoke cannot be used when reference parameters are expected. ReflectionFunction::invokeArgs has to be used instead (passing references in the argument list).

refnamediv.refpurpose: Invokes function args

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Invokes the function and pass its arguments as array.

listitem.simpara: The parameters to be passed to the function, as an array, much like call_user_func_array works.
If the keys of args are all numeric, the keys are ignored and each element is passed to the function as a positional argument, in order.
If any keys of args are strings, those elements are passed to the function as named arguments, with the name given by the key.
An Error is thrown if a numeric key in args appears after a string key, or if a string key does not match the name of any parameter of the function.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the result of the invoked function

row.entry: args keys will now be interpreted as parameter names, instead of being silently ignored.

example.title: ReflectionFunction::invokeArgs example
example.programlisting:
<?php
function title($title, $name)
{
    return sprintf("%s. %s\r\n", $title, $name);
}

$function = new ReflectionFunction('title');

echo $function->invokeArgs(array('Dr', 'Phil'));
?>

example.title: ReflectionFunction::invokeArgs with references example
example.programlisting:
<?php
function get_false_conditions(array $conditions, array &$false_conditions)
{
    foreach ($conditions as $condition) {
        if (!$condition) {
            $false_conditions[] = $condition;
        }
    }
}

$function_ref     = new ReflectionFunction('get_false_conditions');

$conditions       = array(true, false, -1, 0, 1);
$false_conditions = array();

$function_ref->invokeArgs(array($conditions, &$false_conditions));

var_dump($false_conditions);
?>

note.para: If the function has arguments that need to be references, then they must be references in the passed argument list.

listitem.simpara: Filter the results to include only ReflectionAttribute instances for attributes matching this class name.
Flags for determining how to filter the results, if name is provided.
Default is 0 which will only return results for attributes that are of the class name.
The only other option available, is to use ReflectionAttribute::IS_INSTANCEOF, which will instead use instanceof for filtering.

example.title: Basic usage with a class method
example.programlisting:
<?php
#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red {
}

class Factory {
    #[Fruit]
    #[Red]
    public function makeApple(): string
    {
        return 'apple';
    }
}

$method = new ReflectionMethod('Factory', 'makeApple');
$attributes = $method->getAttributes();
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the class corresponding to static:: inside a closure

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns the class as a ReflectionClass that corresponds to resolving the class name corresponding to static:: inside the Closure.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns a ReflectionClass corresponding to the class represented by static:: in the Closure. If the function is not a closure or if it has global scope null is returned instead.

example.title: Example showcasing difference between ReflectionFunctionAbstract::getClosureCalledClass, ReflectionFunctionAbstract::getClosureScopeClass, and ReflectionFunctionAbstract::getClosureThis with a closure in the object context
example.programlisting:
<?php

class A
{
    public function getClosure()
    {
        var_dump(self::class, static::class);

        return function() {};
    }
}

class B extends A {}

$b = new B();
$c = $b->getClosure();
$r = new ReflectionFunction($c);

var_dump($r->getClosureThis()); // $this === $b, since a non-static closure take the object context
var_dump($r->getClosureScopeClass()); // Corresponds to the self::class resolution inside a closure
var_dump($r->getClosureCalledClass()); // Corresponds to the static::class resolution inside a closure

?>

example.title: Example showcasing difference between ReflectionFunctionAbstract::getClosureCalledClass, ReflectionFunctionAbstract::getClosureScopeClass, and ReflectionFunctionAbstract::getClosureThis with a static closure without an object context

}

class B extends A {}

$c = $b->getClosure();
$r = new ReflectionFunction($c);

var_dump($r->getClosureThis()); // NULL, since the pseudo-variable $this is not available in a static context
var_dump($r->getClosureScopeClass()); // Corresponds to the self::class resolution inside a closure
var_dump($r->getClosureCalledClass()); // Corresponds to the static::class resolution inside a closure

?>

section.title: Introduction
section.para: The ReflectionMethod class reports information about a method.

listitem.para: Method name
Class name
Indicates that the method is static. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, the value was 1.
Indicates that the method is public. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, the value was 256.
Indicates that the method is protected. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, the value was 512.
Indicates that the method is private. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, the value was 1024.
Indicates that the method is abstract. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, the value was 2.
Indicates that the method is final. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, the value was 4.

note.para: The values of these constants may change between PHP versions. It is recommended to always use the constants and not rely on the values directly.

row.entry: The class constants are now typed.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Constructs a ReflectionMethod

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Alternative signature (not supported with named arguments):

warning.simpara: The alternative signature is deprecated as of PHP 8.4.0, use ReflectionMethod::createFromMethodName instead.

refsect1.para: Constructs a new ReflectionMethod.

listitem.para: Classname or object (instance of the class) that contains the method.
Name of the method.
Class name and method name delimited by ::.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: A ReflectionException is thrown if the given method does not exist.

example.title: ReflectionMethod::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Counter
{
    private static $c = 0;

    /**
     * Increment counter
     *
     * @final
     * @static
     * @access  public
     * @return  int
     */
    final public static function increment()
    {
        return ++self::$c;
    }
}

// Create an instance of the ReflectionMethod class
$method = new ReflectionMethod('Counter', 'increment');

// Print out basic information
printf(
    "===> The %s%s%s%s%s%s%s method '%s' (which is %s)\n" .
    "     declared in %s\n" .
    "     lines %d to %d\n" .
    "     having the modifiers %d[%s]\n",
        $method->isInternal() ? 'internal' : 'user-defined',
        $method->isAbstract() ? ' abstract' : '',
        $method->isFinal() ? ' final' : '',
        $method->isPublic() ? ' public' : '',
        $method->isPrivate() ? ' private' : '',
        $method->isProtected() ? ' protected' : '',
        $method->isStatic() ? ' static' : '',
        $method->getName(),
        $method->isConstructor() ? 'the constructor' : 'a regular method',
        $method->getFileName(),
        $method->getStartLine(),
        $method->getEndline(),
        $method->getModifiers(),
        implode(' ', Reflection::getModifierNames($method->getModifiers()))
);

// Print documentation comment
printf("---> Documentation:\n %s\n", var_export($method->getDocComment(), true));

// Print static variables if existent
if ($statics= $method->getStaticVariables()) {
    printf("---> Static variables: %s\n", var_export($statics, true));
}

// Invoke the method
printf("---> Invocation results in: ");
var_dump($method->invoke(NULL));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets the method modifiers

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns a bitfield of the access modifiers for this method.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A numeric representation of the modifiers. The actual meaning of these modifiers are described under predefined constants.

example.title: ReflectionMethod::getModifiers example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Testing
{
    final public static function foo()
    {
        return;
    }
    public function bar()
    {
        return;
    }
}

$foo = new ReflectionMethod('Testing', 'foo');

echo "Modifiers for method foo():\n";
echo $foo->getModifiers() . "\n";
echo implode(' ', Reflection::getModifierNames($foo->getModifiers())) . "\n";

$bar = new ReflectionMethod('Testing', 'bar');

echo "Modifiers for method bar():\n";
echo $bar->getModifiers() . "\n";
echo implode(' ', Reflection::getModifierNames($bar->getModifiers()));
?>

example.screen: Modifiers for method foo(): 49 final public static Modifiers for method bar(): 1 public

refnamediv.refpurpose: Invoke

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Invokes a reflected method.

listitem.para: The object to invoke the method on. For static methods, pass null to this parameter.
Zero or more parameters to be passed to the method. It accepts a variable number of parameters which are passed to the method.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the method result.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: A ReflectionException if the object parameter does not contain an instance of the class that this method was declared in.
A ReflectionException if the method invocation failed.

example.title: ReflectionMethod::invoke example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class HelloWorld {

    public function sayHelloTo($name) {
        return 'Hello ' . $name;
    }

}

$reflectionMethod = new ReflectionMethod('HelloWorld', 'sayHelloTo');
echo $reflectionMethod->invoke(new HelloWorld(), 'Mike');
?>

note.para: ReflectionMethod::invoke cannot be used when reference parameters are expected. ReflectionMethod::invokeArgs has to be used instead (passing references in the argument list).

refnamediv.refpurpose: Invoke args

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Invokes the reflected method and pass its arguments as array.

listitem.para: The object to invoke the method on. In case of static methods, you can pass null to this parameter.

listitem.simpara: The parameters to be passed to the method, as an array.
If the keys of args are all numeric, the keys are ignored and each element is passed to the method as a positional argument, in order.
If any keys of args are strings, those elements are passed to the method as named arguments, with the name given by the key.
An Error is thrown if a numeric key in args appears after a string key, or if a string key does not match the name of any parameter of the method.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the method result.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: A ReflectionException if the object parameter does not contain an instance of the class that this method was declared in.
A ReflectionException if the method invocation failed.

row.entry: args keys will now be interpreted as parameter names, instead of being silently ignored.

example.title: ReflectionMethod::invokeArgs example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class HelloWorld {

    public function sayHelloTo($name) {
        return 'Hello ' . $name;
    }

}

$reflectionMethod = new ReflectionMethod('HelloWorld', 'sayHelloTo');
echo $reflectionMethod->invokeArgs(new HelloWorld(), array('Mike'));
?>

note.para: If the function has arguments that need to be references, then they must be references in the passed argument list.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Enables invoking of a protected or private method via the ReflectionMethod::invoke method.

Calling this method has no effect; all methods are invokable by default.

example.title: Simple Class definition
example.programlisting:
<?php
class MyClass
{
    private function foo()
    {
        return 'bar';
    }
}

$method = new ReflectionMethod("MyClass", "foo");
$method->setAccessible(true);

$obj = new MyClass();
echo $method->invoke($obj);
echo $obj->foo();
?>

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks if the type is a built-in type in PHP. A built-in type is any type that is not a class, interface, or trait.

refsect1.para: true if it's a built-in type, otherwise false

refsect1.title: Examples

example.title: ReflectionNamedType::isBuiltin example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class SomeClass {}

function someFunction(string $param, SomeClass $param2, stdClass $param3) {}

refsect1.para: Note that the ReflectionNamedType::isBuiltin method does not distinguish between internal and custom classes. To make this distinction, the ReflectionClass::isInternal method should be used on the returned class name.

section.title: Introduction
section.para: The ReflectionParameter class retrieves information about function's or method's parameters.

To introspect function parameters, first create an instance of the ReflectionFunction or ReflectionMethod classes and then use their ReflectionFunctionAbstract::getParameters method to retrieve an array of parameters.

Either an int specifying the position of the parameter (starting with zero), or the parameter name as string.

example.title: Using the ReflectionParameter class
example.programlisting:
<?php
function foo($a, $b, $c) { }
function bar(Exception $a, &$b, $c) { }
function baz(ReflectionFunction $a, $b = 1, $c = null) { }
function abc() { }

$reflect = new ReflectionFunction('foo');

echo $reflect;

foreach ($reflect->getParameters() as $i => $param) {
    printf(
        "-- Parameter #%d: %s {\n".
        "   Class: %s\n".
        "   Allows NULL: %s\n".
        "   Passed to by reference: %s\n".
        "   Is optional?: %s\n".
        "}\n",
        $i, // $param->getPosition() can be used
        $param->getName(),
        var_export($param->getClass(), 1),
        var_export($param->allowsNull(), 1),
        var_export($param->isPassedByReference(), 1),
        $param->isOptional() ? 'yes' : 'no'
    );
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets Attributes

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns all attributes declared on this parameter as an array of ReflectionAttribute.

listitem.simpara: Filter the results to include only ReflectionAttribute instances for attributes matching this class name.
Flags for determining how to filter the results, if name is provided.
Default is 0 which will only return results for attributes that are of the class name.
The only other option available, is to use ReflectionAttribute::IS_INSTANCEOF, which will instead use instanceof for filtering.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Array of attributes, as a ReflectionAttribute object.

example.title: Basic usage
example.programlisting:
<?php
#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red {
}

function fruitBasket(
   #[Fruit]
   #[Red]
   string $apple
) { }

$reflection = new ReflectionFunction('fruitBasket');
$parameter = $reflection->getParameters()[0];
$attributes = $parameter->getAttributes();
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

example.title: Filtering results by class name
example.programlisting:
<?php
#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red {
}

function fruitBasket(
   #[Fruit]
   #[Red]
   string $apple
) { }

$reflection = new ReflectionFunction('fruitBasket');
$parameter = $reflection->getParameters()[0];
$attributes = $parameter->getAttributes('Fruit');
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

example.title: Filtering results by class name, with inheritance
example.programlisting:
<?php
interface Color {
}

#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red implements Color {
}

function fruitBasket(
   #[Fruit]
   #[Red]
   string $apple
) { }

$reflection = new ReflectionFunction('fruitBasket');
$parameter = $reflection->getParameters()[0];
$attributes = $parameter->getAttributes('Color', ReflectionAttribute::IS_INSTANCEOF);
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

row.entry: This method now allows getting the default value of parameters of built-in functions and built-in class methods. Previously, a ReflectionException was thrown.

example.title: Getting default values of function parameters
example.programlisting:
<?php
function foo($test, $bar = 'baz')
{
    echo $test . $bar;
}

$function = new ReflectionFunction('foo');

foreach ($function->getParameters() as $param) {
    echo 'Name: ' . $param->getName() . PHP_EOL;
    if ($param->isOptional()) {
        echo 'Default value: ' . $param->getDefaultValue() . PHP_EOL;
    }
    echo PHP_EOL;
}
?>

Name: bar Default value: baz

example.title: ReflectionParameter::getType Usage as of PHP 7.1.0
example.simpara: As of PHP 7.1.0, ReflectionType::__toString is deprecated, and ReflectionParameter::getType may return an instance of ReflectionNamedType. To get the name of the parameter type, ReflectionNamedType is available in this case.
example.programlisting:
<?php
function someFunction(int $param, $param2) {}

$reflectionFunc = new ReflectionFunction('someFunction');
$reflectionParams = $reflectionFunc->getParameters();
$reflectionType1 = $reflectionParams[0]->getType();
$reflectionType2 = $reflectionParams[1]->getType();

assert($reflectionType1 instanceof ReflectionNamedType);
echo $reflectionType1->getName(), PHP_EOL;
var_dump($reflectionType2);
?>

example.title: ReflectionParameter::getType Usage in PHP 8.0.0 and later
example.para: As of PHP 8.0.0, this method may return a ReflectionNamedType instance or a ReflectionUnionType instance. The latter is a collection of the former. To analyze a type, it is often convenient to normalize it to an array of ReflectionNamedType objects. The following function will return an array of 0 or more ReflectionNamedType instances.
example.programlisting:
<?php
function getAllTypes(ReflectionParameter $reflectionParameter): array
{
    $reflectionType = $reflectionParameter->getType();

    if (!$reflectionType) return [];

    return $reflectionType instanceof ReflectionUnionType
        ? $reflectionType->getTypes()
        : [$reflectionType];
}
?>

refsynopsisdiv.para: See the example below for an alternative way to derive this information.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks if the parameter expects an array.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: true if an array is expected, false otherwise.

row.entry: This function has been deprecated in favor of ReflectionParameter::getType instead.

example.title: PHP 8.0.0 equivalent
example.para: As of PHP 8.0.0, the following code will report if a type declares arrays, including as part of a union.
example.programlisting:
<?php
function declaresArray(ReflectionParameter $reflectionParameter): bool
{
    $reflectionType = $reflectionParameter->getType();

    if (!$reflectionType) return false;

    $types = $reflectionType instanceof ReflectionUnionType
        ? $reflectionType->getTypes()
        : [$reflectionType];

   return in_array('array', array_map(fn(ReflectionNamedType $t) => $t->getName(), $types));
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns whether parameter MUST be callable

warning.simpara: This function has been DEPRECATED as of PHP 8.0.0. Relying on this function is highly discouraged.

refsynopsisdiv.para: See the example below for an alternative way to derive this information.

warning.simpara: This function is currently not documented; only its argument list is available.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if the parameter is callable, false if it is not or null on failure.

row.entry: This function has been deprecated in favor of ReflectionParameter::getType instead.

example.title: PHP 8.0.0 equivalent
example.para: As of PHP 8.0.0, the following code will report if a type supports callables, including as part of a union.
example.programlisting:
<?php
function declaresCallable(ReflectionParameter $reflectionParameter): bool
{
    $reflectionType = $reflectionParameter->getType();

    if (!$reflectionType) return false;

    $types = $reflectionType instanceof ReflectionUnionType
        ? $reflectionType->getTypes()
        : [$reflectionType];

   return in_array('callable', array_map(fn(ReflectionNamedType $t) => $t->getName(), $types));
}
?>

section.title: Introduction
section.para: The ReflectionProperty class reports information about class properties.

listitem.para: Name of the property. Read-only, throws ReflectionException in attempt to write.
Name of the class where the property is defined. Read-only, throws ReflectionException in attempt to write.
Indicates static properties. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, the value was 1.
Indicates readonly properties. Available as of PHP 8.1.0.
Indicates public properties. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, the value was 256.
Indicates protected properties. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, the value was 512.
Indicates private properties. Prior to PHP 7.4.0, the value was 1024.

listitem.simpara: Indicates the property is abstract. Available as of PHP 8.4.0.
Available as of PHP 8.4.0.
Available as of PHP 8.4.0.
Available as of PHP 8.4.0.
Indicates the property is final. Available as of PHP 8.4.0.

note.para: The values of these constants may change between PHP versions. It is recommended to always use the constants and not rely on the values directly.

row.entry: The class constants are now typed.
Added ReflectionProperty::IS_VIRTUAL, ReflectionProperty::IS_PRIVATE_SET, ReflectionProperty::IS_PROTECTED_SET, ReflectionProperty::IS_ABSTRACT, and ReflectionProperty::IS_FINAL.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Construct a ReflectionProperty object

listitem.para: Either a string containing the name of the class to reflect, or an object.
The name of the property being reflected.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: Trying to get or set private or protected class property's values will result in an exception being thrown.

example.title: ReflectionProperty::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php

class Str
{
    public $length  = 5;
}

// Create an instance of the ReflectionProperty class
$prop = new ReflectionProperty('Str', 'length');

// Print out basic information
printf(
    "===> The%s%s%s%s property '%s' (which was %s)\n" .
    "     having the modifiers %s\n",
        $prop->isPublic() ? ' public' : '',
        $prop->isPrivate() ? ' private' : '',
        $prop->isProtected() ? ' protected' : '',
        $prop->isStatic() ? ' static' : '',
        $prop->getName(),
        $prop->isDefault() ? 'declared at compile-time' : 'created at run-time',
        var_export(Reflection::getModifierNames($prop->getModifiers()), true)
);

// Create an instance of Str
$obj= new Str();

// Get current value
printf("---> Value is: ");
var_dump($prop->getValue($obj));

// Change value
$prop->setValue($obj, 10);
printf("---> Setting value to 10, new value is: ");
var_dump($prop->getValue($obj));

// Dump object
var_dump($obj);

?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

example.title: Getting value from private and protected properties using ReflectionProperty class
example.programlisting:
<?php

class Foo
{
    public $x = 1;
    protected $y = 2;
    private $z = 3;
}

$obj = new Foo;

$prop = new ReflectionProperty('Foo', 'y');
$prop->setAccessible(true);
var_dump($prop->getValue($obj)); // int(2)

$prop = new ReflectionProperty('Foo', 'z');
$prop->setAccessible(true);
var_dump($prop->getValue($obj)); // int(2)

?>

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Exports a reflection.

warning.simpara: This function is currently not documented; only its argument list is available.

listitem.para: The reflection to export.
The property name.
Setting to true will return the export, as opposed to emitting it. Setting to false (the default) will do the opposite.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets Attributes

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns all attributes declared on this class property as an array of ReflectionAttribute.

listitem.simpara: Filter the results to include only ReflectionAttribute instances for attributes matching this class name.
Flags for determining how to filter the results, if name is provided.
Default is 0 which will only return results for attributes that are of the class name.
The only other option available, is to use ReflectionAttribute::IS_INSTANCEOF, which will instead use instanceof for filtering.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Array of attributes, as a ReflectionAttribute object.

example.title: Basic usage
example.programlisting:
<?php
#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red {
}

class Basket {
    #[Fruit]
    #[Red]
    public string $apple = 'apple';
}

$property = new ReflectionProperty('Basket', 'apple');
$attributes = $property->getAttributes();
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

example.title: Filtering results by class name
example.programlisting:
<?php
#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red {
}

class Basket {
    #[Fruit]
    #[Red]
    public string $apple = 'apple';
}

$property = new ReflectionProperty('Basket', 'apple');
$attributes = $property->getAttributes('Fruit');
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

example.title: Filtering results by class name, with inheritance
example.programlisting:
<?php
interface Color {
}

#[Attribute]
class Fruit {
}

#[Attribute]
class Red implements Color {
}

class Basket {
    #[Fruit]
    #[Red]
    public string $apple = 'apple';
}

$property = new ReflectionProperty('Basket', 'apple');
$attributes = $property->getAttributes('Color', ReflectionAttribute::IS_INSTANCEOF);
print_r(array_map(fn($attribute) => $attribute->getName(), $attributes));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the default value declared for a property

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets the implicit or explicitly declared default value for a property.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The default value if the property has any default value (including null). If there is no default value, then null is returned. It is not possible to differentiate between a null default value and an uninitialized typed property. Use ReflectionProperty::hasDefaultValue to detect the difference.

row.entry: Calling ReflectionProperty::getDefaultValue for properties without default values has been deprecated.

example.title: ReflectionProperty::getDefaultValue example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Foo {
    public $bar = 1;
    public ?int $baz;
    public int $boing = 0;
    public function __construct(public string $bak = "default") { }
}

$ro = new ReflectionClass(Foo::class);
var_dump($ro->getProperty('bar')->getDefaultValue());
var_dump($ro->getProperty('baz')->getDefaultValue());
var_dump($ro->getProperty('boing')->getDefaultValue());
var_dump($ro->getProperty('bak')->getDefaultValue());
?>

example.screen: string(53) "/** * @var int The length of the string */"

example.title: Multiple property declarations
example.simpara: If multiple property declarations are preceded by a single doc comment, the doc comment refers to the first property only.
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Foo
{
    /** @var string */
    public $a, $b;
}
$class = new \ReflectionClass('Foo');
foreach ($class->getProperties() as $property) {
    echo $property->getName() . ': ' . var_export($property->getDocComment(), true) . PHP_EOL;
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns a reflection object for a specified hook

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Gets the reflection of the property's hook, if any.

listitem.simpara: The type of hook to request.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: If the requested hook is defined, a ReflectionMethod instance will be returned. If not, the method will return null

example.title: ReflectionProperty::getHook example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Example
{
    public string $name { get => "Name here"; }
}

$rClass = new \ReflectionClass(Example::class);
$rProp = $rClass->getProperty('name');
var_dump($rProp->getHook(PropertyHookType::Get));
var_dump($rProp->getHook(PropertyHookType::Set));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns an array of all hooks on this property

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns a list of all hooks on this property.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: An array of ReflectionMethod objects keyed by the hook they are for. For example, a property with both get and set hooks will return a 2 element array with string keys get and set, each of which are a ReflectionMethod object. The order in which they are returned is explicitly undefined. If no hooks are defined, an empty array is returned.

example.title: ReflectionProperty::getHooks example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Example
{
    public string $name { get => "Name here"; }

    public int $count;
}

$rClass = new \ReflectionClass(Example::class);

$rProp = $rClass->getProperty('name');
var_dump($rProp->getHooks());

$rProp = $rClass->getProperty('count');
var_dump($rProp->getHooks());
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets the mangled name of the property

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns the mangled (internal) name of the property, which encodes the visibility scope for private and protected properties.

For public properties, the mangled name is identical to the property name. For protected properties, the mangled name has the form \0*\0name. For private properties, the mangled name has the form \0ClassName\0name.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The mangled name of the reflected property.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the value of a property, bypassing a get hook if defined

refsect1.title: Description

warning.simpara: This function is currently not documented; only its argument list is available.

refsect1.simpara: Returns the value of a property, bypassing a get hook if defined.

listitem.simpara: The object from which to retrieve a value.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: The stored value of the property, bypassing a get hook if defined.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: If the property is virtual, an Error will be thrown, as there is no raw value to retrieve.

example.title: ReflectionProperty::getRawValue example
example.programlisting:
<?php

class Example
{
    public string $tag {
        get => strtolower($this->tag);
    }
}

$example = new Example();
$example->tag = 'PHP';

$rClass = new \ReflectionClass(Example::class);
$rProp = $rClass->getProperty('tag');

// These would go through the get hook, so would produce "php"
echo $example->tag, PHP_EOL;
echo $rProp->getValue($example), PHP_EOL;

// But this would bypass the hook and produce "PHP"
echo $rProp->getRawValue($example);

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the parameter type of a setter hook

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns the parameter type of a set hook. If no set hook is defined, it behaves identically to ReflectionProperty::getType.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

simplelist.member: This method returns an instance of ReflectionType that matches the settable type for the property.
If there is a set hook that defines an explicit type, that will be returned.
If the hook does not specify a type, or it does not exist, the property type will be returned, identically to ReflectionProperty::getType. This value may be null if the property is untyped.
If the property is virtual and has no set hook, a ReflectionType instance for never will be returned.

example.title: ReflectionProperty::getSettableType example
example.programlisting:
<?php

class Example
{
    public string $basic {
        set => strtolower($value);
    }

    public string $wider {
        set(string|Stringable $value) => (string) $value;
    }

    public string $virtual {
        get => 'Do not change this';
    }

    public $untyped = 'silly';
}

$rClass = new \ReflectionClass(Example::class);

var_dump($rClass->getProperty('basic')->getSettableType());
var_dump($rClass->getProperty('wider')->getSettableType());
var_dump($rClass->getProperty('virtual')->getSettableType());
var_dump($rClass->getProperty('untyped')->getSettableType());

?>
