refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets the property's value.

listitem.para: If the property is non-static an object must be provided to fetch the property from. If you want to fetch the default property without providing an object use ReflectionClass::getDefaultProperties instead.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The current value of the property.

row.entry: Private and protected properties can be accessed by ReflectionProperty::getValue right away. Previously, they needed to be made accessible by calling ReflectionProperty::setAccessible; otherwise a ReflectionException was thrown.

example.title: ReflectionProperty::getValue example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Foo {
    public static $staticProperty = 'foobar';
    
    public $property = 'barfoo';
    protected $privateProperty = 'foofoo';
}

$reflectionClass = new ReflectionClass('Foo');

var_dump($reflectionClass->getProperty('staticProperty')->getValue());
var_dump($reflectionClass->getProperty('property')->getValue(new Foo));

$reflectionProperty = $reflectionClass->getProperty('privateProperty');
$reflectionProperty->setAccessible(true); // only required prior to PHP 8.1.0
var_dump($reflectionProperty->getValue(new Foo));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks if property has a default value declared

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks whether the property was declared with a default value, including an implicit null default value. Only returns false for typed properties without default value (or dynamic properties).

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: If the property has any default value (including null) true is returned; if the property is typed without a default value declared or is a dynamic property, false is returned.

example.title: ReflectionProperty::hasDefaultValue example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Foo {
    public $bar;
    public ?int $baz;
    public ?int $foo = null;
    public int $boing;
    
    public function __construct()
    {
        $this->ping = '';
    }
}

$ro = new ReflectionObject(new Foo());
var_dump($ro->getProperty('bar')->hasDefaultValue());
var_dump($ro->getProperty('baz')->hasDefaultValue());
var_dump($ro->getProperty('foo')->hasDefaultValue());
var_dump($ro->getProperty('boing')->hasDefaultValue());
var_dump($ro->getProperty('ping')->hasDefaultValue()); // Dynamic property
var_dump($ro->getProperty('pong')->hasDefaultValue()); // Not defined property
?>
example.screen:
bool(true) bool(false) bool(true) bool(false) bool(false)
Fatal error: Uncaught ReflectionException: Property Foo::$pong does not exist in example.php

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks if property is a default property

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks whether the property was declared at compile-time, or whether the property was dynamically declared at run-time.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: true if the property was declared at compile-time, or false if it was created at run-time.

example.title: ReflectionProperty::isDefault example
example.programlisting:
<?php

#[\AllowDynamicProperties]
class Foo {
    public $bar;
}

$o = new Foo();
$o->bar = 42;
$o->baz = 42;

$ro = new ReflectionObject($o);
var_dump($ro->getProperty('bar')->isDefault());
var_dump($ro->getProperty('baz')->isDefault());
?>

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks whether a property is initialized.

listitem.para: If the property is non-static an object must be provided to fetch the property from.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns false for typed properties prior to initialization, and for properties that have been explicitly unset. For all other properties true will be returned.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: Throws a ReflectionException if the property is inaccessible. You can make a protected or private property accessible using ReflectionProperty::setAccessible.

example.title: ReflectionProperty::isInitialized example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class User
{
    public string $name;
}

$rp = new ReflectionProperty('User', 'name');
$user = new User;
var_dump($rp->isInitialized($user));
$user->name = 'Nikita';
var_dump($rp->isInitialized($user));
?>

example.title: ReflectionProperty::isPromoted example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Foo {
    public $baz;

    public function __construct(public $bar) {}

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks if property is public

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks whether the property is public.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: true if the property is marked public, false otherwise.

note.simpara: Note this refers only to the main visibility, and not to a set-visibility, if specified.

Be aware that a property being public does not always imply is it publicly writeable. A property could be virtual with no set hook, or it could be readonly and already have been written to, or it could have a set visibility defined that is non-public. In all of those cases, this method will return true but the property will not be writeable.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Determines if a property is virtual

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Determines if a property is virtual.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true if the property is virtual, false otherwise.

example.title: ReflectionProperty::isVirtual example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Example
{
    // None of the hooks reference the property,
    // so this is virtual.
    public string $name { get => "Name here"; }

    // This hook references the property by name,
    // so it is not virtual.
    public int $age {
        set {
            if ($value <= 0) {
               throw new \InvalidArgumentException();
            }
            $this->age = $value;
        }
    }

    // Non-hooked properties are always not-virtual.
    public string $job;
}

$rClass = new \ReflectionClass(Example::class);

var_dump($rClass->getProperty('name')->isVirtual());
var_dump($rClass->getProperty('age')->isVirtual());
var_dump($rClass->getProperty('job')->isVirtual());
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set property accessibility

warning.simpara: This function has been DEPRECATED as of PHP 8.5.0. Relying on this function is highly discouraged.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Enables access to a protected or private property via the ReflectionProperty::getValue and ReflectionProperty::setValue methods.

note.simpara: As of PHP 8.1.0, calling this method has no effect; all properties are accessible by default.

listitem.para: true to allow accessibility, or false.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

row.entry: This method has been deprecated, as it no longer has an effect.
Calling this method has no effect; all properties are accessible by default.

example.title: Simple Class definition
example.programlisting:
<?php
class MyClass
{
    private $foo = 'bar';
}

$property = new ReflectionProperty("MyClass", "foo");
$property->setAccessible(true);

$obj = new MyClass();
echo $property->getValue($obj);
echo $obj->foo;
?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: bar Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Cannot access private property MyClass::$foo in /in/WJqTv:12

refnamediv.refpurpose: Sets the value of a property, bypassing a set hook if defined

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sets the value of a property, bypassing a set hook if defined.

listitem.simpara: The object on which to set the property value.
The value to write. It must still be valid according to the property's type.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: If the property is virtual, an Error will be thrown, as there is no raw value to set.

example.title: ReflectionProperty::setRawValue example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Example
{
    public int $age {
        set {
            if ($value <= 0) {
               throw new \InvalidArgumentException();
            }
            $this->age = $value;
        }
    }
}

$example = new Example();

$rClass = new \ReflectionClass(Example::class);
$rProp = $rClass->getProperty('age');

// These would go through the set hook, and throw an exception.
try {
    $example->age = -2;
} catch (InvalidArgumentException) {
    echo "InvalidArgumentException for setting property to -2\n";
}
try {
    $rProp->setValue($example, -2);
} catch (InvalidArgumentException) {
    echo "InvalidArgumentException for using ReflectionProperty::setValue() with -2\n";
}

// But this would set the $age to -2 without error.
$rProp->setRawValue($example, -2);
echo $example->age;
?>
example.screen: InvalidArgumentException for setting property to -2 InvalidArgumentException for using ReflectionProperty::setValue() with -2 -2

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set raw property value without triggering lazy initialization

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sets (changes) the property's value without triggering lazy initialization and without calling hook functions. The property is marked as non-lazy and can be accessed afterwards without triggering lazy initialization. The property must not be dynamic, static, or virtual, and the object must be an instance of a user defined class or stdClass.
If this was the last lazy property, the object is marked as non-lazy and the initializer or factory function is detached.

listitem.simpara: The object to change the property on.
The new value.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set property value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Sets (changes) the property's value.

note.simpara: To set static property values, use ReflectionProperty::setValue(null, $value).

listitem.para: For static properties, pass in null. For non-static properties, pass in the object.
The new value.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

row.entry: Calling this method with a single argument is deprecated, instead use ReflectionProperty::setValue(null, $value) for static properties.

Private and protected properties can be accessed by ReflectionProperty::setValue right away. Previously, they needed to be made accessible by calling ReflectionProperty::setAccessible; otherwise a ReflectionException was thrown.

example.title: ReflectionProperty::setValue example
example.programlisting:
<?php
class Foo {
    public static $staticProperty;
    
    public $property;
    protected $privateProperty;
}

$reflectionClass = new ReflectionClass('Foo');

// As of PHP 8.3, passing in null as the first argument is required
// to access static properties.
$reflectionProperty = $reflectionClass->getProperty('staticProperty');
$reflectionProperty->setValue(null, 'foo');
var_dump(Foo::$staticProperty);

$foo = new Foo;

$reflectionClass->getProperty('property')->setValue($foo, 'bar');
var_dump($foo->property);

$reflectionProperty = $reflectionClass->getProperty('privateProperty');
$reflectionProperty->setAccessible(true); // only required prior to PHP 8.1.0
$reflectionProperty->setValue($foo, 'foobar');
var_dump($reflectionProperty->getValue($foo));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Marks property as non-lazy

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Marks a property as non-lazy such that it can be accessed directly without triggering lazy initialization. The property is initialized to its default value, if any. The property must not be dynamic, static, or virtual, and the object must be an instance of a user defined class or stdClass.
If this was the last lazy property, the object is marked as non-lazy and the initializer or factory function is detached.

listitem.simpara: The object to mark the property on.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

refnamediv.refpurpose: To string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the string representation of the property.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A string representation of this ReflectionProperty instance.

row.entry: The attached doc comment is now included.

section.title: Introduction
section.para:
The ReflectionType class reports information about a function's parameter/return type or a class's property type. The Reflection extension declares the following subtypes:
ReflectionNamedType (as of PHP 7.1.0) ReflectionUnionType (as of PHP 8.0.0) ReflectionIntersectionType (as of PHP 8.1.0)

row.entry: ReflectionType has become abstract and ReflectionType::isBuiltin has been moved to ReflectionNamedType::isBuiltin.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Checks whether the parameter allows null.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: true if null is allowed, otherwise false

example.title: ReflectionType::allowsNull example
example.programlisting:
<?php
function someFunction(string $param, stdClass $param2 = null) {}

$reflectionFunc = new ReflectionFunction('someFunction');
$reflectionParams = $reflectionFunc->getParameters();

var_dump($reflectionParams[0]->getType()->allowsNull());
var_dump($reflectionParams[1]->getType()->allowsNull());

$reflectionParam = $reflectionFunc->getParameters()[0];

echo $reflectionParam->getType();

section.title: Introduction
section.para: The ReflectionGenerator class reports information about a generator.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Constructs a ReflectionGenerator object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Constructs a ReflectionGenerator object.

listitem.para: A generator object.

example.title: ReflectionGenerator::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php

function gen()
{
    yield 1;
}

$gen = gen();

$reflectionGen = new ReflectionGenerator($gen);

echo <<< output
{$reflectionGen->getFunction()->name}
Line: {$reflectionGen->getExecutingLine()}
File: {$reflectionGen->getExecutingFile()}
output;
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets the trace of the executing generator

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Get the trace of the currently executing generator.

listitem.para: The value of options can be any of the following flags.

row.entry: Don't include the argument information for functions in the stack trace.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the trace of the currently executing generator.

example.title: ReflectionGenerator::getTrace example
example.programlisting:
<?php
function foo() {
    yield 1;
}

function bar()
{
    yield from foo();
}

function baz()
{
    yield from bar();
}

$gen = baz();
$gen->valid(); // start the generator

var_dump((new ReflectionGenerator($gen))->getTrace());
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Checks if execution finished

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Returns whether the execution reached the end of the function, a return statement or if an exception was thrown.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns whether the generator finished executing.

example.title: ReflectionGenerator::isClosed example
example.programlisting:
<?php

function gen()
{
    yield 'a';
    yield 'a';
}

$gen = gen();
$reflectionGen = new ReflectionGenerator($gen);

foreach ($gen as $value) {
    echo $value, PHP_EOL;
    var_dump($reflectionGen->isClosed());
}

var_dump($reflectionGen->isClosed());

?>

section.title: Introduction
section.para: The ReflectionReference class provides information about a reference.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Private constructor to disallow direct instantiation

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Create a ReflectionReference from an array element

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Creates a ReflectionReference from an array element.

listitem.para: The array which contains the potential reference.
The key; either an int or a string.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a ReflectionReference instance if $array[$key] is a reference, or null otherwise.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: If array is not an array, or key is not an int or string, a TypeError is thrown. If $array[$key] does not exist, a ReflectionException is thrown.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get unique ID of a reference

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns an ID which is unique for the reference for the lifetime of that reference. This ID can be used to compare references for equality, or to maintain a map of known references.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a string of unspecified format.

example.title: Basic ReflectionReference::getId usage
example.programlisting:
<?php
$val1 = 'foo';
$val2 = 'bar';
$arr = [&$val1, &$val2, &$val1];

$rr1 = ReflectionReference::fromArrayElement($arr, 0);
$rr2 = ReflectionReference::fromArrayElement($arr, 1);
$rr3 = ReflectionReference::fromArrayElement($arr, 2);

var_dump($rr1->getId() === $rr2->getId());
var_dump($rr1->getId() === $rr3->getId());
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the boolean value of a variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the bool value of value.

listitem.para: The scalar value being converted to a bool.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The bool value of value.

example.title: boolval examples
example.programlisting:
<?php
echo '0:        '.(boolval(0) ? 'true' : 'false')."\n";
echo '42:       '.(boolval(42) ? 'true' : 'false')."\n";
echo '0.0:      '.(boolval(0.0) ? 'true' : 'false')."\n";
echo '4.2:      '.(boolval(4.2) ? 'true' : 'false')."\n";
echo '"":       '.(boolval("") ? 'true' : 'false')."\n";
echo '"string": '.(boolval("string") ? 'true' : 'false')."\n";
echo '"0":      '.(boolval("0") ? 'true' : 'false')."\n";
echo '"1":      '.(boolval("1") ? 'true' : 'false')."\n";
echo '[1, 2]:   '.(boolval([1, 2]) ? 'true' : 'false')."\n";
echo '[]:       '.(boolval([]) ? 'true' : 'false')."\n";
echo 'stdClass: '.(boolval(new stdClass) ? 'true' : 'false')."\n";
?>
example.screen: 0: false 42: true 0.0: false 4.2: true "": false "string": true "0": false "1": true [1, 2]: true []: false stdClass: true

refnamediv.refpurpose: Dumps a string representation of an internal zval structure to output

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Dumps a string representation of an internal zval (Zend value) structure to output. This is mostly useful for understanding or debugging implementation details of the Zend Engine or PHP extensions.

listitem.para: The variable or value to dump.
Further variables or values to dump.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

row.entry: debug_zval_dump now indicates whether an array is packed.

example.title: debug_zval_dump example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$var1 = 'Hello';
$var1 .= ' World';
$var2 = $var1;

debug_zval_dump($var1);
?>

note.title: Understanding the refcount
note.para: The refcount value shown by this function may be surprising without a detailed understanding of the engine's implementation.
The Zend Engine uses reference counting for two different purposes:

simplelist.member: Optimizing memory usage using a technique called "copy on write", where multiple variables holding the same value point to the same copy in memory. When any of the variables is modified, it is pointed to a new copy in memory, and the reference count on the original is decreased by 1.

Tracking variables which have been assigned or passed by reference (see References Explained). This refcount is stored on a separate reference zval, pointing to the zval for the current value. This additional zval is not currently shown by debug_zval_dump.

note.para: Because debug_zval_dump takes its input as normal parameters, passed by value, the copy on write technique will be used to pass them: rather than copying the data, the refcount will be increased by one for the lifetime of the function call. If the function modified the parameter after receiving it, then a copy would be made; since it does not, it will show a refcount one higher than in the calling scope.

Although $var1, $var2, and $var3 are linked as references, only the value is passed to debug_zval_dump. That value is used once by the set of references, and once inside the debug_zval_dump, so shows a refcount of 2.

Further complications arise because of optimisations made in the engine for different data types. Some types such as integers do not use "copy on write", so do not show a refcount at all. In other cases, the refcount shows extra copies used internally, such as when a literal string or array is stored as part of a code instruction.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of floatval

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: floatval.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Determine whether a variable is empty

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Determine whether a variable is considered to be empty. A variable is considered empty if it does not exist or if its value equals false. empty does not generate a warning if the variable does not exist.

listitem.para: Variable to be checked

No warning is generated if the variable does not exist. That means empty is essentially the concise equivalent to !isset($var) || $var == false. This also applies to nested structures, such as a multidimensional array or chained properties.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if var does not exist or has a value that is empty or equal to zero, aka falsey, see conversion to boolean. Otherwise returns false.

example.title: A simple empty / isset comparison.
example.programlisting:
<?php
$var = 0;

// Evaluates to true because $var is empty
if (empty($var)) {
    echo '$var is either 0, empty, or not set at all';
}

// Evaluates as true because $var is set
if (isset($var)) {
    echo '$var is set even though it is empty';
}
?>

example.title: empty on String Offsets
example.programlisting:
<?php
$expected_array_got_string = 'somestring';
var_dump(empty($expected_array_got_string['some_key']));
var_dump(empty($expected_array_got_string[0]));
var_dump(empty($expected_array_got_string['0']));
var_dump(empty($expected_array_got_string['0.5']));
var_dump(empty($expected_array_got_string['0 Mostel']));
?>

example.title: empty on multidimensional arrays
example.programlisting:
<?php
$multidimensional = [
    'some' => [
        'deep' => [
            'nested' => 'value'
        ]
    ]
];

if (!empty($multidimensional['some']['some']['nested'])) {
    $someVariable = $multidimensional['some']['deep']['nested'];
}

var_dump(empty($multidimensional['some-undefined-key']));
var_dump(empty($multidimensional['some']['deep']['unknown']));
var_dump(empty($multidimensional['some']['deep']['nested']));
?>

note.simpara: Because this is a language construct and not a function, it cannot be called using variable functions, or named arguments.

note.para: When using empty on inaccessible object properties, the __isset() overloading method will be called, if declared.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get float value of a variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Gets the float value of value.

listitem.para: May be any scalar type. floatval should not be used on objects, as doing so will emit an E_WARNING level error and return 1.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The float value of the given variable. Empty arrays return 0, non-empty arrays return 1.
Strings will most likely return 0 although this depends on the leftmost characters of the string. The common rules of float casting apply.

row.entry: The error level when converting from object was changed from E_NOTICE to E_WARNING.

example.title: floatval Example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$var = '122.34343The';
$float_value_of_var = floatval($var);
echo $float_value_of_var; // 122.34343
?>

example.title: floatval non-numeric leftmost characters Example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$var = 'The122.34343';
$float_value_of_var = floatval($var);
echo $float_value_of_var; // 0
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets the type name of a variable in a way that is suitable for debugging

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the resolved name of the PHP variable value. This function will resolve objects to their class name, resources to their resource type name, and scalar values to their common name as would be used in type declarations.
This function differs from gettype in that it returns type names that are more consistent with actual usage, rather than those present for historical reasons.

listitem.para: The variable being type checked.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para:
Possible values for the returned string are:
Type + State Return Value Notes
null
"null"
-
Booleans (true or false)
"bool"
-
Integers
"int"
-
Floats
"float"
-
Strings
"string"
-
Arrays
"array"
-
Resources
"resource (resourcename)"
-
Resources (Closed)
"resource (closed)"
Example: A file stream after being closed with fclose.
Objects from Named Classes
The full name of the class including its namespace e.g. Foo\Bar
-
Objects from Anonymous Classes
"class@anonymous" or parent class name/interface name if the class extends another class or implements an interface e.g. "Foo\Bar@anonymous"
Anonymous classes are those created through the $x = new class { ... } syntax

example.title: get_debug_type example
example.programlisting:
<?php

namespace Foo;

echo get_debug_type(null), PHP_EOL;
echo get_debug_type(true), PHP_EOL;
echo get_debug_type(1), PHP_EOL;
echo get_debug_type(0.1), PHP_EOL;
echo get_debug_type("foo"), PHP_EOL;
echo get_debug_type([]), PHP_EOL;

$fp = fopen('/examples/book.xml', 'rb');
echo get_debug_type($fp), PHP_EOL;

fclose($fp);
echo get_debug_type($fp), PHP_EOL;

echo get_debug_type(new \stdClass), PHP_EOL;
echo get_debug_type(new class {}), PHP_EOL;

interface A {}
interface B {}
class C {}

echo get_debug_type(new class implements A {}), PHP_EOL;
echo get_debug_type(new class implements A,B {}), PHP_EOL;
echo get_debug_type(new class extends C {}), PHP_EOL;
echo get_debug_type(new class extends C implements A {}), PHP_EOL;

?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:
example.screen: null bool int float string array resource (stream) resource (closed) stdClass class@anonymous Foo\A@anonymous Foo\A@anonymous Foo\C@anonymous Foo\C@anonymous

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns an array of all defined variables

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function returns a multidimensional array containing a list of all defined variables, be them environment, server or user-defined variables, within the scope that get_defined_vars is called.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: A multidimensional array with all the variables.

example.title: get_defined_vars Example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$b = array(1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8);

$arr = get_defined_vars();

// print $b
print_r($arr["b"]);

/* print path to the PHP interpreter (if used as a CGI)
 * e.g. /usr/local/bin/php */
echo $arr["_"];

// print the command-line parameters if any
print_r($arr["argv"]);

// print all the server vars
print_r($arr["_SERVER"]);

// print all the available keys for the arrays of variables
print_r(array_keys(get_defined_vars()));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns an integer identifier for the given resource

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function provides a type-safe way for generating the integer identifier for a resource.

listitem.para: The evaluated resource handle.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The int identifier for the given resource.
This function is essentially an int cast of resource to make it easier to retrieve the resource ID.

example.title: get_resource_id produces the same result as an int cast
example.programlisting:
<?php
$handle = fopen("php://stdout", "w");

echo (int) $handle . "\n";

echo get_resource_id($handle);

?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Returns the resource type

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: This function gets the type of the given resource.

listitem.para: The evaluated resource handle.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: If the given resource is a resource, this function will return a string representing its type. If the type is not identified by this function, the return value will be the string Unknown.
This function will return null and generate an error if resource is not a resource.

example.title: get_resource_type example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$fp = fopen("foo", "w");
echo get_resource_type($fp) . "\n";
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the type of a variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the type of the PHP variable value. For type checking, use is_* functions.

listitem.para: The variable being type checked.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para:
Possible values for the returned string are:
"boolean"
"integer"
"double" (for historical reasons "double" is returned in case of a float, and not simply "float")
"string"
"array"
"object"
"resource"
"resource (closed)" as of PHP 7.2.0
"NULL"
"unknown type"

row.entry: Closed resources are now reported as 'resource (closed)'. Previously the returned value for closed resources were 'unknown type'.

example.title: gettype example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$data = array(1, 1., NULL, new stdClass, 'foo');

foreach ($data as $value) {
    echo gettype($value), "\n";
}

?>
example.simpara: The above example will output something similar to:

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get the integer value of a variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Returns the int value of value, using the specified base for the conversion (the default is base 10). intval should not be used on objects, as doing so will emit an E_WARNING level error and return 1.

listitem.para: The scalar value being converted to an integer
The base for the conversion

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The integer value of value on success, or 0 on failure. Empty arrays return 0, non-empty arrays return 1.

The maximum value depends on the system. 32 bit systems have a maximum signed integer range of -2147483648 to 2147483647. So for example on such a system, intval('1000000000000') will return 2147483647. The maximum signed integer value for 64 bit systems is 9223372036854775807.
Strings will most likely return 0 although this depends on the leftmost characters of the string. The common rules of integer casting apply.

note.simpara: Numeric strings using scientific notation (containing the letter e or E) are first parsed as numbers before being converted to an integer.
Because the numeric part of the string is parsed as a whole, the result is not simply the leading integer part. Large exponents can additionally overflow to PHP_INT_MAX:
See Numeric strings for details on how such strings are interpreted.

row.entry: The error level when converting from object was changed from E_NOTICE to E_WARNING.

example.title: intval examples
example.para: The following examples are based on a 64 bit system.
example.programlisting: <?php echo intval(42), PHP_EOL; // 42 echo intval(4.7), PHP_EOL; // 4 echo intval('42'), PHP_EOL; // 42 echo intval('+42'), PHP_EOL; // 42 echo intval('-42'), PHP_EOL; // -42 echo intval(042), PHP_EOL; // 34 echo intval('042'), PHP_EOL; // 42 echo intval(1e10), PHP_EOL; // 10000000000 echo intval('1e10'), PHP_EOL; // 10000000000 echo intval(0x1A), PHP_EOL; // 26 echo intval('0x1A'), PHP_EOL; // 0 echo intval('0x1A', 0), PHP_EOL; // 26 echo intval('1A', 16), PHP_EOL; // 26 echo intval(42000000), PHP_EOL; // 42000000 echo intval(420000000000000000000), PHP_EOL; // -4275113695319687168 echo intval('420000000000000000000'), PHP_EOL; // 9223372036854775807 echo intval(42, 8), PHP_EOL; // 42 echo intval('42', 8), PHP_EOL; // 34 echo intval(42, 7), PHP_EOL; // 42 echo intval('42', 7), PHP_EOL; // 30 echo intval('1000', 11), PHP_EOL; // 1331 echo intval('1ya', 36), PHP_EOL; // 2530 echo intval(array()), PHP_EOL; // 0 echo intval(array('foo', 'bar')), PHP_EOL; // 1 echo intval(false), PHP_EOL; // 0 echo intval(true), PHP_EOL; // 1 ?>

note.para: The base parameter has no effect unless the value parameter is a string.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Finds whether a variable is an array

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Finds whether the given variable is an array.

listitem.para: The variable being evaluated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if value is an array, false otherwise.

example.title: Check that variable is an array
example.programlisting:
<?php
$yes = array('this', 'is', 'an array');

echo is_array($yes) ? 'Array' : 'not an Array';
echo "\n";

$no = 'this is a string';

echo is_array($no) ? 'Array' : 'not an Array';
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Finds out whether a variable is a boolean

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Finds whether the given variable is a boolean.

listitem.para: The variable being evaluated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if value is a bool, false otherwise.

example.title: is_bool examples
example.programlisting:
<?php
$a = false;
$b = 0;

// Since $a is a boolean, it will return true
if (is_bool($a) === true) {
    echo "Yes, this is a boolean\n";
}

// Since $b is not a boolean, it will return false
if (is_bool($b) === false) {
    echo "No, this is not a boolean\n";
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Verify that a value can be called as a function from the current scope

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Verifies that value is a callable, or that it can be called using the call_user_func function.

listitem.para: The value to be checked.

If set to true the function only verifies that value might be a function or method. It will reject any values that are not invokable objects, Closure, strings, or arrays that do not have a valid structure to be used as a callback. A valid callable array has 2 entries, the first of which is an object or a string, and the second a string.
Receives the "callable name", e.g. "SomeClass::someMethod". Note, however, that despite the implication that SomeClass::someMethod() is a callable static method, this is not the case.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if value is callable, false otherwise.

example.title: Checking whether a string can be called as a function
example.programlisting:
<?php

function someFunction() {}

$functionVariable = 'someFunction';

var_dump(is_callable($functionVariable, false, $callable_name));

var_dump($callable_name);

?>

example.title: Checking whether an array can be called as a function
example.programlisting:
<?php

class SomeClass
{
    public function someMethod() {}
}

$anObject = new SomeClass();

$methodVariable = [$anObject, 'someMethod'];

var_dump(is_callable($methodVariable, true, $callable_name));

var_dump($callable_name);

?>

example.title: is_callable and constructors
example.simpara: Despite the fact that constructors are the methods that are called when an object is created, they are not static methods and is_callable will return false for them. It's not possible to use is_callable to check if a class can be instantiated from the current scope.
example.programlisting:
<?php

class Foo
{
    public function __construct() {}

    public function foo() {}
}

var_dump(
    is_callable(['Foo', '__construct']),
    is_callable(['Foo', 'foo'])
);

$foo = new Foo();
var_dump(is_callable([$foo, '__construct']));

?>

simplelist.member: An object is always callable if it implements __invoke(), and that method is visible in the current scope.
A class name is callable if it implements __callStatic().
If an object implements __call(), then this function will return true for any method on that object, even if the method is not defined.
This function may trigger autoloading if called with the name of a class.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Verify that the contents of a variable is a countable value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Verify that the contents of a variable is an array or an object implementing Countable

listitem.para: The value to check

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if value is countable, false otherwise.

example.title: is_countable examples
example.programlisting: <?php var_dump(is_countable([1, 2, 3])); // bool(true) var_dump(is_countable(new ArrayIterator(['foo', 'bar', 'baz']))); // bool(true) var_dump(is_countable(new ArrayIterator())); // bool(true) var_dump(is_countable(new stdClass())); // bool(false) ?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of is_float

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: is_float.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Finds whether the type of a variable is float

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Finds whether the type of the given variable is float.

note.para: To test if a variable is a number or a numeric string (such as form input, which is always a string), you must use is_numeric.

listitem.para: The variable being evaluated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if value is a float, false otherwise.

example.title: is_float example
example.programlisting:
<?php

var_dump(is_float(27.25));
var_dump(is_float('abc'));
var_dump(is_float(23));
var_dump(is_float(23.5));
var_dump(is_float(1e7));  //Scientific Notation
var_dump(is_float(true));
?>
example.screen: bool(true) bool(false) bool(false) bool(true) bool(true) bool(false)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Find whether the type of a variable is integer

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Finds whether the type of the given variable is integer.

note.para: To test if a variable is a number or a numeric string (such as form input, which is always a string), you must use is_numeric.

listitem.para: The variable being evaluated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if value is an int, false otherwise.

example.title: is_int example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$values = array(23, "23", 23.5, "23.5", null, true, false);
foreach ($values as $value) {
    echo "is_int(";
    var_export($value);
    echo ") = ";
    var_dump(is_int($value));
}
?>
example.screen: is_int(23) = bool(true) is_int('23') = bool(false) is_int(23.5) = bool(false) is_int('23.5') = bool(false) is_int(NULL) = bool(false) is_int(true) = bool(false) is_int(false) = bool(false)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of is_int

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: is_int.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Verify that the contents of a variable is an iterable value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Verify that the contents of a variable is accepted by the iterable pseudo-type, i.e. that it is either an array or an object implementing Traversable

listitem.para: The value to check

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if value is iterable, false otherwise.

example.title: is_iterable examples
example.programlisting:
<?php
var_dump(is_iterable([1, 2, 3])); // bool(true) var_dump(is_iterable(new ArrayIterator([1, 2, 3]))); // bool(true) var_dump(is_iterable((function () { yield 1; })())); // bool(true) var_dump(is_iterable(1)); // bool(false) var_dump(is_iterable(new stdClass())); // bool(false)
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of is_int

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: is_int.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Finds whether a variable is null

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Finds whether the given variable is null.

listitem.para: The variable being evaluated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if value is null, false otherwise.

example.title: is_null example
example.programlisting:
<?php

error_reporting(E_ALL);

$foo = NULL;
var_dump(is_null($inexistent), is_null($foo));

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Finds whether a variable is a number or a numeric string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Determines if the given variable is a number or a numeric string.

listitem.para: The variable being evaluated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if value is a number or a numeric string, false otherwise.

row.entry: Numeric strings ending with whitespace ("42 ") will now return true. Previously, false was returned instead.

example.title: is_numeric examples
example.programlisting:
<?php
$tests = array(
    "42",
    1337,
    0x539,
    02471,
    0b10100111001,
    1337e0,
    "0x539",
    "02471",
    "0b10100111001",
    "1337e0",
    "not numeric",
    array(),
    9.1,
    null,
    '',
);

foreach ($tests as $element) {
    if (is_numeric($element)) {
        echo var_export($element, true) . " is numeric", PHP_EOL;
    } else {
        echo var_export($element, true) . " is NOT numeric", PHP_EOL;
    }
}
?>
example.screen: '42' is numeric 1337 is numeric 1337 is numeric 1337 is numeric 1337 is numeric 1337.0 is numeric '0x539' is NOT numeric '02471' is numeric '0b10100111001' is NOT numeric '1337e0' is numeric 'not numeric' is NOT numeric array ( ) is NOT numeric 9.1 is numeric NULL is NOT numeric '' is NOT numeric

example.title: is_numeric with whitespace
example.programlisting:
<?php
$tests = [
    " 42",
    "42 ",
    "\u{A0}9001", // non-breaking space
    "9001\u{A0}", // non-breaking space
];

foreach ($tests as $element) {
    if (is_numeric($element)) {
        echo var_export($element, true) . " is numeric", PHP_EOL;
    } else {
        echo var_export($element, true) . " is NOT numeric", PHP_EOL;
    }
}
?>
example.simpara: Output of the above example in PHP 8:
example.screen: ' 42' is numeric '42 ' is numeric ' 9001' is NOT numeric '9001 ' is NOT numeric
example.simpara: Output of the above example in PHP 7:
example.screen: ' 42' is numeric '42 ' is NOT numeric ' 9001' is NOT numeric '9001 ' is NOT numeric

refnamediv.refpurpose: Finds whether a variable is an object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Finds whether the given variable is an object.

listitem.para: The variable being evaluated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if value is an object, false otherwise.

row.entry: is_object now returns true for unserialized objects without a class definition (class of __PHP_Incomplete_Class). Previously false was returned.

example.title: is_object example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// Declare a simple function to return an 
// array from our object
function get_students($obj)
{
    if (!is_object($obj)) {
        return false;
    }

    return $obj->students;
}

// Declare a new class instance and fill up 
// some values
$obj = new stdClass();
$obj->students = array('Kalle', 'Ross', 'Felipe');

var_dump(get_students(null));
var_dump(get_students($obj));
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Alias of is_float

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function is an alias of: is_float.

warning.simpara: This alias was DEPRECATED in PHP 7.4.0, and REMOVED as of PHP 8.0.0.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Finds whether a variable is a resource

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Finds whether the given variable is a resource.

listitem.para: The variable being evaluated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if value is a resource, false otherwise.

example.title: is_resource example
example.programlisting:
<?php

$handle = fopen("php://stdout", "w");
if (is_resource($handle)) {
    echo '$handle is a resource';
}

?>

note.para: is_resource is not a strict type-checking method: it will return false if value is a resource variable that has been closed.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Finds whether a variable is a scalar

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Finds whether an expression is evaluated as a scalar value.
See scalar types for more information.

note.para: is_scalar does not consider resource type values to be scalar as resources are abstract datatypes which are currently based on integers. This implementation detail should not be relied upon, as it may change.
is_scalar does not consider NULL to be scalar.

listitem.para: The variable being evaluated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if value is a scalar, false otherwise.

example.title: is_scalar example
example.programlisting:
<?php
function show_var($var) 
{
    if (is_scalar($var)) {
        echo $var, PHP_EOL;
    } else {
        var_dump($var);
    }
}

$pi = 3.1416;
$proteins = array("hemoglobin", "cytochrome c oxidase", "ferredoxin");

show_var($pi);
show_var($proteins)

?>
example.screen: 3.1416 array(3) { [0]=> string(10) "hemoglobin" [1]=> string(20) "cytochrome c oxidase" [2]=> string(10) "ferredoxin" }

refnamediv.refpurpose: Find whether the type of a variable is string

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Finds whether the type of the given variable is string.

listitem.para: The variable being evaluated.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if value is of type string, false otherwise.

example.title: is_string example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$values = array(false, true, null, 'abc', '23', 23, '23.5', 23.5, '', ' ', '0', 0);
foreach ($values as $value) {
    echo "is_string(";
    var_export($value);
    echo ") = ";
    echo var_dump(is_string($value));
}
?>
example.screen: is_string(false) = bool(false) is_string(true) = bool(false) is_string(NULL) = bool(false) is_string('abc') = bool(true) is_string('23') = bool(true) is_string(23) = bool(false) is_string('23.5') = bool(true) is_string(23.5) = bool(false) is_string('') = bool(true) is_string(' ') = bool(true) is_string('0') = bool(true) is_string(0) = bool(false)

refnamediv.refpurpose: Determine if a variable is declared and is different than null

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Determine if a variable is considered set, this means if a variable is declared and is different than null.
If a variable has been unset with the unset function, it is no longer considered to be set.
isset will return false when checking a variable that has been assigned to null. Also note that a null character ("\0") is not equivalent to the PHP null constant.

If multiple parameters are supplied then isset will return true only if all of the parameters are considered set. Evaluation goes from left to right and stops as soon as an unset variable is encountered.

listitem.para: The variable to be checked.
Further variables.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true if var exists and has any value other than null. false otherwise.

refsect1.title: Examples

example.title: isset Examples
example.programlisting:
<?php

$var = '';

// This will evaluate to TRUE so the text will be printed.
if (isset($var)) {
    echo "This var is set so I will print.", PHP_EOL;
}

// In the next examples we'll use var_dump to output
// the return value of isset().

$a = "test";
$b = "anothertest";

var_dump(isset($a));      // TRUE
var_dump(isset($a, $b)); // TRUE

unset ($a);

var_dump(isset($a));     // FALSE
var_dump(isset($a, $b)); // FALSE

$foo = NULL;
var_dump(isset($foo));   // FALSE

?>

example.title: isset on String Offsets
example.programlisting:
<?php
$expected_array_got_string = 'somestring';
var_dump(isset($expected_array_got_string['some_key']));
var_dump(isset($expected_array_got_string[0]));
var_dump(isset($expected_array_got_string['0']));
var_dump(isset($expected_array_got_string[0.5]));
var_dump(isset($expected_array_got_string['0.5']));
var_dump(isset($expected_array_got_string['0 Mostel']));
?>
example.screen: bool(false) bool(true) bool(true) bool(true) bool(false) bool(false)

warning.para: isset only works with variables as passing anything else will result in a parse error. For checking if constants are set use the defined function.

note.simpara: Because this is a language construct and not a function, it cannot be called using variable functions, or named arguments.

note.para: When using isset on inaccessible object properties, the __isset() overloading method will be called, if declared.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Prints human-readable information about a variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: print_r displays information about a variable in a way that's readable by humans.
print_r, var_dump and var_export will also show protected and private properties of objects. Static class members will not be shown.

listitem.para: The expression to be printed.
If you would like to capture the output of print_r, use the return parameter. When this parameter is set to true, print_r will return the information rather than print it.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: If given a string, int or float, the value itself will be printed. If given an array, values will be presented in a format that shows keys and elements. Similar notation is used for objects.
When the return parameter is true, this function will return a string. Otherwise, the return value is true.

row.entry: Return type changed from stringbool to stringtrue.

example.title: print_r example
example.programlisting:
'apple', 'b' => 'banana', 'c' => array ('x', 'y', 'z'));
print_r($a);
?>
example.screen:
Array
(
    [a] => apple
    [b] => banana
    [c] => Array
        (
            [0] => x
            [1] => y
            [2] => z
        )
)

example.title: return parameter example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$b = array ('m' => 'monkey', 'foo' => 'bar', 'x' => array ('x', 'y', 'z'));
$results = print_r($b, true); // $results now contains output from print_r

print_r($results);
?>

note.simpara: When the return parameter is used, this function uses internal output buffering prior to PHP 7.1.0, so it cannot be used inside an ob_start callback function.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Generates a storable representation of a value

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Generates a storable representation of a value.
This is useful for storing or passing PHP values around without losing their type and structure.
To make the serialized string into a PHP value again, use unserialize.

listitem.para: The value to be serialized. serialize handles all types, except the resource-type and some objects (see note below). You can even serialize arrays that contain references to itself. Circular references inside the array/object you are serializing will also be stored. Any other reference will be lost.

When serializing objects, PHP will attempt to call the member functions __serialize() or __sleep() prior to serialization. This is to allow the object to do any last minute clean-up, etc. prior to being serialized. Likewise, when the object is restored using unserialize the __unserialize() or __wakeup() member function is called.

note.para: Object's private members have the class name prepended to the member name; protected members have a '*' prepended to the member name. These prepended values have null bytes on either side.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns a string containing a byte-stream representation of value that can be stored anywhere.

Note that this is a binary string which may include null bytes, and needs to be stored and handled as such. For example, serialize output should generally be stored in a BLOB field in a database, rather than a CHAR or TEXT field.

example.title: serialize example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// $session_data contains a multi-dimensional array with session
// information for the current user.  We use serialize() to store
// it in a database at the end of the request.

$conn = odbc_connect("webdb", "php", "chicken");
$stmt = odbc_prepare($conn,
      "UPDATE sessions SET data = ? WHERE id = ?");
$sqldata = array (serialize($session_data), $_SERVER['PHP_AUTH_USER']);
if (!odbc_execute($stmt, $sqldata)) {
    $stmt = odbc_prepare($conn,
     "INSERT INTO sessions (id, data) VALUES(?, ?)");
    if (!odbc_execute($stmt, array_reverse($sqldata))) {
        /* Something went wrong.. */
    }
}
?>

note.para: Note that many built-in PHP objects cannot be serialized. However, those with this ability either implement the Serializable interface or the magic __serialize()/__unserialize() or __sleep()/__wakeup() methods. If an internal class does not fulfill any of those requirements, it cannot reliably be serialized.
There are some historical exceptions to the above rule, where some internal objects could be serialized without implementing the interface or exposing the methods.

warning.para: When serialize serializes objects, the leading backslash is not included in the class name of namespaced classes for maximum compatibility.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set the type of a variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Set the type of variable var to type.

listitem.para: The variable being converted.

Possibles values of type are:
"boolean" or "bool"
"integer" or "int"
"float" or "double"
"string"
"array"
"object"
"null"

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns true on success or false on failure.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.para: Throws a ValueError if the value of type is not a valid type, as of PHP 8.0.0. Prior to PHP 8.0.0, a E_WARNING was emitted and false was returned.

row.entry: Now throws a ValueError when an invalid type is passed to type. Previously, a E_WARNING was emitted and the function returned false.

example.title: settype example
example.programlisting:
<?php $foo = "5bar"; // string $bar = true; // boolean
settype($foo, "integer"); // $foo is now 5 (integer) settype($bar, "string"); // $bar is now "1" (string)
var_dump($foo, $bar); ?>

note.para: Maximum value for "int" is PHP_INT_MAX.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Get string value of a variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Get the string value of a variable. See the documentation on string for more information on converting to string.
This function performs no formatting on the returned value. If you are looking for a way to format a numeric value as a string, please see sprintf or number_format.

listitem.para: The variable that is being converted to a string.
value may be any scalar type, null, or an object that implements the __toString() method. You cannot use strval on arrays or on objects that do not implement the __toString() method.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The string value of value.

example.title: strval example using PHP magic __toString() method.
example.programlisting:
<?php
class StrValTest
{
    public function __toString()
    {
        return __CLASS__;
    }
}

// Prints 'StrValTest'
echo strval(new StrValTest);
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Creates a PHP value from a stored representation

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: unserialize takes a single serialized variable and converts it back into a PHP value.

warning.para: Do not pass untrusted user input to unserialize regardless of the options value of allowed_classes. Unserialization can result in code being loaded and executed due to object instantiation and autoloading, and a malicious user may be able to exploit this. Use a safe, standard data interchange format such as JSON (via json_decode and json_encode) if you need to pass serialized data to the user.
If you need to unserialize externally-stored serialized data, consider using hash_hmac for data validation. Make sure data is not modified by anyone but you.

listitem.para: The serialized string.
If the variable being unserialized is an object, after successfully reconstructing the object PHP will automatically attempt to call the __unserialize() or __wakeup() methods (if one exists).

note.title: unserialize_callback_func directive
note.para: The callback specified in the unserialize_callback_func directive is called when an undefined class is unserialized. If no callback is specified, the object will be instantiated as __PHP_Incomplete_Class.

listitem.para: Any options to be provided to unserialize, as an associative array.

entry.simpara: Either an array of class names which should be accepted, false to accept no classes, or true to accept all classes. If this option is defined and unserialize encounters an object of a class that isn't to be accepted, then the object will be instantiated as __PHP_Incomplete_Class instead.
Omitting this option is the same as defining it as true: PHP will attempt to instantiate objects of any class.
This option does not affect Enumerations.
The maximum depth of structures permitted during unserialization, and is intended to prevent stack overflows. The default depth limit is 4096 and can be disabled by setting max_depth to 0.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: The converted value is returned, and can be a bool, int, float, string, array or object.
In case the passed string is not unserializeable, false is returned and E_WARNING is issued.

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: Objects may throw Throwables in their unserialization handlers.
As of PHP 8.4.0, if the allowed_classes element of options is neither an array of class names nor a bool, unserialize throws TypeError and ValueError.

row.entry: Now throws TypeError and ValueError if the allowed_classes element of options is neither an array of class names nor a bool.
Unserializing strings using the uppercase "S" tag is now deprecated; use the lowercase "s" tag instead.
Now emits E_WARNING when the input string has unconsumed data.
Now emits E_WARNING when the passed string is not unserializeable; previously E_NOTICE was emitted.
Added the max_depth element of options to set the maximum depth of structures permitted during unserialization.
The allowed_classes element of options is now strictly typed, i.e. if anything other than an array or a bool is given, unserialize returns false and issues an E_WARNING.

example.title: unserialize example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// Here, we use unserialize() to load session data to the
// $session_data array from the string selected from a database.
// This example complements the one described with serialize().

$conn = odbc_connect("webdb", "php", "chicken");
$stmt = odbc_prepare($conn, "SELECT data FROM sessions WHERE id = ?");
$sqldata = array($_SERVER['PHP_AUTH_USER']);
if (!odbc_execute($stmt, $sqldata) || !odbc_fetch_into($stmt, $tmp)) {
    // if the execute or fetch fails, initialize to empty array
    $session_data = array();
} else {
    // we should now have the serialized data in $tmp[0].
    $session_data = unserialize($tmp[0]);
    if (!is_array($session_data)) {
        // something went wrong, initialize to empty array
        $session_data = array();
    }
}
?>

example.title: unserialize_callback_func example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$serialized_object='O:1:"a":1:{s:5:"value";s:3:"100";}';

ini_set('unserialize_callback_func', 'mycallback'); // set your callback_function

function mycallback($classname)
{
    // just include a file containing your class definition
    // you get $classname to figure out which class definition is required
    var_dump($classname);
}

unserialize($serialized_object);
?>

warning.para: false is returned both in the case of an error and if unserializing the serialized false value. It is possible to catch this special case by comparing data with serialize(false) or by catching the issued E_WARNING.

refnamediv.refpurpose: unset a given variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: unset destroys the specified variables.
The behavior of unset inside of a function can vary depending on what type of variable you are attempting to destroy.

listitem.para: The variable to be unset.
Further variables.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

example.title: unset example
example.programlisting:
<?php
// destroy a single variable
unset($foo);

// destroy a single element of an array
unset($bar['quux']);

// destroy more than one variable
unset($foo1, $foo2, $foo3);
?>

note.simpara: Because this is a language construct and not a function, it cannot be called using variable functions, or named arguments.

note.para: It is possible to unset object properties visible in the current context.
If declared, __get() is called when accessing an unset property, and __set() is called when setting an unset property.
It is not possible to unset $this inside an object method.
When using unset on inaccessible object properties, the __unset() overloading method will be called, if declared.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Dumps information about a variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: This function displays structured information about one or more expressions that includes its type and value. Arrays and objects are explored recursively with values indented to show structure.
All public, private and protected properties of objects will be returned in the output unless the object implements a __debugInfo() method.

tip.simpara: As with anything that outputs its result directly to the browser, the output-control functions can be used to capture the output of this function, and save it in a string (for example).

listitem.para: The expression to dump.
Further expressions to dump.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: No value is returned.

example.title: var_dump example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$a = array(1, 2, array("a", "b", "c"));
var_dump($a);
?>

<?php

$b = 3.1;
$c = true;
var_dump($b, $c);

?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Outputs or returns a parsable string representation of a variable

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: var_export gets structured information about the given variable. It is similar to var_dump with one exception: the returned representation is valid PHP code.

listitem.para: The variable you want to export.
If used and set to true, var_export will return the variable representation instead of outputting it.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.para: Returns the variable representation when the return parameter is used and evaluates to true. Otherwise, this function will return null.

row.entry: Exported class names are now fully qualified; previously, the leading backslash was omitted.

Now exports stdClass objects as an array cast to an object ((object) array( ... )), rather than using the nonexistent method stdClass::__setState. The practical effect is that now stdClass is exportable, and the resulting code will even work on earlier versions of PHP.

example.title: var_export Examples
example.programlisting:
<?php
$a = array (1, 2, array ("a", "b", "c"));
var_export($a);
?>

<?php

$b = 3.1;
$v = var_export($b, true);
echo $v;

?>

example.title: Exporting stdClass (since PHP 7.3.0)
example.programlisting:
<?php
$person = new stdClass;
$person->name = 'ElePHPant ElePHPantsdotter';
$person->website = 'https://php.net/elephpant.php';

var_export($person);

example.title: Exporting classes
example.programlisting:
<?php
class A { public $var; }
$a = new A;
$a->var = 5;
var_export($a);
?>

example.title: Using __set_state()
example.programlisting:
<?php
class A
{
    public $var1;
    public $var2;

    public static function __set_state($an_array)
    {
        $obj = new A;
        $obj->var1 = $an_array['var1'];
        $obj->var2 = $an_array['var2'];
        return $obj;
    }
}

$a = new A;
$a->var1 = 5;
$a->var2 = 'foo';

eval('$b = ' . var_export($a, true) . ';'); // $b = A::__set_state(array(
                                            //    'var1' => 5,
                                            //    'var2' => 'foo',
                                            // ));
var_dump($b);
?>

note.para: Variables of type resource couldn't be exported by this function.

var_export does not handle circular references as it would be close to impossible to generate parsable PHP code for that. If you want to do something with the full representation of an array or object, use serialize.

warning.para: Prior to PHP 8.2.0, when var_export exports objects, the leading backslash is not included in the class name of namespaced classes for maximum compatibility.

note.para: To be able to evaluate the PHP generated by var_export, all processed objects must implement the magic __set_state method. The only exception is stdClass, which is exported using an array cast to an object.

preface.title: Introduction
preface.simpara: This extension provides OAuth 1.0a consumer and provider bindings. OAuth is an authorization protocol built on top of HTTP which allows applications to securely access data without having to store usernames and passwords.

section.title: Requirements
section.simpara: PECL/oauth requires PHP 5.1 or newer, ext/hash and ext/pcre.
PECL/oauth may optionally require libcurl if selected at build time. If configured with libcurl, it must be built with HTTPS support.

section.title: Installation
section.simpara: Information for installing this PECL extension may be found in the manual chapter titled Installation of PECL extensions. Additional information such as new releases, downloads, source files, maintainer information, and a CHANGELOG, can be located here: https://pear.php.net/package/oauth

appendix.title: Predefined Constants
appendix.simpara: The constants below are defined by this extension, and will only be available when the extension has either been compiled into PHP or dynamically loaded at runtime.

Most of these constants involve problems, which are also described within the official OAuth Problem Reporting documentation. Note however, that these constant names are specific to PHP, although the naming scheme is similar.

listitem.simpara: OAuth RSA-SHA1 signature method.
OAuth HMAC-SHA1 signature method.
OAuth HMAC-SHA256 signature method.
This constant represents putting OAuth parameters in the Authorization header.
This constant indicates a NoAuth OAuth request.
This constant represents putting OAuth parameters in the request URI.
This constant represents putting OAuth parameters as part of the HTTP POST body.
Use the GET method for the OAuth request.
Use the POST method for the OAuth request.
Use the PUT method for the OAuth request.
Use the HEAD method for the OAuth request.
Use the DELETE method for the OAuth request.
Used by OAuth::setRequestEngine to set the engine to PHP streams, as opposed to OAUTH_REQENGINE_CURL for Curl.
Used by OAuth::setRequestEngine to set the engine to Curl, as opposed to OAUTH_REQENGINE_STREAMS for PHP streams.
Life is good.
The oauth_nonce value was used in a previous request, therefore it cannot be used now.
The oauth_timestamp value was not accepted by the service provider. In this case, the response should also contain the oauth_acceptable_timestamps parameter.
The oauth_consumer_key is temporarily unacceptable to the service provider. For example, the service provider may be throttling the consumer.
The consumer key was refused.
The oauth_signature is invalid, as it does not match the signature computed by the service provider.
The oauth_token has been consumed. It can no longer be used because it has already been used in the previous request(s).
The oauth_token has expired.
The oauth_token has been revoked, and will never be accepted.

The oauth_token was not accepted by the service provider. The reason is not known, but it might be because the token was never issued, already consumed, expired, and/or forgotten by the service provider.
The oauth_verifier is incorrect.
A required parameter was not received. In this case, the response should also contain the oauth_parameters_absent parameter.
The oauth_signature_method was not accepted by service provider.

example.programlisting:
<?php
$req_url = 'https://fireeagle.yahooapis.com/oauth/request_token';
$authurl = 'https://fireeagle.yahoo.net/oauth/authorize';
$acc_url = 'https://fireeagle.yahooapis.com/oauth/access_token';
$api_url = 'https://fireeagle.yahooapis.com/api/0.1';
$conskey = 'your_consumer_key';
$conssec = 'your_consumer_secret';

session_start();

// In state=1 the next request should include an oauth_token.
// If it doesn't go back to 0
if(!isset($_GET['oauth_token']) && $_SESSION['state']==1) $_SESSION['state'] = 0;
try {
  $oauth = new OAuth($conskey,$conssec,OAUTH_SIG_METHOD_HMACSHA1,OAUTH_AUTH_TYPE_URI);
  $oauth->enableDebug();
  if(!isset($_GET['oauth_token']) && !$_SESSION['state']) {
    $request_token_info = $oauth->getRequestToken($req_url);
    $_SESSION['secret'] = $request_token_info['oauth_token_secret'];
    $_SESSION['state'] = 1;
    header('Location: '.$authurl.'?oauth_token='.$request_token_info['oauth_token']);
    exit;
  } else if($_SESSION['state']==1) {
    $oauth->setToken($_GET['oauth_token'],$_SESSION['secret']);
    $access_token_info = $oauth->getAccessToken($acc_url);
    $_SESSION['state'] = 2;
    $_SESSION['token'] = $access_token_info['oauth_token'];
    $_SESSION['secret'] = $access_token_info['oauth_token_secret'];
  }
  $oauth->setToken($_SESSION['token'],$_SESSION['secret']);
  $oauth->fetch("$api_url/user.json");
  $json = json_decode($oauth->getLastResponse());
  print_r($json);
} catch(OAuthException $E) {
  print_r($E);
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Generate a Signature Base String

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Generates a Signature Base String according to pecl/oauth.

URI to encode.
Array of request parameters.

section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: The OAuth extension provides a simple interface to interact with data providers using the OAuth HTTP specification to protect private resources.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Create a new OAuth object

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Creates a new OAuth object

listitem.simpara: The consumer key provided by the service provider.
The consumer secret provided by the service provider.
This optional parameter defines which signature method to use, by default it is OAUTH_SIG_METHOD_HMACSHA1 (HMAC-SHA1).
This optional parameter defines how to pass the OAuth parameters to a consumer, by default it is OAUTH_AUTH_TYPE_AUTHORIZATION (in the Authorization header).

refnamediv.refpurpose: The destructor

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: The destructor.

warning.simpara: This function is currently not documented; only its argument list is available.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Turn off verbose debugging

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Turns off verbose request information (off by default). Alternatively, the debug property can be set to a false value to turn debug off.

refsect1.title: Parameters
refsect1.simpara: This function has no parameters.

row.entry: The related debug property was added.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Fetch an OAuth protected resource

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Fetch a resource.

listitem.simpara: URL to the OAuth protected resource.
Extra parameters to send with the request for the resource.
One of the OAUTH_HTTP_METHOD_* OAUTH constants, which includes GET, POST, PUT, HEAD, or DELETE.
HEAD (OAUTH_HTTP_METHOD_HEAD) can be useful for discovering information prior to the request (if OAuth credentials are in the Authorization header).
HTTP client headers (such as User-Agent, Accept, etc.)

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns true on success or false on failure.

row.entry: Previously returned null on failure, instead of false.

example.title: OAuth::fetch example
example.programlisting:
<?php
try {
    $oauth = new OAuth("consumer_key","consumer_secret",OAUTH_SIG_METHOD_HMACSHA1,OAUTH_AUTH_TYPE_AUTHORIZATION);
    $oauth->setToken("access_token","access_token_secret");

    $oauth->fetch("http://photos.example.net/photo?file=vacation.jpg");

    $response_info = $oauth->getLastResponseInfo();
    header("Content-Type: {$response_info["content_type"]}");
    echo $oauth->getLastResponse();
} catch(OAuthException $E) {
    echo "Exception caught!\n";
    echo "Response: ". $E->lastResponse . "\n";
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Fetch an access token

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Fetch an access token, secret and any additional response parameters from the service provider.

listitem.simpara: URL to the access token API.
Authorization session handle, this parameter does not have any citation in the core OAuth 1.0 specification but may be implemented by large providers. See ScalableOAuth for more information.

For service providers which support 1.0a, a verifier_token must be passed while exchanging the request token for the access token. If the verifier_token is present in $_GET or $_POST it is passed automatically and the caller does not need to specify a verifier_token (usually if the access token is exchanged at the oauth_callback URL). See ScalableOAuth for more information.
HTTP method to use, e.g. GET or POST.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: Returns an array containing the parsed OAuth response on success or false on failure.

row.entry: Previously returned null on failure, instead of false.

example.title: OAuth::getAccessToken example
example.programlisting:
<?php
try {
    $oauth = new OAuth(OAUTH_CONSUMER_KEY,OAUTH_CONSUMER_SECRET);
    $oauth->setToken($request_token,$request_token_secret);
    $access_token_info = $oauth->getAccessToken("https://example.com/oauth/access_token");
    if(!empty($access_token_info)) {
        print_r($access_token_info);
    } else {
        print "Failed fetching access token, response was: " . $oauth->getLastResponse();
    }
} catch(OAuthException $E) {
    echo "Response: ". $E->lastResponse . "\n";
}
?>

example.title: OAuthProvider::__construct example
example.programlisting:
<?php
try {

    $op = new OAuthProvider();

    // Uses user-defined callback functions
    $op->consumerHandler(array($this, 'lookupConsumer'));
    $op->timestampNonceHandler(array($this, 'timestampNonceChecker'));
    $op->tokenHandler(array($this, 'myTokenHandler'));

    // Ignore the foo_uri parameter
    $op->setParam('foo_uri', NULL);

    // No token needed for this end point
    $op->setRequestTokenPath('/v1/oauth/request_token');

    $op->checkOAuthRequest();

} catch (OAuthException $e) {

    echo OAuthProvider::reportProblem($e);
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Set the consumerHandler handler callback

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Sets the consumer handler callback, which will later be called with OAuthProvider::callConsumerHandler.

listitem.simpara: The callable functions name.

refsect1.title: Return Values
refsect1.simpara: No value is returned.

example.title: Example OAuthProvider::consumerHandler callback
example.programlisting:
<?php
function lookupConsumer($provider) {

    if ($provider->consumer_key === 'unknown') {
        return OAUTH_CONSUMER_KEY_UNKNOWN;
    } else if($provider->consumer_key == 'blacklisted' || $provider->consumer_key === 'throttled') {
        return OAUTH_CONSUMER_KEY_REFUSED;
    }

    $provider->consumer_secret = "the_consumers_secret";

    return OAUTH_OK;
}
?>

refnamediv.refpurpose: Generate a random token

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.simpara: Generates a string of pseudo-random bytes.

listitem.simpara: The desired token length, in terms of bytes.
Setting to true means /dev/random will be used for entropy, as otherwise the non-blocking /dev/urandom is used. This parameter is ignored on Windows.

refsect1.title: Return Values

refsect1.title: Errors/Exceptions
refsect1.simpara: If the strong parameter is true, then an E_WARNING level error will be emitted when the fallback rand implementation is used to fill the remaining random bytes (e.g., when not enough random data was found, initially).

example.title: OAuthProvider::generateToken example
example.programlisting:
<?php
$p = new OAuthProvider();

$t = $p->generateToken(4);

echo strlen($t),  PHP_EOL;
echo bin2hex($t), PHP_EOL;

?>

note.simpara: When not enough random data is available to the system, this function will fill the remaining random bytes using the internal PHP rand implementation.

example.title: Example OAuthProvider::timestampNonceHandler callback
example.programlisting:
<?php
function timestampNonceChecker($provider) {

    if ($provider->nonce === 'bad') {
        return OAUTH_BAD_NONCE;
    } elseif ($provider->timestamp == '0') {
        return OAUTH_BAD_TIMESTAMP;
    }

    return OAUTH_OK;
}
?>

example.title: Example OAuthProvider::tokenHandler callback
example.programlisting:
<?php
function tokenHandler($provider) {

    if ($provider->token === 'rejected') {
        return OAUTH_TOKEN_REJECTED;
    } elseif ($provider->token === 'revoked') {
        return OAUTH_TOKEN_REVOKED;
    }

    $provider->token_secret = "the_tokens_secret";
    return OAUTH_OK;
}
?>

preface.title: Introduction
preface.para: The SOAP extension can be used to write SOAP Servers and Clients. It supports subsets of SOAP 1.1, SOAP 1.2 and WSDL 1.1 specifications.

section.title: Requirements
section.simpara: This extension requires the libxml PHP extension. This means passing the --with-libxml, or prior to PHP 7.4 the --enable-libxml, configuration flag, although this is implicitly accomplished because libxml is enabled by default.

section.title: Installation
section.para: To enable SOAP support, configure PHP with --enable-soap.

section.title: Runtime Configuration
section.simpara: The behaviour of these functions is affected by settings in php.ini.
Here's a short explanation of the configuration directives.

listitem.para: Enables or disables the WSDL caching feature.
Sets the directory name where the SOAP extension will put cache files.
Sets the number of seconds (time to live) that cached files will be used instead of the originals.

If soap.wsdl_cache_enabled is on, this setting determines the type of caching. It can be any of: WSDL_CACHE_NONE (0), WSDL_CACHE_DISK (1), WSDL_CACHE_MEMORY (2) or WSDL_CACHE_BOTH (3). This can also be set via the options array in the SoapClient or SoapServer constructor.
Maximum number of in-memory cached WSDL files. Adding further files into a full memory cache will delete the oldest files from it.

appendix.title: Predefined Constants
appendix.simpara: The constants below are defined by this extension, and will only be available when the extension has either been compiled into PHP or dynamically loaded at runtime.
